One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 43201 ("Artificial intelligence and information technology modernization initiative") appropriates $500 million to the Department of Commerce for FY 2025 to modernize federal IT systems using AI and automation technologies.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 43201 ("Artificial intelligence and information technology modernization initiative") authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to use funds to replace legacy systems, adopt efficient AI models, and enhance cybersecurity with AI solutions.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 43201 ("Artificial intelligence and information technology modernization initiative") enacts a 10-year moratorium preventing state and local governments from regulating AI models or systems.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 43201 ("Artificial intelligence and information technology modernization initiative") exempts laws facilitating AI deployment or removing legal barriers, provided they do not impose additional requirements unless federally mandated or generally applicable.

California Executive Order N-12-23 orders California's Government Operations Agency and related entities to draft a report for the Governor within 60 days on beneficial uses and risks of Generative AI (GenAI) by the state.

California Executive Order N-12-23 requires the California Cybersecurity Integration Center and related bodies to perform a risk analysis by March 2024 on GenAI threats to energy infrastructure, brief the Governor on findings, and make public recommendations for actions to guard against GenAI threats when appropriate.

California Executive Order N-12-23 directs various California departments to issue procurement and training guidelines for GenAI by January 2024.

California Executive Order N-12-23 instructs relevant agencies to develop guidelines by July 2024 for using GenAI tools with vulnerable communities.

California Executive Order N-12-23 mandates establishment of GenAI pilot project infrastructure by March 2024.

California Executive Order N-12-23 urges the Governor's Office to partner with UC Berkeley and Stanford to evaluate GenAI's impact.

California Executive Order N-12-23 tasks legal counsel to assess GenAI's regulatory impact and recommend updates.

California Executive Order N-12-23 emphasizes collaboration with civil society, academia, and industry experts in drafting guidelines and conducting analyses.

California Senate Bill 1288 (2024) requires the Superintendent of Public Instruction to form a working group to address artificial intelligence in public schools.

California Senate Bill 1288 (2024) requires the working group to develop guidance and a model policy for safe AI use in education by January 1, 2026.

California Senate Bill 1288 (2024) instructs the working group to create a model policy by July 1, 2026, for the safe and beneficial use of AI that does not negatively impact students or educators.

California Senate Bill 1288 (2024) mandates that the working group consist of certain stakeholders, including public school teachers and schoolsite administrators.

California Senate Bill 1288 (2024) calls the working group to assess AI use in education, including technologies in use, costs, and impacts on educators, and to detail current uses of artificial intelligence in educational settings.

California Senate Bill 1288 (2024) requires the working group to conduct at least three public meetings for stakeholder feedback.

California Senate Bill 1288 (2024) requires the working group to identify other ways in which the state can promote effective practices that minimize risk and maximize benefits to pupils and educators, including establishing communities of practice on the use of artificial intelligence in education.

California Senate Bill 1288 (2024) obliges the group to report findings and recommendations to the Legislature by January 1, 2027.

California Senate Bill 1288 (2024) dissolves the working group upon report submission and repeals provisions by January 1, 2031.

California (2023-2024) AB 96 require public transit employers in California to notify the exclusive employee representative at least 10 months before starting a procurement process for autonomous transit vehicle technology that could eliminate jobs.

California (2023-2024) AB 96 mandate collective bargaining within 30 days upon notification or within 10 days of the public transit employer receiving a written request from the exclusive employee representative, focusing on developing and implementing the autonomous transit technology, creating transition plans for affected workers, and preparing them for new roles.

California (2023-2024) AB 96 ensure that this chapter does not impose any labor requirements that are less protective than existing statutory or contractual obligations.

California (2023-2024) AB 96 grant the Public Employment Relations Board jurisdiction to handle unfair practice charges related to this chapter.

California (2023-2024) AB 96 authorize the board to establish, amend, or repeal regulations necessary to implement the chapter, including emergency regulations for the immediate preservation of public welfare.

California SJR 6 urges the President and Congress to develop a comprehensive Artificial Intelligence Advisory Committee.

California SJR 6 urges the adoption of a comprehensive artificial intelligence policy.

California SJR 6 highlights the importance of federal government planning for workforce changes due to AI.

California SJR 6 emphasizes the need for ethical standards in AI development and employment.

California SJR 6 encourages promoting innovation to help American companies grow.

California SJR 6 notes that California has attracted significant global AI investment.

California SJR 6 calls for bridging the gap between technological change and regulatory response.

California SJR 6 directs transmission of the resolution to key federal officials and California representatives.

California Assembly Bill 1831 (2024) prohibits the creation, distribution, and possession of child sexual assault material (CSAM) generated by artificial intelligence (AI) in California.

California Assembly Bill 1831 (2024) defines AI as a machine-based system capable of generating outputs that influence environments.

California Assembly Bill 1831 (2024) amends California's Penal Code to include AI-generated CSAM as obscene matter, subject to legal penalties.

California Assembly Bill 1831 (2024) classifies the distribution or possession of AI-generated CSAM depicting minors under 18 engaging in sexual conduct as a felony, punishable by imprisonment and fines.

California Assembly Bill 1831 (2024) omits the necessity to prove commercial intent or obscenity for violations involving depictions of real minors.

California Assembly Bill 1831 (2024) specifies enhanced penalties for repeat offenders and those using government-owned computers for CSAM-related offenses.

California Assembly Bill 1831 (2024) exempts law enforcement, medical, scientific, educational activities, and lawful conduct between spouses from these provisions.

California Assembly Bill 1831 (2024) requires revenue from fines to support sexual assault investigator training and services for human trafficking victims.

California Assembly Bill 1831 (2024) becomes operative only if Senate Bill 1381 is enacted by January 1, 2025.

California Senate Bill 1381 (2024) expands existing child pornography laws to include materials digitally altered or generated by artificial intelligence.

California Senate Bill 1381 (2024) prohibits the production, distribution, or possession of AI-generated depictions involving minors engaging in sexual conduct.

California Senate Bill 1381 (2024) imposes penalties including fines and imprisonment for violations involving AI-generated content depicting minors, including recruiting minors to create such content.

California Senate Bill 1381 (2024) specifies exemptions for legally emancipated minors; law enforcement; legitimate medical, educational, or scientific activities; and lawful conduct between spouses.

California Senate Bill 1381 (2024) allows forfeiture of AI-generated depictions involving minors engaging in sexual conduct that is in the possession of city, county, or state officials or agencies.

California Senate Bill 1381 (2024) allows destruction of AI-generated materials regardless of criminal conviction.

California Senate Bill 1381 (2024) mandates that the act becomes operative only if AB 1831 is enacted by January 1, 2025.

California AB 2839 (2024) prohibits the distribution of materially deceptive AI-generated content related to elections, such as deepfakes, during specified periods before and after elections in California.

California AB 2839 (2024) requires disclosures for manipulated content used by candidates, stating "This [media type] has been manipulated," ensuring transparency.

California AB 2839 (2024) allows recipients of deceptive content, candidates, or election officials to seek injunctive relief and damages against violators.

California AB 2839 (2024) exempts broadcasting stations from liability under certain conditions, such as bona fide news coverage or compliance with existing federal laws.

California AB 2839 (2024) defines key terms like "deepfake," "materially deceptive content," and "malice" to establish clear guidelines.

California AB 2839 (2024) applies provisions to all languages and mandates that disclosures match the language of the advertisement.

California AB 2839 (2024) includes an urgency clause, making the act effective immediately to protect upcoming elections from AI-driven disinformation.

California 2023 SCR 17 (Relative to AI) affirms the California Legislature's commitment to President Biden’s vision for safe AI and the "Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights."

California 2023 SCR 17 (Relative to AI) commits the Legislature to examining and implementing principles, including Safe and Effective Systems, Algorithmic Discrimination Protections, Data Privacy, Notice and Explanation, and Human Alternatives in AI-related policies.

California 2023 SCR 17 (Relative to AI) directs the Secretary of the Senate to transmit copies of this resolution for distribution.

California AB 2885 (2024) requires, by September 1, 2024, the California Department of Technology to inventory high-risk automated decision systems used or proposed by state agencies, detailing decision-making roles, data usage, and risk mitigation measures.

California AB 2885 (2024) mandates an annual report on high-risk systems to legislative committees until 2029.

California AB 2885 (2024) defines "artificial intelligence" as systems that infer inputs to influence environments, and outlines "high-risk automated decision systems" that impact significant areas like housing and employment.

California AB 2885 (2024) obliges the evaluation of deepfake technologies' impact on state governance and residents, with a report due by October 1, 2024.

California AB 2885 (2024) stipulates annual public reporting on automation impacts, including AI, within economic development subsidies for warehouse distribution centers, focusing on job effects and workforce changes.

California AB 2885 (2024) ensures public access to information about economic subsidies and associated impacts from AI and automation developments.

California AB 2355 (2024), Section 8 requires committees creating or distributing qualified political advertisements to include a disclosure stating, “Ad generated or substantially altered using artificial intelligence,” in a clear and conspicuous manner.

California AB 2355 (2024), Section 8 mandates that the disclosure be displayed or spoken as specified in existing sections of the Government Code.

California AB 2355 (2024), Section 8 excludes alteration or negation of rights under Section 230 of Title 47 of the U.S. Code for interactive service providers.

California AB 2355 (2024), Section 8 authorizes the Commission to seek injunctive relief or pursue administrative or civil remedies if committees fail to comply with disclosure requirements.

California AB 2355 (2024), Section 8 defines "artificial intelligence" and specifies conditions under which media is considered "generated or substantially altered using artificial intelligence.”

California AB 2355 (2024), Section 8 clarifies that immaterial alterations, such as cosmetic adjustments or resizing, do not qualify as being substantially altered by artificial intelligence.

California AB 2355 (2024), Section 8 specifies that non-compliance does not constitute a misdemeanor.

California AB 1836 amends the California Civil Code to impose liability on individuals using a deceased personality's likeness without consent, including AI-generated digital replicas. Requires violators to compensate for unauthorized use, with statutory minimums and profit disgorgement. Excludes certain uses such as news, satire, and fleeting references from consent requirements.

California AB 1836 recognizes posthumous rights as transferable property interests, extending rights to heirs or designated persons. Limits rights duration to 70 years post-death and outlines specific inheritance rules. Mandates registration with the Secretary of State for enforcing claims, making these registrations public records.

California AB 1836 clarifies that certain artistic and informational works are exempt unless they serve commercial product promotion. Outlines exceptions for media owners unless knowingly complicit in unauthorized use. Enforces consistency with existing law by rendering remedies cumulative. Establishes retroactive application of rights back to those deceased before January 1, 1985.

Budget Act of 2024 establishes monthly Generative AI meetings with legislative staff to discuss Executive Order N-12-23 implementation.

Budget Act of 2024 requires updates on deliverable completion, proof of concept implementation, and funding source identification.

Budget Act of 2024 supports budget requests for generative AI technology solutions if additional resources are needed.

Budget Act of 2024 defines "artificial intelligence" and "generative artificial intelligence" within the provisions.

Budget Act of 2024 treats data collected in GenAI pilot projects as personal information per Civil Code Section 1798.3.

Budget Act of 2024 prohibits GenAI pilot projects from including sensitive personal information, data on minors, educational records, or medical information.

Budget Act of 2024 mandates compliance with California's GenAI Guidelines for departments in GenAI pilot projects.

Budget Act of 2024 permits the use of de-identified data for research to justify resource requests if expanding pilot program scope.

California Senate Bill 942 (2024) enacts the California AI Transparency Act, requiring covered providers of generative AI systems with significant user bases to offer free AI detection tools.

California Senate Bill 942 (2024) mandates that AI detection tools assess whether content was created or altered by the provider's AI, output system provenance data, and avoid personal provenance data.

California Senate Bill 942 (2024) prohibits the collection or retention of personal information from detection tool users, barring specific opt-in scenarios.

California Senate Bill 942 (2024) requires AI-generated content to include both manifest and latent disclosures identifying it as AI-generated, with details about the provider and system.

California Senate Bill 942 (2024) demands that licenses for GenAI systems include obligations for content disclosures.

California Senate Bill 942 (2024) imposes civil penalties of $5,000 per violation for non-compliance, with each day constituting a separate violation.

California Senate Bill 942 (2024) excludes specific entertainment products from applicability and sets the operative date as January 1, 2026.

California Senate Bill 1120 (2024) mandates health care service plans and disability insurers using AI for utilization review or management to comply with specific regulations.

California Senate Bill 1120 (2024) requires AI tools to base decisions on individual clinical data and prohibits reliance solely on group datasets.

California Senate Bill 1120 (2024) prohibits AI tools from denying, delaying, or modifying health care services based on medical necessity; such determinations must be made by licensed professionals.

California Senate Bill 1120 (2024) ensures AI tools do not replace human decision-making or discriminate against enrollees.

California Senate Bill 1120 (2024) requires AI tools' criteria to comply with state and federal laws and be open for audits.

California Senate Bill 1120 (2024) mandates regular review and revision of AI tools for accuracy and reliability.

California Senate Bill 1120 (2024) prohibits misuse of patient data beyond intended purposes, in line with privacy laws.

California Senate Bill 1120 (2024) stipulates that AI use should not harm enrollees and requires disclosure of AI usage policies.

California Assembly Bill 2876 (2024) mandates the commission to consider incorporating AI literacy content into the mathematics, science, and history-social science curriculum frameworks when those frameworks are next revised after January 1, 2025.

California Assembly Bill 2876 (2024) requires the commission to consider including AI literacy in the criteria for evaluating mathematics, science, and history-social science instructional materials adopted by the state board after January 1, 2025.

California Assembly Bill 2876 (2024) defines "AI literacy" as the knowledge, skills, and attitudes related to how artificial intelligence works, including its principles, concepts, applications, limitations, implications, and ethical considerations.

California Assembly Bill 2876 (2024) directs the commission to also consider including media literacy content in the curriculum frameworks and instructional materials for English language arts and English language development, mathematics, science, and history-social science when these are revised or adopted after specified dates.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title IX "Take It Down Act") amends the Communications Act of 1934 to criminalize the publication of nonconsensual intimate visual depictions, including digital forgeries created using AI, in interstate or foreign commerce.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title IX "Take It Down Act") defines digital forgeries as depictions created with AI or other technological means that are indistinguishable from authentic depictions.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title IX "Take It Down Act") prohibits the publication of such depictions for both adults and minors, with specific intent requirements such as causing harm or for sexual gratification.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title IX "Take It Down Act") imposes penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for offenses involving adults and harsher penalties for those involving minors.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title IX "Take It Down Act") mandates covered platforms, such as websites with user-generated content, to establish a process for the removal of nonconsensual depictions within 48 hours of receiving a request.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title IX "Take It Down Act") enforces compliance through the Federal Trade Commission, treating violations as unfair or deceptive acts.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title IX "Take It Down Act") provides exceptions for certain authorized law enforcement and good faith activities and outlines processes for restitution and forfeiture related to violations.

TAKE IT DOWN Act the TAKE IT DOWN Act mandates covered platforms to remove nonconsensual intimate visual depictions, including those created by artificial intelligence (AI), known as digital forgeries.

TAKE IT DOWN Act prohibits intentional disclosure of such depictions without consent, especially targeting AI-altered, identifiable images.

TAKE IT DOWN Act imposes penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for offenses involving adults and minors.

TAKE IT DOWN Act requires covered platforms to establish a removal process within one year of the Act’s enactment, responding promptly (within 48 hours) upon receiving a valid removal request.

TAKE IT DOWN Act mandates reasonable efforts to remove identical copies across platforms.

TAKE IT DOWN Act exempts platforms from liability for good faith removal of purportedly nonconsensual depictions.

TAKE IT DOWN Act empowers the Federal Trade Commission to enforce compliance, treating noncompliance as an unfair or deceptive act.

TAKE IT DOWN Act specifies legal exceptions, including disclosures for lawful or investigative purposes.

TAKE IT DOWN Act defines covered platforms as public websites or applications hosting user-generated content.

California Assembly Bill 2013 (2024) defines key terms such as "artificial intelligence," "developer," "generative artificial intelligence," and "synthetic data generation" to clarify the scope and applicability of the regulations.

California Assembly Bill 2013 (2024) mandates developers of generative AI systems, including parties that release a new system or make substantial modifications to a system, released on or after January 1, 2022 to publicly disclose training data documentation on their websites by January 1, 2026, and for each subsequent release.

California Assembly Bill 2013 (2024) requires documentation to include a summary of datasets, sources, purposes, data points, intellectual property status, personal information, any data processing or modifications, and the use of synthetic data generation.

California Assembly Bill 2013 (2024) exempts AI systems solely for security, aircraft operation in national airspace, or national security and defense provided they are only available to federal entities.

California Assembly Bill 2905 (2024) amends the Public Utilities Code to regulate the use of automatic dialing-announcing devices in California.

California Assembly Bill 2905 (2024) requires person calling to make a natural voice announcement before using an automatic dialing-announcing device, which includes stating the nature of the call and the business or organization details; inquiring whether the called person consents to hear a prerecorded message; and informing the called person if the message uses an artificial voice.

California Assembly Bill 2905 (2024) requires person calling to disconnect the device after call termination by either party.

California Assembly Bill 2905 (2024) defines the terms “artificial intelligence” and “artificial voice."

California Assembly Bill 3030 (2024) requires health facilities, clinics, and physician offices using generative AI for patient communications in a variety of modalities to include a disclaimer indicating AI generation.

California Assembly Bill 3030 (2024) mandates the disclaimer's prominence at the beginning, end, and/or throughout written, audio, and video communications, with instructions for contacting a human provider.

California Assembly Bill 3030 (2024) exempts communications reviewed by a licensed health care provider from disclaimer requirements.

California Assembly Bill 3030 (2024) defines key terms, including "artificial intelligence," "generative artificial intelligence," and "patient clinical information."

California Assembly Bill 3030 (2024) subjects licensed health facilities, clinics, and physicians violating these requirements to enforcement mechanisms.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 222 ("Modification to artificial intelligence education strategy") amends Section 256 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2020 to mandate the development of AI and machine learning education platforms.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 222 ("Modification to artificial intelligence education strategy") requires the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense, in coordination with the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness, to create distance education courses on foundational AI and machine learning concepts and their ethical and responsible use.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 222 ("Modification to artificial intelligence education strategy") mandates making these courses available to Armed Forces members within 180 days of the enactment of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 222 ("Modification to artificial intelligence education strategy") requires the Secretary of Defense to report to congressional defense committees on the progress of implementing this educational initiative within 270 days of the subsection's enactment.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1066 ("Reports on approval and deployment of lethal autonomous weapon systems") mandates the Secretary of Defense to submit annual reports to congressional defense committees on lethal autonomous weapon systems by December 31, 2025, and annually until December 31, 2029.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1066 ("Reports on approval and deployment of lethal autonomous weapon systems") requires inclusion of a comprehensive list of lethal autonomous weapon systems approved for use, waived from review, under review, and not approved, along with relevant dates.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1066 ("Reports on approval and deployment of lethal autonomous weapon systems") specifies that the initial report should cover all relevant periods as determined by the Secretary, while subsequent reports cover periods since the last report.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1066 ("Reports on approval and deployment of lethal autonomous weapon systems") allows for reports to be unclassified but permits a classified annex.

Foreign Investment Guardrails to Help Thwart (FIGHT) China Act imposes sanctions on certain Chinese entities and individuals engaged in defense or surveillance sectors through the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

Foreign Investment Guardrails to Help Thwart (FIGHT) China Act requires notification for U.S. investments in prohibited technologies and establishes penalties for violations, reflecting stringent oversight on national security transactions involving China.

Foreign Investment Guardrails to Help Thwart (FIGHT) China Act mandates divestment of securities by U.S. persons from entities on the Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies List, prohibiting holding after a specified period.

Foreign Investment Guardrails to Help Thwart (FIGHT) China Act outlines procedures for approving exceptions to these prohibitions through waivers, subject to congressional notification and review.

Foreign Investment Guardrails to Help Thwart (FIGHT) China Act establishes a framework for using collaborative reports and a public database for covered foreign persons while protecting sensitive information.

Foreign Investment Guardrails to Help Thwart (FIGHT) China Act outlines regulations and processes to enforce prohibitions, commands an annual report to assess developments, and encourage multilateral cooperation to prevent China’s acquisition of sensitive technologies.

Foreign Investment Guardrails to Help Thwart (FIGHT) China Act designates Commerce and Treasury authorities to oversee implementation and allows Presidential delegation of some powers.

S257 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025 requires the Assistant Secretary of Commerce to promote the resilience of critical supply chains and emerging technologies vital for U.S. national security, in consultation with key government figures.

S257 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025 mandates the creation of a Supply Chain Resilience Working Group within 120 days, comprising multiple federal agencies, to evaluate and model critical supply chains, including those for emerging technologies such as AI.

S257 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025 directs the Assistant Secretary to identify vulnerabilities, develop response strategies, and assess domestic and allied manufacturing capacities within one year.

S257 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025 prohibits disclosure of voluntarily submitted critical supply chain information under FOIA, providing protection against unauthorized use.

S257 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025 necessitates annual reporting to Congress detailing strategies and evaluations of supply chain resiliency, including the role of technologies such as AI.

S257 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025 limits the Act’s funding to existing resources and imposes a 10-year termination period for the Act’s provisions.

H2444 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025 establishes a Supply Chain Resilience Working Group to assess and address vulnerabilities in critical supply chains and technologies.

H2444 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025 mandates consultations with various stakeholders, including government entities and international allies, to improve supply chain readiness and response to disruptions.

H2444 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025 encourages domestic production and reduced reliance on countries posing national security risks for critical goods and technologies, including AI.

H2444 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025 protects voluntarily submitted critical supply chain information from public disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act.

H2444 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025 requires periodic assessments and strategy reports to Congress on supply chain resiliency and emerging technology impacts.

H2444 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025 sets a 10-year term for the act's provisions and requires a public comment period for certain designations and reports.

Next Generation Pipelines Research and Development Act establishes a demonstration initiative to fund advanced pipeline technologies via competitive merit reviews, focusing on AI-driven advancements in leak detection, sensor technologies, and machine learning for pipeline monitoring.

Next Generation Pipelines Research and Development Act directs funding of $45 million in 2026 and $50 million annually from 2027-2030 for relevant projects, with a sunset provision five years post-enactment.

Next Generation Pipelines Research and Development Act forms a Joint Research and Development Program involving the Department of Energy and other federal agencies to advance AI and machine learning models for pipeline systems, ensuring security and integrity.

Next Generation Pipelines Research and Development Act creates a National Pipeline Modernization Center to commercialize AI-assisted pipeline technologies, requiring competitive selection and location adjacent to existing infrastructure.

Next Generation Pipelines Research and Development Act mandates the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop standards supporting AI in pipeline safety, with a $2.5 million annual allocation from 2026-2030.

Next Generation Pipelines Research and Development Act aims to leverage and complement existing energy and pipeline safety infrastructure and programs through collaborative interagency efforts and non-federal funding matching.

Promoting United States Leadership in Standards Act of 2025 mandates the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), in coordination with the Secretary of State, to brief Congress about opportunities for U.S. support in developing AI standards within one year.

Promoting United States Leadership in Standards Act of 2025 requires the establishment of a web portal to inform U.S. industry and federal agencies about international AI standards efforts and participation opportunities.

Promoting United States Leadership in Standards Act of 2025 initiates a pilot program to support AI standards meetings in the U.S. by awarding grants to eligible entities.

Promoting United States Leadership in Standards Act of 2025 specifies eligibility criteria for these grants and defines allowable costs.

Promoting United States Leadership in Standards Act of 2025 requires annual briefings to Congress on the pilot program's effectiveness.

Promoting United States Leadership in Standards Act of 2025 directs the development of recommendations for a permanent program if deemed feasible within two years.

Promoting United States Leadership in Standards Act of 2025 authorizes a budget of $5 million for the program from fiscal years 2024 through 2028.

Promoting United States Leadership in Standards Act of 2025 ends the pilot program five years post-enactment, with consideration for permanent implementation.

Leading Ethical AI Development (LEAD) for Kids Act establishes the LEAD for Kids Standards Board to govern AI systems affecting children in California.

Leading Ethical AI Development (LEAD) for Kids Act requires AI developers to classify systems as "covered products" with risk assessments ranging from prohibited to low risk.

Leading Ethical AI Development (LEAD) for Kids Act mandates developers to register covered products and submit risk assessments by July 1, 2028.

Leading Ethical AI Development (LEAD) for Kids Act prohibits AI use that adversely impacts children's health, safety, or privacy without informed consent.

Leading Ethical AI Development (LEAD) for Kids Act requires companion chatbots and systems that assess emotional states or collect biometric data to receive additional scrutiny.

Leading Ethical AI Development (LEAD) for Kids Act mandates independent audits based on risk level and public incident reporting for adverse impacts.

Leading Ethical AI Development (LEAD) for Kids Act obligates deployers to prevent unauthorized child access and adhere to usage requirements that do not increase system risk.

Leading Ethical AI Development (LEAD) for Kids Act prohibits retaliation against employees reporting violations.

Leading Ethical AI Development (LEAD) for Kids Act allows the Attorney General to enforce violations with penalties, and provides a private right of action for harmed children.

Leading Ethical AI Development (LEAD) for Kids Act creates the LEAD for Kids AI Fund to support these regulatory activities.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2025, Section 2 "Department of Energy quantum information science research program" amends the National Quantum Initiative Act to enhance quantum information science, engineering, and technology research led by the Secretary of Energy.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2025, Section 2 "Department of Energy quantum information science research program" mandates the establishment of National Quantum Information Science Research Centers to drive breakthroughs and collaborate with industries and other entities.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2025, Section 2 "Department of Energy quantum information science research program" directs cooperative research and commercialization efforts to advance various quantum fields, including AI, quantum computing, communications, and security.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2025, Section 2 "Department of Energy quantum information science research program" requires the development of a strategic 10-year plan for high-performance computing systems integrating quantum and AI.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2025, Section 2 "Department of Energy quantum information science research program" funds a new $20 million per year program for quantum high-performance computing R&D from 2026 to 2030.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2025, Section 2 "Department of Energy quantum information science research program" establishes a university-led traineeship program and prohibits funding to entities affiliated with Confucius Institute or certain foreign entities.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2025, Section 2 "Department of Energy quantum information science research program" prioritizes coordination with other federal agencies and entities.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2025, Section 2 "Department of Energy quantum information science research program" allocates $175 million annually for these initiatives from 2026 to 2030 with specific restrictions.

TAME Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act directs the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to use artificial intelligence (AI) for adapting to extreme weather and wildfires.

TAME Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act mandates the development of comprehensive weather forecasting training datasets and AI weather models.

TAME Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act requires NOAA to explore advanced AI applications to enhance weather forecasts and improve information delivery.

TAME Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act instructs NOAA to provide technical assistance for AI weather model usage and establish best practices.

TAME Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act directs the creation of an AI-driven program to predict, detect, and analyze wildfires.

TAME Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act advocates for partnerships with private and academic entities for innovation in environmental forecasting.

TAME Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act obligates NOAA to strengthen its workforce expertise in AI applications for weather forecasting.

TAME Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act allows public access to data and code developed under the Act, with considerations for national security and intellectual property.

TAME Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act provides guidance on minimizing environmental impacts when using AI technologies in these initiatives.

Responsible AI safety and education act amends New York's general business law to introduce the Responsible AI Safety and Education (RAISE) Act, implementing transparency requirements for deploying AI frontier models.

Responsible AI safety and education act requires large AI developers to implement and retain a written safety and security protocol that must be published with redactions and submitted to the Attorney General and Homeland Security.

Responsible AI safety and education act stipulates annual reviews of the protocol to accommodate any advancements.

Responsible AI safety and education act requires prompt reporting of safety incidents to authorities within 72 hours.

Responsible AI safety and education act prohibits knowingly making false or misleading statements concerning AI documentation.

Responsible AI safety and education act empowers the Attorney General to bring civil actions for violations, with penalties up to $30 million for repeated offenses.

Responsible AI safety and education act confirms that the Act applies exclusively to frontier AI models developed or operating in New York State.

Responsible AI safety and education act clarifies that this Act doesn't establish a private right of action and is cumulative with other legal obligations.

Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025 expands the functions of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to include the development of workforce frameworks for critical and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025 mandates the Director of NIST to develop, publish, and periodically update a workforce framework specifically for artificial intelligence within 540 days of the Act's enactment.

Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025 requires the inclusion of competencies, workforce categories, and work roles relevant to AI in the workforce framework, highlighting career pathways for individuals with nontraditional backgrounds.

Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025 obligates consultation with federal agencies, industry, and educational institutions to develop these frameworks.

Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025 demands reports to Congress on the updates and practical applications of the frameworks, with a focus on increasing employer and educational adoption.

Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025 promotes global adoption by producing resources in multiple languages.

Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025 incorporates professional and employability skills relevant to AI workforce frameworks and assesses additional framework needs for emerging technologies, such as quantum information science.

H.R.1851 Fighter Force Preservation and Recapitalization Act of 2025 amends U.S. Code to increase the required minimum number of fighter aircraft in the Air Force to 1,900, extending compliance to 2030, but allows temporary reductions for transitions, provided levels don't fall below 1,800.

H.R.1851 Fighter Force Preservation and Recapitalization Act of 2025 mandates annual reports by the Secretary of the Air Force to Congress on the status of fighter aircraft inventory, including new acquisitions, unit assignments, and any legacy retirements, with penalties for late submission.

H.R.1851 Fighter Force Preservation and Recapitalization Act of 2025 requires prioritization of recapitalized fighter allocations to existing Air Force squadrons, allowing one-for-one legacy aircraft retirement.

H.R.1851 Fighter Force Preservation and Recapitalization Act of 2025 obligates the Air National Guard to maintain 25 fighter squadrons and restricts retiring legacy or fifth-generation aircraft unless unserviceable.

H.R.1851 Fighter Force Preservation and Recapitalization Act of 2025 directs an annual recapitalization plan for Air National Guard squadrons, assessing financial and readiness impacts, with a focus on acquiring F–16 Block 70 aircraft.

H.R.1851 Fighter Force Preservation and Recapitalization Act of 2025 defines terms such as "advanced capability fighter aircraft," "fifth-generation fighter aircraft," and "next-generation air dominance fighter aircraft."

H.R.1569 CATCH Fentanyl Act mandates the establishment of pilot projects by the Secretary of Homeland Security within one year to evaluate technologies for enhancing inspection processes at U.S. land ports of entry.

H.R.1569 CATCH Fentanyl Act requires testing of at least five types of nonintrusive inspection technology enhancements, including artificial intelligence and machine learning, to aid in detecting contraband and threats.

H.R.1569 CATCH Fentanyl Act ensures private sector involvement and emphasizes cost-effectiveness in technology selection.

H.R.1569 CATCH Fentanyl Act obligates safeguarding data privacy during inspections, with adherence to laws, data anonymization techniques, and regular audits.

H.R.1569 CATCH Fentanyl Act demands reports analyzing effectiveness, recommendations for widespread technology use, and cost breakdowns.

H.R.1569 CATCH Fentanyl Act includes necessary privacy and civil liberties impact assessments and reports before implementation and post-pilot.

H.R.1569 CATCH Fentanyl Act prohibits new appropriations, relying on existing resources for implementation.

Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth establishes a White House Task Force on Artificial Intelligence Education to promote AI literacy and proficiency in the United States, chaired by the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy.

Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth requires the Task Force to coordinate Federal efforts on AI education, including organizing the Presidential Artificial Intelligence Challenge to encourage collaboration and innovation in AI.

Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth mandates public-private partnerships to provide K-12 AI education resources and calls for increased funding and resources to develop AI literacy.

Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth prioritizes AI-focused training for educators and the integration of AI tools in classrooms through grants and public-private partnerships.

Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth instructs the Secretary of Education and other Federal entities to support the use of AI in educational settings to improve outcomes.

Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth directs the Secretary of Labor to increase AI-related Registered Apprenticeships and promote AI skill development through the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA).

Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth encourages agencies to prioritize AI in educational grant programs.

Transformational Artificial intelligence to Modernize the Economy against Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act mandates the improvement of weather, water, and wildfire forecast accuracy through artificial intelligence (AI) by federal agencies.

Transformational Artificial intelligence to Modernize the Economy against Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act promotes public-private partnerships to expedite AI adoption for mitigating environmental hazards.

Transformational Artificial intelligence to Modernize the Economy against Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act directs the development and curation of comprehensive weather forecasting training datasets in consultation with various federal and research entities within four years.

Transformational Artificial intelligence to Modernize the Economy against Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act permits exploration of AI weather models for global, regional, and local forecasting.

Transformational Artificial intelligence to Modernize the Economy against Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act encourages the use of AI to enhance communication and public understanding of weather risks.

Transformational Artificial intelligence to Modernize the Economy against Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act mandates regular reporting to Congress on activities and potential risks of foreign access to U.S. weather data.

Transformational Artificial intelligence to Modernize the Economy against Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act allows the Under Secretary to enter partnerships, including co-investment strategies, for AI and environmental forecasting innovation.

Transformational Artificial intelligence to Modernize the Economy against Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act provides for public access to operational AI weather models, subject to national security and intellectual property considerations.

Transformational Artificial intelligence to Modernize the Economy against Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act authorizes appropriations to support these initiatives through fiscal years 2026 to 2030.

Fair Grocery Pricing Act prohibits food producers from using algorithmic systems to artificially inflate prices or reduce supply through coordinating functions or tacit agreements.

Fair Grocery Pricing Act deems any such use as a per se violation of the Sherman Act.

Fair Grocery Pricing Act mandates the Federal Trade Commission and the Attorney General to enforce this prohibition using applicable antitrust laws.

Fair Grocery Pricing Act authorizes civil actions by the FTC, state attorneys general, and aggrieved persons to recover damages and seek penalties.

Fair Grocery Pricing Act invalidates pre-dispute arbitration agreements and joint action waivers related to violations of this Act at the plaintiff’s election.

Fair Grocery Pricing Act ensures that this Act does not modify existing antitrust laws or preempt state or local laws.

Fair Grocery Pricing Act includes a severability clause to uphold remaining provisions if any part is deemed unconstitutional.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025, Subtitle C--"Matters Involving Uncrewed Systems" establishes a National Advisory Committee on Autonomous Maritime Systems to advise the Secretary on regulation and use within U.S. territorial waters, comprising 15 expert members representing diverse maritime sectors.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025, Subtitle C--"Matters Involving Uncrewed Systems" implements a two-year pilot program exempting small uncrewed maritime systems from certain regulatory requirements when operated by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, unless immediate safety concerns arise.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025, Subtitle C--"Matters Involving Uncrewed Systems" mandates the Coast Guard to develop a training course on small uncrewed maritime systems, addressing operations, safety, and communication aspects over three years.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025, Subtitle C--"Matters Involving Uncrewed Systems" incorporates National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration representation into the Automated and Autonomous Vessel Policy Council.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025, Subtitle C--"Matters Involving Uncrewed Systems" requires the Coast Guard to submit a report within one year establishing an uncrewed systems capabilities office, detailing strategies for technology acquisition, coordination, collaboration, and expanding capabilities using AI and machine learning.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025, Subtitle C--"Matters Involving Uncrewed Systems" defines relevant terms, including "counter-uncrewed system" and "small uncrewed maritime systems."

Wildfire Prevention Act of 2025, Section 302 "Public-private wildfire technology deployment and testbed partnership." establishes a deployment and testbed pilot program for new and innovative wildfire technologies within 60 days of enactment.

Wildfire Prevention Act of 2025, Section 302 "Public-private wildfire technology deployment and testbed partnership." requires coordination among the Secretaries of Agriculture and Interior and covered agencies to identify technology priority areas like AI, quantum sensing, and augmented reality for wildfire prevention and mitigation.

Wildfire Prevention Act of 2025, Section 302 "Public-private wildfire technology deployment and testbed partnership." prioritizes covered entities with emerging technologies that address identified issues for participation in the pilot program.

Wildfire Prevention Act of 2025, Section 302 "Public-private wildfire technology deployment and testbed partnership." mandates real-time testing and on-the-ground coordination between selected entities and covered agencies.

Wildfire Prevention Act of 2025, Section 302 "Public-private wildfire technology deployment and testbed partnership." requires public outreach to invite applications from entities for technology testing and demonstration in key priority areas.

Wildfire Prevention Act of 2025, Section 302 "Public-private wildfire technology deployment and testbed partnership." obligates annual reporting to appropriate committees, detailing participating entities, tested technologies, cost estimates, and outreach efforts.

Wildfire Prevention Act of 2025, Section 302 "Public-private wildfire technology deployment and testbed partnership." sets the program's expiration at 7 years after enactment, with annual assessments and recommendations to foster the adoption of promising technologies.

Supporting Innovation in Agriculture Act of 2025 establishes a tax credit of 30% for investments in innovative agricultural technology projects under the Internal Revenue Code.

Supporting Innovation in Agriculture Act of 2025 defines "innovative agricultural technology project" as technology used to produce, store, process, and package specialty crops with precision agriculture or controlled environment agriculture, effective through December 31, 2035.

Supporting Innovation in Agriculture Act of 2025 specifies "qualified property" includes tangible personal property, software, and technology necessary for these projects and subject to depreciation rules.

Supporting Innovation in Agriculture Act of 2025 includes provisions for specific modern technologies, such as AI, machine learning, robotics, and various sensors, under both controlled environment and precision agriculture technologies.

Supporting Innovation in Agriculture Act of 2025 prohibits double benefit from using both this tax credit and specific government grants.

Supporting Innovation in Agriculture Act of 2025 amends sections of the Internal Revenue Code to incorporate the innovative agricultural technology investment credit.

Supporting Innovation in Agriculture Act of 2025 sets the amendment's applicability to projects starting construction after January 1, 2025.

Department of Homeland Security Vehicular Terrorism Prevention and Mitigation Act of 2025 requires the Secretary of Homeland Security, alongside TSA and CISA, to submit a report on the prevention, deterrence, and response to vehicular terrorism.

Department of Homeland Security Vehicular Terrorism Prevention and Mitigation Act of 2025 mandates the report to assess threats related to connected and autonomous vehicles and ADAS technologies, including AI-driven cybersecurity vulnerabilities.

Department of Homeland Security Vehicular Terrorism Prevention and Mitigation Act of 2025 instructs inclusion of evaluations regarding DHS's engagement with public and private stakeholders, focusing on vehicle rental and ride-sharing platforms to prevent misuse.

Department of Homeland Security Vehicular Terrorism Prevention and Mitigation Act of 2025 calls for recommendations on AI-enabled predictive analytics and vehicle immobilization technologies to detect and mitigate threats.

Department of Homeland Security Vehicular Terrorism Prevention and Mitigation Act of 2025 demands coordination with enforcement agencies to address vehicular terrorism through intelligence sharing and joint training.

Department of Homeland Security Vehicular Terrorism Prevention and Mitigation Act of 2025 ensures countermeasures and AI use respect privacy and civil liberties.

Department of Homeland Security Vehicular Terrorism Prevention and Mitigation Act of 2025 obliges publication of an unclassified report summary for public access and annual briefings to Congress on developments and recommendations.

Department of Homeland Security Vehicular Terrorism Prevention and Mitigation Act of 2025 defines “vehicular terrorism” as the use of vehicles to commit acts of terrorism.

Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Streamline the Code of Federal Regulations Act of 2025 requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, in consultation with the National Institute of Standards and Technology, to annually implement a process using artificial intelligence to identify redundant or outdated federal regulations.

Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Streamline the Code of Federal Regulations Act of 2025 mandates the use of an AI system that meets strict standards for accuracy, transparency, accountability, and national security risk.

Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Streamline the Code of Federal Regulations Act of 2025 obliges agencies to review identified redundant or outdated regulations within 30 days and make a final determination of their status.

Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Streamline the Code of Federal Regulations Act of 2025 commands the rescission or amendment of regulations found to be redundant or outdated within 30 days after determination.

Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Streamline the Code of Federal Regulations Act of 2025 requires the public publication of any determination with a brief explanation, with an option for a classified annex to Congress if necessary.

Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Streamline the Code of Federal Regulations Act of 2025 amends Title 5 of the United States Code to facilitate the expedited rescission and amendment of redundant or outdated regulations identified through AI review.

Promoting Precision Agriculture Act of 2025 mandates the Secretary of Agriculture, in consultation with the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Federal Communications Commission, to develop voluntary interconnectivity standards for precision agriculture within two years of enactment.

Promoting Precision Agriculture Act of 2025 requires coordination with public and private stakeholders, including industry organizations and voluntary standards bodies, to create these standards.

Promoting Precision Agriculture Act of 2025 includes the consideration of evolving demands, connectivity needs, cybersecurity challenges, and the impacts of advanced wireless technology and AI on precision agriculture.

Promoting Precision Agriculture Act of 2025 directs the Comptroller General to conduct studies assessing these standards' development, voluntary nature, industry coordination, and adoption success, with reports due to Senate and House committees.

Promoting Precision Agriculture Act of 2025 aims to enhance precision agriculture participation in the U.S. and promote U.S. leadership in setting standards for precision agriculture through voluntary consensus standards development organizations.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 60003 ("U.S. Customs and Border Protection technology, vetting activities, and other efforts to enhance border security") appropriates $1,076,317,000 to U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) for AI, machine learning, and non-intrusive inspection equipment to combat illicit narcotics at U.S. borders.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 60003 ("U.S. Customs and Border Protection technology, vetting activities, and other efforts to enhance border security") restricts funds for certain surveillance towers unless they are tested and federally accepted for autonomous capabilities.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 60003 ("U.S. Customs and Border Protection technology, vetting activities, and other efforts to enhance border security") defines "autonomous" as systems using AI, sensors, and onboard computing to automate identification tasks traditionally performed manually by CBP personnel.

Health Tech Investment Act amends the Social Security Act to classify algorithm-based healthcare services under Medicare’s new technology ambulatory payment classification.

Health Tech Investment Act requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to assign payment classifications based on cost data submitted by manufacturers, including diverse factors like invoice prices and overhead.

Health Tech Investment Act specifies that algorithm-based services cannot be removed from their payment classification until adequate claims data is available, and mandates a minimum tenure of five years within the initial classification.

Health Tech Investment Act adjusts the criteria for eligibility in new technology classifications to include distinct procedures that use AI, machine learning, or other software when used adjunctively with underlying services.

Health Tech Investment Act defines algorithm-based healthcare services as those using FDA-approved AI or software for clinical guidance.

Health Tech Investment Act mandates the payment system for software services as described in a 2022 Medicare rule, effective from January 2023.

Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 3: Generative AI Training Report Pre-Publication Version 2025 recognizes the importance of voluntary licensing agreements for AI training and notes that these arrangements have developed in some contexts, particularly with high-volume or limited copyright owners.

Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 3: Generative AI Training Report Pre-Publication Version 2025 suggests that voluntary collective licensing can reduce transaction complexity and cost, while offering flexibility for both copyright owners and licensees.

Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 3: Generative AI Training Report Pre-Publication Version 2025 raises concerns that a compulsory licensing regime would inhibit market-based solutions and prove inflexible and slow to adapt.

Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 3: Generative AI Training Report Pre-Publication Version 2025 views Extended Collective Licensing (ECL) as a potentially less intrusive solution in sectors where voluntary licensing fails.

Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 3: Generative AI Training Report Pre-Publication Version 2025 discourages requiring copyright owners to opt out, emphasizing consent for uses within statutory rights, though acknowledges Congress may consider exceptions allowing opt-outs.

Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 3: Generative AI Training Report Pre-Publication Version 2025 encourages the Department of Justice to clarify antitrust concerns related to collective licensing.

Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 3: Generative AI Training Report Pre-Publication Version 2025 recommends allowing the licensing market to evolve organically, suggesting targeted interventions only if specific market failures arise.

Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 3: Generative AI Training Report Pre-Publication Version 2025 notes the nascent state of AI law, markets, and technology, and urges reliance on collaborative market-based solutions as legal clarity evolves.

Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 1: Digital Replicas July 2024 recommends that Congress establish a federal right to protect individuals from the distribution of unauthorized digital replicas during their lifetimes.

Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 1: Digital Replicas July 2024 proposes that this right be licensable and subject to guardrails but not assignable, with remedies such as monetary damages and injunctive relief available.

Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 1: Digital Replicas July 2024 requires traditional rules of secondary liability, with a safe harbor for online service providers suitably conditioned.

Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 1: Digital Replicas July 2024 suggests explicit First Amendment accommodations in the law.

Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 1: Digital Replicas July 2024 advises against full preemption of state laws, recognizing established state rights of publicity.

Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 1: Digital Replicas July 2024 offers the Copyright Office as a resource for Congress, the courts, and the executive branch in implementing these recommendations and addressing future developments in AI governance.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 100001 ("Coast guard assets necessary to secure the maritime border and interdict migrants and drugs") appropriates $140 million for long-range unmanned aircraft systems and related infrastructure to improve the US Coast Guard's capabilities.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 100001 ("Coast guard assets necessary to secure the maritime border and interdict migrants and drugs") allocates $180 million for maritime domain awareness equipment and services, including $75 million specifically for autonomous maritime systems.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 100001 ("Coast guard assets necessary to secure the maritime border and interdict migrants and drugs") allows, through 2030, for entities other than the Coast Guard to acquire, procure, or construct floating dry docks, provided they meet defined requirements.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 100001 ("Coast guard assets necessary to secure the maritime border and interdict migrants and drugs") limits design, planning, and engineering expenses to 15% of specified funding allocations for maintenance facilities.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 100001 ("Coast guard assets necessary to secure the maritime border and interdict migrants and drugs") exempts acquisitions funded under this act from sections 1131, 1132, and 1133 of title 14, United States Code.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 100001 ("Coast guard assets necessary to secure the maritime border and interdict migrants and drugs") mandates compliance with reporting requirements and submission of an expenditure plan to relevant Congressional committees.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 100001 ("Coast guard assets necessary to secure the maritime border and interdict migrants and drugs") prohibits expenditure during any fiscal year if the Coast Guard is non-compliant with specified sections of title 14, United States Code.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 100001 ("Coast guard assets necessary to secure the maritime border and interdict migrants and drugs") requires prior notification to Congress before procurement actions affecting cost or timelines.

Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security to submit a plan within 180 days to integrate and deploy emerging technologies, such as AI and machine learning, for border security.

Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act specifies the contents of the plan, including assessment of privacy impacts, coordination with private and public sectors, and scaling of current programs.

Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act authorizes CBP Innovation Teams to research and adapt commercial technologies for border security, setting strategic goals and operating procedures.

Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act requires annual reporting by CBP on Innovation Teams' activities, including descriptions of piloted technologies and their effectiveness.

Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act promotes identifying and phasing out obsolete technologies in favor of advanced systems, with cost assessments.

Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act encourages collaboration across sectors to leverage innovative technologies and incentivizes private sector participation.

Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act obligates CBP to evaluate authorities and potential needs for new authorization to facilitate technology acquisition and integration, ensuring effective border security operations.

Western Wildfire Support Act of 2025, Section 205 "Study on modernizing wildfire response technologies" require the Secretaries to conduct a study on modernizing wildfire response technologies.

Western Wildfire Support Act of 2025, Section 205 "Study on modernizing wildfire response technologies" include in the study necessary improvements to radio communications systems and infrastructure during wildland fire or prescribed fire operations, assessing the quality, reliability, failure impacts, and improvement options.

Western Wildfire Support Act of 2025, Section 205 "Study on modernizing wildfire response technologies" assess real-time or near-real-time situational awareness tools for operational firefighters, ensuring interoperability and evaluating additional remote sensing and mapping capabilities.

Western Wildfire Support Act of 2025, Section 205 "Study on modernizing wildfire response technologies" conduct a cost analysis of commercially available systems versus internally developed systems.

Western Wildfire Support Act of 2025, Section 205 "Study on modernizing wildfire response technologies" analyze wildland fire predictive modeling, focusing on data requirements, computing needs, and the feasibility of using artificial intelligence for more accurate predictions.

Western Wildfire Support Act of 2025, Section 205 "Study on modernizing wildfire response technologies" require the submission and public availability of the study results within one year of the Act's enactment to congressional committees and the public.

Healthy Technology Act of 2025 amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to include artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies as practitioners eligible to prescribe drugs.

Healthy Technology Act of 2025 requires that such AI and machine learning technologies be authorized by state statutes to prescribe the specific drug involved.

Healthy Technology Act of 2025 mandates that these technologies be approved, cleared, or authorized by the Food and Drug Administration under sections 510(k), 513, 515, or 564.

PATHS Act extends the use of other transaction authority for research and development acquisition under the Homeland Security Act of 2002 from September 30, 2024, to September 30, 2028.

PATHS Act mandates notification to congressional committees within 72 hours after the use or extension of transaction authority involving artificial intelligence (AI) technology.

PATHS Act requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to offer a briefing explaining the reason for using or extending AI-related transaction authority.

PATHS Act reduces the maximum amount for covered contract awards under the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 from $4,000,000 to $1,000,000.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20004 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for munitions and defense supply chain resiliency") appropriates $400 million for accelerated one-way attack unmanned aerial systems with advanced autonomy, emphasizing AI capabilities for defense.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20004 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for munitions and defense supply chain resiliency") allocates $1 billion to expand the industrial base for one-way attack unmanned aerial systems, further enhancing AI-driven military operations.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20004 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for munitions and defense supply chain resiliency") provides $58 million for development, production, and integration of counter-unmanned aerial systems programs, highlighting AI's role in defense against drone threats.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20004 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for munitions and defense supply chain resiliency") designates $350 million for non-kinetic counter-unmanned aerial systems programs, demonstrating focus on AI-based alternatives to traditional munitions.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20004 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for munitions and defense supply chain resiliency") earmarks $250 million for land-based, and $200 million for ship-based counter-unmanned aerial systems programs, underscoring AI use in diverse defense environments.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20004 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for munitions and defense supply chain resiliency") allocates $62 million for AI-enhanced hypersonic strike programs, underscoring importance of AI in cutting-edge military technology.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20004 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for munitions and defense supply chain resiliency") requests $500 million for Department of Defense Credit Program to support critical mineral industries, indirectly promoting AI technology development by ensuring material availability.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20004 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for munitions and defense supply chain resiliency") permits up to $100 billion in loans and guarantees, indicating a strategic commitment to fortifying supply chains essential for AI advancements within the defense sector.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20005 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for scaling low-cost weapons into production") allocates $145 million for developing AI to support one-way attack unmanned aerial systems and naval systems.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20005 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for scaling low-cost weapons into production") assigns $250 million to advance the AI ecosystem and another $250 million to expand Cyber Command's AI initiatives.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20005 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for scaling low-cost weapons into production") provides $250 million to develop the Test Resource Management Center's digital test environment.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20005 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for scaling low-cost weapons into production") designates $1 billion for expanding programs to accelerate innovative technology procurement, affecting AI initiatives.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20005 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for scaling low-cost weapons into production") directs $2 billion to scale commercially developed technology, including AI, for military use through the Defense Innovation Unit.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20005 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for scaling low-cost weapons into production") supports the acceleration of Quantum Benchmarking Initiative with $250 million.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20005 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for scaling low-cost weapons into production") earmarks $500 million to avoid delays in delivering autonomous military capabilities that involve AI technologies.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20005 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for scaling low-cost weapons into production") includes a $1 billion appropriation for a capital assistance program, including loans and guarantees, aiding AI projects.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20005 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for scaling low-cost weapons into production") ensures these appropriations and initiatives remain available until September 30, 2029, supporting ongoing AI and technology development in defense.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 112204 ("Implementing artificial intelligence tools for purposes of reducing and recouping improper payments under Medicare") mandates the implementation of artificial intelligence tools by January 1, 2027, to reduce and identify improper payments under Medicare Parts A and B.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 112204 ("Implementing artificial intelligence tools for purposes of reducing and recouping improper payments under Medicare") directs the Secretary to contract with AI vendors and data scientists to support the implementation.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 112204 ("Implementing artificial intelligence tools for purposes of reducing and recouping improper payments under Medicare") requires the recoupment, where practicable, of improper payments identified through AI tools.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 112204 ("Implementing artificial intelligence tools for purposes of reducing and recouping improper payments under Medicare") obliges the Secretary to report to Congress by January 1, 2029, and annually thereafter on AI implementation and payment recoupment, including potential improvements and recoupment statistics.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 112204 ("Implementing artificial intelligence tools for purposes of reducing and recouping improper payments under Medicare") allocates $12.5 million each from the Federal Hospital Insurance Trust Fund and the Federal Supplementary Medical Insurance Trust Fund to fund these AI initiatives for fiscal year 2025, with funds available until expended.

Duplicative Grant Consolidation Act mandates the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to submit a report to Congressional committees.

Duplicative Grant Consolidation Act requires consultation with the Secretary of Energy, the Director of the National Science Foundation, and the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology.

Duplicative Grant Consolidation Act focuses on assessing the feasibility of using AI to identify duplicative Federal grant applications.

Duplicative Grant Consolidation Act seeks to determine whether an applicant has received or submitted another grant application for the same purpose.

Duplicative Grant Consolidation Act aims to identify waste, fraud, and abuse in the grant application process through AI technology.

Nondiscrimination in Health Programs and Activities prohibits covered entities from discriminating based on race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability through the use of patient care decision support tools in health programs or activities.

Nondiscrimination in Health Programs and Activities requires covered entities to make reasonable efforts to identify uses of such tools that employ input variables or factors measuring race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability.

Nondiscrimination in Health Programs and Activities mandates covered entities to make reasonable efforts to mitigate discrimination risks from identified tools in their health programs or activities.

United States-Israel Defense Partnership Act of 2025 supports and encourages defense collaboration between the United States and Israel in emerging technologies, specifically artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, robotics, quantum, and automation.

United States-Israel Defense Partnership Act of 2025 authorizes the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretary of State and the Director of National Intelligence, to jointly conduct research, development, testing, and evaluation with Israel in these areas.

United States-Israel Defense Partnership Act of 2025 requires protection of sensitive information and national security interests during any activities carried out under this authority.

United States-Israel Defense Partnership Act of 2025 prohibits activities from commencing until a report is submitted detailing a memorandum of agreement for cost-sharing and intellectual property rights, and ensuring semiannual expenditure reporting by Israel.

United States-Israel Defense Partnership Act of 2025 designates the Irregular Warfare Technology Support Directorate as the lead agency once the report is submitted.

United States-Israel Defense Partnership Act of 2025 mandates semiannual reports to Congress on program developments.

United States-Israel Defense Partnership Act of 2025 authorizes $50,000,000 annually from 2026 to 2030 for this program.
