Air National Guard Squadron Preservation Act of 2025 mandates the Secretary, with the Air National Guard Director, to study the necessity of acquiring advanced capability fighter aircraft for the Air Force.

Air National Guard Squadron Preservation Act of 2025 requires consideration of plans to implement unmanned or autonomous capabilities in fighter aircraft.

Air National Guard Squadron Preservation Act of 2025 includes evaluation of cost savings linked to foreign sales of F-16 variants.

Air National Guard Squadron Preservation Act of 2025 identifies eligible Air Force units for recapitalization with advanced fighter aircraft.

Air National Guard Squadron Preservation Act of 2025 assesses how these aircraft meet current and contingency mission needs of combatant commanders.

Air National Guard Squadron Preservation Act of 2025 determines whether a multiyear contract is the optimal acquisition method.

Air National Guard Squadron Preservation Act of 2025 obligates the Secretary to report findings to congressional defense committees within 180 days of enactment.

IRONDOME Act of 2025 accelerates the development of autonomous agents to defend against cruise missiles and drones.

IRONDOME Act of 2025 requires the Secretary to use all available authorities to achieve this goal.

IRONDOME Act of 2025 aims to enhance cost-effective defense of the United States homeland and forward-deployed armed forces.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20006 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for improving the efficiency and cybersecurity of the Department of Defense") appropriates $200 million for the deployment of automation and artificial intelligence to accelerate audits of the Department of Defense's financial statements, as outlined in chapter 9A and section 2222 of title 10, United States Code.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20006 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for improving the efficiency and cybersecurity of the Department of Defense") specifies that these funds remain available until September 30, 2029.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1638 ("Sense of Congress with respect to use of artificial intelligence to support strategic deterrence") emphasizes the need for caution to prevent AI from compromising critical strategic assets.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1638 ("Sense of Congress with respect to use of artificial intelligence to support strategic deterrence") establishes U.S. policy that AI use should not undermine nuclear safeguards, affect weapon system functionality, or alter the validation of command communications.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1638 ("Sense of Congress with respect to use of artificial intelligence to support strategic deterrence") requires positive human actions for nuclear weapon employment decisions by the President to remain intact.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 149) regulates AI systems in Texas under the Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 149) prohibits AI systems from inciting harm, criminality, manipulation, or discrimination based on political viewpoints or protected classes.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 149) establishes the Artificial Intelligence Council and a regulatory sandbox program for controlled AI testing.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 149) requires government disclosure to consumers when AI is used in interactions.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 149) instructs the attorney general to enforce regulations, manage complaints, and impose fines for non-compliance.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 149) prohibits government use of AI for social scoring or capturing biometric identifiers in violation of rights.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 149) mandates that AI must not produce certain unlawful content and must adhere to consumer protections and data privacy.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 233 ("Management and utilization of digital data to enhance maintenance activities") mandates the development and implementation of policies to manage and utilize digital data for maintenance of aircraft, ships, and ground vehicles within one year.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 233 ("Management and utilization of digital data to enhance maintenance activities") requires investment in advanced data infrastructure for efficient data processing.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 233 ("Management and utilization of digital data to enhance maintenance activities") instructs the development of a strategy incorporating AI and automated systems for data organization.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 233 ("Management and utilization of digital data to enhance maintenance activities") demands collaboration with vendors to overcome proprietary data limitations through open data approaches.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 233 ("Management and utilization of digital data to enhance maintenance activities") addresses enhancement of data transmission capabilities with high-speed technologies and secure methods.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 233 ("Management and utilization of digital data to enhance maintenance activities") mandates central compilation of maintenance data and creation of user interfaces for data analysis.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 233 ("Management and utilization of digital data to enhance maintenance activities") requires vendor-agnostic, interoperable tagging systems unless exceptions are justified.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 233 ("Management and utilization of digital data to enhance maintenance activities") calls for review of classification policies to ensure appropriate classification without limiting usability.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 233 ("Management and utilization of digital data to enhance maintenance activities") establishes protocols for detecting unauthorized access to vehicle or platform systems.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 233 ("Management and utilization of digital data to enhance maintenance activities") obligates a briefing to Senate and House Armed Services Committees on policy development and implementation status.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 237 ("Pilot program on use of artificial intelligence for certain workflow and operations tasks") mandates the use of top-tier software platforms, consideration of industry best practices, implementation based on human-centered design, and connection to authoritative enterprise data sources.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 237 ("Pilot program on use of artificial intelligence for certain workflow and operations tasks") obliges consultation with the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, and the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, and Air Force.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 237 ("Pilot program on use of artificial intelligence for certain workflow and operations tasks") requires a report within one year detailing software evaluations, workflow modifications, and a quantitative assessment of the software's impact.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 6504 ("Establishment of Artificial Intelligence Security Center") requires the Center to develop guidance to prevent or mitigate counter-artificial intelligence techniques.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 6504 ("Establishment of Artificial Intelligence Security Center") promotes secure artificial intelligence adoption practices for managers of national security systems and the defense industrial base.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1069 ("Biodefense posture reviews") requires the Secretary of Defense to conduct comprehensive biodefense posture reviews by December 31, 2026, and December 31, 2029.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1069 ("Biodefense posture reviews") mandates inclusion of an inventory and assessment of existing biodefense strategies and policies, relevant biological threats, and current Department of Defense programs related to biological threats.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1069 ("Biodefense posture reviews") identifies methods using artificial intelligence and cyber capabilities to address biological attacks.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1069 ("Biodefense posture reviews") recommends strengthening biodefense capabilities and improving interagency coordination.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1069 ("Biodefense posture reviews") requires submittal of a review to congressional defense committees within 30 days of completion.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1069 ("Biodefense posture reviews") specifies that reviews must be unclassified but may include a classified annex.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1032 ("Competitive demonstration of large and extra large unmanned underwater vehicles") requires evaluation of user feedback on these vehicles as well as vehicles' integration with mission autonomy planning, capability in contested environments, performance attributes, technical maturity, and cost to procure, operate, and sustain.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1032 ("Competitive demonstration of large and extra large unmanned underwater vehicles") permits the use of fiscal year 2025 Navy funds for research, development, and demonstration activities.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1032 ("Competitive demonstration of large and extra large unmanned underwater vehicles") obligates the Secretary of the Navy and the Commander of the United States Indo-Pacific Command to submit assessments to congressional defense committees by September 1, 2025, which may include recommendations and validation of underwater vehicle requirements.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1032 ("Competitive demonstration of large and extra large unmanned underwater vehicles") defines the vehicles as capable of submerged operation while supporting one or more missions with modular payload integration and a minimum range of 1,000 nautical miles.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 232 ("Expansion of participation in the Digital On-Demand Program") requires active promotion of the Program throughout the Department.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 232 ("Expansion of participation in the Digital On-Demand Program") obligates the Secretary of Defense to submit a progress report to the Senate and House Armed Services Committees within 180 days of enactment and annually through 2029.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1515 ("Protective measures for mobile devices within the Department of Defense") evaluates technologies such as anonymizing-enabling technologies, network-enabled content inspection, on-device VPNs, and AI-based protection against smishing, phishing, and text/email compromises.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1515 ("Protective measures for mobile devices within the Department of Defense") assesses the efficacy and scalability of these technologies within the Department of Defense and their integration with existing cybersecurity architecture.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1515 ("Protective measures for mobile devices within the Department of Defense") mandates submission of a report to congressional defense committees within 270 days detailing findings and recommendations on procuring or incorporating evaluated technologies.

Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law mandates Parties to adopt measures ensuring AI systems align with human rights, democracy, and the rule of law.

Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law requires transparency, accountability, and non-discrimination in AI systems' lifecycle.

Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law obligates implementation of measures to protect privacy, human dignity, and democratic processes.

Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law demands risk assessment and mitigation strategies for AI, considering human rights impacts.

Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law establishes a follow-up mechanism for international cooperation and compliance monitoring.

Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law provides for accessible remedies for human rights violations arising from AI systems.

Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law calls for public consultation and digital literacy to address AI-related impacts.

Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law stipulates that Parties must ensure effective procedural safeguards and oversight mechanisms.

Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law allows exceptions for artificial intelligence systems related to the protection of national security interests but insists on adherence to international human rights law and democratic processes.

Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law facilitates international cooperation and information exchange on AI's human rights impacts.

Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law permits amendments and dispute settlements through negotiation or the Conference of the Parties.

Security Management Measures for the Application of Facial Recognition Technology regulates the use of facial recognition technology for processing facial information within China, ensuring compliance with relevant laws and ethical standards.

Security Management Measures for the Application of Facial Recognition Technology exempts the use of facial recognition in research and development or algorithm training.

Security Management Measures for the Application of Facial Recognition Technology requires a specific, necessary purpose for processing, with minimized impact on individual rights.

Security Management Measures for the Application of Facial Recognition Technology obligates personal information processors to inform individuals transparently about processing activities, including purposes, methods, and rights.

Security Management Measures for the Application of Facial Recognition Technology mandates obtaining consent separately for processing, with provision for withdrawal.

Security Management Measures for the Application of Facial Recognition Technology requires parental consent for processing minors' facial information and formulating specific rules for handling such data.

Security Management Measures for the Application of Facial Recognition Technology restricts storing facial information within devices unless consent or laws allow external transmission and limits retention to what is necessary.

Security Management Measures for the Application of Facial Recognition Technology mandates conducting personal information protection impact assessments in advance and retaining assessment reports for three years.

Security Management Measures for the Application of Facial Recognition Technology prohibits using facial recognition as the sole identity verification method if alternatives exist.

Security Management Measures for the Application of Facial Recognition Technology requires filing procedures with local cyberspace administrations if information volume reaches 100,000 individuals.

Security Management Measures for the Application of Facial Recognition Technology empowers cyberspace administrations and public security authorities to supervise, inspect, and handle complaints regarding facial recognition misuse.

Illinois HB 0645 creates the Illinois Future of Work Task Force to proactively plan for the future of work and address current labor issues.

Illinois HB 0645 requires the Task Force to identify and assess emerging technologies, particularly automation and AI, that significantly impact employment, wages, and skills.

Illinois HB 0645 mandates the development of job standards and working conditions to build a vibrant middle class.

Illinois HB 0645 instructs the Task Force to identify future job opportunities and shape them to improve life in Illinois.

Illinois HB 0645 compiles research and best practices from other regions on deploying technology for the public good.

Illinois HB 0645 develops tools to evaluate the impact of proposed technologies on workers, employers, and the state.

Illinois HB 0645 proposes workforce development and training programs for future jobs.

Illinois HB 0645 requires the Task Force to submit a report with findings to the Governor and General Assembly by May 1, 2022, and dissolves upon report submission.

New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection Amendment to Rules of NY City (Use of Automated Employment Decisionmaking Tools) mandates that employers or employment agencies conduct a bias audit of Automated Employment Decision Tools (AEDTs) at least annually.

New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection Amendment to Rules of NY City (Use of Automated Employment Decisionmaking Tools) requires bias audits to calculate selection and scoring rates, and impact ratios across sex, race/ethnicity, and intersectional categories.

New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection Amendment to Rules of NY City (Use of Automated Employment Decisionmaking Tools) mandates AEDT users to publish bias audit summaries online, detailing data sources and impact ratios, accessible for at least 6 months after each AEDT use.

New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection Amendment to Rules of NY City (Use of Automated Employment Decisionmaking Tools) requires notification to candidates and employees 10 business days before AEDT use, offering options via website, job postings, mail, or email.

New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection Amendment to Rules of NY City (Use of Automated Employment Decisionmaking Tools) enforces online publication of AEDT data retention policies and types of data collected.

National Standard of the People’s Republic of China: Cybersecurity Technology – Basic Safety Requirements for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Draft for Feedback) establishes basic safety requirements for generative AI services, focusing on training data safety, model safety, and safety measures.

National Standard of the People’s Republic of China: Cybersecurity Technology – Basic Safety Requirements for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Draft for Feedback) requires service providers to conduct safety assessments and manage training data sources, ensuring data does not contain over 5% illegal content.

National Standard of the People’s Republic of China: Cybersecurity Technology – Basic Safety Requirements for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Draft for Feedback) mandates the verification of intellectual property rights and personal information consent before using data for training.

National Standard of the People’s Republic of China: Cybersecurity Technology – Basic Safety Requirements for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Draft for Feedback) stipulates regular security audits and monitoring of models to prevent malicious attacks and ensure content accuracy.

National Standard of the People’s Republic of China: Cybersecurity Technology – Basic Safety Requirements for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Draft for Feedback) obliges disclosure of service limitations, models, and personal data usage to users.

National Standard of the People’s Republic of China: Cybersecurity Technology – Basic Safety Requirements for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Draft for Feedback) demands the implementation of mechanisms for complaints and a backup strategy for service continuity.

National Standard of the People’s Republic of China: Cybersecurity Technology – Basic Safety Requirements for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Draft for Feedback) sets specific guidelines for minors, requiring parental controls and restrictions on unsuitable content.

National Standard of the People’s Republic of China: Cybersecurity Technology – Basic Safety Requirements for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Draft for Feedback) requires transparency in service provision, detailing applicable scenarios and user consent for data use in training.

National Standard of the People’s Republic of China: Cybersecurity Technology – Basic Safety Requirements for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Draft for Feedback) mandates service providers to construct banks of unsafe key words and questions which AI models should and should not refuse to answer.

JSP 936 V1.1 Dependable Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Defence (part 1: directive) sets the Ministry of Defence (MOD) Responsible Officers to ensure the ethical and safe development and use of AI in Defence.

JSP 936 V1.1 Dependable Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Defence (part 1: directive) requires MOD staff to implement this JSP in AI system lifecycles, from inception to disposal, ensuring alignment with MOD's AI Ethical Principles: Human-centricity, Responsibility, Understanding, Bias and Harm Mitigation, and Reliability.

JSP 936 V1.1 Dependable Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Defence (part 1: directive) mandates TLB Holders and Chief Executives to issue appropriate AI-related directions and ensure competent management within their areas and maintaining Governance as outlined in Section 4.

JSP 936 V1.1 Dependable Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Defence (part 1: directive) stresses the need for a holistic approach aligned with the UK National AI Strategy and addresses unique AI security risks, advocating continuous security monitoring.

JSP 936 V1.1 Dependable Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Defence (part 1: directive) obliges the assessment and mitigation of ethical risks, providing evidence of responsible AI use, and addressing novel and contentious AI applications with special attention.

JSP 936 V1.1 Dependable Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Defence (part 1: directive) emphasizes human collaboration with AI, requiring competency assessments, training, and ethical governance, particularly in human/AI teams, AI legal considerations, and supplier competence and conformance with AI-specific requirements.

Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion imposes export controls on AI models, excluding publicly available models, and expands licensing requirements for AI chips to additional countries.

Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion establishes three tiers of countries for purposes of determining applicable export restrictions, including eighteen countries able to import AI chips without restrictions (tier 1); countries able to import AI chips through validated end-user (VEU) programs, limited-volume exceptions, and licensing, but otherwise subject to restrictions (tier 2); and countries subject to ongoing restrictions, including arms-embargoed countries (tier 3).

Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion establishes a Data Center Validated End User (DC VEU) program to govern compute exports related to major AI infrastructure development in second-tier countries, with different pathways and restrictions depending on data center operator nationality. Imposes cybersecurity, physical and personnel security, and sourcing mandates on DC VEU participants, as well as reporting requirements.

Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion imposes specific computing power deployment restrictions on companies operating in second-tier countries, including relative ratios and numerical caps.

Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion controls the export of AI models developed using compute above a given threshold, to be adjusted over time based on assessments of publicly available models. Requires cloud computing providers to implement security measures preventing the unauthorized training of models otherwise subject to export controls.

Guidance on Algorithmic Discrimination and the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination clarifies that the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD) applies to algorithmic discrimination through automated decision-making tools similarly to traditional discrimination.

Guidance on Algorithmic Discrimination and the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination prohibits any form of discrimination facilitated by automated tools, regardless of intent or third-party involvement in tool development.

Guidance on Algorithmic Discrimination and the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination requires covered entities, like employers and housing providers, to avoid disparate treatment and disparate impact discrimination in using these tools.

Guidance on Algorithmic Discrimination and the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination mandates that entities provide reasonable accommodations to avoid discriminatory impacts, even if automated tools fail to recognize accommodations.

Guidance on Algorithmic Discrimination and the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination holds entities liable for discrimination resulting from their use of third-party developed tools, emphasizing the importance of evaluating these tools for bias.

Guidance on Algorithmic Discrimination and the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination encourages developers and vendors to design and test automated tools to minimize discriminatory outcomes, thus reducing liability risk under the LAD.

Guidance on Algorithmic Discrimination and the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination reiterates the LAD's comprehensive protections against discrimination, regardless of the technology used, and provides resources for understanding these protections.

Common Intelligence Community Interim Guidance Regarding the Acquisition and Use of Foundation AI Models provides interim guidance for the Intelligence Community (IC) on acquiring and using foundation AI models, focusing on model acquisition, modification, and outputs.

Common Intelligence Community Interim Guidance Regarding the Acquisition and Use of Foundation AI Models requires model acquisition to comply with legal standards, ensuring alignment with established IC frameworks.

Common Intelligence Community Interim Guidance Regarding the Acquisition and Use of Foundation AI Models mandates prompts and outputs be used for authorized purposes and treated as collected data when applicable, ensuring compliance with existing guidelines on retention and dissemination.

Common Intelligence Community Interim Guidance Regarding the Acquisition and Use of Foundation AI Models emphasizes the need for oversight mechanisms to track U.S. person information used or retrieved from AI models.

Securing Growth and Robust Leadership in American Aviation Act, Sec. 1024 ("Technology Review of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Technologies") requires the Administrator to conduct a review of current and planned AI and machine learning technologies to enhance airport efficiency and safety.

Securing Growth and Robust Leadership in American Aviation Act, Sec. 1024 ("Technology Review of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Technologies") asks the Administrator to consider best practices and lessons learned from domestic and international AI and machine learning applications.

Securing Growth and Robust Leadership in American Aviation Act, Sec. 1024 ("Technology Review of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Technologies") permits coordination with other Federal agencies to identify China's use of AI and machine learning in airport operations.

Securing Growth and Robust Leadership in American Aviation Act, Sec. 1024 ("Technology Review of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Technologies") mandates the review to include AI and machine learning applications in jet bridges, airport service vehicles, aircraft taxi, air traffic control operations, and other areas deemed necessary by the Administrator.

Securing Growth and Robust Leadership in American Aviation Act, Sec. 1024 ("Technology Review of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Technologies") obligates the Administrator to submit a report to Congress within one year detailing the review's findings.

Securing Growth and Robust Leadership in American Aviation Act, Sec. 1028 ("Air Traffic Control Training") requires the Administrator to include collaboration with labor organizations and other stakeholders in the research program.

Securing Growth and Robust Leadership in American Aviation Act, Sec. 1028 ("Air Traffic Control Training") mandates the Administrator to report findings to Congress within 1 year of the Act's enactment.

REAL Political Advertisements Act amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to require any political advertisement containing images or video footage generated in whole or in part using artificial intelligence to include a clear and conspicuous disclaimer, with specific formatting requirements for text, audio, video, and other media to ensure visibility and audibility.

REAL Political Advertisements Act directs the Federal Election Commission to promulgate regulations within 120 days of enactment to implement the disclaimer requirement and define "content generated by artificial intelligence" to reflect both current and emerging uses of generative AI.

REAL Political Advertisements Act requires the FEC to submit biennial reports to Congress assessing compliance and enforcement, recommending modifications, and identifying further measures to enhance transparency and accountability in political advertising.

Directive on Automated Decision-Making (Canada) requires Algorithmic Impact Assessments before production of any automated decision system, with regular updates and public disclosure of results in accessible formats.

Directive on Automated Decision-Making (Canada) mandate transparency by notifying individuals when decisions are made in whole or in part by automated systems, and by providing plain-language explanations of how and why decisions were made.

Directive on Automated Decision-Making (Canada) direct rigorous testing and continuous monitoring of automated decision systems to detect and mitigate unintended biases and ensure compliance with laws.

Directive on Automated Decision-Making (Canada) obligates data governance and quality assurance, including peer reviews and Gender-based Analysis Plus.

Directive on Automated Decision-Making (Canada) ensures the possibility of human intervention in automated decisions and provides clients with recourse options to challenge decisions.

Directive on Automated Decision-Making (Canada) specifies consequences for non-compliance under the Financial Administration Act.

Directive on Automated Decision-Making (Canada) designates the Chief Information Officer to provide guidance and maintain the Algorithmic Impact Assessment.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 125 ("Designation of official responsible for autonomous surface and underwater dual-modality vehicles") requires the Secretary of the Navy to designate an official responsible for developing and acquiring advanced autonomous surface and underwater vehicles within 180 days of enactment.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 125 ("Designation of official responsible for autonomous surface and underwater dual-modality vehicles") mandates the inclusion of a dedicated program element in the Navy's budget for the development and acquisition of these autonomous vehicles.

Regulations of Shenzhen Special Economic Zone on Promoting the Artificial Intelligence Industry establishes mechanisms for promoting the AI industry in Shenzhen, emphasizing high-quality AI development and integration across social and economic sectors.

Regulations of Shenzhen Special Economic Zone on Promoting the Artificial Intelligence Industry mandates the Shenzhen Municipal Government to coordinate AI development and safety, incorporating AI development into national plans and setting clear industry standards.

Regulations of Shenzhen Special Economic Zone on Promoting the Artificial Intelligence Industry encourages international collaboration in AI research and development and emphasizes ethical safety norms.

Regulations of Shenzhen Special Economic Zone on Promoting the Artificial Intelligence Industry requires construction of AI infrastructure, such as data centers, public data platforms, and open-source systems.

Regulations of Shenzhen Special Economic Zone on Promoting the Artificial Intelligence Industry encourages application of AI technologies in societal areas, such as healthcare, social governance, and education, and supports AI projects strategically.

Regulations of Shenzhen Special Economic Zone on Promoting the Artificial Intelligence Industry calls for an AI ethics committee to oversee ethical norms and governance structures, ensuring compliance with safety standards.

Regulations of Shenzhen Special Economic Zone on Promoting the Artificial Intelligence Industry implements differentiated supervision based on AI application risk levels, with high-risk applications requiring pre-evaluation.

Regulations of Shenzhen Special Economic Zone on Promoting the Artificial Intelligence Industry prohibits AI use for unlawful activities or discrimination and mandates consumer protection and privacy safeguards.

Regulations of Shenzhen Special Economic Zone on Promoting the Artificial Intelligence Industry regulations effective November 1, 2022.

CREATE AI Act of 2023 establishes the National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource (NAIRR) to democratize access to AI research resources and spur innovation.

CREATE AI Act of 2023 creates a NAIRR Steering Subcommittee chaired by the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy to oversee governance and resource allocation.

CREATE AI Act of 2023 mandates the National Science Foundation to establish a Program Management Office to coordinate day-to-day operations and compliance of the NAIRR.

CREATE AI Act of 2023 requires development of an Operating Entity through competitive processes to manage the NAIRR.

CREATE AI Act of 2023 ensures resources include computational resources, data repositories, educational tools, and AI testbeds.

CREATE AI Act of 2023 specifies criteria for user eligibility, emphasizing U.S.-based researchers and entities.

CREATE AI Act of 2023 imposes requirements and audits for privacy, ethics, civil rights, and security in AI research using NAIRR.

CREATE AI Act of 2023 allows establishment of a fee schedule with a free access tier to support research.

CREATE AI Act of 2023 ensures adherence to national security policies and scientific integrity standards.

Virginia 2025-HB2094 enacts stringent frameworks for the development and deployment of high-risk AI systems in Virginia.

Virginia 2025-HB2094 defines consequential decisions as those which may affect access to the justice system, education, employment, and financial or other such services.

Virginia 2025-HB2094 defines high-risk AI systems as those used in a consequential decision, excluding systems restricted to narrows tasks, pattern detection, and human assistance.

Virginia 2025-HB2094 mandates developers to disclose intended uses, data inputs, potential risks of algorithmic discrimination, and performance evaluations to deployers.

Virginia 2025-HB2094 requires deployers to implement risk management policies, conduct pre and post deployment impact assessments, and disclose AI system interactions to consumers, especially when making consequential decisions.

Virginia 2025-HB2094 establishes a duty of care for developers and deployers to protect against algorithmic discrimination.

Virginia 2025-HB2094 outlines civil penalties for violations, including a fine up to $1,000, with enforcement authority granted exclusively to the Attorney General.

Virginia 2025-HB2094 provides exemptions for various sectors and situations, including federal compliance and actions in the public interest.

Virginia 2025-HB2094 allows for updates post-modification of AI systems and sets guidelines for consumer notifications and appeal processes in case of adverse decisions due to AI use.

Washington (2018) HB 2970 mandates the Washington State Transportation Commission to establish a work group to develop policy recommendations for autonomous vehicle operation on public roadways.

Washington (2018) HB 2970 requires executive branch membership from various state departments and branches, alongside legislative members and additional stakeholders from sectors including technology and motor vehicle manufacturing.

Washington (2018) HB 2970 directs the work group to monitor advancements in autonomous vehicle technology, including federal and state regulatory frameworks, and to prepare state policies for autonomous commercial and passenger vehicles.

Washington (2018) HB 2970 necessitates consideration of diverse policy areas, such as vehicle testing, registration, driver's license requirements, traffic laws, cybersecurity, and impacts on labor and businesses.

Washington (2018) HB 2970 instructs the commission to report annually to the governor and legislature on progress and propose legal modifications.

Washington (2018) HB 2970 sets an expiration date of December 31, 2023, for sections detailing the establishment and function of the work group.

Washington (2022) SB 5460 amends requirements for testing autonomous vehicles on public roads in Washington State.

Washington (2022) SB 5460 mandates that self-certifying entities provide contact information, test locations, vehicle identification numbers, and proof of insurance for testing.

Washington (2022) SB 5460 requires assignment of a unique identification number for autonomous vehicles lacking a vehicle ID as mandated by law.

Washington (2022) SB 5460 obliges reporting of collisions and moving violations involving autonomous vehicles on public roads, including whether the autonomous system was active during incidents.

Washington (2022) SB 5460 demands advance written notice to relevant law enforcement agencies before testing, detailing the expected testing period, vehicle description, and contact information.

Washington (2022) SB 5460 allows the Department of Licensing to charge a fee to offset administrative costs of the self-certification testing program.

Washington (2022) SB 5460 ensures public access to information submitted by testing entities, with annual legislative reporting.

Washington (2022) SB 5460 defines "autonomous" vehicle levels per Society of Automotive Engineers standards J3016.

Washington (2022) SB 5460 prohibits autonomous vehicle testing without fulfilling initial information requirements.

Florida House Bill 919 establishes requirements for disclaimers on political advertisements using generative artificial intelligence in Florida.

Florida House Bill 919 defines "generative artificial intelligence" as a system emulating input data to create synthetic content.

Florida House Bill 919 requires advertisements with AI-generated content depicting actions that did not occur to include a prominent disclaimer stating "Created in whole or in part with the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI)."

Florida House Bill 919 specifies format requirements for disclaimers across various media, including print, television, internet, and audio.

Florida House Bill 919 imposes first-degree misdemeanor penalties for failure to include required disclaimers, in addition to other civil penalties.

Florida House Bill 919 authorizes any person to file complaints with the Florida Elections Commission for violations of this requirement.

Florida House Bill 919 mandates expedited hearings for such complaints.

Florida House Bill 919 sets an effective date of July 1, 2024.

Facial Recognition Act of 2023 prohibits law enforcement from using facial recognition without a court order, except in defined emergency circumstances.

Facial Recognition Act of 2023 mandates regular removal of photos from databases used for facial recognition, including minors and individuals not charged or acquitted.

Facial Recognition Act of 2023 requires detailed applications from prosecutors and approval from courts for authorized use of facial recognition.

Facial Recognition Act of 2023 prohibits the use of facial recognition with body cameras, for face surveillance, or for immigration enforcement.

Facial Recognition Act of 2023 enforces annual accuracy and bias testing by independent entities and prohibits systems that fail to meet minimum standards.

Facial Recognition Act of 2023 requires public reporting and logging of facial recognition use, including demographic data.

Facial Recognition Act of 2023 mandates audits of law enforcement agencies' use of facial recognition to ensure compliance and prevent misuse.

Measures for Labeling of AI-Generated Synthetic Content requires online information service providers to label AI-generated synthetic content with both explicit and implicit labels, ensuring that users can easily recognize AI-generated content.

Measures for Labeling of AI-Generated Synthetic Content instructs service providers to embed implicit labels in digital file metadata, indicating the content’s origin and attributes.

Measures for Labeling of AI-Generated Synthetic Content mandates content transmission platforms to verify metadata for implicit labels and add notifications if AI-origin is detected or suspected.

Measures for Labeling of AI-Generated Synthetic Content obligates application distribution platforms to assess apps for compliance with generative AI services and labeling.

Measures for Labeling of AI-Generated Synthetic Content permits exceptions for omitting explicit labels if users assume responsibility, with logs stored for a period of six months.

Measures for Labeling of AI-Generated Synthetic Content sets penalties for non-compliance to be enforced by the relevant regulatory authorities.

Oklahoma House Bill 1916 enacts the "Responsible Deployment of AI Systems Act," mandating comprehensive governance structures for AI deployment in Oklahoma and requiring classification of all AI systems by risk level based on their potential impact on safety, civil liberties, and fundamental rights.

Oklahoma House Bill 1916 prohibits the development and deployment of Unacceptable Risk AI systems, such as social scoring or AI-driven misinformation, while imposing strict oversight, audits, and transparency requirements on high-risk systems.

Oklahoma House Bill 1916 requires deployers to assess AI systems for biases, safety risks, and rights violations before deployment, implement mitigation strategies, and ensure qualified human oversight that can override system decisions.

Oklahoma House Bill 1916 requires public notification and appeal mechanisms when high-risk AI systems are used to make decisions that impact individuals, ensuring transparency and recourse.

Oklahoma House Bill 1916 establishes the Artificial Intelligence Council (AI Council) to regulate ethical AI use, including the AI Regulatory Sandbox Program and Workforce Development Program, to allow controlled testing of AI systems.

Oklahoma House Bill 1916 launches the AI Workforce Development Program to expand AI literacy and skills in underserved communities, prioritizing affordable training through grants to small businesses and educational institutions.

Oklahoma House Bill 1916 permits the AI Council to issue penalties for noncompliance and requires deployers to disclose related incidents.

Memorandum 25-21 (Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust) directs all Executive Branch departments and agencies to adopt AI by accelerating AI use and innovation while ensuring responsible deployment and governance.

Memorandum 25-21 (Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust) requires removal of barriers to AI innovation, focusing on delivering value for taxpayers and improving public services.

Memorandum 25-21 (Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust) instructs agencies to develop and share AI strategies, prioritize American AI products, and enhance workforce AI readiness.

Memorandum 25-21 (Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust) directs agencies to designate a Chief AI Officer (CAIO) to oversee AI efforts and improve public accountability.

Memorandum 25-21 (Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust) mandates implementation of minimum risk management practices for high-impact AI and provides guidance on AI governance, including creating AI impact assessments and ensuring human oversight.

Memorandum 25-21 (Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust) encourages sharing and reusing of AI resources across federal agencies to prevent redundancy and foster collaboration.

Memorandum 25-21 (Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust) implements public trust in AI use by requiring performance monitoring and mechanisms for public consultation and feedback.

Memorandum 25-21 (Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust) excludes specific domains like national security systems from AI governance requirements.

Memorandum 25-22 (Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government) promotes the competitive American AI marketplace by mandating federal agencies to procure AI systems that enhance efficiency and mission effectiveness while avoiding dependence on single vendors.

Memorandum 25-22 (Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government) ensures taxpayer dollars are safeguarded by tracking AI performance and managing risks as outlined in Executive Order 13960.

Memorandum 25-22 (Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government) directs agencies to update internal procedures within 270 days to align with this memorandum and OMB Memorandum M-25-21, requiring cross-functional teams for AI acquisitions and addressing intellectual property rights.

Memorandum 25-22 (Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government) mandates the protection of privacy and intellectual property, emphasizing compliance with federal law and policy.

Memorandum 25-22 (Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government) specifies that future AI contracts comply with new guidelines by establishing a clear timeline for implementation.

Memorandum 25-22 (Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government) excludes certain AI acquisitions and activities, such as national security systems and incidental AI use by contractors.

Memorandum 25-22 (Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government) requires GSA to develop AI acquisition guides within 100 days and establish a shared repository of best practices within 200 days.

Create AI Act of 2025 establishes a National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource (NAIRR) to enhance AI research accessibility and spur innovation.

Create AI Act of 2025 requires the Director of the National Science Foundation, in coordination with a NAIRR Steering Subcommittee, to oversee NAIRR’s establishment and governance.

Create AI Act of 2025 forms a Program Management Office to manage NAIRR’s daily operations, select an Operating Entity, and oversee asset allocation.

Create AI Act of 2025 defines user eligibility criteria for accessing NAIRR, including U.S.-based researchers and institutions.

Create AI Act of 2025 mandates policies for privacy, ethics, scientific integrity, and system security, with input from various advisory committees.

Create AI Act of 2025 authorizes the establishment of a fee schedule for NAIRR access, ensuring a free tier for research purposes.

Create AI Act of 2025 permits acceptance of donations to support NAIRR’s operation from the private sector.

Create AI Act of 2025 coordinates with relevant federal entities to integrate AI testbeds and educational resources.

Create AI Act of 2025 emphasizes research security compliance, aligning with national security guidelines on research integrity.

Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025 prohibits United States persons from importing AI technology from China and exporting AI technology to China after 180 days of enactment.

Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025 establishes penalties for individuals and entities violating these prohibitions, including fines and forfeiture of federal contracts.

Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025 requires the Secretary of Commerce to issue regulations implementing these prohibitions within 90 days of enactment.

Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025 prohibits United States persons from conducting AI research and development for or with Chinese entities or nationals of concern.

Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025 enforces penalties for these violations, including fines and federal benefits forfeiture.

Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025 emphasizes penalties disqualifying violators from federal financial assistance for five years.

Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025 restricts U.S. persons from having financial interests in Chinese AI research entities involved in military or surveillance activities.

Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025 permits the President to use emergency economic powers for enforcing these prohibitions.

Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025 involves multiple federal departments in enforcing these regulations.

HEARTS Act of 2025 establishes the National Center for Alternatives to Animals in Research and Testing to promote and fund nonanimal research methods, including artificial intelligence, within one year of the Act's enactment, under the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

HEARTS Act of 2025 requires the NIH to prioritize nonanimal methods in research proposals, assess the feasibility of nonanimal methods before approving research, and ensure proposals are reviewed by experts in nonanimal techniques.

HEARTS Act of 2025 instructs the Director of the National Center to support federally funded researchers in developing and adopting alternatives to animal testing, including AI, and report on animal usage publicly.

HEARTS Act of 2025 mandates each federally funded research entity using animals to report biannually on the number and species of animals used and submit and update plans to reduce these numbers.

HEARTS Act of 2025 defines "animal" to include any live nonhuman vertebrate or cephalopod used in research or testing.

Promoting Precision Agriculture Act require the Secretary of Agriculture, in consultation with the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Federal Communications Commission, to develop voluntary, consensus-based interconnectivity standards for precision agriculture within two years.

Promoting Precision Agriculture Act direct the Secretary to coordinate with relevant stakeholders, including public, private, and industry organizations, while considering factors such as the evolving demands and connectivity needs of precision agriculture, cybersecurity challenges, and the impact of AI and advanced wireless communications technology.

Promoting Precision Agriculture Act instruct the Comptroller General of the United States to conduct a study one year after the standards' development and every two years thereafter for eight years, assessing these standards for their voluntariness and effectiveness in fostering precision agriculture.

Promoting Precision Agriculture Act require submission of a report to relevant Senate and House Committees summarizing the findings from each study.

Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to conduct annual assessments, in consultation with the Director of National Intelligence, on terrorism threats posed by terrorist organizations using generative AI applications.

Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act instructs inclusion of analysis on incidents involving extremist messaging, recruitment, and WMD capabilities linked to generative AI in these assessments, plus recommendations for countermeasures.

Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act ensures these assessments are coordinated with DHS legal and rights offices to protect privacy and civil liberties, and shared in unclassified form publicly, with classified annexes if necessary.

Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act mandates a briefing to congressional committees within 30 days of assessment submission.

Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act directs the Secretary to incorporate and disseminate terrorism threat information from fusion centers into DHS systems.

Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act defines "generative AI applications" as AI models generating synthetic content and clarifies terms for fusion centers and terrorist organizations.

Protect Victims of Digital Exploitation and Manipulation Act of 2025 amends title 18, United States Code, to prohibit the production or distribution of digital forgeries of intimate visual depictions without the consent of the identifiable individual involved.

Protect Victims of Digital Exploitation and Manipulation Act of 2025 defines digital forgery as an intimate visual depiction created or altered using software, machine learning, artificial intelligence, or other computer-generated means that appears authentic to a reasonable person.

Protect Victims of Digital Exploitation and Manipulation Act of 2025 exempts actions taken in good faith during legal proceedings, medical applications, law enforcement, or investigations of unlawful content or conduct.

Protect Victims of Digital Exploitation and Manipulation Act of 2025 excludes communications service providers from liability unless they recklessly distribute the content.

Protect Victims of Digital Exploitation and Manipulation Act of 2025 applies regulations if either the offender or the victim is a U.S. national.

Protect Victims of Digital Exploitation and Manipulation Act of 2025 defines terms such as consent, digital forgery, identifiable individual, intimate visual depiction, and communications service.

Protect Victims of Digital Exploitation and Manipulation Act of 2025 provides severability to ensure the statute's provisions remain effective even if parts are judged unconstitutional.

China Technology Transfer Control Act of 2025 control the export, re-export, and transfer of certain national interest technology and intellectual property, including AI, to China, starting 180 days after the Act's enactment.

China Technology Transfer Control Act of 2025 require the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Commerce to report within 90 days on the necessity of controls under specific export regulations.

China Technology Transfer Control Act of 2025 prescribe regulations within 180 days to enforce these controls.

China Technology Transfer Control Act of 2025 impose sanctions under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act on entities engaging in the unlawful transfer or use of controlled technologies with China, excluding goods importation.

China Technology Transfer Control Act of 2025 empower the President to waive sanctions if deemed in U.S. national security interests.

China Technology Transfer Control Act of 2025 instruct the United States Trade Representative to annually list Chinese products, including AI, that receive government support or assist in human rights violations.

China Technology Transfer Control Act of 2025 include AI technologies in products receiving Chinese support under its industrial policy, "Made in China 2025."

AI PLAN Act require the Secretary of the Treasury, Secretary of Homeland Security, and Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with specified officials, to jointly submit annual reports to Congress on defending against financial crime risks posed by AI, including fraud and misinformation.

AI PLAN Act describe interagency policies and procedures to protect against these risks, listing available and needed resources, technologies, and budget estimates.

AI PLAN Act consider risks such as deepfakes, voice cloning, and foreign election interference.

AI PLAN Act list officials consulted as the U.S. Trade Representative, Attorney General, Federal Reserve Chairman, NIST Director, Undersecretary of Commerce for Industry and Security, and SEC Chairman.

AI PLAN Act submit recommendations to Congress within 90 days post-report, including legislative suggestions and best practices for risk mitigation related to AI-driven financial crimes.

S.305 Small Business Technological Act of 2025 authorize the Small Business Administration to provide loans for business software, cloud computing services, and technology that utilize artificial intelligence.

S.305 Small Business Technological Act of 2025 permit these loans to support business operations, including the processing, payment, or tracking of payroll expenses, human resources, sales and billing functions, and accounting or tracking of supplies, inventory, records, and expenses.

S.305 Small Business Technological Act of 2025 clarify that this provision does not invalidate prior loans made for similar purposes under the Small Business Act.

S.305 Small Business Technological Act of 2025 prohibit the use of these loans for research and development activities.

S.305 Small Business Technological Act of 2025 ensure the amendment does not alter the definition of working capital in the context of the Small Business Act.

Protecting Our Children in an AI World Act of 2025 amends title 18 of the United States Code to prohibit child pornography produced using artificial intelligence.

Protecting Our Children in an AI World Act of 2025 eliminates the affirmative defense in prosecutions involving AI-generated child pornography by removing certain clauses in Section 2252A(c).

Protecting Our Children in an AI World Act of 2025 expands the definition of sexually explicit conduct in Section 2256(2)(B) to include actual or simulated obscene exhibition of the clothed or unclothed genitals, pubic area, buttocks, or female nipple.

Protecting Our Children in an AI World Act of 2025 ensures that if any provision of the Act is held unconstitutional, the remaining provisions continue to have effect.

CORE Act of 2025 leverages artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies to approximate the resources in transboundary hydrocarbon reservoirs.

CORE Act of 2025 requires the application of data analysis tools, AI, quantum computing, and modeling to refine resource estimates and reduce uncertainty.

CORE Act of 2025 instructs the Secretaries to prioritize advanced geophysical, geological, and geotechnical data in the report.

CORE Act of 2025 encourages partnerships with federal agencies such as the National Science Foundation and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to utilize existing maritime technologies.

CORE Act of 2025 tasks the report preparation with addressing uncertainties using AI and other technologies for informed decision-making on transboundary hydrocarbon reservoirs.

Bipartisan Health Care Act instructs the Comptroller General of the United States to conduct a technology assessment and submit a report to Congress on wearable medical devices.

Bipartisan Health Care Act requires the report to assess the capabilities and limitations of these devices in supporting clinical decision-making.

Bipartisan Health Care Act includes an evaluation of the potential for such devices to accurately prescribe treatments.

Bipartisan Health Care Act examines the benefits and challenges of integrating artificial intelligence to enhance these devices.

Bipartisan Health Care Act provides policy options to maximize benefits and mitigate challenges associated with the development or use of wearable medical devices.

City of San Jose Artificial Intelligence Policy 1.7.12 establishes a governance framework for AI use in San José, aligning with the City’s data security, privacy, and existing policies.

City of San Jose Artificial Intelligence Policy 1.7.12 directs the Chief Information Officer (CIO) to manage the AI Handbook, with the City Information Security Officer (CISO) and City Digital Privacy Officer (CDPO) ensuring system security, resilience, privacy, and policy compliance.

City of San Jose Artificial Intelligence Policy 1.7.12 requires users to uphold guiding principles such as effectiveness, transparency, equity, accountability, privacy, and security.

City of San Jose Artificial Intelligence Policy 1.7.12 prohibits AI applications involving real-time biometric identification, emotion analysis, fully automated impactful decisions, social scoring, and cognitive manipulation.

City of San Jose Artificial Intelligence Policy 1.7.12 mandates reporting AI-caused harm within 24 hours.

City of San Jose Artificial Intelligence Policy 1.7.12 implements sunset procedures for outdated AI systems.

City of San Jose Artificial Intelligence Policy 1.7.12 obliges compliance with public records laws and City’s transparency policies.

City of San Jose Artificial Intelligence Policy 1.7.12 enforces policy adherence, with violations subject to disciplinary action.

City of San Jose Artificial Intelligence Policy 1.7.12 requires Finance to obtain AI usage disclosures in procurement.

City of San Jose Artificial Intelligence Policy 1.7.12 defines AI and related system terms within the policy context.

California Attorney General’s Legal Advisory on the Application of Existing California Laws to Artificial Intelligence guides AI developers, sellers, and users in California on legal obligations under state consumer protection, civil rights, competition, and data privacy laws.

California Attorney General’s Legal Advisory on the Application of Existing California Laws to Artificial Intelligence requires that AI systems comply with laws against unfair practices, deceptive advertising, false advertising, and any antitrust violations.

California Attorney General’s Legal Advisory on the Application of Existing California Laws to Artificial Intelligence addresses risks of bias and discrimination in AI systems under civil rights laws, enforcing accountability for discriminatory outcomes.

California Attorney General’s Legal Advisory on the Application of Existing California Laws to Artificial Intelligence mandates transparency about AI's use, dataset training, and impact assessment.

California Attorney General’s Legal Advisory on the Application of Existing California Laws to Artificial Intelligence prohibits misuse of AI for impersonation, false representation, and creation of deceptive political content.

California Attorney General’s Legal Advisory on the Application of Existing California Laws to Artificial Intelligence enforces privacy compliance under the California Consumer Privacy Act, ensuring data protection and informed consent from consumers when AI systems use personal information.

California Attorney General’s Legal Advisory on the Application of Existing California Laws to Artificial Intelligence introduces new AI legislation, effective January 2025, mandating disclosures, detection tools for AI-generated content, and accountability in entertainment and election contexts.

California Attorney General’s Legal Advisory on the Application of Existing California Laws to Artificial Intelligence expands prohibitions on exploitative AI uses, including specific amendments addressing child pornography and deepfake technologies.

California Attorney General’s Legal Advisory on the Application of Existing California Laws to Artificial Intelligence ensures AI tools in healthcare require supervision by licensed physicians.

Meta Frontier AI Framework (Version 1.1) establishes a Frontier AI Framework at Meta to manage risks of advanced AI, focusing on models exceeding current advanced capabilities.

Meta Frontier AI Framework (Version 1.1) implements processes to prevent catastrophic outcomes by identifying threat scenarios and developing threat models.

Meta Frontier AI Framework (Version 1.1) defines risk thresholds to categorize AI models; critical threshold results in ceasing development, while high and moderate thresholds dictate further risk mitigation measures.

Meta Frontier AI Framework (Version 1.1) outlines governance and transparency processes in AI development, including stages of planning, evaluation, mitigation, and decision-making policies.

Meta Frontier AI Framework (Version 1.1) emphasizes threat modeling exercises to assess catastrophic risks and ensure models do not uniquely enable harmful scenarios.

Meta Frontier AI Framework (Version 1.1) focuses on cybersecurity and chemical/biological risks by specifying threat scenarios and enabling capabilities to guide risk assessments.

Meta Frontier AI Framework (Version 1.1) plans to update the framework by integrating evolving AI risks and research, actively engaging with AI communities, and enhancing evaluation and post-release monitoring techniques.

Establishment of Reporting Requirements for the Development of Advanced Artificial Intelligence Models and Computing Clusters amends 15 CFR part 702 to introduce special reporting requirements for U.S. entities involved in advanced AI model development and computing clusters.

Establishment of Reporting Requirements for the Development of Advanced Artificial Intelligence Models and Computing Clusters requires covered U.S. persons to notify the Department quarterly if engaging in AI activities exceeding specified computational thresholds.

Establishment of Reporting Requirements for the Development of Advanced Artificial Intelligence Models and Computing Clusters mandates covered U.S. persons to respond to BIS inquiries within 30 days and correct incomplete submissions within 14 days.

Establishment of Reporting Requirements for the Development of Advanced Artificial Intelligence Models and Computing Clusters obliges entities to report any training or development of dual-use foundation models, including security measures and model performance in AI red-team testing.

Establishment of Reporting Requirements for the Development of Advanced Artificial Intelligence Models and Computing Clusters stipulates that entities submit affirmations of no applicable activities if none occur for seven consecutive quarters.

Establishment of Reporting Requirements for the Development of Advanced Artificial Intelligence Models and Computing Clusters defines key terms, including AI red-teaming, dual-use foundation models, and large-scale computing clusters, to specify the scope of activities to which these requirements apply.

Establishment of Reporting Requirements for the Development of Advanced Artificial Intelligence Models and Computing Clusters establishes quarterly notification deadlines and processes for requesting extensions if additional response time is needed.

Illinois SB2203 enacts the Preventing Algorithmic Discrimination Act in Illinois to combat discrimination by automated decision tools.

Illinois SB2203 defines "algorithmic discrimination" as resulting from AI tool usage that causes discrimination against protected classes.

Illinois SB2203 requires deployers to perform annual impact assessments on automated tools by January 2027, analyzing potential biases and preventing discrimination.

Illinois SB2203 mandates notifications to individuals affected by AI decisions, with options for alternative processes.

Illinois SB2203 requires an alternative process for those that request AI tools not be used in a decision.

Illinois SB2203 obliges deployers to establish comprehensive governance programs to manage discrimination risks, requiring technical safeguards and annual compliance reviews.

Illinois SB2203 mandates public availability of policies on AI tool usage and discrimination management.

Illinois SB2203 prohibits use of tools resulting in algorithmic discrimination, with civil actions allowed from January 2028 for violations, including compensatory damages and legal fees.

Illinois SB2203 obliges deployers to submit impact assessments to the Attorney General, with fines for non-compliance.

Illinois SB2203 integrates enforcement with the Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Business Practices Act.

AI Incident Reporting and Security Enhancement Act directs the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to update the National Vulnerability Database to include AI security vulnerabilities.

AI Incident Reporting and Security Enhancement Act requires NIST to establish common definitions for AI security vulnerabilities and develop standards for managing these vulnerabilities.

AI Incident Reporting and Security Enhancement Act mandates a multi-stakeholder process to assess voluntary reporting and tracking of substantial AI security and safety incidents, and to establish guidelines, best practices, and standardized mechanisms for reporting AI incidents.

AI Incident Reporting and Security Enhancement Act obligates NIST to submit a report to Congress within three years, detailing the findings and recommendations from the multi-stakeholder process on AI incident reporting and tracking.

Artificial Intelligence Literacy Act of 2023 amends the Digital Equity Act of 2021 to include artificial intelligence (AI) literacy within the scope of digital literacy.

Artificial Intelligence Literacy Act of 2023 defines "artificial intelligence literacy" as understanding basic AI principles, applications, implications, limitations, and ethical considerations.

Artificial Intelligence Literacy Act of 2023 requires grants to support AI literacy initiatives in public elementary and secondary schools, including teacher training, professional development, and resource development.

Artificial Intelligence Literacy Act of 2023 supports higher education institutions to develop AI learning labs, virtual platforms, and educational tools for teachers and community educators.

Artificial Intelligence Literacy Act of 2023 includes grants to community anchor institutions for AI education and training programs.

Artificial Intelligence Literacy Act of 2023 mandates an annual report to Congress summarizing and analyzing the progress and impact of AI literacy initiatives, with recommendations for expansion or modification.

AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2024 requires the inclusion of disclaimers on political advertisements containing content substantially generated by AI.

AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2024 mandates that disclaimers must clearly state the use of AI in creating or materially altering the content.

AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2024 establishes safe harbor guidelines for what constitutes a "clear and conspicuous manner" in disclaimers for image, audio, and video communications.

AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2024 amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to include penalties for violations of the disclaimer requirements, with fines up to $50,000.

AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2024 directs the Federal Election Commission (FEC) to issue regulations outlining criteria for determining substantially AI-generated content and requirements for the disclosure statement.

AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2024 requires the FEC to report on compliance and enforcement within two years and biannually thereafter to Congress.

Colorado SB21-169 prohibits insurers from using external consumer data, algorithms, and predictive models that result in unfair discrimination based on various protected characteristics such as race, gender, or sexual orientation.

Colorado SB21-169 requires the Commissioner of Insurance to adopt rules ensuring insurers demonstrate their data and models do not result in unfair discrimination.

Colorado SB21-169 engages a stakeholder process to gather input from insurers, consumers, and other parties before rule adoption.

Colorado SB21-169 obliges insurers to provide detailed information about their data usage and implement risk management frameworks to minimize discrimination risks.

Colorado SB21-169 allows the Commissioner to examine and investigate insurers' data practices.

Colorado SB21-169 permits exemption for certain insurance types such as title insurance and high-premium commercial insurance policies.

Colorado SB21-169 defines key terms like "algorithm" and "predictive model" as related to insurance practices, emphasizing consumer data's impact on discrimination.

New York SB5959 (2020) establishes the right of publicity, allowing individuals to control the use of their name, voice, signature, photograph, or likeness, especially for deceased performers and personalities.

New York SB5959 (2020) prohibits unauthorized use of digital replicas in fictional works without clear disclaimers or consent from rights holders.

New York SB5959 (2020) defines penalties for illicit use, including compensatory and punitive damages, and requires proof of unauthorized profits for damages calculation.

New York SB5959 (2020) clarifies exceptions for newsworthy, educational, or political contexts where rights protection does not apply.

New York SB5959 (2020) allows a private right of action for individuals depicted in non-consensual, sexually explicit material, prohibiting dissemination.

New York SB5959 (2020) requires disclaimers be insufficient defense in unauthorized explicit material cases.

New York SB5959 (2020) enables registration of deceased personalities' rights with the Secretary of State.

New York SB5959 (2020) establishes a 40-year post-mortem protection limit for these rights.

New York SB5959 (2020) specifies severability and additional legal recourse without superseding existing legal protections.

Washington SB 5092 (2021-22), Section 151 establishes a work group led by the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) to develop recommendations for automated decision systems, including AI-enabled profiling, focusing on fairness, transparency, and non-discrimination.

Washington SB 5092 (2021-22), Section 151 requires the OCIO to oversee procurement and contracting for IT goods and services, ensuring cloud technology fee recovery and project data posting on the statewide IT dashboard.

Washington SB 5092 (2021-22), Section 151 provides $12,000 for examining and auditing automated decision-making systems to ensure fairness and transparency.

Washington SB 5092 (2021-22), Section 151 allocates $23,150,000 for Microsoft's 365 licenses with advanced security features, alongside distribution and annual license reporting requirements.

Washington SB 5092 (2021-22), Section 151 designates $12,393,000 for cybersecurity efforts, $4,303,000 for small agency IT services, and $1,493,000 for cybersecurity implementation, pending bill enactment.

Washington SB 5092 (2021-22), Section 151 involves various state departments in creating a health and human services enterprise coalition led by the Health Care Authority.

Washington SB 5092 (2021-22), Section 151 directs collaborative data management efforts for a state-operated geospatial data portal related to natural hazards.
