Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomy require States to ensure military AI use complies with international law, particularly international humanitarian law.

Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomy mandate accountability through a responsible human command chain.

Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomy impose legal reviews to align military AI with international obligations and enhance civilian protection.

Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomy demand oversight by senior officials for high-consequence AI applications.

Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomy advocate minimizing unintended bias in military AI.

Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomy insist on transparent, auditable methodologies and documentation for military AI development.

Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomy oblige training for personnel to understand AI capabilities and limitations, preventing automation bias.

Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomy prescribe explicit, well-defined uses for military AI, with rigorous testing for safety and effectiveness.

Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomy implement safeguards to detect and mitigate AI failures, with the ability to deactivate systems if needed.

Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomy encourage States to publicly commit to these measures, support responsible AI use, and engage internationally to refine and promote these standards.

An Act to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 39, Chapter 14, Part 1 and Title 47, relative to the protection of personal rights. expands the "Personal Rights Protection Act of 1984," renaming it the "Ensuring Likeness, Voice, and Image Security Act of 2024."

An Act to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 39, Chapter 14, Part 1 and Title 47, relative to the protection of personal rights. grants individuals property rights over their name, photograph, voice, or likeness across all mediums.

An Act to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 39, Chapter 14, Part 1 and Title 47, relative to the protection of personal rights. defines "voice" to include both actual and simulated sounds identifiable to an individual.

An Act to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 39, Chapter 14, Part 1 and Title 47, relative to the protection of personal rights. terminates exclusive commercial rights after two years of non-use, beginning ten years after death.

An Act to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 39, Chapter 14, Part 1 and Title 47, relative to the protection of personal rights. imposes civil liability for the unauthorized commercial use of an individual's name, photograph, voice, or likeness.

An Act to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 39, Chapter 14, Part 1 and Title 47, relative to the protection of personal rights. prohibits distribution of technology primarily used to produce unauthorized likenesses.

An Act to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 39, Chapter 14, Part 1 and Title 47, relative to the protection of personal rights. allows individuals or parties with exclusive contracts for personal services or sound recordings to enforce rights.

An Act to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 39, Chapter 14, Part 1 and Title 47, relative to the protection of personal rights. exempts certain uses protected by the First Amendment as fair use, including news, commentary, and satire.

An Act to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 39, Chapter 14, Part 1 and Title 47, relative to the protection of personal rights. mandates that employees or owners of any medium used for advertising be liable if they publish or disseminate an advertisement in violation of this act, and if they should have known about the violation.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section Title XV, Subtitle D ("Artificial Intelligence") establishes an initiative to improve the usability of AI systems, that are used by Department of Defense personnel, by considering human factors and cognitive ergonomics. It mandates the development of a guidance plan for their inclusion and evaluation in current and future programs.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section Title XV, Subtitle D ("Artificial Intelligence") establishes a program for high-performance computing infrastructure to support advanced AI capabilities, ensuring non-duplication with Department of Energy efforts. The instrument mandates the development of a roadmap that assesses the anticipated compute requirements, security standards, and relevant resources for the infrastructure required to enable advanced AI capabilities.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section Title XV, Subtitle D ("Artificial Intelligence") mandates developing a plan for costs and budgeting related to data used for various stages in the AI development and deployment lifecycle. This plan must include budgets for current programs and programs established by the enactment of this Act, as well as, costs related to data procurement, preparation, protection, and analysis.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section Title XV, Subtitle D ("Artificial Intelligence") requires the Secretary of Defense to evaluate the feasibility of centers of excellence for AI-enabled weapon systems, focusing on national and international collaboration, training of personnel, and best practices. Requires a report and briefing to Congress.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 221 ("Improvements relating to defining, identifying, and planning the artificial intelligence workforce of the Department of Defense") requires the Officer to define and identify the AI workforce, clarify roles, code roles in workforce data systems, and develop qualification programs.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 221 ("Improvements relating to defining, identifying, and planning the artificial intelligence workforce of the Department of Defense") mandates updating the Department's Human Capital Operating Plan to align with strategic goals and ensure consistent AI terminology.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 221 ("Improvements relating to defining, identifying, and planning the artificial intelligence workforce of the Department of Defense") sets the expiration of the Officer's appointment on September 30, 2030.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 221 ("Improvements relating to defining, identifying, and planning the artificial intelligence workforce of the Department of Defense") demands a briefing to congressional defense committees within 240 days, detailing AI workforce positions, required skills, current workforce state, and future requirements.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1087 ("Establishment of Department of Defense working group on multilateral artificial intelligence coordination") demands the Secretary of Defense to establish a Department of Defense working group to coordinate AI initiatives with U.S. allies and partners within 90 days of the Act's enactment.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1087 ("Establishment of Department of Defense working group on multilateral artificial intelligence coordination") designates a senior civilian or military officer to lead the group and determines allied participation.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1087 ("Establishment of Department of Defense working group on multilateral artificial intelligence coordination") requires the group to develop AI strategies and interoperability for intelligence sharing, battlespace awareness, and other defense operations.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1087 ("Establishment of Department of Defense working group on multilateral artificial intelligence coordination") mandates managing AI data security and evaluating defense industrial capabilities for AI integration.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1087 ("Establishment of Department of Defense working group on multilateral artificial intelligence coordination") ensures knowledge and technical data remain under the control of the originating country’s export laws.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1087 ("Establishment of Department of Defense working group on multilateral artificial intelligence coordination") terminates the group on September 30, 2028, unless extended for national security reasons by the Secretary.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1087 ("Establishment of Department of Defense working group on multilateral artificial intelligence coordination") defines key terms such as "battlespace awareness" and "covered operational use."

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 236 ("Pilot program on development of near-term use cases and demonstration of artificial intelligence toward biotechnology applications for national security") mandates the Secretary of Defense to implement a pilot program demonstrating artificial intelligence in national security-related biotechnology applications.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 236 ("Pilot program on development of near-term use cases and demonstration of artificial intelligence toward biotechnology applications for national security") requires collaboration through public-private partnerships to execute the program.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 236 ("Pilot program on development of near-term use cases and demonstration of artificial intelligence toward biotechnology applications for national security") permits the use of Department of Defense laboratory facilities and computing infrastructure to support biotechnology experimentation and AI model validation.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 236 ("Pilot program on development of near-term use cases and demonstration of artificial intelligence toward biotechnology applications for national security") stipulates the program's commencement within one year of enactment and its termination five years after starting.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 236 ("Pilot program on development of near-term use cases and demonstration of artificial intelligence toward biotechnology applications for national security") obligates the Secretary to submit annual reports to congressional defense committees, detailing program progress, data resource assessments, cybersecurity measures, collaboration mechanisms, and AI roles in biotechnology.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 236 ("Pilot program on development of near-term use cases and demonstration of artificial intelligence toward biotechnology applications for national security") requires a transition plan to be submitted one year before program termination, outlining steps for operationalization, including costs, infrastructure needs, and ecosystem analysis.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 236 ("Pilot program on development of near-term use cases and demonstration of artificial intelligence toward biotechnology applications for national security") aims to assess the viability of transitioning technology developed in the pilot into operational use within the Department.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 6506 ("Enhancement of authority for intelligence community public-private talent exchanges") extends the duration of temporary details for such exchanges from 3 years to 5 years.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 6506 ("Enhancement of authority for intelligence community public-private talent exchanges") prohibits private-sector employees detailed to the intelligence community from accessing trade secrets or proprietary information.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 6506 ("Enhancement of authority for intelligence community public-private talent exchanges") clarifies that participation in the exchange program does not create an organizational conflict of interest solely by virtue of involvement.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 6506 ("Enhancement of authority for intelligence community public-private talent exchanges") requires implementation of systems to address any identified conflicts of interest.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 6506 ("Enhancement of authority for intelligence community public-private talent exchanges") mandates the Director of National Intelligence to submit annual reports to Congress on the implementation and use of the exchange program, including recommendations for improvements, for three consecutive years.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1078 ("Study and report on Department of Defense use of unmanned ground vehicle systems manufactured by certain foreign entities") mandates the Secretary of Defense to study the use of unmanned ground vehicle systems by the Department of Defense manufactured by certain foreign entities.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1078 ("Study and report on Department of Defense use of unmanned ground vehicle systems manufactured by certain foreign entities") requires submission of a report to congressional defense committees within 180 days, assessing usage, national security threats, and identifying foreign manufacturers.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1078 ("Study and report on Department of Defense use of unmanned ground vehicle systems manufactured by certain foreign entities") calls for the evaluation of cybersecurity risks, technological vulnerabilities, and the foreign entities' military-civil nexus.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1078 ("Study and report on Department of Defense use of unmanned ground vehicle systems manufactured by certain foreign entities") demands an assessment of the feasibility of the Defense Innovation Unit developing a list of U.S. manufacturers.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1078 ("Study and report on Department of Defense use of unmanned ground vehicle systems manufactured by certain foreign entities") mandates an evaluation of whether a prohibition on procuring and operating these systems is advisable for U.S. national security.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1078 ("Study and report on Department of Defense use of unmanned ground vehicle systems manufactured by certain foreign entities") prohibits procurement and operation of these systems by the Department of Defense one year after the report submission, unless deemed in the national interest.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1078 ("Study and report on Department of Defense use of unmanned ground vehicle systems manufactured by certain foreign entities") exempts this prohibition if recommended as not in the best national security interest.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1078 ("Study and report on Department of Defense use of unmanned ground vehicle systems manufactured by certain foreign entities") defines "covered foreign countries" including China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1031 ("Requirements for the unmanned maritime autonomy architecture") adopt or join a governance model that includes both Government and industry for the maritime unmanned systems standards.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1031 ("Requirements for the unmanned maritime autonomy architecture") implement a process for incorporating industry feedback into these standards and align them with leading industry practices.

Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1031 ("Requirements for the unmanned maritime autonomy architecture") label and distribute the standards as open and publicly releasable information to the greatest extent possible.

Executive Order on Advancing United States Leadership in Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure (EO 14141) requires federal agencies to identify, solicit proposals for, and lease federal lands suitable for AI data centers and related clean energy projects, aiming for full-capacity operation by the end of 2027.

Executive Order on Advancing United States Leadership in Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure (EO 14141) emphasizes high labor standards and community collaboration, among other factors, in the selection of projects to account for health, safety, and ecological risks/harms.

Executive Order on Advancing United States Leadership in Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure (EO 14141) mandates cybersecurity, model evaluation, supply-chain protection, and other requirements for AI infrastructure developed pursuant to the executive order.

Executive Order on Advancing United States Leadership in Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure (EO 14141) requires the Secretary of Energy to facilitate grid interconnection for AI infrastructure developed pursuant to the executive order.

Executive Order on Advancing United States Leadership in Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure (EO 14141) directs expedited permit processing for federal sites hosting the infrastructure.

Executive Order on Advancing United States Leadership in Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure (EO 14141) requires relevant agencies to take additional enumerated measures to expedite permitting and power procurement for AI infrastructure nationwide.

Executive Order on Advancing United States Leadership in Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure (EO 14141) directs creation of a plan for robust engagement with allies to encourage global AI infrastructure development including the necessary workforce, ensuring security and resilience in international supply chains.

Executive Order on Removing Barriers To American Leadership In Artificial Intelligence mandates review and potential suspension, revision, or rescission of actions under the revoked Executive Order 14110 that conflict with the new policy.

Executive Order on Removing Barriers To American Leadership In Artificial Intelligence instructs Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to revise relevant memoranda to align with the new policy.

Executive Order on Removing Barriers To American Leadership In Artificial Intelligence directs that implementation not impair existing legal authority of departments or create enforceable rights against the U.S.

Executive Order on Removing Barriers To American Leadership In Artificial Intelligence ensures that actions are consistent with applicable laws.

New York artificial intelligence act (New York AI act) establishes the "New York AI Act" to ensure AI development and use in New York State is safe, responsible and non-discriminatory.

New York artificial intelligence act (New York AI act) requires developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to undergo independent audits for algorithmic discrimination before and after deployment.

New York artificial intelligence act (New York AI act) mandates detailed reporting by developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to the Attorney General, covering system capabilities and potential risks.

New York artificial intelligence act (New York AI act) prohibits the deployment of AI causing algorithmic discrimination or of systems that have not passed the mandated audit.

New York artificial intelligence act (New York AI act) establishes whistleblower protections for employees disclosing AI-related non-compliance.

New York artificial intelligence act (New York AI act) forbids the use of social scoring AI systems evaluating individuals based on behavioral data resulting in unfair treatment.

New York artificial intelligence act (New York AI act) allows the Attorney General to enforce compliance and allows a private right of action for those harmed by AI non-compliance.

Framework to Mitigate AI-Enabled Extreme Risks establishes a framework for federal oversight of advanced AI models, termed "frontier models," to mitigate extreme AI-enabled risks like biological, chemical, cyber, and nuclear threats.

Framework to Mitigate AI-Enabled Extreme Risks defines frontier models as those requiring computing power exceeding 10^26 operations, and capable of diverse tasks or intended for specific high-risk areas.

Framework to Mitigate AI-Enabled Extreme Risks mandates entities selling or renting large computing resources to report usage and exercise due diligence, particularly concerning foreign clients.

Framework to Mitigate AI-Enabled Extreme Risks requires developers to notify an oversight entity before training frontier models and integrate safeguards against extreme risks.

Framework to Mitigate AI-Enabled Extreme Risks obligates developers to adhere to cybersecurity standards and report risk mitigation steps.

Framework to Mitigate AI-Enabled Extreme Risks imposes an evaluation and licensing process before deploying frontier models, using a tiered structure based on risk level to determine deployment scope.

Framework to Mitigate AI-Enabled Extreme Risks suggests options for an oversight entity, including an interagency body, new agency, or existing federal agencies, emphasizing expert involvement.

Framework to Mitigate AI-Enabled Extreme Risks tasks the oversight entity to report on emerging challenges and risks, ensuring framework adaptability.

Artificial Intelligence Safety Commitments (China AI Industry Alliance) calls for the establishment of safety teams and risk management mechanisms for AI safety and security.

Artificial Intelligence Safety Commitments (China AI Industry Alliance) mandates safety and security testing for AI models, prioritizing evaluations in critical domains.

Artificial Intelligence Safety Commitments (China AI Industry Alliance) implements data security measures to protect training and operational data, ensuring privacy and accuracy.

Artificial Intelligence Safety Commitments (China AI Industry Alliance) enhances infrastructure security through regular penetration tests and incident response protocols.

Artificial Intelligence Safety Commitments (China AI Industry Alliance) requires transparency in AI model capabilities, limitations, and risk disclosures.

Artificial Intelligence Safety Commitments (China AI Industry Alliance) advances research in AI safety and security, addressing potential biases and risks in frontier applications.

Artificial Intelligence Safety Commitments (China AI Industry Alliance) signatories include Alibaba, Baidu, Huawei, Tencent, and other major Chinese tech companies.

AI Safety Governance Framework v1.0 (National Technical Committee 260 on Cybersecurity of SAC) establishes principles and mechanisms for AI safety governance, emphasizing a balance between development and security and involving all stakeholders in a coordinated approach.

AI Safety Governance Framework v1.0 (National Technical Committee 260 on Cybersecurity of SAC) commits to enhancing AI safety by identifying risks, promoting inclusivity, and ensuring all participants take responsibility.

AI Safety Governance Framework v1.0 (National Technical Committee 260 on Cybersecurity of SAC) advocates for international cooperation in AI safety governance, pursuing best practices and consensus building.

AI Safety Governance Framework v1.0 (National Technical Committee 260 on Cybersecurity of SAC) outlines safety guidelines for developers, service providers, and users, focusing on ethics, data protection, risk assessment, and mitigation strategies.

AI Safety Governance Framework v1.0 (National Technical Committee 260 on Cybersecurity of SAC) mandates developers to uphold a people-centered approach, strengthen data security, and assess the risk of biases in AI models.

AI Safety Governance Framework v1.0 (National Technical Committee 260 on Cybersecurity of SAC) requires service providers to disclose the capabilities and limitations of AI systems, ensure users can make informed choices about their use of AI, and provide users with information on the accuracy of AI products.

AI Safety Governance Framework v1.0 (National Technical Committee 260 on Cybersecurity of SAC) encourages users in key areas to assess AI impacts, ensure protection of sensitive data in usage of AI systems, guarantee AI products remain subject to human control, and avoid complete reliance on AI for decision making.

AI Safety Governance Framework v1.0 (National Technical Committee 260 on Cybersecurity of SAC) recommends general users of AI systems to increase their awareness of potential risks, review the terms and conditions of AI products before use, be wary of entering sensitive information unnecessarily, and keep in mind the potential impact of AI products on minors.

Joint Statement on Risk Assessment of Advanced AI Systems (International Network of AI Safety Institutes) highlights six key aspects for risk assessment of advanced AI systems: actionable, transparent, comprehensive, multistakeholder, iterative, and reproducible.

Joint Statement on Risk Assessment of Advanced AI Systems (International Network of AI Safety Institutes) commits to developing a shared scientific basis for risk assessments via joint evaluations and cooperative research, allowing flexibility for members to adapt assessments according to international and domestic frameworks.

Joint Statement on Risk Assessment of Advanced AI Systems (International Network of AI Safety Institutes) emphasizes actionable assessments that inform effective mitigation based on specified criteria, and transparency to ensure evidence-based outcomes and broader understanding.

Joint Statement on Risk Assessment of Advanced AI Systems (International Network of AI Safety Institutes) advocates for comprehensiveness by linking potential risks to real-world harms and benefits, considering impacts from large-scale AI adoption, and aligning assessments with Sustainable Development Goals.

Joint Statement on Risk Assessment of Advanced AI Systems (International Network of AI Safety Institutes) stresses a multistakeholder approach, incorporating diverse perspectives from industry, academia, civil society, government, and multiple disciplines.

Joint Statement on Risk Assessment of Advanced AI Systems (International Network of AI Safety Institutes) calls for iterative assessments, adapting to AI advancements, ongoing safety research, and post-deployment monitoring.

Joint Statement on Risk Assessment of Advanced AI Systems (International Network of AI Safety Institutes) encourages reproducibility to enhance verification, validation, and interoperability among methods and actors.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 1709) establishes the Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act to regulate high-risk AI systems and prohibit certain harmful AI uses.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 1709) requires developers, distributors, and deployers of high-risk AI systems to protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination and complete impact assessments.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 1709) mandates the disclosure to consumers when interacting with high-risk AI systems and provides consumer rights to contest decisions made by these systems.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 1709) prohibits AI systems from manipulating behavior, social scoring, using biometric identifiers without consent, inferring sensitive attributes, causing harm, and producing unlawful content.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 1709) creates an Artificial Intelligence Council to guide ethical AI use, issue advisory opinions, and suggest legislative reforms.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 1709) initiates an AI Regulatory Sandbox Program for controlled testing without full compliance.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 1709) implements AI workforce development grants to address workforce gaps and support AI-related education.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 1709) allows enforcement by the Attorney General with civil penalties for non-compliance.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 1709) effective from September 1, 2025.

Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI requires organizations to raise awareness of AI security and incorporate AI security content into cyber security training, tailored to staff roles.

Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI requires assessments of AI system design for security alongside functionality and performance, including documentation of business needs, data needs, and potential security risks.

Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI mandates threat modeling and risk management targeting AI-specific attacks and ensure human oversight capabilities in AI systems.

Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI requires asset tracking and protection, disaster recovery strategies for AI systems, and secure data management.

Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI specifies secure infrastructure practices, including strong access control, secure development environments, and clear vulnerability disclosure policies.

Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI mandates secure supply chain processes and thorough documentation of data, models, and prompts.

Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI calls for rigorous security assessment testing, share findings, and support End-users during incidents.

Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI encourages maintaining regular security updates and system behavior monitoring.

Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI ensures secure disposal of data and models during transfer or decommissioning processes.

Freedom Online Coalition Joint Statement on Responsible Government Practices for AI Technologies endorses the responsible use and regulation of AI to enhance public service delivery while safeguarding human rights, as reiterated by the Freedom Online Coalition (FOC).

Freedom Online Coalition Joint Statement on Responsible Government Practices for AI Technologies acknowledges the potential risks of AI misuse, including bias, privacy violations, and exacerbation of inequalities, especially for marginalized populations.

Freedom Online Coalition Joint Statement on Responsible Government Practices for AI Technologies urges governments to adhere to international legal obligations, including the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, when employing AI systems.

Freedom Online Coalition Joint Statement on Responsible Government Practices for AI Technologies mandates assessment and management of AI risks in high-risk contexts.

Freedom Online Coalition Joint Statement on Responsible Government Practices for AI Technologies advocates for continuous monitoring and external audits of AI systems to maintain fairness and rights protection.

Freedom Online Coalition Joint Statement on Responsible Government Practices for AI Technologies mandates support for adequate training for personnel involved in AI to comprehend its impact on human rights.

Freedom Online Coalition Joint Statement on Responsible Government Practices for AI Technologies demands transparency, public consultation on AI uses, and mechanisms for public feedback and opting out of AI-enabled decisions.

Freedom Online Coalition Joint Statement on Responsible Government Practices for AI Technologies calls for effective remedies and redress for individuals harmed by AI systems.

Freedom Online Coalition Joint Statement on Responsible Government Practices for AI Technologies incorporates these practices into government procurement to ensure AI trustworthiness and conformity with human rights standards.

Freedom Online Coalition Joint Statement on Responsible Government Practices for AI Technologies defines high-risk AI as those that may impact human rights and safety with likely applications in healthcare, law enforcement and justice, and provision of public benefits.

Massachusetts House Docket 4053 (2025) amends state law to introduce Chapter 93M, mandating consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence (AI) systems.

Massachusetts House Docket 4053 (2025) requires developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to use reasonable care to prevent algorithmic discrimination and disclose foreseeable risks.

Massachusetts House Docket 4053 (2025) defines "high-risk AI systems" as those influencing consequential decisions in areas like education, employment, and healthcare.

Massachusetts House Docket 4053 (2025) mandates developers to provide detailed documentation about AI system data usage, limitations, and discrimination mitigation measures.

Massachusetts House Docket 4053 (2025) obligates deployers to establish risk management policies aligned with recognized standards, and perform annual impact assessments.

Massachusetts House Docket 4053 (2025) demands transparency from deployers by notifying consumers before consequential decisions are made using high-risk AI systems, and offering appeal opportunities for adverse decisions.

Massachusetts House Docket 4053 (2025) empowers the attorney general with exclusive enforcement authority, classifying violations as unfair trade practices.

Massachusetts House Docket 4053 (2025) prohibits private rights of action, leaving enforcement to the state.

Massachusetts House Docket 4053 (2025) allows attorney general to create rules for implementing these requirements, ensuring alignment with national standards.

California Privacy Protection Agency Draft Risk Assessment and Automated Decisionmaking Technology Regulations defines "artificial intelligence" as a machine-based system generating outputs to influence environments, recognizing variations in autonomy and adaptiveness post-deployment.

California Privacy Protection Agency Draft Risk Assessment and Automated Decisionmaking Technology Regulations mandates businesses to conduct risk assessments for using AI and automated decision-making technology when handling consumer data, especially for decisions impacting financial, employment, or educational opportunities.

California Privacy Protection Agency Draft Risk Assessment and Automated Decisionmaking Technology Regulations requires transparency through Pre-use Notices for consumers, detailing the use of AI in decision-making and providing opt-out or appeal options.

California Privacy Protection Agency Draft Risk Assessment and Automated Decisionmaking Technology Regulations specifies exceptions where consumers cannot opt-out, relying on the necessity of the use, with provisions for human review.

California Privacy Protection Agency Draft Risk Assessment and Automated Decisionmaking Technology Regulations demands businesses to ensure AI does not discriminate against protected classes through evaluations and safeguards.

California Privacy Protection Agency Draft Risk Assessment and Automated Decisionmaking Technology Regulations obliges businesses to disclose AI processes upon consumer request and prohibits retaliatory actions against consumers exercising their rights.

California Privacy Protection Agency Draft Risk Assessment and Automated Decisionmaking Technology Regulations mandates comprehensive documentation and regular updates for risk assessments, maintaining consumer privacy as a priority.

Provisions Pertaining to U.S. Investments in Certain National Security Technologies and Products in Countries of Concern implements Executive Order 14105 by requiring U.S. persons to notify the Department of the Treasury about transactions involving national security technologies in "countries of concern," and prohibits certain transactions that pose acute national security threats.

Provisions Pertaining to U.S. Investments in Certain National Security Technologies and Products in Countries of Concern defines AI systems as machine-based systems capable of making predictions, recommendations, or decisions that affect environments, thereby impacting transactions involving AI development and deployment.

Provisions Pertaining to U.S. Investments in Certain National Security Technologies and Products in Countries of Concern specifies which transactions are notifiable or prohibited, including those involving AI systems intended for military, intelligence, or surveillance uses as well as those of a specified computing power.

Provisions Pertaining to U.S. Investments in Certain National Security Technologies and Products in Countries of Concern mandates U.S. persons to file notifications and prohibits knowingly directing others to undertake prohibited transactions.

Provisions Pertaining to U.S. Investments in Certain National Security Technologies and Products in Countries of Concern details civil and criminal penalties for violations, including fines up to $250,000 or imprisonment up to 20 years.

Provisions Pertaining to U.S. Investments in Certain National Security Technologies and Products in Countries of Concern outlines exceptions, including certain public securities transactions and specific national interest exemptions.

Provisions Pertaining to U.S. Investments in Certain National Security Technologies and Products in Countries of Concern permits the Secretary of the Treasury to compel divestment of any prohibited transaction, with the aid of the Attorney General.

Artificial Intelligence Law Proposal (Grand National Assembly of Turkey) ensure the safe, ethical, and fair use of AI technologies to protect personal data and privacy rights.

Artificial Intelligence Law Proposal (Grand National Assembly of Turkey) apply to all stakeholders, including providers, users, importers, and distributors of AI systems.

Artificial Intelligence Law Proposal (Grand National Assembly of Turkey) mandate adherence to principles of safety, transparency, fairness, accountability, and privacy in AI systems.

Artificial Intelligence Law Proposal (Grand National Assembly of Turkey) require risk assessments and registration for high-risk AI systems with supervisory authorities.

Artificial Intelligence Law Proposal (Grand National Assembly of Turkey) obligate AI operators to comply with the Law and allow supervisory authorities to monitor compliance and detect violations.

Artificial Intelligence Law Proposal (Grand National Assembly of Turkey) impose fines up to 35 million Turkish Liras or 7% of annual turnover for violations, with varying penalties based on the nature of the breach.

Artificial Intelligence Law Proposal (Grand National Assembly of Turkey) enforce the Law upon publication, with the President executing its provisions.

California SB 53 establishes a consortium to create CalCompute, a public cloud computing framework promoting safe and ethical AI.

California SB 53 mandates CalCompute to foster research benefiting the public and expanding access to computational resources.

California SB 53 obligates submission of a report by January 1, 2027, detailing CalCompute's framework, including infrastructure analysis, costs, governance, and workforce recommendations.

California SB 53 introduces whistleblower protections for employees disclosing critical AI risks, including practices leading to severe harm, damage, or misinformation.

California SB 53 mandates developers to establish anonymous internal reporting processes and ensures responsive investigation.

California SB 53 authorizes courts to grant attorney’s fees, shift burdens of proof to developers, and issue injunctive relief in whistleblower cases, prioritizing employee protections.

(Trial) Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Reviews (Draft for Feedback) establishes that work units engaged in sensitive areas, including AI, must form ethics committees to conduct thorough ethical reviews of S&T activities.

(Trial) Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Reviews (Draft for Feedback) requires these reviews to ensure AI activities comply with ethics principles, such as fairness and controllability.

(Trial) Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Reviews (Draft for Feedback) stipulates review committees to include diverse experts and provide training on ethics reviews.

(Trial) Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Reviews (Draft for Feedback) mandates reviews of AI systems and algorithms adhere to national data security and ethical norms, ensuring transparency and reliability.

(Trial) Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Reviews (Draft for Feedback) grants committees the authority to approve, revise, or reject AI projects based on ethical evaluations.

(Trial) Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Reviews (Draft for Feedback) introduces simplified and emergency review procedures for low-risk or urgent situations, with detailed conditions.

(Trial) Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Reviews (Draft for Feedback) calls for procedures to handle violations within AI ethics reviews, including potential penalties.

(Trial) Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Reviews (Draft for Feedback) insists on a national ethics management registry for committee activities and checklisted high-risk AI activities.

(Trial) Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Reviews (Draft for Feedback) implies that the Ministry of Science and Technology oversees interpretation and enforcement of these measures, which include significant provisions for governance of AI research and its ethical implications.

Guiding Opinions on Strengthening the Governance of Science and Technology Ethics (Draft for Feedback) establishes the National Science and Technology Ethics Commission to guide and coordinate the governance of S&T ethics, with the Ministry of Science and Technology handling day-to-day affairs.

Guiding Opinions on Strengthening the Governance of Science and Technology Ethics (Draft for Feedback) requires institutions in life sciences, medicine, and AI to create S&T ethics (review) committees.

Guiding Opinions on Strengthening the Governance of Science and Technology Ethics (Draft for Feedback) mandates comprehensive ethics reviews for S&T activities with high ethical risks, ensuring adherence to principles of independence and transparency.

Guiding Opinions on Strengthening the Governance of Science and Technology Ethics (Draft for Feedback) instructs local governments and relevant departments to oversee S&T ethics, including risk assessment and emergency handling in high-ethics-risk fields.

Guiding Opinions on Strengthening the Governance of Science and Technology Ethics (Draft for Feedback) promotes legislative development for S&T ethics, focusing on transforming norms into regulations and ensuring accountability for violations.

Guiding Opinions on Strengthening the Governance of Science and Technology Ethics (Draft for Feedback) encourages S&T personnel to enhance ethical awareness and report violations.

Guiding Opinions on Strengthening the Governance of Science and Technology Ethics (Draft for Feedback) supports educational initiatives in S&T ethics for students and professionals.

Guiding Opinions on Strengthening the Governance of Science and Technology Ethics (Draft for Feedback) urges transparent communication with the public about S&T ethics issues.

Guiding Opinions on Strengthening the Governance of Science and Technology Ethics (Draft for Feedback) outlines punitive measures for S&T ethics violations, including restrictions on government-funded activities and legal consequences for violators.

Boise Regulations 4.30q City Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) requires fact-checking and reviewing AI-generated content, especially for public communications, to ensure accuracy, proper attribution, and absence of bias or harmful material.

Boise Regulations 4.30q City Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) stipulates disclosure of AI usage in significant public communications to build trust and transparency.

Boise Regulations 4.30q City Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) prohibits sharing sensitive or private information in AI prompts to prevent unintended data exposure.

Boise Regulations 4.30q City Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) directs annual reviews and updates of the regulation to align with technological advancements and best practices.

Boise Regulations 4.30q City Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tasks the Information Technology department with overseeing AI initiatives, compliance, and periodic audits for effectiveness and ethical considerations.

Boise Regulations 4.30q City Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) aims to govern AI use responsibly and ethically, enhancing public services and fostering innovation for community benefit.

Oversee Emerging Technology Act requires the head of each covered federal agency engaged in emerging technologies to appoint or designate a Senior Executive Service individual or equivalent as an emerging technology lead.

Oversee Emerging Technology Act mandates that these leads advise agencies on the responsible use of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Oversee Emerging Technology Act obliges these leads to provide expertise on responsible policies and practices, collaborate with interagency bodies, and input on procurement policies.

Oversee Emerging Technology Act instructs the President to inform Congress within 180 days of enactment about the appointed leads and their authorities and responsibilities.

To establish in the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration a program to improve precipitation forecasts, and for other purposes. establishes a program within the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to improve precipitation forecasts.

To establish in the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration a program to improve precipitation forecasts, and for other purposes. requires the use of fully coupled Earth System Models to enhance precipitation prediction.

To establish in the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration a program to improve precipitation forecasts, and for other purposes. mandates the utilization of high performance computing and other technologies, including machine learning and artificial intelligence, to advance precipitation forecasts.

AI Grand Challenges Act of 2024 mandates the creation of a specific grand challenge for AI-enabled cancer breakthroughs.

Singapore National AI Strategy 2.0 sets two primary goals: achieving excellence in AI to maximize value creation and empowering communities to use AI with confidence.

Singapore National AI Strategy 2.0 outlines a focus on three systems: Activity Drivers, People & Communities, and Infrastructure & Environment, supported by 10 enablers.

Singapore National AI Strategy 2.0 plans to establish AI Centers of Excellence, strengthen the AI start-up ecosystem, and drive public sector AI adoption.

Singapore National AI Strategy 2.0 aims to attract global AI talent and boost its AI practitioner pool to support AI demand.

Singapore National AI Strategy 2.0 emphasizes building a trusted AI environment through updated regulatory frameworks, security measures, and international collaboration.

Singapore National AI Strategy 2.0 seeks to enhance data management and privacy technologies for responsible AI development and position Singapore as a global AI governance leader.

Singapore National AI Strategy 2.0 encourages making more public sector data available for AI development that serves the Public Good.

Wisconsin Executive Order #211 appoints additional members from key state departments, educational institutions, and other stakeholders, as determined by the Governor.

Wisconsin Executive Order #211 instructs the Task Force to gather and analyze information to produce an advisory action plan for the Governor.

Wisconsin Executive Order #211 requires the plan to assess generative AI’s impact on Wisconsin’s labor market, predict future impacts, and identify effects on key industries and skillsets.

Wisconsin Executive Order #211 explores initiatives to advance equity and economic opportunity related to AI-driven changes.

Wisconsin Executive Order #211 recommends solutions, including policy changes in workforce development and education, based on identified impacts.

Wisconsin Executive Order #211 attaches the Task Force to the Department of Workforce Development.

Indianapolis City Council Proposal No.362, 2023 establishes a study commission named the "Commission on Artificial Intelligence Development" to review and analyze the City and County's current use of artificial intelligence.

Indianapolis City Council Proposal No.362, 2023 requires the commission to gather insights from AI experts, industry leaders, and community members on future AI applications to improve city services.

Indianapolis City Council Proposal No.362, 2023 mandates the commission to recommend policies for trustworthy and transparent AI usage to the Mayor and City-County Council.

Indianapolis City Council Proposal No.362, 2023 directs the commission to suggest modifications or new ordinances for AI usage.

Indianapolis City Council Proposal No.362, 2023 composes the commission of nine members, including Councillors, IT directors, and citizen members, all residents of Marion County.

Indianapolis City Council Proposal No.362, 2023 requires city departments to share information and cooperate with the commission.

Indianapolis City Council Proposal No.362, 2023 obligates the commission to present a final report by the July 2024 meeting, available on the City’s website.

Indianapolis City Council Proposal No.362, 2023 initiates operations as soon as practical and outlines a meeting and research timeline.

Indianapolis City Council Proposal No.362, 2023 permits public comment under commission-devised rules.

New York A7838 mandates the Department of Labor to begin a study on the long-term impact of artificial intelligence on the state workforce within six months.

New York A7838 requires consultation with the Department of Civil Service and the Office of Information Technology Services.

New York A7838 calls for examination of job performance, productivity, training, education requirements, privacy, and security.

New York A7838 obligates the Department of Labor to issue an interim report every five years and a final report by January 1, 2035, with recommendations for legislative action.

New York A7838 prohibits all state departments and governmental entities from using AI to displace any natural person from their employment until the final report and recommendations are received.

New York A7838 ensures immediate effect upon enactment.

Rhode Island SB 146 prohibits the use of facial recognition technology and biometric recognition programs in video-lottery terminals and online betting applications.

Rhode Island SB 146 prohibits the use of algorithmic programs that modify gaming based on a consumer's betting history to increase wagers.

Rhode Island SB 146 prohibits the use of artificial intelligence or automated decision systems to promote increased play through intermittent reinforcement based on cognitive-behavioral algorithms and prior gaming data.

Rhode Island SB 146 applies these prohibitions to sports betting applications and vendors of gambling products licensed by Rhode Island.

Rhode Island SB 146 excludes standardized rewards programs from these prohibitions.

Rhode Island SB 146 takes effect upon passage.

Pennsylvania HR 170 directs the Joint State Government Commission to establish an advisory committee to study artificial intelligence's impact in Pennsylvania.

Pennsylvania HR 170 mandates an assessment of AI development and use, including benefits, risks, and fiscal impacts on the state.

Pennsylvania HR 170 proposes legislation for state AI regulation and a definition for AI.

Pennsylvania HR 170 recommends evaluating AI's effects on students' academic performance and addressing AI-driven disinformation.

Pennsylvania HR 170 urges studying potential job displacement due to AI automation and assessing implications for organized labor.

Pennsylvania HR 170 calls for a proposal on ethical and responsible AI development in Pennsylvania.

Pennsylvania HR 170 advises considering the creation of a permanent commission for AI study.

Pennsylvania HR 170 allows the Joint State Government Commission to request information from state agencies for the study.

Pennsylvania HR 170 requires a report with findings and recommendations within 18 months to various governmental leaders and committees.

Protecting Kids on Social Media Act requires social media platforms to verify the age of users beyond simple attestations, using current age verification technologies.

Protecting Kids on Social Media Act prohibits social media platforms from allowing individuals under 13 from accessing their services.

Protecting Kids on Social Media Act mandates parental or guardian consent for users under 18, requiring platforms to take reasonable steps to verify this consent.

Protecting Kids on Social Media Act prohibits the use of algorithmic recommendation systems on individuals under 18, except for contextual suggestions or advertising.

Protecting Kids on Social Media Act establishes a Pilot Program for secure digital identification credentials to facilitate age and parental consent verification, overseen by the Secretary of Commerce.

Protecting Kids on Social Media Act empowers the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and state attorneys general to enforce compliance, with civil penalties for violations.

Protecting Kids on Social Media Act grants extraterritorial jurisdiction for violations involving individuals in the United States.

Transparent Automated Governance Act instructs agencies to design systems providing plain language notifications and establish appeals processes for decisions made using AI-augmented processes.

Transparent Automated Governance Act obligates agencies to track the accuracy and reliability of AI systems, and share data with relevant authorities; encourages consultation with governmental and private sectors for guidance development.

Transparent Automated Governance Act requires the Comptroller General to report on agency compliance, with reports submitted biennially.

Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act requires the establishment of a memorandum of understanding to facilitate this collaboration through a competitive, merit-reviewed process.

Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act authorizes the Secretary of Energy and NOAA Administrator to conduct research on modeling, simulation, machine learning, data assimilation, and predictive analysis techniques.

Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act mandates the promotion of collaboration and data sharing among federal agencies, National Laboratories, educational institutions, and nonprofits, while ensuring compliance with national security policies.

Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act instructs the submission of a report within two years detailing interagency coordination, research achievements, and future opportunities.

Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act initiates a high-performance computing project to enhance weather prediction models, requiring a comparative analysis with current forecasts.

Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act sunsets the authority for this initiative five years post-enactment.

Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act ensures compliance with research security provisions under the CHIPS Act of 2022.

City of San Jose Generative AI Guidelines establishes guidelines for using Generative AI within the City of San José, emphasizing privacy, accuracy, transparency, equity, accountability, and beneficial use.

City of San Jose Generative AI Guidelines requires users to cite AI where substantial content is AI-generated and to verify AI output against trustworthy sources.

City of San Jose Generative AI Guidelines prohibits submission of personal or confidential information into Generative AI platforms and mandates the creation of separate accounts for City-related work using Generative AI.

City of San Jose Generative AI Guidelines subjects AI usage to public records laws, recommending users to opt out of data collection where possible and verify AI-generated content for copyright compliance.

City of San Jose Generative AI Guidelines offers collaborative working groups to enhance AI governance and provides risk assessment criteria for Generative AI use cases.

City of San Jose Generative AI Guidelines encourages active participation in AI workgroups and emphasizes the importance of adapting guidelines as technology and laws evolve.

Los Angeles AI Roadmap 2024, Best Practices and Roadmap establishes two distinct user segments for AI tools: City Employees and IT Professionals, requiring tailored training for each group.

Los Angeles AI Roadmap 2024, Best Practices and Roadmap instructs non-technical department leadership to set clear goals before AI tool deployment.

Los Angeles AI Roadmap 2024, Best Practices and Roadmap encourages piloting AI tools to understand their strengths and weaknesses before widespread use.

Los Angeles AI Roadmap 2024, Best Practices and Roadmap anticipates most AI tools will be accessed through existing software platforms.

Los Angeles AI Roadmap 2024, Best Practices and Roadmap emphasizes the need for adaptable AI tools that align with evolving data and requirements.

Los Angeles AI Roadmap 2024, Best Practices and Roadmap advises staying current on AI tools and frameworks for maximized effectiveness.

Los Angeles AI Roadmap 2024, Best Practices and Roadmap requires comprehensive AI training for both users and developers, highlighting security and ethical considerations.

Los Angeles AI Roadmap 2024, Best Practices and Roadmap insists on cybersecurity and data privacy for AI implementation.

Los Angeles AI Roadmap 2024, Best Practices and Roadmap highlights AI as a long-term investment needing high-quality data and data transparency.

Los Angeles AI Roadmap 2024, Best Practices and Roadmap asserts City data ownership and the need for ethical, transparent, and human-centered AI tools.

Los Angeles AI Roadmap 2024, Best Practices and Roadmap outlines a roadmap for training, deploying AI tools, and developing ethics guidelines for the City.

City of Boston Interim Guidelines for Using Generative AI instructs the City agencies and departments of Boston, excluding Boston Public Schools, to use generative AI responsibly, with guidelines focusing on transparency, accountability, and inclusiveness.

City of Boston Interim Guidelines for Using Generative AI requires fact-checking and reviewing AI-generated content for public communication to avoid inaccuracies and biases.

City of Boston Interim Guidelines for Using Generative AI emphasizes disclosing AI usage, including model type and version, to promote trust and transparency.

City of Boston Interim Guidelines for Using Generative AI prohibits sharing of sensitive or private information in AI prompts to protect residents' data privacy.

City of Boston Interim Guidelines for Using Generative AI encourages responsible experimentation with generative AI to support efficient, equitable city services while managing risks.

City of Boston Interim Guidelines for Using Generative AI directs the Department of Innovation and Technology to facilitate learning events and workshops on generative AI.

City of Boston Interim Guidelines for Using Generative AI advises consultation with relevant city offices and community organizations before publicizing AI-created content to ensure accessibility, accuracy, and sensitivity.

City of Boston Interim Guidelines for Using Generative AI promotes AI use in drafting documents, summarizing text, coding, and creating multimedia, while highlighting the importance of human oversight and editing.

City of Boston Interim Guidelines for Using Generative AI encourages engaging stakeholders for potential impacts on arts and society.

Miami Dade County Artificial Intelligence Report: Policies, Principles & Guidelines guides Miami-Dade County employees in the responsible and ethical use of AI, focusing on transparency, data security, and privacy.

Miami Dade County Artificial Intelligence Report: Policies, Principles & Guidelines requires adherence to public records laws and ethical guidelines.

Miami Dade County Artificial Intelligence Report: Policies, Principles & Guidelines instructs the Human Resources and Information Technology Departments to provide AI training, emphasizing ethical use, bias recognition, and data management.

Miami Dade County Artificial Intelligence Report: Policies, Principles & Guidelines mandates risk assessments prior to AI implementation.

Miami Dade County Artificial Intelligence Report: Policies, Principles & Guidelines tasks the Information Technology Department with overseeing AI procurement, deployment, and system security.

Miami Dade County Artificial Intelligence Report: Policies, Principles & Guidelines establishes protocols for data governance, encryption, and privacy.

Miami Dade County Artificial Intelligence Report: Policies, Principles & Guidelines defines roles for directors, supervisors, and employees in AI project management, ethical leadership, and compliance.

Miami Dade County Artificial Intelligence Report: Policies, Principles & Guidelines implements regular audits, assessments, and vendor evaluations to maintain AI system integrity.

Miami Dade County Artificial Intelligence Report: Policies, Principles & Guidelines encourages community engagement and stakeholder discussions on AI deployment.

Miami Dade County Artificial Intelligence Report: Policies, Principles & Guidelines commits to continuous improvement with annual assessments and updates by the IT Department, involving multidisciplinary teams and beta testing initiatives.

Miami Dade County Artificial Intelligence Report: Policies, Principles & Guidelines provides resources through the IT Department’s website.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2024, Section 2 amends the National Quantum Initiative Act to mandate the Secretary of Energy to conduct a program focusing on quantum information science research, development, and commercialization.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2024, Section 2 operates National Quantum Information Science Research Centers to facilitate breakthroughs in quantum technologies.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2024, Section 2 requires collaboration with industry, National Laboratories, and educational institutions for technology development.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2024, Section 2 engages with the quantum technology industry to promote the commercialization of applications relevant to the Department of Energy's activities.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2024, Section 2 submits a 10-year strategic plan to integrate quantum and AI with high-performance computing systems.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2024, Section 2 establishes an early-stage quantum high-performance computing research program.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2024, Section 2 conducts a study on the quantum supply chain to identify growth obstacles and recommends strategies to bolster domestic manufacturing and workforce development.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2024, Section 2 launches a university-led traineeship program to develop the quantum workforce.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2024, Section 2 coordinates activities with other federal entities to prevent duplication.

Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2024, Section 2 restricts funding from foreign countries of concern and entities deemed harmful to U.S. national security.

Open Translation Center Act of 2024 establishes the Open Translation Center (OTC) to translate and analyze foreign language materials from designated countries for public dissemination, enhancing understanding of foreign governments, economies, and cultures.

Open Translation Center Act of 2024 administers OTC either as a separate entity or a nonprofit and requires a governing board of five appointed members with relevant expertise, independent of the U.S. Government.

Open Translation Center Act of 2024 tasks OTC with translating documents into English, providing analyses, and making materials publicly available while respecting copyright laws.

Open Translation Center Act of 2024 requires cooperation with federal agencies and stakeholders, and authorizes consultation with foreign governments after certification by the Secretary of State.

Open Translation Center Act of 2024 designates the Secretary of State as the primary sponsor, with potential sponsorship from other federal agencies such as the CIA.

Open Translation Center Act of 2024 allocates funding of $85 million for fiscal year 2024 and $80 million for subsequent years through 2028 for OTC operations.

City of Seattle Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy regulates City departments' acquisition and use of generative AI, requiring adherence to principles of innovation, transparency, and bias reduction.

City of Seattle Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy requires Seattle IT to evaluate generative AI acquisition requests and has authority to approve, deny, or revoke use based on risk assessments.

City of Seattle Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy mandates human review of AI-generated outputs before official use with documentation of review processes.

City of Seattle Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy requires attribution for AI-generated content, specifying inclusion of system names and review assertions.

City of Seattle Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy obliges the use of Racial Equity Toolkit prior to using generative AI tools to combat bias and discrimination.

City of Seattle Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy prohibits submission of confidential City data to AI systems without adequate enterprise controls and data protection.

City of Seattle Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy classifies AI-generated records as public and mandates retention and disclosure compliance.

City of Seattle Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy assigns the Chief Technology Officer responsibility for policy enforcement, with potential penalties for non-compliance.

City of Seattle Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy specifies the Director of DPAC and Chief Privacy Officer maintain risk criteria and exception processes.

City of Tempe Ethical Artificial Intelligence Policy establishes the City of Tempe's commitment to ethical AI use, emphasizing transparency, fairness, accountability, and protection of rights.

City of Tempe Ethical Artificial Intelligence Policy applies this policy to all AI technologies in city operations, including predictive analytics, machine learning, and automated decision-making.

City of Tempe Ethical Artificial Intelligence Policy requires defined objectives, data privacy, and human-AI collaboration, while ensuring human control.

City of Tempe Ethical Artificial Intelligence Policy tasks departments with setting AI objectives, conducting reviews, and collaborating with IT for oversight.

City of Tempe Ethical Artificial Intelligence Policy instructs the Technology and Innovation Steering Committee to monitor AI compliance, develop reporting mechanisms, and define non-compliance consequences.

City of Tempe Ethical Artificial Intelligence Policy mandates Information Technology to develop a review process, conduct training, and support compliance.

City of Tempe Ethical Artificial Intelligence Policy commits to ongoing monitoring, stakeholder engagement, and ethical improvement of AI practices.

City of Tempe Ethical Artificial Intelligence Policy promotes public engagement and awareness campaigns about AI activities.

City of Tempe Ethical Artificial Intelligence Policy requires compliance with applicable laws and regulations and supports ethical AI frameworks development.

City of Tempe Ethical Artificial Intelligence Policy commits to periodic policy reviews to address emerging AI challenges and advancements.

County of Santa Cruz Artificial Intelligence Appropriate Use Policy establishes the County of Santa Cruz's principles for responsible use of generative AI by employees, contractors, and third parties, ensuring alignment with ethical and legal standards.

County of Santa Cruz Artificial Intelligence Appropriate Use Policy requires compliance with data privacy laws, such as HIPAA and CCPA, and informs the public of AI tool interactions, offering alternatives.

County of Santa Cruz Artificial Intelligence Appropriate Use Policy prohibits the use of AI for unauthorized access, handling of personally identifiable information, unlawful activities, hiring decisions, and entering sensitive data into AI systems.

County of Santa Cruz Artificial Intelligence Appropriate Use Policy permits only approved AI tools like Google Bard, OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, and Scribe.

County of Santa Cruz Artificial Intelligence Appropriate Use Policy requires employees to exercise judgment, report concerns, and use County email for AI tool accounts.

County of Santa Cruz Artificial Intelligence Appropriate Use Policy encourages comprehension of AI policies and participation in workgroups while emphasizing responsible, ethical, and transparent AI usage, avoiding bias, and not relying on AI for significant decision-making.

Kendall County Generative AI Chatbot Usage Policy prohibits using county email addresses and submitting proprietary or confidential data into these platforms.

Kendall County Generative AI Chatbot Usage Policy requires employees to consult with Executives regarding chatbot use, who may approve, deny, or modify usage parameters.

Kendall County Generative AI Chatbot Usage Policy mandates proper citation and accuracy checks for AI-generated content.

Kendall County Generative AI Chatbot Usage Policy enforces disciplinary actions, including termination, for policy violations or inappropriate use, ensuring ethical compliance with conduct and antidiscrimination policies.

Kendall County Generative AI Chatbot Usage Policy instructs employees to undergo training on proper chatbot use.

Kendall County Generative AI Chatbot Usage Policy applies Technology and Record Retention Policies when using AI with County equipment.

Kendall County Generative AI Chatbot Usage Policy addresses training queries with Human Resources or the Information, Communication and Technology Department Director.

The City of Tulsa Municipal Court Rules 2024 require any attorney, pro se defendant, victim, or other party using generative AI in drafting documents for the Municipal Criminal Court to disclose the use of such AI.

The City of Tulsa Municipal Court Rules 2024 specify the name of the generative AI tool used in the filing.

The City of Tulsa Municipal Court Rules 2024 include ChatGPT, Bing AI, and Google Bard under the definition of generative AI.

The City of Tulsa Municipal Court Rules 2024 maintain the applicability of 12 O.S. §2011 to all filings, ensuring compliance is certified by the person signing the document.

City of St. Louis Information Technology Policy #2023-001 Guidance on Generative AI instructs City employees to adhere to the Information Technology Acceptable Use Policy when using generative AI tools.

City of St. Louis Information Technology Policy #2023-001 Guidance on Generative AI requires ITSA to vet the purchase of AI-related technology and software.

City of St. Louis Information Technology Policy #2023-001 Guidance on Generative AI prohibits the use of City passwords for logging onto AI platforms and advises caution due to evolving malware threats.

City of St. Louis Information Technology Policy #2023-001 Guidance on Generative AI forbids the upload of sensitive or confidential information when using AI systems.

City of St. Louis Information Technology Policy #2023-001 Guidance on Generative AI advises a review and validation of AI-generated content due to potential bias or inaccuracies.

City of St. Louis Information Technology Policy #2023-001 Guidance on Generative AI cautions that AI-generated content might be copyright-protected and requires proper attribution.

City of St. Louis Information Technology Policy #2023-001 Guidance on Generative AI warns that content generated by AI may be subject to disclosure under Sunshine Law.

City of St. Louis Information Technology Policy #2023-001 Guidance on Generative AI indicates that ITSA and the Mayor’s Office will continue to evaluate the use of AI and develop policies accordingly.

Artificial Intelligence (Regulation) Act 2024 establishes the AI Authority to ensure regulators take accountability for AI, align regulatory approaches, review legislation, monitor regulatory frameworks, assess risks, support testbeds, and promote international interoperability.

Artificial Intelligence (Regulation) Act 2024 mandates the AI Authority to adhere to principles ensuring AI safety, transparency, fairness, accountability, compliance with laws, and inclusivity.

Artificial Intelligence (Regulation) Act 2024 requires the creation of regulatory sandboxes for testing AI innovations with consumer protections.

Artificial Intelligence (Regulation) Act 2024 obligates businesses using AI to appoint AI responsible officers to ensure ethical use and unbiased data.

Artificial Intelligence (Regulation) Act 2024 imposes transparency and IP obligations, requiring disclosing records of data used in AI training and independent audits.

Artificial Intelligence (Regulation) Act 2024 mandates the implementation of public engagement programs on AI opportunities and risks.

Candidate Voice Fraud Prohibition Act prohibits the distribution of political communications containing materially deceptive AI-generated audio that impersonates a candidate’s voice, with actual malice, intended to harm the candidate’s reputation or deceive voters.

Candidate Voice Fraud Prohibition Act applies to communications distributed within 90 days of a general election or 60 days of a primary, special, or runoff election.

Candidate Voice Fraud Prohibition Act exempts certain entities from liability such as radio or television stations that air deceptive AI-generated content as part of news coverage or communications that clearly constitute satire.

Candidate Voice Fraud Prohibition Act defines "materially deceptive audio" as AI-generated impersonation of a candidate’s voice without approval and lacking a clear disclaimer.

Candidate Voice Fraud Prohibition Act imposes criminal penalties of fines or up to 2 years imprisonment for individuals who knowingly and willfully violate the prohibition.

Candidate Voice Fraud Prohibition Act requires the Federal Election Commission (FEC) to issue regulations to clarify disclaimer requirements and mandates the submission of annual compliance reports to Congress.

Integrating New Technologies to Empower Law Enforcement at Our Borders Act requires the Department of Homeland Security to develop a comprehensive plan within 180 days to identify, deploy, and integrate emerging and advanced technologies to enhance situational awareness along the northern and southern borders of the United States.

Integrating New Technologies to Empower Law Enforcement at Our Borders Act mandates the inclusion of artificial intelligence, machine learning, automation, fiber-optic sensing, nanotechnology, optical and cognitive radar, modeling and simulation technology, hyperspectral and LIDAR sensors, and other similar technologies.

Integrating New Technologies to Empower Law Enforcement at Our Borders Act includes an assessment of current technology utilization by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and how capability gaps can be addressed through technology integration.

Integrating New Technologies to Empower Law Enforcement at Our Borders Act requires cost estimates for technology acquisition and maintenance, metrics for measuring technology impact, and an assessment of multi-domain awareness improvements.

Integrating New Technologies to Empower Law Enforcement at Our Borders Act mandates an analysis of other Federal technologies, procurement authorities, and the transition of new technology systems.

Integrating New Technologies to Empower Law Enforcement at Our Borders Act requires coordination with the Department of Homeland Security's Science and Technology Directorate for research, development, and incentivizing private sector innovation.
