Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title VIII "Prohibition and Notification on Investments Relating to Covered National Security Transactions") prohibits U.S. persons from engaging in investments involving covered national security transactions in prohibited technologies, with exemptions permissible by the Secretary for activities deemed in the national interest.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title VIII "Prohibition and Notification on Investments Relating to Covered National Security Transactions") allows the Secretary to issue regulations that require notifications for such transactions.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title VIII "Prohibition and Notification on Investments Relating to Covered National Security Transactions") introduces penalties for violations, including civil penalties and potential divestment requirements, with the burden of proof resting on the Secretary in enforcement actions.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title VIII "Prohibition and Notification on Investments Relating to Covered National Security Transactions") establishes processes for self-disclosure of violations and requests for non-binding feedback regarding transactions.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title VIII "Prohibition and Notification on Investments Relating to Covered National Security Transactions") mandates annual reports to Congress detailing enforcement actions and technology assessments.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title VIII "Prohibition and Notification on Investments Relating to Covered National Security Transactions") provides for confidentiality of transaction information, but outlines exceptions for disclosure relevant to U.S. national security interests.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title VIII "Prohibition and Notification on Investments Relating to Covered National Security Transactions") encourages international cooperation to prevent prohibited technology development or acquisition by countries of concern, such as China.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title VIII "Prohibition and Notification on Investments Relating to Covered National Security Transactions") defines key terms, including "prohibited technology" and "country of concern."

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title V "Promoting Resilient Supply Chains") expands the responsibilities of the Assistant Secretary of Commerce to include promoting the resilience of supply chains related to critical and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title V "Promoting Resilient Supply Chains") mandates the creation of the Supply Chain Resilience Working Group composed of relevant federal agencies to assess and model supply chain stability, including those involving AI technologies.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title V "Promoting Resilient Supply Chains") requires the group to identify vulnerabilities and prepare for potential supply chain shocks that might impact AI and other critical technologies.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title V "Promoting Resilient Supply Chains") encourages domestic production and manufacturing, specifically focusing on AI and technological advancements.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title V "Promoting Resilient Supply Chains") obligates periodic reports and assessments to Congress regarding the resilience and capacity of AI-related supply chains and industry preparedness for shocks.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title V "Promoting Resilient Supply Chains") prohibits reliance on critical goods from countries identified as risks to national security, advocating for sourcing from allies.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title V "Promoting Resilient Supply Chains") sets a 10-year expiration for these provisions.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title V "Promoting Resilient Supply Chains") protects confidential data shared voluntarily under this title from disclosure, ensuring privacy concerns in relation to AI-related supply chain information.

Diabetes Act ensures care continuity for individuals using diabetes technology when enrolling in Medicare Part B by January 2026.

Diabetes Act requires development of a process to consider diabetes technologies not currently covered under Medicare Part B for potential inclusion.

Diabetes Act mandates creation of new coding for insulin pump training and education by 2026, to enhance billing and reimbursement transparency.

Diabetes Act obligates the issuance of a national coverage determination for insulin pumps within 180 days from enactment.

Diabetes Act instructs the Comptroller General to report within a year on barriers hindering access to diabetes technologies and services in Federal healthcare programs, reviewing legal and policy issues affecting access.

Executive order No. 78 (St. Louis) establishes transparency and accountability requirements for the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department’s (SLMPD) use of surveillance technology, including artificial intelligence (AI).

Executive order No. 78 (St. Louis) prohibits using surveillance technology to monitor political, religious, or social groups unless tied to criminal activity or public safety threats.

Executive order No. 78 (St. Louis) mandates public, written policies for SLMPD’s use of surveillance technology and AI.

Executive order No. 78 (St. Louis) requires annual transparency reports detailing the SLMPD’s surveillance technology usage, capabilities, impacts, and related complaints.

Executive order No. 78 (St. Louis) obliges vendors to protect data privacy, prohibiting unauthorized access or sale of collected data.

Executive order No. 78 (St. Louis) ensures compliance with federal and state laws regarding data storage, retention, and access.

Executive order No. 78 (St. Louis) directs cooperation with the City’s Information Technology Services for technology acquisitions.

Executive order No. 78 (St. Louis) requires adherence to 28 C.F.R. Part 23 for participation in criminal intelligence systems.

Executive order No. 78 (St. Louis) mandates policies for data sharing, following "need to know" and "right to know" standards for law enforcement agencies.

Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security to submit a plan for deploying innovative border technologies within 180 days.

Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act requires the plan to assess artificial intelligence’s impact on privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties, and include mitigation measures.

Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act directs the establishment of CBP Innovation Teams to evaluate and integrate advanced technologies, ensuring compliance with DHS policies on AI use.

Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act focuses on transitioning technologies to CBP programs, addressing potential negative outcomes and capability gaps.

Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act instructs annual reporting on Innovation Teams’ activities, technologies piloted, and their success rates.

Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act requires coordination with DHS's AI policies to ensure responsible AI use.

Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act demands cost-benefit analysis before large-scale technology deployment, ensuring security effectiveness and governmental cost-efficiency.

Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act emphasizes collaboration with the private sector, other government entities, and stakeholders for optimizing advanced technology deployment.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Section 217 "Report on Wearable Medical Devices") requires submission of a report to Congress on the capabilities and limitations of these devices in supporting clinical decision-making.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Section 217 "Report on Wearable Medical Devices") includes a description of the potential for wearable devices to accurately prescribe treatments.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Section 217 "Report on Wearable Medical Devices") examines the benefits and challenges of using artificial intelligence to augment these capabilities.

Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Section 217 "Report on Wearable Medical Devices") suggests policy options to enhance the benefits and address the challenges of developing or using wearable medical devices.

Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework Version 1.0 establishes protocols within the Frontier Safety Framework to address severe risks from future foundation models' capabilities.

Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework Version 1.0 defines "Critical Capability Levels" (CCLs) to identify when AI models pose heightened risks, focusing initially on Autonomy, Biosecurity, Cybersecurity, and Machine Learning R&D.

Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework Version 1.0 implements periodic evaluations to detect when models approach CCLs and articulates developing mitigation plans.

Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework Version 1.0 proposes security mitigations to prevent model weight exfiltration and deployment mitigations to control access and expression of critical capabilities.

Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework Version 1.0 outlines graded mitigation and security protocols based on AI capabilities and risks from potential misuse.

Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework Version 1.0 plans to implement the framework by early 2025 and expects it to evolve with emerging risks and insights.

Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework Version 1.0 commits to periodically reviewing and updating the framework as understanding of AI risks and benefits improves.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 1554 ("Roadmap and implementation plan for cyber adoption of artificial intelligence") requires the Commander of the United States Cyber Command and the Chief Information Officer of the Department of Defense to develop a five-year implementation plan for rapidly adopting artificial intelligence systems to support the Department of Defense.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 1554 ("Roadmap and implementation plan for cyber adoption of artificial intelligence") the plan shall:

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 1554 ("Roadmap and implementation plan for cyber adoption of artificial intelligence") (a) Identify and prioritize AI systems and data that currently affect, or may benefit in the future, the Department's cybersecurity and cyber operations.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 1554 ("Roadmap and implementation plan for cyber adoption of artificial intelligence") (b) Lay out a plan to acquire AI systems and data identified in part (a).

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 1554 ("Roadmap and implementation plan for cyber adoption of artificial intelligence") (c) Identify relevant skill deficiencies.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 1554 ("Roadmap and implementation plan for cyber adoption of artificial intelligence") (d) Identify opportunities to solicit AI system operator feedback.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 1554 ("Roadmap and implementation plan for cyber adoption of artificial intelligence") (e) Identify and address long term technology gaps for the Department's cyber war fighting mission.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 1554 ("Roadmap and implementation plan for cyber adoption of artificial intelligence") (f) Evaluate the risks posed by adversary AI-based attacks.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 1554 ("Roadmap and implementation plan for cyber adoption of artificial intelligence") (g) Furnish a timeline with target milestones, investments, and required expenditures.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 1554 ("Roadmap and implementation plan for cyber adoption of artificial intelligence") (h) Incorporate metrics to evaluate AI adoption.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 1554 ("Roadmap and implementation plan for cyber adoption of artificial intelligence") (i) Identify further funding, authorities, and policies that may be necessary.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 1554 ("Roadmap and implementation plan for cyber adoption of artificial intelligence") (j) Define a maturity model describing desired cyber capabilities independent of specific technology solutions.

Energy Act of 2020, Title VI, Section 6006 ("Development of National Smart Manufacturing Plan") requires that the plan be submitted within 3 years and revised every two years after initial submission.

Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence requires federal government to develop and apply standards to ensure the safety and security of AI systems and minimize their risks, including biological risks, cybersecurity risks, and deceptive content risks.

Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence orders the development of a National Security Memorandum that directs further actions on AI and security.

Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence directs federal government to support privacy-preserving research and technologies and develop guidance on the collection and usage of commercially available information by federal agencies.

Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence instructs federal government to prevent algorithmic discrimination by developing guidance and best practices in order to ensure fairness.

Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence calls for federal government to support the safe, responsible deployment of AI in healthcare, transportation, education, and communications networks.

Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence requires a report on AI's potential labor-market impacts and the identification of options for strengthening federal support for workers facing labor disruptions

Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence urges federal government to facilitate the immigration of AI talent to the U.S., catalyze AI research and innovation through a pilot of the National AI Research Resource, and promote competition in the AI ecosystem by providing resources to small businesses.

Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence directs federal government to maintain U.S. leadership in global AI efforts by expanding multilateral engagements, implementing international standards, and developing guidelines to secure critical infrastructure.

Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence calls for the advancement of federal government use of AI through the issuance of guidance for agency use of AI, support for agency acquisition of AI products/services, and authorization of rapid hiring of AI professionals.

An Act Concerning Artificial Intelligence, Automated Decision-Making and Personal Data Privacy establishes a working group comprising industry representatives and academics to engage stakeholders and experts and make recommendations on the state government's use of AI; this includes recommendations on the adoption of a Connecticut artificial intelligence bill of rights based on the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy's 'Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights'

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Section 247 ("Pilot program on the use of electronic portfolios to evaluate certain applicants for technical positions") defines the term "technical position" as a Department of Defense position that (1) requires expertise in artificial intelligence, data science, or software development and (2) is eligible for direct hire authority under section 9905 of title 5, United States Code, or section 2358a of title 10, United States Code.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Section 247 ("Pilot program on the use of electronic portfolios to evaluate certain applicants for technical positions") instructs the human resources manager of each Department of Defense participating organization to identify a subset of technical positions for which electronic portfolios should be evaluated during the hiring process.

(Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Section 247 ("Pilot program on the use of electronic portfolios to evaluate certain applicants for technical positions") requires the Human Resources manager to evaluate applicants for such positions by reviewing their best electronic portfolios, as chosen by the applicant.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Section 247 ("Pilot program on the use of electronic portfolios to evaluate certain applicants for technical positions") directs the Secretary of Defense to submit a report to the congressional defense committee on the results of the program that describes how electronic portfolios affected the timeliness of technical position hiring, the level of satisfaction with new hires based on electronic portfolio evaluations, and recommends expanding the use of electronic portfolios in the hiring process or making it permanent.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XCII, Section 9203 ("Spectrum information technology modernization efforts") use updated algorithms, data, AI tools, and algorithms to modernize infrastructure. Ways to improve infrastructure include efficiency, validation, accuracy, modeling, and monitoring. The directive aims to enhance covered agencies' capacity to meet mission requirements in congested Federal spectrum environments through the implementation of automated adjustments, the creation of a time-based mechanism for collaborative spectrum sharing among agencies, and fostering collaboration to ensure interoperability.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XCII, Section 9203 ("Spectrum information technology modernization efforts") within 240 days of the enactment of this Act, the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information is required to submit to Congress a report outlining a plan for the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) to modernize and automate its infrastructure for managing the use of Federal spectrum by covered agencies, with the goal of improving efficiency in spectrum management in ways such as a timeline for implementation, plans for security enhancement, data model improvement, and workflow automation.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XCII, Section 9203 ("Spectrum information technology modernization efforts") within one year of the enactment of this Act, the head of each covered agency is required to submit a report to the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information and the Policy and Plans Steering Group outlining a plan to modernize the agency's infrastructure. Each submitted report must include an assessment of their current capabilities, a timeline for completion, management capabilities, agency requirements or restrictions, existing infrastructure, and a plan for safe integration of government data.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XCII, Section 9203 ("Spectrum information technology modernization efforts") the Comptroller General of the United States is mandated to conduct a review of covered agencies' infrastructure within 180 days of the Act's enactment and subsequently oversee the implementation of modernization plans submitted by the Assistant Secretary and covered agencies, providing regular reports and briefings to relevant congressional committees until December 31, 2030. The term "covered agency" includes any Federal entity, as determined by the Assistant Secretary, encompassing the Department of Defense, and "infrastructure" is defined as information technology systems and related tools and databases.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Subtitle C ("Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology") supports the incorporation of standards for artificial intelligence into the strategies and doctrine of the Department.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Subtitle C ("Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology") stipulates the roles of the Director of the joint Artificial Intelligence center.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Subtitle C ("Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology") encourages the systematic evaluation of AI systems.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Subtitle C ("Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology") instructs the Secretary of Defense to establish a board of advisors for the Joint Artificial Intelligence Center with responsibilities like providing strategic advice and expertise to the Secretary and the Director on matters relating to the development and use of artificial intelligence.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Subtitle C ("Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology") instructs the Secretary of Defense to identify a set of no fewer than five use cases of the application of existing artificial intelligence enabled systems to support improved management of enterprise acquisition, personnel, audit, or financial management functions.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Subtitle C ("Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology") instructs the Secretary of Defense to conduct an assessment to determine how the Department can most effectively implement ethically and responsibly developed artificial intelligence.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Subtitle C ("Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology") requires the secretary to pilot technology development and prototyping activities that leverage commercially available technologies and systems to demonstrate new artificial intelligence enabled capabilities to support the use cases.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Subtitle C ("Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology") permits the secretary of Defense to establish a steering committee on emerging technology and national security threats, which committee shall develop a strategy for the organizational change, capability development, and technology investments in emerging technologies needed to maintain the technological superiority of the United States military.

(Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title I, Section 152 ("Transfer of responsibilities and functions relating to electromagnetic spectrum operations") instructs the Secretary of Defense to transfer all the responsibilities of the Commander of the US Strategic Command that are germane to electromagnetic spectrum operations (EMSO).

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title I, Section 152 ("Transfer of responsibilities and functions relating to electromagnetic spectrum operations") instructs the Secretary to develop a transfer plan with consideration of all appropriate entities, while considering whether the receiving electromagnetic spectrum operations organization should have a unitary structure or hybrid structure.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title I, Section 152 ("Transfer of responsibilities and functions relating to electromagnetic spectrum operations") requires the Secretary to develop the transfer plan while considering the resources required by the receiving electromagnetic spectrum operations organization to fulfill the responsibilities and functions as well as the results of the evaluations carried out.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title I, Section 152 ("Transfer of responsibilities and functions relating to electromagnetic spectrum operations") requires an evaluation and assessment of the need for automated and machine learning- or artificial intelligence-assisted electronic warfare capabilities.

(Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XCIV, Section 9414 ("Study on Chinese policies and influence in the development of international standards for emerging technologies") instructs the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to work with an entity with relevant expertise to conduct a study on PRC policies and influence in the development of emerging technology international standards, and make recommendations on how the U.S. can mitigate PRC influence and bolster U.S. participation in international standards-setting bodies.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XCIV, Section 9414 ("Study on Chinese policies and influence in the development of international standards for emerging technologies") identifies potential areas of study, including examining previous PRC practices in international standards setting organizations to predict future international standardization engagement in critical technologies like artificial intelligence and quantum information science.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XCIV, Section 9414 ("Study on Chinese policies and influence in the development of international standards for emerging technologies") requires the entity conducting the study to submit a report on its findings to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, on Foreign Affairs, on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, and on Foreign Relations.

(Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Section 513 ("Grants to support STEM education in the Junior Reserve Officers’ Training Corps") instructs the Secretary and Secretary of Education to create and support grants to fund STEM education programs for students specifically in the Junior Reserve Corps.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Section 513 ("Grants to support STEM education in the Junior Reserve Officers’ Training Corps") instructs different departments of the government, such as the National Science foundation, as well as local governments to carry out programs that are supported by said grants.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Section 513 ("Grants to support STEM education in the Junior Reserve Officers’ Training Corps") outlines what activities are allowed under the grants, and what specific area of studies and subjects that they would work under.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Section 513 ("Grants to support STEM education in the Junior Reserve Officers’ Training Corps") details subjects that are eligible for said grants, which include science, technology, engineering, mathematics, computer science, and more.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Section 513 ("Grants to support STEM education in the Junior Reserve Officers’ Training Corps") allows for the Secretary of Defense to determine which additional subjects and areas of studies could be applicable to the grant.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XV, Section 6505 ("GAO studies on trafficking") instructs the Comptroller General of the United States to carry out a study in consultation with law enforcement, relevant federal agencies, private sector stakeholders (such as financial institutions, data and technology companies), to investigate major trafficking routes used by transnational criminal organizations and to what extent the trafficking routes are related.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XV, Section 6505 ("GAO studies on trafficking") directs the study to include commonly used methods to launder and move the proceeds of trafficking; the types of suspicious financial activity that are associated with illicit trafficking networks, and how financial institutions identify and report such activity.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XV, Section 6505 ("GAO studies on trafficking") directs the study to include steps financial institutions are taking to detect and prevent bad actors who are laundering the proceeds of illicit trafficking, including data analysis, policies, training procedures, rules, and guidance,

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XV, Section 6505 ("GAO studies on trafficking") necessitates the study to include the role those emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, digital identity technologies, distributed ledger technologies, virtual assets and online marketplaces can play in enabling the laundering of proceeds from trafficking.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XV, Section 6505 ("GAO studies on trafficking") requires the Comptroller General of the United States to submit a report to the congres, summarizing the results of the study and any recommendations for regulatory action.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title LXII, Section 6211 ("Financial crimes tech symposium") requires the Secretary of the Treasury to periodically convene a global anti-money laundering and financial crime symposium -- attended by domestic and international financial regulators, senior executives from regulated firms, technology providers, representatives from law enforcement and national security agencies, and experts -- focused on how new technology can be used to more effectively combat financial crimes and other illicit activities.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title LXII, Section 6211 ("Financial crimes tech symposium") requires the Director of the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network -- a bureau of the Treasury Department -- to brief the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives on the current and potential future use of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies in its work, along with policy recommendations for enhancing the efficacy of utilizing such technologies in combating financial crimes.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XC, Section 9004 ("Department of Homeland Security reports on digital content forgery technology") instructs the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security to submit annually, for a period of 5 years, a report to Congress on the state of digital content forgery technology.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XC, Section 9004 ("Department of Homeland Security reports on digital content forgery technology") requires the report to include an assessment of the underlying technologies used to create or propagate digital content forgeries, including the evolution of such technologies and patterns of dissemination of such technologies.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XC, Section 9004 ("Department of Homeland Security reports on digital content forgery technology") requires the report to include a description of the types of digital content forgeries, including those used to commit fraud, cause harm, harass, coerce, or silence vulnerable groups or individuals, or violate civil rights.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XC, Section 9004 ("Department of Homeland Security reports on digital content forgery technology") requires the report to include an assessment of how foreign governments, proxies and networks thereof, and non-governmental entities use, or could use, digital content forgeries to harm national security.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XC, Section 9004 ("Department of Homeland Security reports on digital content forgery technology") requires the report to include an assessment of the uses, applications, dangers, benefits, and impact on individuals of deep learning or digital content forgery technologies used to generate realistic depictions of events that did not occur.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XC, Section 9004 ("Department of Homeland Security reports on digital content forgery technology") requires the report to include a description of the methods and technological countermeasures that are, or could be, used to identify forgeries and address concerns with digital content forgery technology.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title LVXXXIV, Section 8411 ("Unmanned maritime systems and satellite vessel tracking technologies") requires that the Commandant submit a report to Congress on the actual and potential effects of such technologies on the mission effectiveness of the Coast Guard.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title VII, Section 808 ("Acquisition authority of the Director of the Joint Artificial Intelligence Center") allocates personnel and funding to support Center missions and the transition of artificial intelligence capabilities into appropriate acquisition programs or into operational use.

William M. William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XI, Section 1102 ("Enhancement of public-private talent exchange programs in the Department of Defense") requires the Secretary of Defense to use their authority for personnel exchanges with private sector entities focusing on Department of Defence modernization priorities.  Including exchanges in Research and Engineering, the Chief Information Officer, and each Armed Force under the jurisdiction of a military department.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XI, Section 1102 ("Enhancement of public-private talent exchange programs in the Department of Defense") insructs the Secretary of Defense to develop a system to identify, mitigate, and manage public-private talent exchange conflicts of interest.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XI, Section 1102 ("Enhancement of public-private talent exchange programs in the Department of Defense") requires the Secretary of Defense to brief the Senate and House Armed Services Committees on Public-Private Exchange programmes. This briefing should highlight seeking opportunities for exchanges with private sector entities working on Department of Defense modernization priorities, including Artificial Intelligence.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XI, Section 1102 ("Enhancement of public-private talent exchange programs in the Department of Defense") requires such briefing to explain barriers preventing supervisors from nominating staff for and encouraging participation in public-private exchange programmes; ways to incentivize senior leaders for programme encouragement, and the Department's conflict of interest requirements.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XVI, Section 1601 ("Space Development Agency development requirements and transfer to Space Force") instructs the Director to lead the integration of next-generation space capabilities, including novel sensors and autonomous battle features.

(Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XVI, Section 1601 ("Space Development Agency development requirements and transfer to Space Force") instructs the Director to lead the procurement of relevant commercial capabilities and services, including low-Earth orbit or innovative capabilities.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title XVI, Section 1601 ("Space Development Agency development requirements and transfer to Space Force") instructs the Secretary of Defense to transfer the Space Development Agency from the Office of the Secretary of Defense to the Space Force by October 1, 2022.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Section 241 ("Measuring and incentivizing programming proficiency") authorizes resources for managing government support for AI-related education and proficiency

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Section 241 ("Measuring and incentivizing programming proficiency") instructs the Secretary of Defense to leverage existing civilian software development and architecture certification programmes to implement DOD coding language proficiency and AI competency tests.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Section 241 ("Measuring and incentivizing programming proficiency") requires the Secretary of Defense to update record keeping systems to track artificial intelligence and programming certification testing results just like the foreign language competency system.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Section 241 ("Measuring and incentivizing programming proficiency") instructs the secretary of Defense to share information with the heads of other intelligence agencies about the coding language proficiency and artificial intelligence competency tests and encourages them to implement tracking and reward systems.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Section 241 ("Measuring and incentivizing programming proficiency") requires the Secretary of Defense to implement a system of rewards for Department of Defense employees who perform successfully on specific language coding proficiency and artificial intelligence competency tests.

William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Division A, Title II, Section 241 ("Measuring and incentivizing programming proficiency") advocates for special pay for a Department of Defense employee who is certified and proficient in a computer or digital programming language but may not exceed 20% of basic pay.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 7510 ("Requirement to ensure intelligence community directives appropriately account for artificial intelligence and machine learning tools in intelligence products") requires the Director to either (a) justify the assertion that existing intelligence community directives do sufficiently provide such guidance or (b) provide a plan and timeline for updating the directives as necessary.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 7513 ("Policies established by Director of National Intelligence for artificial intelligence capabilities") requires the establishment of a lexicon relating to machine learning and AI use by the intelligence community.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 7513 ("Policies established by Director of National Intelligence for artificial intelligence capabilities") requires the establishment of guidelines for evaluating model performance by specifying conditions for AI capability monitoring, documenting performance objectives, specifying model auditing processes, and specifying conditions for vulnerability testing and privacy evaluations.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 7513 ("Policies established by Director of National Intelligence for artificial intelligence capabilities") requires the establishment of guidelines for tracking dependencies in related systems, documentation requirements for capabilities procured from third-party and training data usage, and guidance on the usage of third-party-trained models.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 856 ("Pilot program to analyze and monitor certain supply chains") requires the Under Secretary to submit an annual report (until 2028) that specifies the vulnerabilities of the supply chains and the efficiencies achieved through using the new tools.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 811 ("Modernizing the Department of Defense requirements process") requires the Secretary of Defense in coordination with military leaders to develop streamlined requirements of development processes for the Department of Defense, in order to modernize war fighting technology and reduce the time needed to deliver capabilities to warfighters.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 811 ("Modernizing the Department of Defense requirements process") requires revisions to requirements management practices that maximizes the use of commercial products or services and allow for a broader range of new or alternative technological opportunities to be incorporated without the requirement being validated again.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 811 ("Modernizing the Department of Defense requirements process") establishes a process to rapidly validate the ability of commercial products and services to meet capability needs or opportunities.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 811 ("Modernizing the Department of Defense requirements process") requires retiring and replacing the Department of Defense Architecture Framework with a new structure focused on enabling interoperability  through application program interfaces, enterprise architectures and platforms, and government and commercial standards.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 811 ("Modernizing the Department of Defense requirements process") requires the secretary to develop a formal career path, training, and structure for requirements managers.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 811 ("Modernizing the Department of Defense requirements process") establishes the required processes for software, artificial intelligence, data, and related capability areas to be more rapid and iterative than the requirements processes for traditional hardware systems.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 811 ("Modernizing the Department of Defense requirements process") requires the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff to collaborate with industry partners, contractors, and Department of Defense science and technology reinvention laboratories in designing the new requirements development process.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 811 ("Modernizing the Department of Defense requirements process") requires the Secretary of Defense to submit to the congressional defense committees an interim report and a final report on the development and implementation of the new requirements development process.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 1507 ("Review and plan relating to cyber red teams of Department of Defense") requires the same officials listed above to submit to Congress a plan for ensuring that the Department's cyber red teams possess the capabilities necessary to execute their duties, including with respect to threats stemming from artificial intelligence systems abroad.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 1507 ("Review and plan relating to cyber red teams of Department of Defense") requires the Director of Operational Test and Evaluation to evaluate annually, from 2025 through 2031, the status of the implementation of the plan described in the paragraph above.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 7507 ("Programs for next-generation microelectronics in support of artificial intelligence") requires the Director of National Intelligence, acting through the Director of the Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity, to establish or oversee a program to advance microelectronics research.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 7507 ("Programs for next-generation microelectronics in support of artificial intelligence") requires the program described above to focus on applications in artificial intelligence, advanced computing, advanced computing materials, optical communication networks, quantum technologies, or other emerging technologies.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 7507 ("Programs for next-generation microelectronics in support of artificial intelligence") requires the Director of National Intelligence to consider a variety of factors when crafting the research program, including input from the Secretary of Commerce and from an array of stakeholders including representatives of industry and academia.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 7507 ("Programs for next-generation microelectronics in support of artificial intelligence") requires the Director of the Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity to brief the congressional intelligence, appropriations, and commerce committees on the progress of the research program described above and recommendations for future research priorities.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 224 ("Next Generation Air Dominance family of systems development program accountability matrices") submit goals for Next Generation Air Dominance and Collaborative Combat Aircraft programs to congressional defense committees and the Comptroller General concurrent with the President's budget submission. Include key milestones, testing events, and performance goals, subdivided into six-month increments.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 224 ("Next Generation Air Dominance family of systems development program accountability matrices") provide information on technology readiness levels, design maturity, software maturity, integration maturity, manufacturing readiness levels, reliability, availability for flight operations, and maintainability.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 224 ("Next Generation Air Dominance family of systems development program accountability matrices") provide updates on progress and cost estimates for the program every 6 months. It details progress made toward the goals identified in the matrices and provides updated cost estimates for air vehicles, propulsion, mission systems, software, program management, system test and evaluation, support and training systems, and more.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 224 ("Next Generation Air Dominance family of systems development program accountability matrices") develop key performance parameters (cost KPPs) for cost thresholds and objectives for the programs. Specify threshold and objective values for categories such as unit recurring flyaway cost, average procurement unit cost, gross/weapon system unit cost, aircraft cost-per-tail-per-year, and aircraft cost-per-flight-hour.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 224 ("Next Generation Air Dominance family of systems development program accountability matrices") ensure that each Secretary concerned works on these parameters for the respective programs and includes them in the related documents.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 224 ("Next Generation Air Dominance family of systems development program accountability matrices") ensure assessment of the sufficiency of matrices by the Comptroller General, who will review them and submit assessments to congressional defense committees, identifying any cost, schedule, or performance trends.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 1090 ("Conduct of weather reconnaissance in the United States") permits the 53rd Weather Reconnaissance Squadron of the Air Force Reserve Command and the Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to use aircraft, personnel, and equipment necessary to improve the accuracy and efficacy of weather monitoring and water management, including through advanced technological methods.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 1090 ("Conduct of weather reconnaissance in the United States") instructs the Squadron to use autonomous platform observations to improve water management decision-making and flood forecasting, if it uses the resources named in the above paragraph.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 1090 ("Conduct of weather reconnaissance in the United States") requires the Secretary of the Air Force to submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report on the resources used and required by the Air Force and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to improve weather monitoring and water management.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 903 ("Establishment of Office of Strategic Capital") creates a new Office of Strategic Capital in the Department of Defense.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 903 ("Establishment of Office of Strategic Capital") directs the new Office to invest in companies developing critical technologies, including autonomous robots, that may benefit the Department of Defense.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 903 ("Establishment of Office of Strategic Capital") permits the Office to launch a pilot program for providing capital assistance that supports the defense industrial base.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 903 ("Establishment of Office of Strategic Capital") requires the Office's investments to meet certain criteria, including restrictions on interest rates and loan repayment periods as well as requirements for non-Federal investments in selected companies, subject to various exceptions.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 903 ("Establishment of Office of Strategic Capital") requires the Secretary of Defense to submit to the congressional defense committees an annual report on the Office's activities, in addition to notifying the congressional defense committees whenever it provides capital assistance.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 253 ("Annual review of status of implementation plan for digital engineering career tracks") requires the Secretary to submit annually, through 2029, a report to the congressional defense committees on the findings of that internal review. National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 7356 ("Analysis of commercial cloud initiatives of intelligence community") requires the above analysis to include projected cloud computing costs, plans for the termination of legacy data storage mechanisms, an assessment of the value and efficacy of cloud computing tools and analytics, and the suitability of existing computing arrangements to service artificial intelligence systems for the intelligence community.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 350 ("Strategy and assessment on use of automation and artificial intelligence for shipyard optimization") requires the Secretary of the Navy to evaluate the potential cost savings of adopting artificial intelligence predictive maintenance technologies.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 1521 ("Control and management of Department of Defense data; establishment of Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council") requires the Secretary to establish the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council, which will provide policy oversight to ensure the responsible, coordinated, and ethical deployment of AI across Department of Defense missions and operations.

The report shall be submitted with the budget justification materials submitted in support of the budget of the Department of Defense for each of FY 2025, 2030, and 2035.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 112 ("Strategy for Army tactical wheeled vehicle program") requires the report to include a description of the force structure and funding necessary for the tactical wheeled vehicle program to support the U.S.'s national security strategy, along with detailed rundown of a program for the construction of tactical wheeled vehicles and the estimated cost of such a program.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 112 ("Strategy for Army tactical wheeled vehicle program") requires the Secretary of the Army to, within 15 days of the budget materials submission described above, brief the congressional defense committees on the investment needed for each platform of tactical wheeled vehicle.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Title XV, Subtitle E ("Artificial Intelligence") updates and extends the DoD's AI and ML acquisition framework and requires a plan for acquisition authority delegation and a demonstration of acquisition authority capabilities.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Title XV, Subtitle E ("Artificial Intelligence") mandates the creation of a bug bounty program for foundational AI models within the DoD, promoting collaboration with federal entities and cybersecurity experts. Requires briefing the congressional defense committees on the program within one year.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Title XV, Subtitle E ("Artificial Intelligence") instructs the Secretary of Defense to establish a competition to advance technologies for detecting and watermarking generative AI content. Requires annual briefing to the congressional defense committees.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Title XV, Subtitle E ("Artificial Intelligence") directs the Secretary of Defense to issue DoD-wide guidance and policy on AI, including with regard to ethical AI use, bias mitigation, cybersecurity, technical workforce assessments, AI literacy needs and related training programs, protection against adversarial AI, protecting the intellectual property of DoD AI system suppliers, AI's potential role in developing offensive actions, availability of inputs for AI, verification and evaluation frameworks, potential vulnerabilities of AI models and human oversight of autonomous systems. Requires briefing the congressional defense committees within 150 days.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Title XV, Subtitle E ("Artificial Intelligence") requires a study on the vulnerabilities of AI-enabled military applications, focusing on explainability, security risks, and the integration of decision support systems, with a final report for the congressional defense committees detailing findings and research gaps.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Title XV, Subtitle C ("Cyberspace-Related Matters: Information Technology and Data Management") instructs the Secretary of Defense to establish the 'Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council' to oversee policy ensuring responsible and ethical use of data and AI in Department of Defense missions.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Title XV, Subtitle C ("Cyberspace-Related Matters: Information Technology and Data Management") requires  The council, led by the Chief Digital and AI Officer, to develop, implement, and oversee AI, coordinating governance, and providing ethical guidance.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Title XV, Subtitle C ("Cyberspace-Related Matters: Information Technology and Data Management") instructs the council to identify, monitor, and update recommendations for AI use, review program funding,  and ensure compliance with AI policies.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Title XV, Subtitle C ("Cyberspace-Related Matters: Information Technology and Data Management") instructs the council to issue guidance on access and distribution restrictions relating to data, models, tool sets, testing or validation infrastructure.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Title XV, Subtitle C ("Cyberspace-Related Matters: Information Technology and Data Management") instructs the council to implement and oversee an educational program on data and artificial intelligence, to familiarize personnel department on the applications of artificial intelligence.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Title XV, Subtitle C ("Cyberspace-Related Matters: Information Technology and Data Management") mandates all data collection, use, or retention measures  to comply with relevant laws and regulations, including those concerning data related to US persons.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Title XV, Subtitle C ("Cyberspace-Related Matters: Information Technology and Data Management") requires an establishment of a course of education at the Defense Information School, the purpose of which shall be to provide instruction on the practical concepts and skills.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Title XV, Subtitle C ("Cyberspace-Related Matters: Information Technology and Data Management") instructs the Director of the Defense Media Activity to carry out a pilot program to assess the feasibility and advisability of implementing industry open technical standards for digital content provenance for official photographs and videos of the Department of Defense

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 346 ("Pilot program on optimization of aerial refueling and fuel management in contested logistics environments through use of artificial intelligence") mandates the Department of Defense and the Air Force to work together in launching a pilot program that optimizes aerial refueling and fuel management using artificial intelligence and advanced digital technologies.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 346 ("Pilot program on optimization of aerial refueling and fuel management in contested logistics environments through use of artificial intelligence") directs the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer to (a) coordinate with the Commander of the United States Transportation Command and the Commander of the United States Indo-Pacific Command to align the pilot program with existing operational requirements and (b) consult relevant experts in AI.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 346 ("Pilot program on optimization of aerial refueling and fuel management in contested logistics environments through use of artificial intelligence") requires the pilot program to assess the feasibility and effectiveness of artificial intelligence-driven approaches and evaluate the interoperability and compatibility of artificial intelligence-enabled systems with the existing logistics infrastructure of the Department of Defense.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 346 ("Pilot program on optimization of aerial refueling and fuel management in contested logistics environments through use of artificial intelligence") requires an assessment of potential challenges and risks associated with the integration of artificial intelligence and other advanced digital technologies, including those related to cybersecurity.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 346 ("Pilot program on optimization of aerial refueling and fuel management in contested logistics environments through use of artificial intelligence") requires the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer to submit a report on the pilot program's design, progress, and results to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate within one year.

Virginia HB 2154 requires hospitals, nursing homes, and certified nursing facilities to establish and implement policies for patient access to intelligent personal assistants while receiving inpatient services.

Virginia HB 2154 ensures policies protect health information in accordance with the federal Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

Virginia HB 2154 defines "intelligent personal assistant" as a combination of an electronic device and specialized software application that assists users with tasks using natural language processing and artificial intelligence.

Virginia HB 2154 mandates that these facilities allow the use of intelligent personal assistants for patients, ensuring compliance with privacy and security standards.

Virginia HB 2154 includes intelligent personal assistants like "digital assistants" or "virtual assistants" in the definition provided.

Illinois HB 3563 amends the Department of Innovation and Technology Act to establish the Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force.

Illinois HB 3563 requires the Task Force to investigate and report on generative AI and natural language processing software.

Illinois HB 3563 comprises the Task Force of appointed members from various government, educational, and expert backgrounds.

Illinois HB 3563 mandates the Task Force to hold at least five public meetings across different regions of Illinois.

Illinois HB 3563 tasks the Task Force with recommending legislation for consumer information protection, model policies for schools, and assessing AI's impact on public services, civil rights, employment, and cybersecurity.

Illinois HB 3563 obligates the Department to provide administrative and technical support to the Task Force.

Illinois HB 3563 requires the Task Force to file a comprehensive report by December 31, 2024, with the Governor and the General Assembly.

Alabama SB 78 establishes the Alabama Council on Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence.

Alabama SB 78 requires the council to review and advise the Governor and Legislature on the use and development of advanced technology and artificial intelligence.

Alabama SB 78 composes the council of 22 members, including appointees from the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Speaker of the House, and Senate President Pro Tempore, and ex officio members from commerce and information technology departments.

Alabama SB 78 mandates that non-legislative appointees have expertise in AI, technology, ethics, privacy, workforce development, or computer science.

Alabama SB 78 stipulates that the council meets at least twice a year and allows virtual participation.

Alabama SB 78 obliges the council to submit an annual report with recommendations on AI and advanced technology to the Governor and Legislature.

Alabama SB 78 enforces diversity in appointments regarding gender, race, and geography.

Alabama SB 78 prohibits salary for non-legislative members but allows expense reimbursement; provides legislative members with regular compensation for meeting attendance.

Alabama SB 78 sets the act’s effective date to one year post-approval.

New Jersey S 2723 requires each state agency to develop and submit an information technology modernization and improvement plan to the Chief Technology Officer within one year of request.

New Jersey S 2723 mandates the plan to include strategies for improving digital services using data analytics, cloud computing, electronic forms, and digitized workflows, ensuring mobile-friendly and accessible websites.

New Jersey S 2723 authorizes the Chief Technology Officer to review these plans in collaboration with the Chief Innovation Officer.

New Jersey S 2723 mandates the Chief Technology Officer to annually evaluate the feasibility of using AI, machine learning, and cloud services for public services, and to develop data analytics capabilities for policy development.

New Jersey S 2723 requires the development of metrics to assess each agency's implementation of a modern digital experience, updated at least every two years and reevaluated every three years.

Arkansas SB 656 creates the Data-Sharing and Data-Driven Decision-Making Task Force, comprised of twelve members appointed from the Senate and House of Representatives.

Arkansas SB 656 mandates the task force to study and recommend the implementation of a statewide data-sharing system across state agencies.

Arkansas SB 656 requires the task force to evaluate current data management inefficiencies, and propose necessary legislation and funding mechanisms for system implementation. Empowers the task force to hire external consultants if necessary.

Arkansas SB 656 requires the task force to meet at least monthly and report findings to the Governor and legislative leaders by December 31, 2019; expires the task force on January 1, 2020.

Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 6513 ("Lead intelligence community coordinator for countering and neutralizing proliferation of Iran-origin unmanned aircraft systems") instructs the Director of National Intelligence to designate an official from the intelligence community to serve as the lead coordinator for countering and neutralizing the proliferation of Iran-origin unmanned aircraft systems.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 6513 ("Lead intelligence community coordinator for countering and neutralizing proliferation of Iran-origin unmanned aircraft systems") requires this Coordinator to develop a comprehensive plan of action, driven by intelligence information, for countering and neutralizing the threats posed by the proliferation of Iran-origin unmanned aircraft systems and submit a briefing of such plans to the Congress.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 6513 ("Lead intelligence community coordinator for countering and neutralizing proliferation of Iran-origin unmanned aircraft systems") mandates the report to include recommendations for any changes in United States policy designed to improve the capacity of the intelligence community to assist in countering such threats.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 6513 ("Lead intelligence community coordinator for countering and neutralizing proliferation of Iran-origin unmanned aircraft systems") encourages collaboration and the expansion of existing cooperative efforts among members of the Five Eyes Partnership and Israel for the purpose of countering Iran-origin unmanned aircraft systems.

Advancing American Artificial Intelligence Act encourages AI-related programs and initiatives to enhance the competitiveness of the US based on innovation and entrepreneurialism.

Advancing American Artificial Intelligence Act promotes modernized business practices and advanced technologies aligned with US values, including protection of privacy, civil rights and civil liberties across the Federal Government.

Advancing American Artificial Intelligence Act defines the term "artificial intelligence system".

Advancing American Artificial Intelligence Act instructs the Secretary of Homeland Security, Chief Procurement Officer, Chief Information Officer, Chief Privacy Officer, and the Officer for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties of the Department to work together on policies for acquiring AI and considering the risks of AI.

Advancing American Artificial Intelligence Act instructs the Inspector General to identify training and investments to enable the employees of the Office of the Inspector General to advance their understanding of AI and its usage.

Advancing American Artificial Intelligence Act instructs Director of the Office of Management and Budget to develop guidance for policies for AI use in government, with inputs from both government agencies and non-governmental actors.

Advancing American Artificial Intelligence Act requests the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to brief congressional committees on the activities carried out under this Act.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 1535 ("Department of Defense Cyber and Digital Service Academy") requires the Secretary of Defense to establish a new program that provides financial support to individuals studying digital technology-related areas critical to the Department of Defense, including AI. The program shall be called "Department of Defense Cyber and Digital Service Academy" and have a board of directors consisting of representatives from federal departments and agencies.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 1535 ("Department of Defense Cyber and Digital Service Academy") eligible individuals need to be enrolled in a relevant program at an institution of higher education and commit to work for the Department of Defense in an area relevant to the program for a duration equivalent to the duration of the scholarship.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 1535 ("Department of Defense Cyber and Digital Service Academy") requires a report to Congress on the success of the program every two years.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 9506 ("Cybersecurity recruitment and retention") requires the Secretary to submit a plan to the appropriate congressional committees that describes how the initiative described above will be implemented.

Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 6505 ("Assessments of production of semiconductors by the People's Republic of China") begins discussing the phrase “appropriate committees of Congress” and what organizations are actually a part of this phrase when benign referred. Also defines the term “legacy semiconductor” in terms of the definition given in another legislation document.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 6505 ("Assessments of production of semiconductors by the People's Republic of China") annually for 3 years after this act is passed, the Director of National Intelligence must submit an unclassified assessment report regarding China’s production of semiconductors through China’s firms and business sectors to the appropriate committees of Congress.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 6505 ("Assessments of production of semiconductors by the People's Republic of China") the Director of National Intelligence must meet with the heads of federal agencies to discuss the elements of the assessment. They must discuss the self-sufficiency of China in the fields of artificial intelligence, cloud computing, autonomous vehicles, and other newer-technological areas. They must discuss China’s access to intellectual property related to leading edge process nodes, including electronic design automation technology. They must discuss Chinese firms’s production of semiconductors that are not legacy conductors and stockpiling efforts of semiconductor manufacturing equipment. They must discuss the relative market share and its trends of Chinese semiconductor manufacturers at different process nodes. They must discuss the outside recruitment activity into Chinese semiconductors firms and the capability of the Chinese workforce in developing semiconductors that are not legacy semiconductors and relevant equipment.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 162 ("Assessment and strategy for fielding capabilities to counter threats posed by unmanned aerial system swarms") directs the Secretary of Defense to assess threats posed by unmanned aerial system swarms to installations and deployed Armed Forces, the use of these swarms by adversaries and their national security implications such as autonomous intelligence and machine learning, current capabilities of the Defense Department and their effectiveness in countering these threats, and efforts by the Defense Department to develop and field technology that can counter swarms.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 162 ("Assessment and strategy for fielding capabilities to counter threats posed by unmanned aerial system swarms") directs the Secretary of Defense to develop and implement a strategy to field capabilities to counter threats from unmanned aerial system swarms. The strategy should define "unmanned aerial system swarm," outline plans for developing, testing, fielding, and acquiring capabilities to counter swarms, estimate resources needed by each Armed Force to implement the strategy, and determine the legislative action necessary for the Defense Department to counter swarm threats.

James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 162 ("Assessment and strategy for fielding capabilities to counter threats posed by unmanned aerial system swarms") directs the Secretary of Defense to consider incorporating the strategy into a comprehensive strategy to defend against unmanned aerial systems and to report the assessment findings and strategy to the congressional defense committees within 270 days.

An Act Establishing the Alabama Commission on Artificial Intelligence and Associated Technologies. establishes the Alabama Commission on Artificial Intelligence to review and advise on AI growth and use in governance, healthcare, education, transportation, and future industries.

An Act Establishing the Alabama Commission on Artificial Intelligence and Associated Technologies. requires the commission to consider the establishment of a permanent AI commission.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022, Section 216 ("Improvements relating to steering committee on emerging technology and national security threats") amends Section 236 of the FY 2021 National Defense Authorization Act by adding the Director of National Intelligence as an official that can, with the Secretary of Defense, establish a steering committee on emerging technology and national security and receive recommendations from the committee. Amends members of the steering committee to consist of the Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence, the Deputy Sector of Defense, the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staffs, and other appropriate officials. Adds that the Steering Committee shall be chaired by the Deputy Secretary of Defense, the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and the Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence jointly.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022, Section 216 ("Improvements relating to steering committee on emerging technology and national security threats") amends the responsibilities of the steering committee by clarifying that the committee's strategy is to maintain the technological superiority of both the US military and intelligence community according to not only the National Defense Strategy, but also the National Intelligence Strategy and the National Security Strategy. Adds that the steering committee is responsible for making recommendations on any changes to the guidance for developing the National Intelligence Program budget and determining whether sufficient resources are available for the intelligence community, in addition to the Department of Defense, to defeat threats to the US.

National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022, Section 216 ("Improvements relating to steering committee on emerging technology and national security threats") adds that the list of technologies classified as emerging technologies is to be determined jointly by the Secretary of Defense and the Director of National Intelligence. Adds the definition of intelligence community from the National Security Act of 1947.
