AI in Government Act of 2020 defines Artificial Intelligence

AI in Government Act of 2020 creates a program called ‘‘AI Center of Excellence’’, (CoE) which shall facilitate the adoption of AI technologies in the Federal Government and improve cohesion in the adoption of artificial intelligence.

AI in Government Act of 2020 stipulates certain functions of this program which includes;

AI in Government Act of 2020 a.  Collaborating with individual agencies, federal laboratories, nonprofit organizations, institutions and other entities to discuss recent developments in AI.

AI in Government Act of 2020 b. Assisting agencies in applying Federal policies on the management and use of data in the use of AI.

AI in Government Act of 2020 c. Consulting with agencies, including the Department of Defense, the Department of Commerce, the Department of Energy, the Department of Homeland Security, the Office of Management and Budget, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, and the National Science Foundation, on issues relating to AI.

AI in Government Act of 2020 identifies the skills needed for future job positions within the CoE and establishes jobs within the CoE and their duration (2 and 5 years).

AI in Government Act of 2020 instructs the Director of the CoE to submit a comprehensive plan to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and the Committee on Oversight and Reform with a timeline to achieve paragraphs a,b,c,d within 120 days of the date of the enactment of the instrument.

AI in Government Act of 2020 instructs the Director of the AI CoE to recommend approaches to remove barriers for use by agencies of AI technologies in order to promote their innovative application while protecting civil rights, and economic and national security; identify best practices for assessing and mitigating any discriminatory impact or bias on the basis of any classification protected under Federal nondiscrimination laws, or any unintended consequence of the use of AI.

Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, Title III ("National Science Foundation for the Future") instructs the Director of the National Science Foundation (Director) to develop a report on the need and feasibility as well as construct plans to implement a program to recruit and train the next generation of AI professionals in US government. Mandates that the report include statistical data on the federal AI workforce, assessments of current and future demand for AI expertise across the federal government and the ability of higher education institutions to prepare students to meet this demand, and an evaluation of the need for and feasibility of establishing a scholarship-for-service program for AI professionals in US government, as well as the possibility of leveraging existing programs such as the Federal Cyber Scholarship-for-Service Program.

Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, Title III ("National Science Foundation for the Future") authorizes the Director and other appropriate agency heads to establish a Federal AI scholarship-for-service program to recruit and train AI professionals to achieve the missions of US government. Requires the Director, in coordination with other agency heads, to establish criteria such as excellence in AI education and the ability to attract diverse students to designate qualified institutions of higher education that shall be eligible to participate in the program. Requires the program to provide scholarships through qualified higher education institutions to students pursuing fields of study related to AI, provide scholarship recipients with temporary appointments related to work on AI in the federal government, prioritize placement of scholarship recipients in executive agencies, identify opportunities to promote multidisciplinary programs of study, support capacity building for educational institutions to enable them to train the next-generation AI workforce, create courses in technology ethics for scholarship recipients, and award fellowships to masters and doctoral students who are pursuing degrees or research in AI and related fields. Instructs scholarship amounts to cover a student’s tuition and fees for not more than 3 years with an additional stipend, and obligates scholarship recipients to work for a period of time equivalent to the length of the scholarship in the AI mission of the US government entity or affiliated entity.

Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, Title III ("National Science Foundation for the Future") instructs the Director to establish competitive awards to institutions to advance knowledge of risk assessment including the utilization of AI in our ability to understand and predict extreme events and natural hazards, create engineered system solutions and develop instrumentation for innovation in resilient infrastructure, and advance research on multidisciplinary wildfire science and behaviors related to increasing resilience.

Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, Title III ("National Science Foundation for the Future") amends Section 506(a) of the America COMPETES Reauthorization Act of 2010 by adding AI and machine learning to the list of research areas that fall under information technologies for manufacturing that the Director can award grants to.

Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, Title III ("National Science Foundation for the Future") instructs the Director to make competitive awards to institutions to support basic research to advance critical minerals mining strategies to make better use of domestic resources and eliminate national reliance on minerals subject to supply chain disruptions, including the application of AI for geological exploration of critical minerals and the application of machine learning for detection and sorting of critical minerals.

Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, Title III ("National Science Foundation for the Future") requires the Director to conduct or support the development of a study on AI research capacity at US institutions of higher education. Requires the study to, at minimum, address which universities are putting out significant peer-reviewed AI research based on quantity and number of citations, which factors of these universities such as computing power enable their research, promising practices at these universities for advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion in AI research programs, geographic diversity of universities that have AI research-enabling factors, and how universities that are not currently top producers of AI research could improve, including potential pilot programs that the federal government could develop or support to help universities produce AI research.

Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, Title III ("National Science Foundation for the Future") instructs the Director, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget and the interagency committee established under the National AI Initiative Act of 2020, to develop and test models to inform the implementation of a government-wide data linkage and access infrastructure for statistical activities.

Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, Title III ("National Science Foundation for the Future") requires the Director to identify, and annually review and update a list of not more than 10 key technology focus areas, which includes AI, machine learning, autonomy, and related advances.

21 CFR § 870.2210 ("Adjunctive predictive cardiovascular indicator") requires that adjunctive predictive cardiovascular indicators -- medical devices used to predict cardiovascular health -- be subject to special controls in the U.S. Those controls include the following:

21 CFR § 870.2210 ("Adjunctive predictive cardiovascular indicator") requires a risk assessment of the device, including full disclosure of software specs and different inputs considered when making predictions about future cardiovascular health.

21 CFR § 870.2210 ("Adjunctive predictive cardiovascular indicator") requires scientific justification for the device's efficacy, including verification of algorithm calculations and validation using an independent data set.

21 CFR § 870.2210 ("Adjunctive predictive cardiovascular indicator") requires a human factors and usability engineering assessment to evaluate the risk of misinterpretation of device output.

21 CFR § 870.2210 ("Adjunctive predictive cardiovascular indicator") requires a clinical data assessment that specifies the clinical data used and an evaluation of output consistency.

That set of special controls:

21 CFR § 864.3750 ("Software algorithm device to assist users in digital pathology") requires detailed product labeling, including instructions for use and notices of the device's limitations.

21 CFR § 864.3750 ("Software algorithm device to assist users in digital pathology") requires performance assessments of the device that meets pre-set standards for rigor, evaluate the device's performance when used by its intended users, and cover the entire spectrum of challenging cases likely to be encountered in the device's operation.

21 CFR § 864.3750 ("Software algorithm device to assist users in digital pathology") requires a detailed description of the workings of the device's software.

21 CFR § 864.3750 ("Software algorithm device to assist users in digital pathology") requires a risk management plan, including mechanisms to mitigate cybersecurity risks.

21 CFR § 870.2345 ("Electrocardiograph software for over-the-counter use") labels over-the-counter use of electrocardiograph software devices as Class II (special controls), which requires manufactures to verify, validate, and conduct hazard analysis of detection algorithms in the devices.

21 CFR § 870.2345 ("Electrocardiograph software for over-the-counter use") mandates manufactures to produce clinical performance testing results that shows the performance characteristics of the detection algorithm by sensitivity and either specificity or positive predictive value.

21 CFR § 870.2345 ("Electrocardiograph software for over-the-counter use") requires manufacturers who fail to conduct non-clinical performance testing to validate detection algorithm performance using a previously adjudicated data set.

21 CFR § 870.2345 ("Electrocardiograph software for over-the-counter use") requires human factors and usability testing to demonstrate that the user can correctly interpret the device output and understand when to seek medical care.

21 CFR § 864.3750 ("Adjunctive hemodynamic indicator with decision point") classifies the adjunctive hemodynamic indicator with decision point -- a device that monitors medical conditions relating to blood flow -- into the Food & Drug Administration's class II, requiring special controls. That set of controls:

21 CFR § 864.3750 ("Adjunctive hemodynamic indicator with decision point") requires a full description of the technical parameters of the device's software and sensors.

21 CFR § 864.3750 ("Adjunctive hemodynamic indicator with decision point") requires a risk assessment for the device.

21 CFR § 864.3750 ("Adjunctive hemodynamic indicator with decision point") requires mechanisms designed to mitigate the impact of user error or failure of any subsystem components (signal detection and analysis, data display, and storage) on the accuracy of the device's output.

21 CFR § 864.3750 ("Adjunctive hemodynamic indicator with decision point") requires statistical documentation, based on robust clinical data, of the device's efficacy. The accuracy of the device's algorithm must be tested using an independent dataset.

21 CFR § 864.3750 ("Adjunctive hemodynamic indicator with decision point") requires a usability assessment to demonstrate that the risk of misinterpretation of the status indicator is appropriately mitigated.

21 CFR § 864.3750 ("Adjunctive hemodynamic indicator with decision point") requires detailed product labeling.

Limited Applicability of Consumer Financial Protection Act's “Time or Space” Exception With Respect to Digital Marketing Providers clarifies Section 1002 of the Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010's definition of "service provider" to include digital marketing providers that use algorithmic models or other analytics to commingle the targeting and delivery of advertisements to consumers, rendering those providers subject to the Act's prohibition on unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices.

Limited Applicability of Consumer Financial Protection Act's “Time or Space” Exception With Respect to Digital Marketing Providers outlines the ways in which digital marketers provide additional services beyond "time or space" and are materially involved in the development of content strategy -- often through the use of targeting and delivering algorithms -- thus qualifying them as "service providers" under the law.

Limited Applicability of Consumer Financial Protection Act's “Time or Space” Exception With Respect to Digital Marketing Providers outlines specific circumstances in which digital marketers are and are not considered service providers under the CFPA; they qualify as service providers when using algorithms and data to target and deliver advertisements with certain characteristics, or when using algorithms and business-specific data to determine when to display specific advertisements to specific consumers.

21 CFR § 882.1491 ("Pediatric Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis aid") classifies the Cognoa ASD Diagnosis Aid, a machine-learning software program and device used in the diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder, into the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's class II regulatory category requiring special controls. The mandated special controls are as follows:

21 CFR § 882.1491 ("Pediatric Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis aid") requires clinical performance testing to demonstrate that the device performs as intended under anticipated conditions of use, including an evaluation of sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value using a reference method of diagnosis and assessment of patient behavioral symptomology.

21 CFR § 882.1491 ("Pediatric Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis aid") requires software verification, validation, and hazard analysis to be provided for the device. Software documentation must include a detailed, technical description of the algorithm(s) used to generate device output(s), and a cybersecurity assessment of the impact of threats and vulnerabilities on device functionality and user(s).

21 CFR § 882.1491 ("Pediatric Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis aid") requires a usability assessment that must demonstrate that the intended user(s) can safely and correctly use the device.

21 CFR § 882.1491 ("Pediatric Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis aid") requires detailed product labeling that includes instructions for the device's use and a summary of any clinical testing done to demonstrate the device's functionality.

21 CFR § 892.2070 ("Medical image analyzer") requires disclosure of inputs, outputs, components, and limitations of image analysis algorithms used in medical image analyzers.

21 CFR § 892.2070 ("Medical image analyzer") requires performance testing that demonstrates the algorithms meaningfully improve the detection of abnormalities during patient radiographs.

21 CFR § 892.2070 ("Medical image analyzer") requires appropriate software documentation including device hazard analysis, software specs, traceability analysis, pass/fail criteria, and cybersecurity.

21 CFR § 892.2070 ("Medical image analyzer") requires a detailed summary of the methodology behind the performance testing.

21 CFR § 870.2785 ("Software for optical camera-based measurement of pulse rate, heart rate, breathing rate, and/or respiratory rate") classifies the Oxehealth Vital Signs device -- which uses software to enable camera-based measurement of pulse rate, heart rate, breathing rate, and/or respiratory rate -- into the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's class II, requiring special controls. The set of special controls:

21 CFR § 870.2785 ("Software for optical camera-based measurement of pulse rate, heart rate, breathing rate, and/or respiratory rate") requires a full characterization of the technical parameters of the device's software, as well as documentation of a cybersecurity vulnerability and management process to assure software functionality.

21 CFR § 870.2785 ("Software for optical camera-based measurement of pulse rate, heart rate, breathing rate, and/or respiratory rate") requires the results of verification and validation testing based on a comprehensive hazard analysis and risk assessment of the software and associated device, to include a description of all mitigations for user error or failure of any subsystem components (including signal detection, signal analysis, data display, and storage) on output accuracy.

21 CFR § 870.2785 ("Software for optical camera-based measurement of pulse rate, heart rate, breathing rate, and/or respiratory rate") requires clinical data demonstrating the software and device's efficacy, including comparing the device's output with a clinically accurate patient-contacting relevant comparator device in an accurate and reproducible manner.

21 CFR § 870.2785 ("Software for optical camera-based measurement of pulse rate, heart rate, breathing rate, and/or respiratory rate") requires a human factors and usability engineering assessment that evaluates the risk of improper measurement.

21 CFR § 870.2785 ("Software for optical camera-based measurement of pulse rate, heart rate, breathing rate, and/or respiratory rate") requires detailed product labeling, to include instructions for using the device and interpreting its output; warnings of factors that may impede proper functionality; and a description of the measurements the device takes.

Literacy in Future Technologies Artificial Intelligence Act empowers the Director of the National Science Foundation to award competitive grants to higher education institutions or nonprofits for developing AI literacy curricula and evaluation methods.

Literacy in Future Technologies Artificial Intelligence Act endorses AI literacy education to prepare a skilled workforce and maintain U.S. leadership in AI.

Literacy in Future Technologies Artificial Intelligence Act recognizes the importance of AI literacy in mitigating ethical challenges and adapting to rapidly evolving AI technologies.

Literacy in Future Technologies Artificial Intelligence Act supports the development of curricula focussed on AI competency, AI literacy evaluation tools, and professional development courses in AI literacy for educators.

Literacy in Future Technologies Artificial Intelligence Act encourages incorporating AI literacy in existing curricula, emphasizing responsible AI use.

Artificial Intelligence Acquisitions Act of 2024 mandates the development of a list of artificial intelligence products or services posing national security risks, focusing on those associated with foreign entities of concern.

Artificial Intelligence Acquisitions Act of 2024 requires the Executive Director, alongside the Under Secretary of Commerce and the Federal Acquisition Security Council, to publish and annually update this list.

Artificial Intelligence Acquisitions Act of 2024 prohibits federal agencies from purchasing or procuring AI products or services included on this list.

Artificial Intelligence Acquisitions Act of 2024 obligates contractors with federal agencies to divest from listed AI products within specified timeframes.

Artificial Intelligence Acquisitions Act of 2024 allows exceptions for intelligence activities and specific Department of Defense operations related to defense intelligence and adversarial AI research.

Artificial Intelligence Acquisitions Act of 2024 defines key terms including "artificial intelligence," "foreign person of concern," and "country of concern," specifying entities like China, Russia, and Iran as countries of concern.

Artificial Intelligence Acquisitions Act of 2024 sets a timeline for initial list publication within one year of the Act's enactment and mandates public notification if no updates are made annually.

Idaho House Bill 575 establishes the crime of disclosing or threatening to disclose explicit synthetic media without consent, intending to cause distress or obtain valuables, punishable as a misdemeanor or felony for repeat offenders.

Idaho House Bill 575 defines "explicit synthetic media" as AI-altered images or videos depicting sexual conduct involving identifiable individuals without their engagement.

Idaho House Bill 575 exempts disclosures for lawful purposes, such as criminal investigations, public interest reporting, scientific research, or legal proceedings.

Idaho House Bill 575 excludes liability for interactive computer services and telecommunications providers for third-party content, unless they intentionally aid disclosures.

Idaho House Bill 575 declares provisions severable, ensuring unaffected sections remain valid if parts are invalidated.

Idaho House Bill 575 declares an emergency and sets the effective date for July 1, 2024.

A bill to specify control and management of Department of Defense data and to establish the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council, and for other purposes. establishes the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council to oversee and ensure ethical AI and data policies within the Department of Defense.

A bill to specify control and management of Department of Defense data and to establish the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council, and for other purposes. requires the Council to oversee AI ethics, governance, and operational usage, with the aim of improving AI governance coordination and mitigating bias in AI systems.

A bill to specify control and management of Department of Defense data and to establish the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council, and for other purposes. mandates the Council to submit reports to the Secretary of Defense and congressional defense committees every 180 days initially and at least every 18 months thereafter.

Digital Platform Commission Act of 2023 defines algorithmic processes as including artificial intelligence techniques and refers to processes that can make decisions, generate content, or provide information, especially as used in social media

Digital Platform Commission Act of 2023 establishes the Federal Digital Platform Commission to regulate digital platforms, including social media.

Digital Platform Commission Act of 2023 provides for the creation of a Code Council to develop voluntary or enforceable behavioral codes, technical standards, and other policies related to digital platforms and AI processes.

Digital Platform Commission Act of 2023 mandates oversight of algorithmic processes, including those using AI, for fairness, transparency, and safety.

Digital Platform Commission Act of 2023 obligates platforms to ensure recommendation systems and other algorithmic processes are free from harmful, abusive, anticompetitive, or deceptive biases.

Digital Platform Commission Act of 2023 imposes regular public risk assessments for harmful content distribution and steps to mitigate such harms, including those from algorithmic processes..

Cooper Davis Act requires electronic communication service providers and remote computing services to report to the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) any knowledge of crimes involving fentanyl, methamphetamine, or counterfeit substances.

Cooper Davis Act mandates the report to be filed within 60 days of obtaining such knowledge, including detailed contact and relevant information about the involved accounts.

Cooper Davis Act allows reports based on reasonable belief and includes optional additional information like geographic location and complete communication data.

Cooper Davis Act subjects providers to criminal and civil penalties for failing to report or submitting false reports.

Cooper Davis Act states that providers are not required to monitor users or the content of communications proactively.

Cooper Davis Act obliges DEA to review and potentially investigate reports, sharing them with other law enforcement agencies as needed.

Cooper Davis Act mandates the Attorney General to enforce these requirements and take measures for data minimization.

Cooper Davis Act requires DEA to publish annual reports on the number and outcomes of reports received.

Cooper Davis Act exempts broadband internet access service providers from these reporting requirements.

AI Ads Act amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to include fraudulent misrepresentation through content generated with artificial intelligence (AI) under its prohibitions.

AI Ads Act clarifies that fraudulent misrepresentation of campaign authority or solicitation of funds includes the use of AI-generated content.

AI Ads Act extends the prohibition against fraudulent misrepresentation beyond candidates to any person misrepresenting candidates, political parties, or committees for any purpose.

AI Ads Act broadens the scope of prohibited fraudulent solicitation to encompass any candidate, political party, or fictitious political organization, not just those directly involving a candidate or party employee.

AI Ads Act expands the provisions to cover AI-generated content used in misrepresentation or solicitation within political campaigns, ensuring comprehensive regulation of AI's role in electoral fraud.

S.4306, Five AIs Act 2024 establishes the "Five AIs Strategic Artificial Intelligence Working Group" within 90 days to coordinate AI initiatives among the Five Eyes countries (Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the UK, and the US).

S.4306, Five AIs Act 2024 requires the Secretary of Defense and Director of National Intelligence to lead and designate a head for the Working Group.

S.4306, Five AIs Act 2024 mandates the Working Group to develop strategies for AI interoperability, ethical frameworks, and innovation among the Five Eyes countries.

S.4306, Five AIs Act 2024 instructs testing and evaluation of AI systems for intelligence sharing and battlespace awareness.

S.4306, Five AIs Act 2024 emphasizes leveraging commercial AI technologies and managing data-informed AI systems.

S.4306, Five AIs Act 2024 requires submission of a plan within 60 days and biannual reports on the Working Group's activities.

S.4306, Five AIs Act 2024 specifies control of knowledge and technical data by individual countries under their export laws.

S.4306, Five AIs Act 2024 allows termination of the Working Group on September 30, 2028, with possible extension for national security interests.

Preserving American Dominance in Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 establishes the Artificial Intelligence Safety Review Office to oversee national security risks from advanced AI, particularly chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and cyber threats.

Preserving American Dominance in Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 mandates developers of AI models with significant computational power to report red-teaming and cybersecurity practices.

Preserving American Dominance in Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 requires evaluations and pre-deployment reviews for AI models posing potential threats, overseen by an Under Secretary of Commerce for AI Safety.

Preserving American Dominance in Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 orders creation of standards for know-your-customer protocols and red-teaming techniques to mitigate advanced AI risks.

Preserving American Dominance in Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 permits the Attorney General to enforce compliance, with civil fines up to $1,000,000 daily and potential imprisonment for violations.

Preserving American Dominance in Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 allocates $50,000,000 for implementing these measures to ensure AI advancements remain secure and beneficial for U.S. interests.

AI Act of 2024 mandates financial regulators to submit reports within 180 days assessing the benefits and risks of AI in their sectors.

AI Act of 2024 requires banking regulators to examine AI's role in banking operations, fraud detection, cybersecurity, and fair lending practices, with a focus on smaller and community financial institutions.

AI Act of 2024 directs the Securities and Exchange Commission to explore AI's use in market research, portfolio management, and fraud detection in securities markets.

AI Act of 2024 instructs housing and mortgage regulators to evaluate AI's impact on mortgage efficiency, credit decisions, and real estate practices, particularly for underserved communities.

AI Act of 2024 requests the Treasury Department to report on AI's application in compliance with the Bank Secrecy Act, cybersecurity, and protection against national security threats.

AI Act of 2024 mandates inclusion of legislative recommendations to responsibly adopt AI across these sectors.

AI Act of 2024 requires public consultation to gather input for each report, involving self-regulatory organizations and relevant agencies.

Trustworthy By Design Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 mandates the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop guidelines for evaluating the trustworthiness of AI systems within one year, covering models, data, and human-AI interactions.

Trustworthy By Design Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 requires periodic updates of these guidelines, addressing elements like safety, security, privacy, and bias, especially concerning protected classes under Federal law.

Trustworthy By Design Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 obliges Federal agencies to ensure new AI systems conform to guidelines before deployment and evaluate existing systems within two years to ensure compliance.

Trustworthy By Design Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 specifies designation of a Chief AI Officer in each Federal agency responsible for AI governance and guideline implementation.

Trustworthy By Design Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 requires transparency in labeling AI systems as compliant and mandates agencies to report noncompliance and barriers to Congress within specific timelines.

Trustworthy By Design Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 encourages collaboration with developers and stakeholders to verify elements of trustworthiness throughout the AI lifecycle.

Trustworthy By Design Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 sets the guidelines' effective date as the trigger for these provisions.

Chinese Military and Surveillance Company Sanctions Act of 2024 prohibits U.S. jurisdictional foreign exchange transactions involving sanctioned entities.

Chinese Military and Surveillance Company Sanctions Act of 2024 requires strict conditions or bans on U.S. accounts for foreign financial institutions conducting significant transactions with these entities.

Chinese Military and Surveillance Company Sanctions Act of 2024 obliges the President to respond to congressional queries regarding sanction eligibility within 30 days.

Chinese Military and Surveillance Company Sanctions Act of 2024 instructs the Secretary of the Treasury to annually assess sanction criteria compliance for specified entities and report to Congress.

Chinese Military and Surveillance Company Sanctions Act of 2024 encourages focus on sectors like AI, quantum tech, robotics, and others in sanction assessments.

Chinese Military and Surveillance Company Sanctions Act of 2024 implements penalties under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act for violations.

Chinese Military and Surveillance Company Sanctions Act of 2024 allows waiver of sanctions if deemed necessary for U.S. national security.

Chinese Military and Surveillance Company Sanctions Act of 2024 excludes intelligence, law enforcement, and humanitarian activities from sanctions.

Chinese Military and Surveillance Company Sanctions Act of 2024 sunsets authority to impose sanctions 7 years after enactment.

Workforce Data Enhancement Act establishes a grant program under the amended Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act for a workforce data quality initiative aimed at integrating and improving statewide longitudinal data systems.

Workforce Data Enhancement Act requires the Secretary to allocate up to 10% of specific funds to eligible entities, mainly state agencies, for enhancing data integration from education and workforce systems to strengthen program quality.

Workforce Data Enhancement Act mandates that eligible entities submit detailed applications describing proposed improvements, expected outcomes, and privacy measures.

Workforce Data Enhancement Act prioritizes grants to entities with multistate collaboration or those focusing on advancing interoperable data, private partnerships, and real-time data reporting, especially concerning emerging technologies like AI.

Workforce Data Enhancement Act permits grant use for developing state data systems, enhancing data standardization, and fostering data-driven decision-making.

Workforce Data Enhancement Act specifies requirements for a maximum three-year grant duration, supplemental funding use, and post-grant reporting on achievements.

Workforce Data Enhancement Act amends funding source provisions to include these new initiatives.

Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024 establishes research and extension grants for developing and evaluating the agricultural application of artificial intelligence.

Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024 emphasizes the use of AI to improve specialty crop production.

Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024 authorizes these initiatives under the amendments to the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990.

Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024 encourages research projects that focus on innovative methods and technologies enhancing agricultural efficiency.

Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024 places potential emphasis on mechanizing agricultural processes, though AI-specific focus is primarily on specialty crop production.

Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024 mandates the Department of Agriculture, Department of Energy, and National Science Foundation to conduct joint R&D activities.

Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024 requires establishing memoranda of understanding to coordinate efforts.

Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024 authorizes collaborative research in AI, machine learning, large-scale data analytics, and predictive analysis to optimize agricultural and rural energy systems.

Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024 facilitates development of methods for handling large data sets related to agriculture, environment, and supply chain.

Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024 promotes open data sharing and collaboration between federal agencies, labs, educational and nonprofit institutions, industry, and more, ensuring compliance with federal regulations.

Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024 supports infrastructure and workforce development for research identified as necessary by the involved agencies.

Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024 permits reimbursable agreements and collaborations with other federal agencies to enhance R&D effectiveness.

Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024 requires a report within two years detailing interagency coordination, achievements, future opportunities, and ongoing coordination efforts.

Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024 stipulates consistency with existing research security regulations.

Leadership in CET Act establishes a pilot program for expediting patent applications related to critical and emerging technologies, including AI, microelectronics, and quantum information science.

Leadership in CET Act requires the Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office to expedite patent processing through petitions.

Leadership in CET Act permits waiver of certain fees and requirements for accelerated examination processes.

Leadership in CET Act limits eligibility to U.S.-based entities or inventors and restricts applications to original, nonprovisional patents.

Leadership in CET Act terminates the program after issuing a patent within five years or upon accepting 10,000 applications, with a potential renewal for the same criteria.

Leadership in CET Act mandates public availability of information regarding application numbers, acceptance, and issued patents on the Office's website.

Leadership in CET Act requires a report to Congress assessing the pilot program's effectiveness post-termination, exempting this data collection from the Paperwork Reduction Act.

Improving Atmospheric River Forecasts Act mandates the establishment of an atmospheric river forecast improvement program aimed at reducing loss of life and property due to atmospheric river events.

Improving Atmospheric River Forecasts Act requires development of quantitative forecast metrics, incorporating machine learning and data assimilation for improved landfall predictions of atmospheric rivers and associated extreme weather conditions.

Improving Atmospheric River Forecasts Act directs the enhancement of dynamic modeling systems to provide detailed forecasts, including snow accumulation and hydrological impacts.

Improving Atmospheric River Forecasts Act encourages the integration of innovative observation technologies and AI methods to refine forecasting and improve water resource management.

Improving Atmospheric River Forecasts Act supports atmospheric river reconnaissance efforts, ensuring data availability and integration into forecasting systems, and mandates the establishment of observatories along the U.S. West Coast.

Improving Atmospheric River Forecasts Act focuses on improved communication and categorization of atmospheric river hazards to aid public understanding and preparedness.

Improving Atmospheric River Forecasts Act obliges submission of a comprehensive program plan detailing research activities and resources within 270 days of enactment.

Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act of 2024 mandates the Secretary of Defense to require competitive awards for cloud computing, data infrastructure, and foundation model solutions to promote security, resiliency, and competition.

Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act of 2024 ensures that the Government retains exclusive data access and use rights.

Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act of 2024 requires prioritization of intellectual property, data rights, and interoperability during procurement processes, with consideration for multi-cloud technology where suitable.

Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act of 2024 directs updates to the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to protect government-furnished data used in AI development and prevent unauthorized disclosure.

Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act of 2024 imposes penalties for violations, including fines and contract termination, but allows exemptions where national security is not compromised.

Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act of 2024 obliges annual reports from the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff assessing competition and market dynamics in the AI industry, with recommendations for legislative and administrative actions.

Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act of 2024 ensures public accessibility of these reports through the Department of Defense's website and other no-cost methods.

TRAIN Act enacts the "Transparency and Responsibility for Artificial Intelligence Networks Act" or "TRAIN Act."

TRAIN Act requires the United States district court clerk to issue a subpoena to AI model developers or deployers upon request from copyright owners.

TRAIN Act defines artificial intelligence terms including AI models and generative AI models used in the legal context.

TRAIN Act allows copyright owners, with a good faith belief of infringement, to request AI training data records.

TRAIN Act mandates that a subpoena requires model developers or deployers to disclose records of copyrighted works used in AI model training.

TRAIN Act details the procedure for the issuance and execution of subpoenas under the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.

TRAIN Act creates a rebuttable presumption of copyright copying if the subpoenaed party fails to comply.

TRAIN Act implements the new rules on the date of enactment.

Iowa (2019) SB 302 (Automated Driving System Motor Vehicles) defines key terms like "automated driving system" and "driverless-capable vehicle" relevant to motor vehicles operated by autonomous systems.

Iowa (2019) SB 302 (Automated Driving System Motor Vehicles) allows the operation of driverless-capable vehicles on public highways without a human driver present, provided they meet safety and compliance standards.

Iowa (2019) SB 302 (Automated Driving System Motor Vehicles) requires system-equipped vehicles to operate within designated operational domains and comply with state traffic and safety laws unless exempted.

Iowa (2019) SB 302 (Automated Driving System Motor Vehicles) mandates financial liability coverage for system-equipped vehicles before they can operate on public highways.

Iowa (2019) SB 302 (Automated Driving System Motor Vehicles) stipulates that automated vehicles involved in accidents must remain at the scene and report to law enforcement, holding vehicle owners accountable for compliance.

Iowa (2019) SB 302 (Automated Driving System Motor Vehicles) permits the operation of on-demand driverless-capable vehicle networks for transporting persons or goods, integrating with digital transport services.

Iowa (2019) SB 302 (Automated Driving System Motor Vehicles) grants exclusive governance and regulatory authority over automated systems to the state department, prohibiting additional local regulations or taxes on such systems.

S5344 Advancing Digital Freedom Act of 2024 requires the United States to prioritize digital freedom in foreign policy and diplomatic engagements.

S5344 Advancing Digital Freedom Act of 2024 mandates cooperation with countries committed to democratic technology use and development.

S5344 Advancing Digital Freedom Act of 2024 appoints a Coordinator for Digital Freedom within the Bureau of Cyberspace and Digital Policy to advance global digital freedom.

S5344 Advancing Digital Freedom Act of 2024 directs the Coordinator to engage with international actors to counter digital authoritarianism and support human rights-compliant technology governance.

S5344 Advancing Digital Freedom Act of 2024 instructs the Coordinator to promote democratic governance of artificial intelligence, emphasizing human rights and democracy.

S5344 Advancing Digital Freedom Act of 2024 requires ongoing publication of guidelines for protecting digital freedom in cyberspace, including the AI Risk Management Profile.

S5344 Advancing Digital Freedom Act of 2024 obliges annual reporting on global digital freedom, analyzing threats like digital authoritarianism, censorship, and AI governance risks.

S5344 Advancing Digital Freedom Act of 2024 advises on improving digital inclusion and information integrity.

S5344 Advancing Digital Freedom Act of 2024 tasks the Coordinator with making recommendations to enhance digital freedom through diplomatic channels.

DOGE Act mandates the prohibition of federal grant awards to applicants submitting duplicative or fraudulent applications, with an exception for institutions of higher education.

DOGE Act requires the joint determination of appropriate agencies to award grants when duplicative applications are identified.

DOGE Act obliges the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to establish an electronic system to track federal grant applications, preventing awards for identical purposes across executive agencies.

DOGE Act includes specific system requirements, such as storing awardee details and facilitating identification of essentially equivalent work.

DOGE Act directs the OMB, along with specific federal bodies, to report to Congress on the feasibility of using artificial intelligence to identify duplicative grant applications and detect waste, fraud, and abuse.

DOGE Act defines terms essential for the Act's implementation, including covered applications and executive agencies.

Enable Intelligence Community Partnerships Act of 2024 encourages the intelligence community to form private sector capital partnerships and consult with federal partners to improve technological advantages.

Enable Intelligence Community Partnerships Act of 2024 amends public-private talent exchange authority to focus on fields including artificial intelligence, computing, and cybersecurity.

Enable Intelligence Community Partnerships Act of 2024 extends the duration for temporary detail exchanges from 3 to 5 years.

Enable Intelligence Community Partnerships Act of 2024 prohibits detailed private-sector employees from accessing trade secrets or proprietary information of commercial value.

Enable Intelligence Community Partnerships Act of 2024 excludes private-sector organizations involved in employee detail exchanges from being considered as having organizational conflicts of interest by default.

Enable Intelligence Community Partnerships Act of 2024 requires identification and mitigation of conflicts of interest based on specific participation details.

Enable Intelligence Community Partnerships Act of 2024 mandates the Director of National Intelligence to submit annual reports to appropriate Congressional committees on program implementation and recommendations for enhancing the use of authorities.

Responsible AI Disclosure Act of 2024 enacts the "Responsible AI Disclosure Act of 2024".

Responsible AI Disclosure Act of 2024 mandates a study by covered agencies to establish and recommend standards for AI data categorization, AI model training practices, and data source identification.

Responsible AI Disclosure Act of 2024 requires assessment of AI model design, functionality, and compliance with federal laws including anti-discrimination and consumer protection.

Responsible AI Disclosure Act of 2024 obligates the issuance of a report within six months from enactment, detailing study findings and advising on potential legislative or regulatory revisions regarding AI disclosures.

Responsible AI Disclosure Act of 2024 empowers covered agencies, post-report, to mandate AI data reporting and disclosure by regulated entities and vendors, including data sources and model training specifics.

Responsible AI Disclosure Act of 2024 urges implementation of such requirements prior to report completion if deemed necessary.

Responsible AI Disclosure Act of 2024 defines "covered agencies" as key financial regulatory bodies, and "regulated entities" as those overseen by these agencies, including credit unions and financially regulated persons.

American Foreign Affairs Talent Expansion Act: Diversity in Diplomacy and Development, Section 112 (Mitigating bias in artificial intelligence use.) require international affairs agencies to employ experts, including technologists, social scientists, and legal experts, to develop a risk-mitigation framework for trustworthy AI systems, addressing bias in AI training data and applications.

American Foreign Affairs Talent Expansion Act: Diversity in Diplomacy and Development, Section 112 (Mitigating bias in artificial intelligence use.) mandate reports from each agency to appropriate congressional committees, describing efforts to ensure safe, secure, and trustworthy AI development and use, including testing and correcting for bias, starting one year after the enactment of the Act and every two years for the following eight years.

American Foreign Affairs Talent Expansion Act: Diversity in Diplomacy and Development, Section 112 (Mitigating bias in artificial intelligence use.) impose a congressional expectation to implement measures addressing AI bias to prevent negative or discriminatory outcomes in agency operations.

A bill to require a study on the use of commercial-off-the-shelf products and artificial intelligence technologies by the Internal Revenue Service. identifies the IRS's use of such technologies to enhance operational efficiency, improve taxpayer services, generate cost savings, ensure fair enforcement, and improve tax collection efforts.

A bill to require a study on the use of commercial-off-the-shelf products and artificial intelligence technologies by the Internal Revenue Service. requires the study to assess how the IRS manages AI-related risks, including errors, bias in audit selection, and data security.

A bill to require a study on the use of commercial-off-the-shelf products and artificial intelligence technologies by the Internal Revenue Service. includes information on IT modernization projects, detailing contractors, project scope, costs, and contracting approaches.

A bill to require a study on the use of commercial-off-the-shelf products and artificial intelligence technologies by the Internal Revenue Service. analyzes the allocation of expenses between contractors and IRS employees and compares costs between customized projects and commercial product alternatives.

Stop Smuggling Illicit Synthetic Drugs on U.S. Transportation Networks Act of 2024 mandate coordination with multiple agencies, including the National Science Foundation and the National Institute of Standards and Technology.

Stop Smuggling Illicit Synthetic Drugs on U.S. Transportation Networks Act of 2024 instruct submission of a report on the strategy to specified congressional committees within two years of the Act's enactment.

To amend and reauthorize the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and the Older Americans Act of 1965. mandates studies to assess AI's effectiveness in workforce systems, emphasizing technology's impact on service delivery, labor market data, end-user tools, and potential biases.

To amend and reauthorize the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and the Older Americans Act of 1965. requires analysis of how automation affects employment, skills development, and worker displacement.

To amend and reauthorize the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and the Older Americans Act of 1965. demands evaluation of AI and machine learning adoption by States in workforce systems, assessing accuracy and identifying biases.

To amend and reauthorize the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and the Older Americans Act of 1965. calls for alignment studies between workforce and education systems, using data integration to improve outcomes.

To amend and reauthorize the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and the Older Americans Act of 1965. obliges reports on AI-related studies and evaluations to be submitted to relevant Senate and House Committees and published publicly.

To amend and reauthorize the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and the Older Americans Act of 1965. sets limits on using authority if certain evaluations are not initiated or completed timely.

To amend and reauthorize the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and the Older Americans Act of 1965. requires Secretary-conducted evaluations on the effectiveness of programs under various conditions.

Transparency in Bureaucratic Communications Act amends the Inspector General Act of 1978 to require a detailed description of communications between federal establishments and internet service or content providers.

Transparency in Bureaucratic Communications Act includes communications concerning content moderation, user content such as posts, photos, and videos, and any interactions related to data inputs, algorithms, modeling, simulation processes, analysis tools, or related technologies.

Transparency in Bureaucratic Communications Act aims to enhance transparency in bureaucratic communications with digital platforms.

SCAM Platform Act mandates the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to develop an artificial intelligence-based tool to help the public identify likely scams within one year of this Act's enactment.

SCAM Platform Act requires the AI tool to accept various submission formats including emails, text messages, website URLs, and scans or photographs of physical materials.

SCAM Platform Act obliges the tool to evaluate the likelihood of submissions being scams and provide a rating to reflect this likelihood.

SCAM Platform Act defines "artificial intelligence" as per the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020.

SCAM Platform Act defines "scam" as any scheme designed to defraud by inducing a recipient to take actions against their interest, through false or misleading information.

Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Securing AI Task Force Act requires coordination of Agency efforts to improve the safe and secure design, development, adoption, and deployment of AI.

Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Securing AI Task Force Act ensures Agency collaboration in interagency and nongovernment AI-related initiatives.

Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Securing AI Task Force Act mandates assessment and evaluation of Agency safety initiatives to address AI challenges.

Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Securing AI Task Force Act leverages expertise to use AI in defending against cyber threats.

Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Securing AI Task Force Act coordinates efforts to advise stakeholders on AI-related cyber risks.

Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Securing AI Task Force Act identifies AI workforce gaps and proposes solutions.

Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Securing AI Task Force Act promotes secure adoption of AI-based software.

Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Securing AI Task Force Act recommends new initiatives for AI safety and security.

Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Securing AI Task Force Act ensures AI efforts meet privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties standards.

Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Securing AI Task Force Act supports publication and accuracy of the Agency’s AI use inventory.

Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Securing AI Task Force Act mandates biannual briefings to Congress on Task Force activities.

Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Securing AI Task Force Act sunsets the Act 5 years after enactment.

No AI Audits Act limits the Internal Revenue Service's (IRS) use of artificial intelligence (AI) for audits or investigations.

No AI Audits Act requires any IRS guidance on AI for audits to follow rule-making procedures under Section 553 of Title 5, U.S. Code.

No AI Audits Act prohibits the IRS from conducting audits or investigations initiated by AI unless the AI meets explainability principles set by the National Institute of Standards and Technology.

No AI Audits Act defines "artificial intelligence" according to the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020.

No AI Audits Act mandates the Comptroller General to audit and report on the IRS's AI use, including a cost-benefit analysis and the impact on taxpayer rights.

No AI Audits Act stipulates that IRS investigations or examinations must be initiated by a staff investigator, with documentation including the investigator's contact information.

Artificial Intelligence Weapon Accountability and Risk Evaluation Act of 2024 mandates the Secretary of Defense to create a ledger of all uses by the Department of Defense of AI-enabled weapon, targeting, and decision support systems within three years.

Artificial Intelligence Weapon Accountability and Risk Evaluation Act of 2024 requires the ledger to be a structured, indexed database that is regularly updated.

Artificial Intelligence Weapon Accountability and Risk Evaluation Act of 2024 calls on the Secretary of Defense to develop a risk assessment process to evaluate dependability, cybersecurity, privacy, and civilian harm risk for each AI system.

Artificial Intelligence Weapon Accountability and Risk Evaluation Act of 2024 mandates annual reevaluations of each system, and when an AI model receives an update, a new system is procured, or a new weapons review is conducted.

Artificial Intelligence Weapon Accountability and Risk Evaluation Act of 2024 requires annotations in the ledger when AI systems are shared, exported, or used internationally, noting additional risks.

Artificial Intelligence Weapon Accountability and Risk Evaluation Act of 2024 obligates annual progress reports and submissions to Congress, including the ledger and risk assessment findings, to be publicly accessible

Data Protection Act of 2024 establishes the Data Protection Agency (DPA) as an independent entity responsible for regulating high-risk data practices and the collection, processing, and sharing of personal data.

Data Protection Act of 2024 defines high-risk data practices, which include the use of automated decision systems and processes involving biometric information, and mandates high-risk data practice risk assessments and impact evaluations.

Data Protection Act of 2024 empowers the DPA to issue rules, conduct investigations, enforce federal privacy law, and impose penalties on violators.

Data Protection Act of 2024 requires large data aggregators, those with significant revenue or who process data of many individuals, to report compliance and undergo regular examinations.

Data Protection Act of 2024 transfers certain rulemaking and enforcement powers from the Federal Trade Commission to the DPA.

Data Protection Act of 2024 mandates coordination with other federal and state agencies to ensure consistent privacy regulation.

Data Protection Act of 2024 allows states to enforce protections, provided they do not conflict with this act.

Data Protection Act of 2024 authorizes appropriations for the DPA's operations and activities.

New York Assembly Bill A8808A enacts laws addressing artificial intelligence (AI) deceptive practices to protect privacy and combat unauthorized digital alterations.

New York Assembly Bill A8808A defines "digitization" as using AI and other technologies to alter realistic images or audio.

New York Assembly Bill A8808A amends civil rights laws to establish a private right of action for false light invasion of privacy and unauthorized use of likeness or voice, including digitally altered depictions.

New York Assembly Bill A8808A requires platforms and individuals to obtain consent before disseminating digitized images or audio depicting individuals in sensitive contexts without consent.

New York Assembly Bill A8808A mandates disclosures for political communications produced with digitized deceptive media within 60 days of an election, excluding satire, parody, or news reporting.

New York Assembly Bill A8808A prohibits coercion or impersonation using digitization, with heightened penalties for identity theft involving AI-altered representations.

New York Assembly Bill A8808A allows legal actions against those intentionally causing emotional, financial, or social harm via AI-fabricated media.

New York Assembly Bill A8808A incorporates these provisions into criminal and election laws, with penalties for violations and the possibility for injunctive relief.

North Carolina House Bill 591 amends offenses related to sexual extortion by making it a criminal act to use threats involving private images, including those modified by AI, to coerce victims, punishable as felonies depending on the circumstances.

North Carolina House Bill 591 enhances definitions related to minors in sexual content, including AI-modified images, and escalates penalties for various degrees of exploitation, employing AI tools.

North Carolina House Bill 591 mandates reporting to authorities if AI technology is used to distribute unlawful material depicting minors, extending jurisdiction over such offenses.

North Carolina House Bill 591 incorporates AI-generated images into existing laws against the unauthorized disclosure of private images, classifying violations as felonies and establishing a civil cause of action.

North Carolina House Bill 591 updates sex offender registration guidelines, emphasizing offenses involving digital or AI-enhanced sexual exploits of minors.

North Carolina House Bill 591 sets effective date for enforcement of these provisions as December 1, 2024.

Proposed Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI proposes a Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI emphasizing accountability, data quality, trusted development, and deployment, aligning with global best practices.

Proposed Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI establishes accountability by encouraging clear responsibility allocation among stakeholders within AI development chains and calls for extending cloud shared responsibility models to AI.

Proposed Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI emphasizes data quality, including the use of trusted data sources and addressing issues around personal data and copyright material for model training.

Proposed Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI calls for transparency in AI model safety measures, akin to "food labels," and suggests industry-standard practices for development, safety evaluation, and disclosure.

Proposed Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI proposes implementing incident reporting and third-party testing frameworks for AI safety and assurance.

Proposed Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI advocates for security measures specifically adapted for generative AI, including new tools and methods.

Proposed Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI highlights the importance of research in AI safety and alignment, international cooperation, and the use of AI for public good, including democratization of access and responsible AI adoption in public services.

Michigan House Bill 5507 allocates up to $500,000 to enhance awareness and responsible use of artificial intelligence in schools.

Michigan House Bill 5507 requires Michigan Virtual University to integrate AI principles in its training programs for educational personnel.

Michigan House Bill 5507 mandates the Michigan Virtual Learning Research Institute to research and recommend virtual education delivery models leveraging AI.

Michigan House Bill 5507 instructs the institute to analyze and report on AI-enhanced virtual learning effectiveness by reviewing data from virtual course providers.

Michigan House Bill 5507 encourages partnerships with districts to study AI-driven competency-based virtual learning models.

Michigan House Bill 5507 tasks the institute with policy recommendations to the governor on AI and virtual learning implementation.

Michigan House Bill 5507 designates funds for AI-related professional development programs for educators and stakeholders.

Michigan House Bill 5507 requires ongoing reports on the implementation of AI in virtual education, including its effectiveness, with a focus on elevating education delivery models in Michigan.

Michigan House Bill 5507 supports the dissemination of best practices and standards for AI-integrated virtual learning across the state.

New Jersey Senate Bill 3432 establishes the "Next New Jersey Program" to drive investment into New Jersey’s AI sector, creating jobs and economic opportunities.

New Jersey Senate Bill 3432 requires businesses to invest a minimum of $100 million in capital and create at least 100 new full-time jobs to be eligible for tax credits.

New Jersey Senate Bill 3432 mandates businesses or divisions engaged in AI or large-scale AI data centers, demonstrating over 50% of revenue or employment in AI activities.

New Jersey Senate Bill 3432 stipulates collaboration with New Jersey-based research entities or startups.

New Jersey Senate Bill 3432 enforces compliance with environmental and labor standards, including prevailing wage for construction workers.

New Jersey Senate Bill 3432 enables businesses meeting criteria to apply for tax credits valid until March 1, 2029.

New Jersey Senate Bill 3432 empowers the New Jersey Economic Development Authority to oversee eligibility and award decisions, ensuring businesses remain compliant to retain credits.

New Jersey Senate Bill 3432 allows tax credit transfer certificates, with conditions on their sale and application.

New Jersey Senate Bill 3432 caps overall tax credits under the act at $250 million annually from a broader $11.5 billion limit across various programs over nine years.

Wyoming House Bill 1 appropriates $2.5 million for building artificial intelligence expertise at the University of Wyoming, requiring a matching ratio of 1:1 from non-public sources.

Wyoming House Bill 1 specifies that the AI-related funding should not be included in the university's standard budget for the next fiscal biennium.

Wyoming House Bill 1 conditions the use of AI funds upon securing matched contributions from individuals, partnerships, corporations, or other entities.

Wyoming House Bill 1 prohibits the transfer or expenditure of AI appropriation for any purpose other than building AI expertise.

Wyoming House Bill 1 includes intent for developing AI expertise funding to be temporary and contingent on nonstate matching funds.

Wyoming House Bill 1 states that the appropriation's intent is not to support any office or program related to diversity, equity, and inclusion.

Wyoming House Bill 1 overall, emphasizes the development of AI expertise through matched funding, with specific conditions and limitations on its use and future budget inclusion.

Utah House Bill 534 amends legislation to define "deep technology" to include artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies.

Utah House Bill 534 mandates the development and oversight of a deep technology talent initiative by the board, effective May 1, 2024.

Utah House Bill 534 requires institutions of higher education to submit proposals for partnering with employers to create programs in deep technology fields.

Utah House Bill 534 stipulates proposal criteria must include program responsiveness to state needs, partnerships, and employer involvement.

Utah House Bill 534 obligates the advisory council to review and prioritize program proposals based on capacity expansion, integration, and cost-effectiveness.

Utah House Bill 534 directs the board to fund approved programs by evaluating recommendations from the advisory council and considering legislative appropriations.

Utah House Bill 534 requires funded institutions to report annually on program activities and outcomes, including student enrollment and employment metrics.

Utah House Bill 534 compels the board to provide an annual report on program successes and challenges to legislative committees.

Measures of Beijing Municipality on Promoting the Innovative Development of Artificial General Intelligence mobilizes commercial computing resources to meet the requirements of the AGI sector, showcasing cooperation with cloud service providers to enhance access to diverse and high-quality computing power.

Measures of Beijing Municipality on Promoting the Innovative Development of Artificial General Intelligence promotes the construction of new computing facilities, including the Beijing AI Public Computing Power Center, to advance computing capabilities.

Measures of Beijing Municipality on Promoting the Innovative Development of Artificial General Intelligence establishes an integrated multi-cloud computing management platform to optimize computing power management and operations.

Measures of Beijing Municipality on Promoting the Innovative Development of Artificial General Intelligence collects high-quality training datasets, ensuring legal compliance and promoting the trading of data through legitimate channels.

Measures of Beijing Municipality on Promoting the Innovative Development of Artificial General Intelligence plans to set up data training bases and a crowdsourcing service platform for dataset annotation, enhancing data quality and collaboration.

Measures of Beijing Municipality on Promoting the Innovative Development of Artificial General Intelligence explores innovative algorithms for large models, supporting an open-source technical ecosystem and developing governance tools for data management.

Measures of Beijing Municipality on Promoting the Innovative Development of Artificial General Intelligence facilitates the practical application of AGI in various sectors, including government, medicine, finance, and urban governance.

Measures of Beijing Municipality on Promoting the Innovative Development of Artificial General Intelligence innovates regulatory policies, promoting inclusive and prudent supervision systems while strengthening network and data security.

Virginia 2024 SB 731 defines "child pornography" to include sexually explicit visual material involving identifiable or depicted minors, affecting both real and digitally created images.

Virginia 2024 SB 731 establishes penalties for production, solicitation, and financing of child pornography, escalating based on the minor’s age and the offender's age difference, with mandatory minimum sentences.

Virginia 2024 SB 731 infers depicted individuals presented as minors under 18 in visual material are minors for the purposes of prosecution.

Virginia 2024 SB 731 allows prosecution in the jurisdiction where the act occurs, the offender resides, or where the material is associated.

Virginia 2024 SB 731 notes potential increases in imprisonment periods, requiring a minimum fiscal impact assignment of $50,000 due to unknown appropriations for adult and juvenile facilities.

G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy (Annex "G20 AI Principles") support the responsible stewardship of trustworthy AI by engaging stakeholders to achieve inclusive growth, sustainable development, and well-being.

G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy (Annex "G20 AI Principles") require AI actors to respect human-centered values, including the rule of law, human rights, and democratic values, throughout the AI lifecycle, supported by appropriate safeguards.

G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy (Annex "G20 AI Principles") commit AI actors to transparency and explainability, providing clear information to foster AI understanding and accountability.

G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy (Annex "G20 AI Principles") ensure robustness, security, and safety of AI systems, with traceability and systematic risk management throughout their lifecycle.

G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy (Annex "G20 AI Principles") hold AI actors accountable for aligning with the principles based on roles and context.

G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy (Annex "G20 AI Principles") encourage governments to invest in AI R&D, supporting open, unbiased datasets, and fostering a digital AI ecosystem.

G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy (Annex "G20 AI Principles") promote an enabling policy environment for AI, ensuring policy adaptation, assessment mechanisms, and readiness for labor market transformation.

G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy (Annex "G20 AI Principles") engage in international cooperation to advance AI principles, share AI knowledge, and develop global technical standards.

G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy (Annex "G20 AI Principles") encourage multi-stakeholder collaboration to monitor AI developments and ensure adherence to these principles.

Dubai International Financial Centre Data Protection Regulations, Regulation 10 ("Personal data processed through autonomous and semi-autonomous systems") requires Deployers and Operators of autonomous and semi-autonomous systems to adhere to personal data processing principles.

Dubai International Financial Centre Data Protection Regulations, Regulation 10 ("Personal data processed through autonomous and semi-autonomous systems") mandates clear notification to users of such systems about underlying technology and data processing purposes, with detailed descriptions of system capabilities and safeguards.

Dubai International Financial Centre Data Protection Regulations, Regulation 10 ("Personal data processed through autonomous and semi-autonomous systems") obligates the provision of evidence of compliance with audit and certification requirements, and human intervention algorithms in cases of bias or legal non-compliance.

Dubai International Financial Centre Data Protection Regulations, Regulation 10 ("Personal data processed through autonomous and semi-autonomous systems") imposes design requirements focused on ethics, fairness, transparency, security, and accountability.

Dubai International Financial Centre Data Protection Regulations, Regulation 10 ("Personal data processed through autonomous and semi-autonomous systems") prohibits systems from processing personal data unless in compliance with human-defined purposes and legal frameworks.

Dubai International Financial Centre Data Protection Regulations, Regulation 10 ("Personal data processed through autonomous and semi-autonomous systems") forbids use in high-risk processing without compliance with certification requirements and appointment of an Autonomous Systems Officer.

Dubai International Financial Centre Data Protection Regulations, Regulation 10 ("Personal data processed through autonomous and semi-autonomous systems") deems Deployers as Controllers and Operators as Processors of personal data.

Dubai International Financial Centre Data Protection Regulations, Regulation 10 ("Personal data processed through autonomous and semi-autonomous systems") allows data subjects to challenge processing outcomes per applicable law.

Connecticut (2017) SB 260 establishes a pilot program for testing fully autonomous vehicles in up to four municipalities, requiring participation from autonomous vehicle testers and compliance with specific operational constraints.

Connecticut (2017) SB 260 mandates that autonomous vehicle testers register vehicles, provide liability insurance, and ensure a licensed operator is present who can take manual control if needed.

Connecticut (2017) SB 260 prohibits testing on limited access highways and allows the Secretary of the Office of Policy and Management to halt testing if public safety is at risk or compliance issues arise.

Connecticut (2017) SB 260 creates a task force to study autonomous vehicle regulation, evaluate national and state standards, and assess the pilot program, providing reports on findings and recommendations for potential legislation.

Connecticut (2017) SB 260 requires the Secretary to submit annual reports on the pilot program's progress to the General Assembly’s transportation committee.

Connecticut (2017) SB 260 stipulates the task force composition, appointment deadlines, and reporting requirements, with a final report due by January 1, 2019.

Simplify, Don't Amplify the IRS Act, Sec. 201 ("Tax Gap Projection") mandates the Commissioner of Internal Revenue to use artificial intelligence, including neural machine learning, to reduce taxpayer burden during National Research Program audits and improve the accuracy of tax gap projections.

Simplify, Don't Amplify the IRS Act, Sec. 201 ("Tax Gap Projection") requires use of AI and data analysis tools to calculate and project the tax gap, which is the difference between taxes owed and taxes collected.

Simplify, Don't Amplify the IRS Act, Sec. 201 ("Tax Gap Projection") prohibits conducting more National Research Program audits in any fiscal year than the number conducted in fiscal year 2022.

Simplify, Don't Amplify the IRS Act, Sec. 201 ("Tax Gap Projection") obligates the Commissioner to submit an annual tax gap projection to Congress, detailing the estimate using the latest data available, by July 31 each year.

Simplify, Don't Amplify the IRS Act, Sec. 201 ("Tax Gap Projection") defines the term "tax gap" as the difference between tax liabilities owed under the Internal Revenue Code and those actually collected by the IRS.
