text: New Mexico Senate Bill 192 appropriates $290,000 for the purchase of artificial intelligence equipment and to contract with consultants at the ASK Academy Charter School in Sandoval County.

Oklahoma H 3642 amends Oklahoma laws to enhance penalties for offenses involving child pornography, specifically targeting AI-generated images.

Oklahoma H 3642 defines "child pornography" to include computer-generated images and altered images that depict minors in sexually explicit conduct, regardless of whether the image is real or synthetic.

Oklahoma H 3642 establishes that possessing, distributing, or creating such images, including those utilizing AI technology, is a felony with penalties up to 20 years imprisonment and a $25,000 fine.

Oklahoma H 3642 specifies that possession of 100 or more images constitutes aggravated possession, punishable by life imprisonment and a $10,000 fine, with required sex offender registration.

Oklahoma H 3642 clarifies that AI-generated and computer-altered images count as independent offenses.

Oklahoma H 3642 mandates that this act becomes effective on November 1, 2024.

Minnesota House Bill 4772 amends Minnesota law to criminalize the dissemination of deep fakes intended to influence elections.

Minnesota House Bill 4772 prohibits the distribution of deep fakes within 90 days before elections or political conventions without consent if intended to harm a candidate or influence election outcomes.

Minnesota House Bill 4772 excludes broadcasters following federal law from these prohibitions.

Minnesota House Bill 4772 imposes penalties for violations, including imprisonment up to five years and fines up to $10,000 based on prior offenses or intent to cause harm.

Minnesota House Bill 4772 requires that candidates convicted under this law forfeit their nomination or office.

Minnesota House Bill 4772 disqualifies individuals convicted under this law from holding certain public offices.

Minnesota House Bill 4772 sets the effective date for July 1, 2024, applicable to crimes committed thereafter.

Minnesota Senate Bill 2909 requires the superintendent to prepare an annual report on the Minnesota Fusion Center (MNFC), detailing its general activities and monitored types, including AI or social media analysis tools.

Minnesota Senate Bill 2909 mandates inclusion of the MNFC's budget, staffing, and the technological tools utilized, specifically AI and data analysis technologies.

Minnesota Senate Bill 2909 obliges reporting on audit findings, data requests, suspicious activity reports (SARs), and the impact of AI tools in processing these reports.

Minnesota Senate Bill 2909 specifies the report must contain information on the MNFC's collaborations with local, state, and federal agencies, including data sharing and investigations aided by SARs and requests for information (RFIs).

Minnesota Senate Bill 2909 ensures the report's availability to relevant legislative committees and online by February 15 each year, starting in 2024.

California (2017) AB 1444 authorize the Livermore Amador Valley Transit Authority to conduct a shared autonomous vehicle (SAV) demonstration project in the City of Dublin, California, for vehicles lacking traditional controls such as a steering wheel or pedals.

California (2017) AB 1444 require vehicles to operate below 35 miles per hour.

California (2017) AB 1444 mandate obtaining insurance or self-insurance of five million dollars and approval from local authorities.

California (2017) AB 1444 certify compliance with federal safety standards and National Highway Traffic Safety Administration guidance, ensuring vehicles operate only in approved conditions.

California (2017) AB 1444 require disclosure of personal data collection to participants and establish a law enforcement interaction plan.

California (2017) AB 1444 oblige reporting of accidents and disengagements during testing to the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV).

California (2017) AB 1444 allow the DMV to require data collection for safety evaluations.

California (2017) AB 1444 specify that the section becomes inoperative on May 1, 2018, and repeals on January 1, 2019.

California (2017) AB 1444 clarify that this project does not influence statewide autonomous vehicle regulations.

Remarks by Ambassador Zhang Jun at the UN Security Council Briefing on Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities and Risks for International Peace and Security calls for adherence to ethical principles in AI development, emphasizing people-oriented AI and the need to establish ethical norms and regulatory systems tailored to national conditions.

Remarks by Ambassador Zhang Jun at the UN Security Council Briefing on Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities and Risks for International Peace and Security stresses safety and controllability, urging the international community to establish risk control mechanisms and accountability structures to prevent AI misuse and autonomous lethal technologies.

Remarks by Ambassador Zhang Jun at the UN Security Council Briefing on Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities and Risks for International Peace and Security advocates for fairness and inclusiveness, highlighting the importance of ensuring equal access to AI benefits for developing countries and opposing technological hegemony and exclusionary practices.

Remarks by Ambassador Zhang Jun at the UN Security Council Briefing on Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities and Risks for International Peace and Security promotes openness and inclusivity, encouraging international cooperation across disciplines, regions, and organizations under the UN framework to create a non-discriminatory environment for AI.

Remarks by Ambassador Zhang Jun at the UN Security Council Briefing on Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities and Risks for International Peace and Security emphasizes peaceful utilization of AI, underscoring the necessity of AI for sustainable development and responsible defense policies to prevent its misuse in military contexts.

Remarks by Ambassador Zhang Jun at the UN Security Council Briefing on Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities and Risks for International Peace and Security underlines China's commitment to international cooperation in AI governance, referencing past initiatives and ongoing efforts to establish a global framework for AI security governance.

Michigan HB 5143 define "artificial intelligence" as a machine-based system capable of making predictions, recommendations, or decisions for human-defined objectives, affecting real or virtual environments, using both machine and human inputs.

Michigan HB 5143 mandate AI systems to perceive environments, abstract perceptions into models through automated analysis, and use model inference for decision-making.

Michigan HB 5143 condition enactment of this amendment on the passage of House Bill No. 5141.

California (2021-2022) SB 1398 prohibits dealers or manufacturers in California from selling or upgrading vehicles with partial driving automation features without providing a distinct notice, including the feature's name, functions, and limitations.

California (2021-2022) SB 1398 prevents manufacturers or dealers from using language in marketing materials that implies partial driving automation features make a vehicle autonomous when it does not.

California (2021-2022) SB 1398 defines "partial driving automation feature" according to the Society of Automotive Engineers' Level 2 partial driving automation.

California (2021-2022) SB 1398 affirms that compliance with these provisions does not alter existing duty of care or civil liability for manufacturers or dealers.

California (2021-2022) SB 1398 obligates manufacturers to provide dealers with necessary information to comply with notice requirements.

California (2021-2022) SB 1398 exempts manufacturers from violation if they provide required information to dealers and dealers fail to notify buyers.

California (2021-2022) SB 1398 states that no reimbursement is needed under California's constitutional provisions due to changes in crime definition or penalties.

Google AI Principles commit to developing AI responsibly, focusing on social benefits by evaluating potential applications for transformative impacts in various fields.

Google AI Principles seek to avoid creating or reinforcing unfair biases, particularly concerning sensitive characteristics.

Google AI Principles ensure AI systems are designed and tested for safety, applying strong security practices and closely monitoring post-deployment.

Google AI Principles maintain accountability to people by allowing for feedback, explanations, and human control over AI technologies.

Google AI Principles incorporate privacy principles, offering notice, consent, and transparency, while upholding privacy safeguards in AI architecture.

Google AI Principles aspire to scientific excellence, leveraging AI for advancements in critical scientific areas.

Google AI Principles limit use to applications adhering to these principles, considering factors like purpose, uniqueness, scale, and Google's role.

Google AI Principles prohibit AI involvement in technologies causing harm, weapons, surveillance violating norms, or contravening international law.

Google AI Principles adapt the prohibitions list as AI experience grows.

Maryland House Bill 1390 directs the Interagency Commission on School Construction to report to the General Assembly by December 15, 2024.

Maryland House Bill 1390 requires the report to assess the eligibility for school construction funding for artificial intelligence weapon detection systems.

Illinois HB 4844 (2024), Section 90 ("Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force") amends the Department of Innovation and Technology Act by establishing the Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force.

Illinois HB 4844 (2024), Section 90 ("Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force") mandates the Task Force to investigate and report on generative AI and natural language processing software.

Illinois HB 4844 (2024), Section 90 ("Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force") comprises the Task Force of government officials, educators, cybersecurity experts, AI experts, business and labor association members, and other stakeholders.

Illinois HB 4844 (2024), Section 90 ("Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force") requires the Task Force to hold at least five public meetings across various Illinois regions in a hybrid format.

Illinois HB 4844 (2024), Section 90 ("Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force") obligates the Task Force to recommend legislation to protect consumer information, suggest model policies for AI use in schools, and assess AI's impact on public services, civil rights, the workforce, and cybersecurity.

Illinois HB 4844 (2024), Section 90 ("Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force") instructs the Department to provide administrative and technical support to the Task Force.

Illinois HB 4844 (2024), Section 90 ("Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force") requires the Task Force to file a report by December 31, 2024, with the Governor and the General Assembly summarizing its findings and recommendations.

New Jersey (2019) Assembly Joint Resolution 164 establishes the "New Jersey Advanced Autonomous Vehicle Task Force" to study and recommend policies for the safe integration of autonomous vehicles on state roads.

New Jersey (2019) Assembly Joint Resolution 164 comprises 11 members, including key state officials and public experts appointed by the Governor.

New Jersey (2019) Assembly Joint Resolution 164 mandates the task force to hold its initial meeting within 90 days of the law's effective date and to elect a chair from among its members.

New Jersey (2019) Assembly Joint Resolution 164 requires the task force to issue a report within 180 days after its first meeting, evaluating existing laws, proposing pilot programs, and suggesting legislative measures.

New Jersey (2019) Assembly Joint Resolution 164 entitles the task force to utilize the services of state employees and receive assistance from the New Jersey Motor Vehicle Commission, Department of Transportation, and Alan M. Voorhees Transportation Center.

New Jersey (2019) Assembly Joint Resolution 164 defines "advanced autonomous vehicle" as one with a driving automation level of 3, 4, or 5, per SAE J3016 standards.

New Jersey (2019) Assembly Joint Resolution 164 expires the act upon the report's submission.

Iowa S 2243 (Sexual Exploitation of Minors, Use of Falsely Created Images) amends existing law to make it unlawful to knowingly purchase or possess visual depictions of a minor engaging in a prohibited sexual act or its simulation.

Iowa S 2243 (Sexual Exploitation of Minors, Use of Falsely Created Images) requires separate prosecution and punishment for each different minor depicted in such visual content, though multiple depictions of the same minor are treated as a single offense.

Iowa S 2243 (Sexual Exploitation of Minors, Use of Falsely Created Images) classifies a first offense as a class "D" felony and a second or subsequent offense as a class "C" felony.

Iowa S 2243 (Sexual Exploitation of Minors, Use of Falsely Created Images) establishes that prior convictions or deferred judgments under this law, or similar laws in other jurisdictions, constitute second or subsequent offenses.

South Carolina 2023 H 4754 (Section 4) holds a licensee accountable for all work produced with the assistance of artificial intelligence, machine learning, or similar programs.

South Carolina 2023 H 4754 (Section 4) treats violations committed through the use of these technologies as if committed directly by the licensee.

Oregon Senate Bill 5701 increases the General Fund appropriation to the Higher Education Coordinating Commission for public university programs by $100,000.

Oregon Senate Bill 5701 allocates this increased funding to the University of Oregon Labor Education and Research Center.

Oregon Senate Bill 5701 directs the Center to research the potential workforce impacts of automation and artificial intelligence across Oregon’s key economic industries.

G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy (Section I, Subsection 3 "Human-centered Artificial Intelligence") recognizes AI's potential to promote inclusive economic growth and societal benefits, advancing sustainable and inclusive societies while empowering individuals.

G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy (Section I, Subsection 3 "Human-centered Artificial Intelligence") commits to addressing societal challenges posed by AI, such as transitions in the labor market, privacy, security, and ethical issues, through a human-centered approach guided by the G20 AI Principles.

G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy (Section I, Subsection 3 "Human-centered Artificial Intelligence") stipulates principles of inclusive growth, human-centered values, transparency, robustness, and accountability to maximize AI benefits while minimizing risks, with a focus on international cooperation and inclusion of developing countries.

G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy (Section I, Subsection 3 "Human-centered Artificial Intelligence") affirms the need to promote privacy protection, AI capacity building, and skills development.

G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy (Section I, Subsection 3 "Human-centered Artificial Intelligence") commits to international cooperation in research, policy development, and information sharing through the G20 Repository of Digital Policies and collaborative efforts.

North Carolina House Bill 259 allocates $3.2 million to New Hanover County Schools and $2 million to Davidson County Schools for an AI School Safety Pilot Program.

North Carolina House Bill 259 requires use of funds to implement AI technology into existing school safety systems, including access controls, alerting protocols, and intercom systems.

North Carolina House Bill 259 mandates participating public school units to report to the Joint Legislative Education Oversight Committee by January 15, 2025.

North Carolina House Bill 259 directs reports to include details on school participation, fund usage, impact on safety outcomes, AI system capabilities compared to traditional safety measures, and any additional relevant information.

Maryland Senate Bill 360 adds $500,000 in general funds to support the Center for Equitable Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Systems at Morgan State University.

Maryland Senate Bill 360 prohibits the transfer of unexpended funds to any other purpose.

Maryland Senate Bill 360 requires unspent funds to revert to the General Fund.

Maryland Senate Bill 1068 requires the Maryland Department of Information Technology to evaluate the potential use of artificial intelligence in developing a statewide virtual 3-1-1 portal for nonemergency government information and services.

Maryland Senate Bill 1068 mandates the prioritization of creating the virtual 3-1-1 portal if the AI application is deemed feasible.

Maryland Senate Bill 1068 sets the effective date of this Act as July 1, 2024.

Maryland Senate Bill 1068 receives approval from the Governor on May 9, 2024.

Washington Senate Bill 5950 allocate $300,000 from the general fund for fiscal year 2024 to the city of Seattle for leasing space dedicated to nonprofit and academic institutions.

Washington Senate Bill 5950 provide $500,000 for fiscal year 2025 for the same purpose.

Washington Senate Bill 5950 focus efforts on incubating technology business startups with an emphasis on artificial intelligence.

Washington Senate Bill 5950 support the development and teaching of curricula aimed at equipping workers with skills to utilize AI as a business resource.

DEEPFAKES Accountability Act, Sec. 2 ("Transparency Requirements") outlines transparency requirements for advanced technological false personation records, requiring producers of such records to include content provenance technologies to identify alterations, as well as disclosures to detail the extent of alterations.

DEEPFAKES Accountability Act, Sec. 2 ("Transparency Requirements") mandates specific disclosure formats for audiovisual, visual, and audio records.

DEEPFAKES Accountability Act, Sec. 2 ("Transparency Requirements") imposes criminal penalties, including fines and imprisonment of up to 5 years, for intentionally failing to disclose or altering existing disclosures.

DEEPFAKES Accountability Act, Sec. 2 ("Transparency Requirements") imposes civil penalties up to $150,000 per violation and allows for private rights of action for damages and injunctive relief.

DEEPFAKES Accountability Act, Sec. 2 ("Transparency Requirements") establishes coordinators for deepfake-related violations in each U.S. Attorney’s Office.

Sensible Classification Act of 2023 mandates the research and recommendation of AI and machine learning solutions for efficient classification and declassification systems, to be interoperable across the Federal Government.

Sensible Classification Act of 2023 requires the Administrator of the Office of Electronic Government to consult with key defense and intelligence agencies for technology implementation and submit a report on the recommended solution.

Federal AI Governance and Transparency Act amends chapter 35 of title 44, United States Code, to establish Federal AI system governance requirements.

Federal AI Governance and Transparency Act instructs Federal actions involving AI to align with the Constitution, relevant laws, and policies, protecting civil rights and privacy.

Federal AI Governance and Transparency Act mandates the assessment and management of AI risks before deployment, ensuring AI outcomes remain ethical and accurate.

Federal AI Governance and Transparency Act requires transparency and explainability of AI systems' purpose, operations, and outcomes to maintain safety and security, and protect against vulnerabilities.

Federal AI Governance and Transparency Act obligates regular testing and oversight of AI applications to ensure they align with intended purposes and create mechanisms to deactivate AI systems that do not meet standards.

Federal AI Governance and Transparency Act instructs agencies to publicly disclose AI use to stakeholders and establish notification and appeal processes for AI-based decisions.

Federal AI Governance and Transparency Act establishes a Federal AI System Inventory for cataloging agency AI governance charters to be publicly available and regularly updated.

To direct the Director of the National Institutes of Health to establish a grant program to facilitate research regarding the use of generative artificial intelligence in health care, and for other purposes. prioritizes grants for entities promoting AI adoption in health care, investing in workforce development, mitigating workforce burnout, reducing health disparities, and improving care for medically underserved populations.

Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy establishes AI Safety Level (ASL) Standards to guide safe deployment and security for current and future AI models, categorizing measures into Deployment and Security Standards.

Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy requires all current models to meet ASL-2 standards, focusing on safe usage and protection from unauthorized access.

Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy introduces Capability Thresholds to determine when stronger safeguards (ASL-3 or higher) are needed, specifying Required Safeguards for particular risks including Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) capabilities and Autonomous AI R&D.

Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy mandates comprehensive assessments to ensure models remain below Capability Thresholds, with stricter ASL-3 standards implemented if thresholds are surpassed.

Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy outlines internal governance practices including a Responsible Scaling Officer role, transparency measures, and procedures for noncompliance whistleblowing.

Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy commits to public transparency, expert input, and notifying US Government if standards beyond ASL-2 are needed.

Tools to Address Known Exploitation by Immobilizing Technological Deepfakes on Websites and Networks Act requires covered platforms to establish a takedown process for such depictions, and mandates them to remove the content within 48 hours upon valid request.

Tools to Address Known Exploitation by Immobilizing Technological Deepfakes on Websites and Networks Act levels criminal punishments, including imprisonment, on violators of this law.

Tools to Address Known Exploitation by Immobilizing Technological Deepfakes on Websites and Networks Act grants enforcement authority to the Federal Trade Commission.

Tools to Address Known Exploitation by Immobilizing Technological Deepfakes on Websites and Networks Act defines key terms relevant to the instrument, including "covered platform," "deepfake," and "intimate visual depiction."

Safe and Secure Innovation for Frontier Artificial Intelligence Models Act (SB 1047) mandates annual independent audits and public disclosure of redacted audit reports and obligates developers to report AI safety incidents to the Attorney General within 72 hours.

Safe and Secure Innovation for Frontier Artificial Intelligence Models Act (SB 1047) establishes policies for entities operating computer clusters to assess whether customers intend to use the clusters for training covered models.

Safe and Secure Innovation for Frontier Artificial Intelligence Models Act (SB 1047) creates the Board of Frontier Models to update AI model thresholds and auditing requirements, ensuring alignment with technological advancements and best practices.

Safe and Secure Innovation for Frontier Artificial Intelligence Models Act (SB 1047) imposes penalties for non-compliance, including civil penalties, injunctive relief, and punitive damages.

Safe and Secure Innovation for Frontier Artificial Intelligence Models Act (SB 1047) introduces CalCompute, a public cloud computing cluster to support AI research and innovation, with a framework to be developed by a consortium.

OpenAI Charter pledges to assist other safety-conscious AGI projects nearing completion, rather than compete, under specific conditions.

OpenAI Charter strive for technical leadership within OpenAI and cooperate with other research and policy institutions.

OpenAI Charter commit to multistakeholder cooperation and publish its research while acknowledging potential safety and security constraints on traditional AI research publishing.

Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis Internet Information Services prohibits generative AI ("deep synthesis") systems in China from producing a variety of forms of unwanted content, including false information or content that harms lawful rights, national security and "social order."

Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis Internet Information Services requires deep synthesis systems to verify the true identity of each of their users.

Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis Internet Information Services requires deep synthesis developers to assess the security of their AI systems, including by assessing the systems' cybersecurity attributes and their ability to abide by relevant regulations.

Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis Internet Information Services requires deep synthesis systems to notify any individuals whose biometric information is edited in the production of AI-generated content.

Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis Internet Information Services requires the labelling or watermarking  of realistic deep synthesis content that could potentially mislead or confuse the public.

Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis Internet Information Services requires deep synthesis developers to submit filings with the relevant authorities, and requires regulators to carry out inspections of deep synthesis systems.

STAND with Taiwan Act of 2023 mandates the imposition of sanctions on the People's Republic of China if the People’s Liberation Army initiates a military invasion of Taiwan.

STAND with Taiwan Act of 2023 requires sanctions against Chinese officials and entities involved in military campaigns or efforts undermining Taiwan's security and infrastructure.

STAND with Taiwan Act of 2023 blocks property and imposes visa restrictions on identified Chinese officials and affiliates involved in military and coercive actions against Taiwan.

STAND with Taiwan Act of 2023 prohibits U.S. financial institutions from investments that benefit Chinese government-controlled entities or priority sectors like artificial intelligence and other advanced technologies.

STAND with Taiwan Act of 2023 bans the listing and trading of securities of Chinese entities on U.S. securities exchanges following an invasion.

STAND with Taiwan Act of 2023 prohibits the importation of goods from China post-invasion unless exceptions for national security are made.

STAND with Taiwan Act of 2023 grants the President authority to enforce sanctions and provides for penalties under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 articulates characteristics of trustworthy AI, including validity, reliability, safety, security, accountability, explainability, privacy enhancement, and fairness in managing harmful bias.

NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 encourages a balance of these characteristics based on AI systems' context of use, noting tradeoffs such as interpretability versus privacy.

NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 emphasizes the importance of human judgment in deciding metrics and thresholds for AI trustworthiness.

NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 stipulates that trustworthy AI depends on social and organizational behavior, datasets, model choices, and human interactions.

NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 mandates addressing AI risks through ongoing testing, monitoring, and balancing accuracy and robustness.

NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 calls for clear information and responsible decision-making to ensure safe AI operation.

NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 advocates for secure and resilient AI systems that withstand adverse events and protect against unauthorized access.

NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 promotes transparency and accountability to enhance confidence in AI systems, with transparency enabling actionable redress.

NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 urges explainability and interpretability to improve understanding of AI system operations and outputs.

NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 encourages privacy-enhancing technologies to safeguard autonomy and identity, acknowledging tradeoffs with accuracy.

NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 highlights fairness in AI, addressing harmful bias and discrimination, and recognizing systemic, computational, and human-cognitive biases.

NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 outlines AI risk management framework (AI RMF) functions: GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE, emphasizing a continuous and iterative process.

NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 specifies GOVERN function for cultivating risk management culture, policies, and accountability in AI development and deployment.

NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 describes MAP function for establishing context and understanding AI system impacts to inform risk management decisions.

NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 details MEASURE function for using tools and methodologies to assess AI risks and system trustworthiness.

NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 explains MANAGE function for prioritizing and responding to AI risks, maximizing benefits, and managing third-party risks.

Artificial Intelligence Bug Bounty Act of 2023 mandates the Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense to develop a bug bounty program for AI products within 180 days of enactment.

Artificial Intelligence Bug Bounty Act of 2023 allows collaboration with other government agencies possessing cybersecurity and AI expertise during program development.

Artificial Intelligence Bug Bounty Act of 2023 authorizes the implementation of the developed bug bounty program.

Artificial Intelligence Bug Bounty Act of 2023 ensures that Department of Defense contracts permit participation in the bug bounty program.

Artificial Intelligence Bug Bounty Act of 2023 requires the Chief to brief congressional defense committees within one year on the development, implementation, and long-term plans of relevant bug bounty programs.

AI Labeling Act of 2023 requires content generated by AI to include clear and conspicuous disclosures marking content as AI-generated.

AI Labeling Act of 2023 mandates the disclosure to identify content as AI-generated, the tool used to create output, and the creation date and time, ensuring disclosures are permanent or not easily removed.

AI Labeling Act of 2023 compels developers and third-party licensees of generative AI systems to implement procedures preventing content distribution without disclosures, including contractual obligations and certifying compliance.

AI Labeling Act of 2023 treats violations as unfair or deceptive acts under the Federal Trade Commission Act, granting enforcement powers to the FTC.

AI Labeling Act of 2023 establishes a working group to develop AI-generated content detection standards and assist platforms in identifying AI-generated content.

AI Labeling Act of 2023 requires the working group to publish a framework with guidelines and submit a report to Congress recommending legislative or administrative actions.

An Act concerning consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems. requires developers of high-risk AI systems to disclose foreseeable uses and risks of their systems, the inputs used in their training data, and how the systems were evaluated for performance.

An Act concerning consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems. requires developers to display these disclosures publicly on their websites in a public use case inventory.

An Act concerning consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems. mandates developers to disclose to the Colorado Attorney General, within 90 days, if their systems have caused or will likely cause algorithmic discrimination.

An Act concerning consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems. requires deployers of high-risk AI systems to notify consumers of how AI is used to make consequential decisions and inform them of their right to opt out of the processing of their personal data.

An Act concerning consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems. requires deployers to give consumers the opportunity to correct erroneous personal data and appeal adverse consequential decisions.

An Act concerning consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems. mandates deployers to make all these disclosures publicly available on their websites.

An Act concerning consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems. provides exemptions to the Colorado AI Act for certain deployers of high-risk AI systems including those who employ less than 50 people and do not use thier own data to train the system.

An Act concerning consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems. grants the Colorado Attorney General exclusive authority to enforce all regulations laid out by this act and engage in any additional rulemaking necessary for the implementation and enforcement of this act.

Microsoft Responsible AI Standard, v2 mandates Microsoft to conduct Impact Assessments for AI systems early in development to evaluate societal impacts, ensuring AI systems are fit for purpose, with annual updates and reviews for significant adverse impacts.

Microsoft Responsible AI Standard, v2 demands human oversight by identifying responsible stakeholders, providing necessary tools, and ensuring appropriate documentation for system control and intervention.

Microsoft Responsible AI Standard, v2 requires intelligibility for decision-making, enabling stakeholders to interpret system outputs and minimize automation bias.

Microsoft Responsible AI Standard, v2 mandates transparency and communication about system capabilities, limitations, and any AI-generated content.

Microsoft Responsible AI Standard, v2 ensures fairness by focusing on quality of service and opportunities and minimizing disparities for demographic groups in AI system outputs.

Microsoft Responsible AI Standard, v2 emphasizes reliability and safety, requiring evaluation for safe performance within operational ranges, and ongoing monitoring and feedback.

Microsoft Responsible AI Standard, v2 insists on compliance with Microsoft’s Privacy, Security, and Accessibility Standards to ensure AI systems are inclusive, secure, and respect privacy.

Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2023 directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to mandate impact assessments of automated decision systems, especially in critical areas like employment, education, and healthcare.

Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2023 requires covered entities to conduct ongoing evaluations of their systems, including privacy, performance, and potential negative impacts on consumers.

Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2023 mandates transparency and stakeholder consultation in system development and deployment.

Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2023 obligates covered entities to remedy any material negative impacts on consumers.

Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2023 establishes guidelines for identifying covered entities, prioritizing impact assessments, and reporting findings in a machine-readable format.

Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2023 develops a publicly accessible repository for summaries of impact assessments to aid consumer protection and promote research.

Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2023 enforces compliance under the FTC Act and allows state attorneys general to take legal action.

Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2023 establishes a Bureau of Technology within the FTC to support implementation and enforcement.

Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2023 preserves state laws and coordination with federal agencies to ensure consistent regulatory practices.

LISTOS Act mandates large online platforms to ensure consistent enforcement of content moderation across all languages where monetization occurs.

LISTOS Act requires platforms to annually disclose staffing and automated processes used for content moderation, including staffing levels, language proficiency, and monetization across languages.

LISTOS Act obligates platforms to provide user tools for content reporting and platform policies consistently in all languages offered.

LISTOS Act establishes the Advisory Group on Language-Sensitive Technologies to advise on best practices for non-discriminatory application of language-based technology.

LISTOS Act empowers the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general to enforce compliance, treating violations as unfair or deceptive practices.

LISTOS Act directs the FTC to issue regulations to implement the Act's provisions within specified timeframes.

LISTOS Act initiates a pilot program through USAID for international research on non-English online communication that incites harm or misinformation, with authorized funding for 2024 and 2025.

Promoting Precision Agriculture Act of 2023 mandates the Secretary of Agriculture, in coordination with the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Federal Communications Commission, to develop voluntary interconnectivity standards for precision agriculture within two years.

Promoting Precision Agriculture Act of 2023 requires these standards to address the evolving demands and connectivity needs of precision agriculture and consider cybersecurity challenges and the impact of AI and advanced wireless technology.

Promoting Precision Agriculture Act of 2023 obligates the Secretary to collaborate with relevant stakeholders, including public and private sector organizations and local governments, when developing these standards.

Promoting Precision Agriculture Act of 2023 directs the Comptroller General to conduct a study one year after the development of these standards and biennially thereafter for eight years, assessing the voluntary nature of the standards and their effectiveness in encouraging the adoption of precision agriculture.

Promoting Precision Agriculture Act of 2023 requires the findings of these studies to be reported to relevant Congressional committees.

Preventing PLA Acquisition of United States Technology Act of 2023 mandates covered entities to report annually on any research relationships with Chinese entities of concern and allows audits to ensure compliance.

Preventing PLA Acquisition of United States Technology Act of 2023 precludes entities violating prohibitions from receiving federal financial assistance.

Preventing PLA Acquisition of United States Technology Act of 2023 permits exceptions for fields not substantially contributing to military-civil fusion.

Preventing PLA Acquisition of United States Technology Act of 2023 directs the Secretary of Defense to issue regulations to enforce these provisions and coordinate enforcement across federal agencies.

Alabama (2019) SB 47 authorizes autonomous commercial vehicles and vehicles with teleoperation systems to operate without a conventional driver physically present in Alabama.

Alabama (2019) SB 47 grants jurisdiction exclusively to the Department of Transportation over these vehicles and prohibits additional requirements by local entities.

Alabama (2019) SB 47 requires automated vehicles to comply with federal motor vehicle safety standards and maintain motor vehicle liability coverage of at least $2,000,000.

Alabama (2019) SB 47 establishes that the vehicle owner or lessee is considered the operator for legal compliance and that automated driving systems are licensed operators.

Alabama (2019) SB 47 mandates accident protocols requiring vehicles remain on the scene with prompt law enforcement notification.

Alabama (2019) SB 47 requires remote drivers to hold the appropriate licenses and obey state traffic laws, subject to alcohol and drug testing in cooperation with local law enforcement.

Alabama (2019) SB 47 clarifies that this act does not alter existing liability laws for vehicle stakeholders.

Alabama (2019) SB 47 specifies that the act is effective upon the Governor’s approval or enactment into law.

DOE and USDA Interagency Research Act allows collaborative research in areas including artificial intelligence, machine learning, and modeling for optimizing agriculture and energy algorithms.

DOE and USDA Interagency Research Act promotes data integration, sharing, and secure access aligned with Federal regulations.

DOE and USDA Interagency Research Act encourages workforce development and infrastructure support as deemed necessary by the Secretaries.

DOE and USDA Interagency Research Act authorizes reimbursable agreements and collaboration with other Federal agencies to enhance research effectiveness.

DOE and USDA Interagency Research Act obliges the Secretaries to report on interagency coordination, research achievements, and future opportunities within two years to relevant Congressional Committees.

DOE and USDA Interagency Research Act ensures activities comply with research security mandates under relevant U.S. Code.

Americas Act, Title II ("Trade and Investment for the Americas"), Sec. 202 ("Americas Partnership Business Advisory Board") allows the board to advise on issues including regulatory hurdles, labor issues, dispute resolution, legal investment hurdles, and alignment on regulations related to emerging technologies like artificial intelligence.

Medicare Transaction Fraud Prevention Act establishes a pilot program under the Medicare program to test the use of a predictive risk-scoring algorithm for overseeing payments related to durable medical equipment and clinical diagnostic laboratory tests.

Medicare Transaction Fraud Prevention Act requires the pilot to run for two years, starting no later than January 1, 2025, with voluntary beneficiary participation.

Medicare Transaction Fraud Prevention Act mandates algorithm development in collaboration with industry representatives and modeled after real-time consumer feedback mechanisms, with scores ranging from 1 (least risky) to 99 (most risky).

Medicare Transaction Fraud Prevention Act conditions use of the algorithm on prior testing and evaluation considering the AI Bill of Rights and requires notifying affected beneficiaries about data processing and implications.

Medicare Transaction Fraud Prevention Act allows transaction review and possible suspension based on high-risk scores, offering beneficiaries the chance to dispute inaccuracies.

Medicare Transaction Fraud Prevention Act requires that alerts for identified fraud risks be communicated to beneficiaries, along with guidance on reporting suspected fraud to law enforcement, and authorizes determination of Medicare card termination to prevent fraud.

Tech to Save Moms Act, Sec. 5 ("Report on the Use of Technology in Maternity Care") mandates the Secretary of Health and Human Services to arrange a study with the National Academies on technology use in maternity care.

Tech to Save Moms Act, Sec. 5 ("Report on the Use of Technology in Maternity Care") requires examination of innovative technology, including AI, and its impact on racial or ethnic biases in maternal health.

Tech to Save Moms Act, Sec. 5 ("Report on the Use of Technology in Maternity Care") demands analysis of patient monitoring devices and their influence on racial or ethnic biases.

Tech to Save Moms Act, Sec. 5 ("Report on the Use of Technology in Maternity Care") calls for identification of best practices to reduce and prevent racial or ethnic biases in technology and device use.

Tech to Save Moms Act, Sec. 5 ("Report on the Use of Technology in Maternity Care") seeks best practices for using these technologies specifically for racial and ethnic minority groups in maternity care.

Tech to Save Moms Act, Sec. 5 ("Report on the Use of Technology in Maternity Care") instructs evaluation of privacy and security safeguards related to these technologies.

Tech to Save Moms Act, Sec. 5 ("Report on the Use of Technology in Maternity Care") obliges the National Academies to complete the study and report results to Congress within 24 months of enactment.

Targeting Online Sales of Fentanyl Act analyzes existing federal law enforcement procedures and outcomes over the past 10 years to identify patterns and improvement areas.

Targeting Online Sales of Fentanyl Act explores how providers use machine learning and other technologies to detect and combat sales of these substances on their platforms.

Targeting Online Sales of Fentanyl Act evaluates enforcement mechanisms by providers, such as user identification and account suspension.

Targeting Online Sales of Fentanyl Act requires assessment of referrals to the Federal Government from providers, including investigations and outcomes.

Targeting Online Sales of Fentanyl Act obligates submission of a report to Congress within one year detailing study findings and determinations.

Artificial Intelligence Accountability Act requires the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information to study accountability mechanisms (e.g., audits, certifications, and assessments) that provide assurances that an AI system is trustworthy. This includes defining terms around AI “trustworthiness,” examining how mechanisms are incorporated into AI systems, and assessing their ability to reduce risks related to AI systems, such as cybersecurity threats.

Artificial Intelligence Accountability Act requires the Assistant Secretary to solicit stakeholder feedback through public meetings while carrying out the study above and to report the study’s findings to Congress, including recommendations on effective accountability measures for AI systems.

Artificial Intelligence Accountability Act requires the Assistant Secretary to consult with stakeholders through public meetings and report to Congress on what information should be disclosed to those who interact with, are affected by, or study AI systems, and the most effective methods for doing so.

Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024 requires the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to establish a program (“Testing Standards”) to create and maintain testing standards for computational forensic software, which includes software that relies on AI-enabled automated or semiautomated computational processes to analyze or interpret evidence.

Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024 requires Testing Standards to solicit public input, address the potential for disparate impacts on protected groups, and specify requirements for publicly available documentation by developers, validation processes by those using computational forensic software, reports provided to defendants regarding software used, and how to test software and report results.

Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024 requires the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to establish a program (“Testing Program”) that tests computational forensic algorithms according to the testing standards, using realistic and representative sample data and adversarial examples, and publishing results. Requires software to be re-tested after significant changes.

Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024 requires Federal law enforcement agencies only to use computational forensic software tested by NIST’s Testing Program and only after conducting an internal validation and making results publicly available.

Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024 requires evidence from computational forensic software to be admissible only if it has been submitted to NIST’s Testing Program and the developers waive legal claims against the defense analyzing or testing it. Requires information about the software (e.g., source code) and results from analyses by the software to be shared with the defendant.

Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2023 requires the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to issue guidance on how federal agencies can use NIST’s AI Risk Management Framework (RMF) to reduce risks, covering cybersecurity for AI systems, requirements for AI suppliers, and training for agencies.

Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2023 requires the Comptroller General of the United States to assess the impact of NIST's AI RMF on agencies' AI use within a year, and requires the Director of OMB to report to Congress on agency implementation and adherence to NIST’s AI RMF within a year, and subsequently, at least once every three years.

Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2023 excludes national security systems from the requirements above to adhere to NIST’s AI RMF.

Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2023 requires the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council to issue guidance on agency AI procurement within a year, to ensure compliance with NIST’s AI RMF.

Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2023 requires the Director of OMB to establish an initiative to build agencies’ AI expertise, focusing on hiring interdisciplinary experts and incorporating best practices from existing initiatives.

Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2023 requires the Director of NIST to conduct a study on and convene stakeholders to develop voluntary consensus standards to test and evaluate AI acquisitions, develop methods and conduct evaluations, monitor evaluations and adjust methods, and make recommendations to each agency on risks from relevant AI acquisitions.

Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2024 prohibits the use of pricing algorithms incorporating nonpublic competitor data.

Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2024 requires entities using or distributing pricing algorithms to submit detailed reports to the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) or Attorney General upon request, detailing development, data usage, and algorithmic rules.

Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2024 mandates certification of report accuracy by a high-level corporate officer.

Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2024 ensures confidentiality of submitted reports, allowing information sharing only between the Department of Justice, FTC, and National Institute of Standards and Technology.

Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2024 imposes civil penalties for violations, including fines and injunctive relief.

Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2024 presumes collusive behavior in antitrust cases involving certain uses of pricing algorithms, allowing for rebuttal and assigning joint liability.

Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2024 obligates disclosure to customers and employees when prices or terms are set by algorithms, including specifics on price discrimination and third-party algorithm developers.

Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2024 directs the FTC to study and report on the impact and prevalence of pricing algorithms within two years, including potential consumer harm and benefits.

Strategy for Public Health Preparedness and Response to Artificial Intelligence Threats mandates consultation with stakeholders, including those developing countermeasures and those with AI expertise, for strategy formulation.

Strategy for Public Health Preparedness and Response to Artificial Intelligence Threats includes a framework for mitigating AI misuse risks threatening national health security and outlines duties, functions, and metrics for preparedness and response.

Strategy for Public Health Preparedness and Response to Artificial Intelligence Threats identifies gaps in public health capabilities and proposes strategies to address these gaps and strengthen emergency preparedness against AI threats.

Strategy for Public Health Preparedness and Response to Artificial Intelligence Threats focuses on mitigating risks such as the development of biological weapons and drug-resistant viruses and bacteria.

Strategy for Public Health Preparedness and Response to Artificial Intelligence Threats requires the strategy to be submitted to relevant congressional committees without compromising national security.

Strategy for Public Health Preparedness and Response to Artificial Intelligence Threats amends the Public Health Service Act to integrate this AI threat strategy into the broader federal response to public health emergencies.

text: Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act of 2023 requires a report on artificial intelligence regulation in the financial services industry, establishes artificial intelligence bug bounty programs, requires a vulnerability analysis study for artificial intelligence-enabled military applications, and requires a report on data sharing and coordination.

Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2023 requires agencies which use or oversee a covered algorithm to have an office of civil rights employing experts and technologists on bias, discrimination, and algorithmic harms.

Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2023 mandates these offices to submit biennial reports to Congress detailing risks from use of algorithms using artificial intelligence techniques within the agency's jurisdiction, mitigation steps, actions taken to engage stakeholders, and recommendations for further mitigation of algorithmic bias and discrimination.

Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2023 establishes an interagency working group on covered algorithms and civil rights, led by the Department of Justice's Civil Rights Division.

A bill to promote United States leadership in technical standards by directing the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Department of State to take certain actions to encourage and enable United States participation in developing standards and specifications for artificial intelligence and other critical and emerging technologies, and for other purposes. directs federal agencies to notify NIST of their involvement in AI standards activities and mandates NIST to create a reporting mechanism for this purpose.

A bill to promote United States leadership in technical standards by directing the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Department of State to take certain actions to encourage and enable United States participation in developing standards and specifications for artificial intelligence and other critical and emerging technologies, and for other purposes. mandates NIST to establish a web portal to inform U.S. industry and federal agencies about international standards efforts and participation opportunities.

A bill to promote United States leadership in technical standards by directing the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Department of State to take certain actions to encourage and enable United States participation in developing standards and specifications for artificial intelligence and other critical and emerging technologies, and for other purposes. establishes a pilot program for supporting U.S.-based standards meetings, including prestandardization and coordination meetings, through grants to eligible entities.

A bill to promote United States leadership in technical standards by directing the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Department of State to take certain actions to encourage and enable United States participation in developing standards and specifications for artificial intelligence and other critical and emerging technologies, and for other purposes. obligates NIST to brief Congress annually on the pilot program’s effectiveness and provide recommendations for permanent implementation if deemed feasible.

FAIRR Act amends the Financial Stability Act of 2010 to assign the Financial Stability Oversight Council duties regarding AI in the financial sector.

FAIRR Act requires the Council to coordinate with member agencies on AI-related financial system risks and direct the Office of Financial Research to study AI use by financial institutions.

FAIRR Act obligates the Council to identify AI-related threats to financial stability, including market manipulation and disruption by malign actors.

FAIRR Act mandates submission of a report within 180 days identifying regulatory gaps and recommending solutions, including referencing the NSA's September 2023 Cybersecurity Information Sheet.

FAIRR Act calls for scenario-based exercises to test AI-related financial disruption defenses.

FAIRR Act expands authority to oversee third-party AI service providers to financial institutions.

FAIRR Act increases penalties for securities violations involving machine-manipulated media to three times the standard amount.

FAIRR Act imposes liability on developers for AI model outcomes under Federal securities laws, with limited potential for waivers.

To require a briefing on the national security threats associated with Chinese autonomous ground vehicles operating in the United States. require the Secretary of Defense to provide a briefing by March 30, 2024, on national security threats from Chinese autonomous ground vehicles in the U.S.

To require a briefing on the national security threats associated with Chinese autonomous ground vehicles operating in the United States. mandate the briefing to address vehicles near Department of Defense bases and sensitive U.S. Government facilities.

To require a briefing on the national security threats associated with Chinese autonomous ground vehicles operating in the United States. specify inclusion of information on data types collected by these vehicles and dual-use implications of their technologies.

To require a briefing on the national security threats associated with Chinese autonomous ground vehicles operating in the United States. include analysis of how the Chinese Communist Party or People’s Liberation Army could use collected data for military planning.

National AI Commission Act establishes the National AI Commission, an independent and bi-partisan commission in the legislative branch responsible for reviewing and recommending measures for the US to mitigate the risks and possible harms of AI, and to ensure US leadership in AI innovation and development.

National AI Commission Act directs the National AI Commission to review the Federal Government's existing approach to AI oversight and regulation, including the existing distribution of oversight and regulatory authorities across various agencies, and to recommend governmental structures that may be needed to regulate powerful general-purpose AI systems.

National AI Commission Act instruct the National AI Commission to submit an interim report to Congress and the President within six months, a final report with its findings and recommendations for a binding regulatory framework no later than six months after the interim report, and a follow-up report within one year of the final report's submission.

National AI Commission Act requires the National AI Commission to comprise twenty commissioners appointed by the President and by Congressional leadership, with ten appointed by each party and co-chaired by a Democratic appointee and a Republican appointee.

No AI FRAUD Act establishes property rights for individuals in their likeness and voice, treating them as intellectual property that is transferable and descendible for ten years post-mortem.

No AI FRAUD Act prohibits unauthorized distribution, transmission, or availability of personalized cloning services, digital voice replicas, or digital depictions without the individual’s consent, imposing liabilities for violations.

No AI FRAUD Act specifies that unauthorized use incurs damages of $50,000 per violation for cloning services and $5,000 per violation for voice replicas or depictions, plus actual damages and profits.

No AI FRAUD Act allows for punitive damages and attorney fees for injured parties and invalidates disclaimers as a defense.

No AI FRAUD Act provides a First Amendment defense, balancing public interest with intellectual property rights, and considers commercial use and impact on the value of the original work.

No AI FRAUD Act exempts negligible harm from liability and defines harm to include financial, physical, and severe emotional distress.

No AI FRAUD Act sets a four-year limitations period for civil actions and ensures no preemption of other rights or laws.

To establish a Joint Autonomy Office in the Department of Defense, and for other purposes. directs the Secretary of Defense to establish the Joint Autonomy Office in the Department of Defense, responsible for coordinating and accelerating the adoption of all-domain autonomous systems for operational users, including through the adoption of commercial and defense best practices

To establish a Joint Autonomy Office in the Department of Defense, and for other purposes. requires the Office to implement an all-domain enterprise autonomous systems software development and testing platform across DoD's classification levels, including an all-domain data acquisition and curation process to build and manage datasets; these datasets and platforms should be released to various services and acquisition programs as they mature.

To establish a Joint Autonomy Office in the Department of Defense, and for other purposes. requires the Secretary of Defense to ensure that the Office has unlimited access to existing datasets regardless of classification level, and to introduce security protocols to protect data shared with or maintained by the Office.

To establish a Joint Autonomy Office in the Department of Defense, and for other purposes. requires the Director of the Office must establish a Department-wide classification framework for autonomous capabilities, considering the complexity of autonomous systems, the necessity of human supervision or control, their applicability to various warfighting domains, and costs; the Director must submit this framework along with an explanation of its criteria and requirements to Congress, with updates released no less frequently than once every two years.

To establish a Joint Autonomy Office in the Department of Defense, and for other purposes. requires the Director to develop and implement plans to standardize planning, resource and integration of autonomous capabilities across the Department; this includes a report assessing the Department's current efforts which identifies acquisition, training and evaluation gaps, as well as recommendations to address these.

ASK Act directs the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), in consultation with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), to issue rules prohibiting the offer of artificial intelligence products to minors without parental consent.

ASK Act mandates the rule to include a provision allowing parents and guardians to revoke consent at any time.

Preventing Deep Fake Scams Act establishes a task force examining the fraudulent use of artificial intelligence in the financial services sector.

Preventing Deep Fake Scams Act instruct the task force to solicit public feedback from industry and expert stakeholders, including depository institutions, credit unions, third-party vendors, and AI experts.

Preventing Deep Fake Scams Act directs the task force to produce a report for Congress within one year that identifies potential risks from AI misuse, and proposes AI fraud detection measures, among other legislative recommendations.

Preventing Deep Fake Scams Act terminates the task force 90 days after the final report's issue.

AI Leadership Training Act establishes an AI leadership training program for management officials, supervisors, and other designated employees in executive agencies, to be developed and implemented within 18 months.

AI Leadership Training Act requires annual training to cover AI capabilities, risks, safety, ethics, Federal Government requirements, and best practices related to AI procurement, use, testing, evaluation, and auditing.

AI Leadership Training Act mandates program topics include AI basics, benefits, risks, data significance, AI system failures, continuous refinement, risk mitigation, organizational considerations, and constitutional risks related to AI use.

AI Leadership Training Act obligates updates to the program every two years to incorporate new AI information and ensure compliance with training requirements.

AI Leadership Training Act demands metrics to measure participation and feedback for program improvements.

AI Leadership Training Act permits Congress to request detailed information about the program materials and responsible personnel.

AI Leadership Training Act encourages interaction with experts from various sectors as part of the training.

AI Leadership Training Act sets a sunset clause for the program 10 years after enactment.

DOE and NSF Interagency Research Act requires the Department of Energy (DOE) and the National Science Foundation (NSF) to coordinate research and development activities.

DOE and NSF Interagency Research Act mandates the establishment of a memorandum of understanding between the DOE and NSF, utilizing a competitive, merit-reviewed process for project applications.

DOE and NSF Interagency Research Act authorizes collaborative research in key areas including artificial intelligence, machine learning, data analytics, quantum computing, and computational sciences.

DOE and NSF Interagency Research Act promotes interagency collaboration and data sharing among Federal agencies, National Laboratories, and other institutions.

DOE and NSF Interagency Research Act supports research infrastructure development and STEM education initiatives, including internships and professional development.

DOE and NSF Interagency Research Act allows reimbursable agreements between the DOE and NSF to enhance research effectiveness.

DOE and NSF Interagency Research Act obligates the DOE and NSF to report on interagency coordination, research achievements, and future opportunities within two years of enactment.

DOE and NSF Interagency Research Act ensures activities comply with research security provisions under existing law.

Political BIAS Emails Act of 2023 prohibits email service providers from using filtering algorithms to flag emails from political campaigns that consumers have elected to receive as spam without user direction.

Political BIAS Emails Act of 2023 requires providers to publish quarterly transparency reports detailing instances of political emails flagged as spam, including breakdowns by political party and filtering algorithm usage.

Political BIAS Emails Act of 2023 mandates email providers to disclose specific spam-filtering data to political campaigns upon request, with limitations on request frequency.

Political BIAS Emails Act of 2023 obliges providers to offer best practices to political campaigns for improving email deliverability to primary inboxes.

Political BIAS Emails Act of 2023 enforces these provisions through the Federal Trade Commission, treating violations as unfair or deceptive acts under the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Political BIAS Emails Act of 2023 defines key terms including “filtering algorithm,” “operator,” and “political campaign.”

ASSESS AI Act establishes a task force to assess privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties implications of artificial intelligence.

ASSESS AI Act charges the task force to evaluate existing policy, regulatory, and legal gaps for AI applications and make legislative and regulatory recommendations.

ASSESS AI Act directs the task force to address the application of federal antidiscrimination laws, disparate impact standards, AI validation, and auditing in federal use of AI.

ASSESS AI Act instructs the task force to consider institutional changes for ongoing AI governance and the potential creation of a new oversight organization.

ASSESS AI Act requires the task force to submit an interim report within one year and a final report within 18 months.

AI Disclosure Act of 2023 requires generative artificial intelligence to include a disclaimer on any output. Mandates the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to enforce this disclosure requirement.

AI Disclosure Act of 2023 classifies violations of the disclosure requirement as unfair or deceptive acts or practices under the Federal Trade Commission Act.Empowers the FTC to enforce the disclosure requirement using the same means, jurisdiction, powers, and duties as provided in the Federal Trade Commission Act. Subjects violators to penalties and grants them privileges and immunities in accordance with the Federal Trade Commission Act.

R U REAL Act directs the FTC to revise the Telemarketing Sales Rule to require the disclosure of AI usage to impersonate a human being in telemarketing.

R U REAL Act mandates the FTC to impose financial penalties on violators of this new rule, especially towards individuals and entities with the intent to defraud, cause harm, or wrongfully obtain anything of value through AI telemarketing techniques.

AI LEAD Act establishes the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officers (CAIO) Council to coordinate federal AI practices, interagency activities, and risk management. Mandates each federal agency to appoint a Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer responsible for promoting AI innovation, policy development, and risk management.

AI LEAD Act requires the creation of Artificial Intelligence Governance Boards within each agency to oversee AI issues and ensure compliance with relevant laws and standards. Obligates agencies to develop AI strategies emphasizing trustworthy adoption, risk mitigation, transparency, and the protection of individual rights. Directs the Comptroller General to report on the effectiveness of the AI Governance Boards and CAIOs within two years of enactment.

AI Foundation Model Transparency Act of 2023 directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to establish and routinely update standards for making training data and algorithms of AI foundation models publicly available.

AI Foundation Model Transparency Act of 2023 requires the FTC to promulgate regulations within 9 months and specifies information to be disclosed, including sources of training data and model performance evaluations.

AI Foundation Model Transparency Act of 2023 mandates consultation with relevant stakeholders, including NIST, OSTP, and the Register of Copyrights, in establishing these standards.

AI Foundation Model Transparency Act of 2023 treats violations of these regulations as violations under the FTC Act regarding unfair or deceptive acts or practices.

AI Foundation Model Transparency Act of 2023 authorizes $10 million for fiscal year 2025 and $3 million annually thereafter for implementation.

“Managing Active and Reserve Tech Talent Effectively Act of 2023” establishes a robust human capital infrastructure for computer programming, coding, and AI skills within the U.S. Armed Forces.

“Managing Active and Reserve Tech Talent Effectively Act of 2023” requires the development of career field occupational codes aligned with AI and coding competencies under the Department of Defense Cyber Workforce Framework.

“Managing Active and Reserve Tech Talent Effectively Act of 2023” mandates the assessment and tracking of personnel with AI and coding skills.

“Managing Active and Reserve Tech Talent Effectively Act of 2023” obliges the military departments to develop and execute a coherent strategy for presenting these skills to combatant commands.

“Managing Active and Reserve Tech Talent Effectively Act of 2023” tasks the Secretary of each military department, in consultation with relevant officials, to implement the policy and submit implementation plans within 180 days.

“Managing Active and Reserve Tech Talent Effectively Act of 2023” calls for similar policies for reserve components to leverage civilian-acquired AI and coding skills.

“Managing Active and Reserve Tech Talent Effectively Act of 2023” requires updates on policy implementation in the Department of Defense's budget justification materials until all milestones are met.

Water Quality and Environmental Innovation Act authorizes the Environmental Protection Agency's (EPA) Administrator to award grants and contracts for projects using emerging technologies to address water quality threats.

Water Quality and Environmental Innovation Act establishes the Water Quality and Environmental Innovation Fund, funding it through fiscal years 2024-2028 using fees from the EPA's Motor Vehicle and Engine Compliance Program.

Water Quality and Environmental Innovation Act mandates the use of technologies, including artificial intelligence, quantum information science, and robotics, among others, for water quality projects.

Water Quality and Environmental Innovation Act requires that project results, including data and statistics, be publicly accessible.

Water Quality and Environmental Innovation Act directs the EPA Administrator to report annually to Congress on the benefits, recipients, goals, and effectiveness of funded projects, starting one year after the Act's enactment.

Basic Allowance for Housing Calculation Improvement Act of 2023 mandates the submission of a report to the Senate and House Armed Services Committees evaluating the AI-calculated rates.

QUIET Act directs Congress to amend the Communications Act of 1934 to mandate the disclosure of artificial intelligence usage in voice call or text message impersonations.

QUIET Act mandates the imposition of financial penalties on those who fail to complete the required disclosure of artificial intelligence usage during robocalls.

Farm Tech Act mandates the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a program to certify AI software for the production of agricultural products.

Farm Tech Act bases the certification program on the  National Institute of Standards and Technology's Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework.

Farm Tech Act permits certification only if the software performs accurately and meets or exceeds relevant Federal and State standards for licensure, certification, and permitting.

Farm Tech Act details specific licensure and certification requirements for various tasks, including commercial driving, manure application, pesticide application and handling hazardous materials.

Jobs of the Future Act of 2023 requires the Secretary of Labor and the Director of the National Science Foundation to submit interim and final reports on AI's impact on the U.S. workforce.

Jobs of the Future Act of 2023 mandates these reports to identify data necessary for analyzing AI's workforce impact, industries most affected by AI, and demographics vulnerable to job displacement.

Jobs of the Future Act of 2023 requires analysis of skills, expertise, and education needed to work alongside AI and methods to deliver these to the workforce.

Jobs of the Future Act of 2023 demands recommendations to mitigate workforce displacement, promote knowledge sharing, and ensure underserved demographics have access to necessary AI-related education.

Jobs of the Future Act of 2023 requires collaboration with educational institutions, industry stakeholders, and federal agencies in preparing the reports.

Building Resilient Supply Chains Act mandates the DOC to improve the competitiveness of the advanced tech manufacturing sector, minimize supply chain shocks, and support the creation of related jobs in key technology focus areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and quantum computing.

Building Resilient Supply Chains Act directs the Inspector General of the DOC to audit activities supported by the Supply Chain Resiliency and Crisis Response Office's grants, loans, and loan guarantees every four years.

Small Business Broadband and Emerging Information Technology Enhancement Act of 2023 requires the coordinator to work with the SBA's chief information officer, chief technology officer, and other relevant federal agencies.

Small Business Broadband and Emerging Information Technology Enhancement Act of 2023 mandates the coordinator to identify best practices and catalog tools and training for small businesses on broadband and emerging technologies.

Small Business Broadband and Emerging Information Technology Enhancement Act of 2023 obligates the coordinator to provide training to SBA employees on these technologies and relevant federal programs.

Small Business Broadband and Emerging Information Technology Enhancement Act of 2023 requires biennial reports on the SBA's activities related to broadband and emerging technologies.

Small Business Broadband and Emerging Information Technology Enhancement Act of 2023 instructs the Chief Counsel for Advocacy to study and report on the impact of broadband availability, speed, and price, and the deployment of emerging technologies on small businesses.

Small Business Broadband and Emerging Information Technology Enhancement Act of 2023 amends the Small Business Act to include provisions for increasing small business access to broadband and emerging technologies.

Computer Science for All Act of 2023 requires the Secretary of Education to award grants to states, local educational agencies, and eligible Tribal schools for expanding computer science education.

Computer Science for All Act of 2023 mandates grant recipients to provide every high school student with access to computer science education within five years and ensure a progression of computer science education from prekindergarten through middle school.

Computer Science for All Act of 2023 requires the use of grant funds for teacher training, expanding access to learning materials, and reducing equity gaps in STEAM education for underrepresented groups.

Computer Science for All Act of 2023 permits grant funds to be used for building regional collaborations, hiring instructional personnel, and disseminating effective practices.

Computer Science for All Act of 2023 limits use of grant funds for equipment purchases to 15%.

Computer Science for All Act of 2023 authorizes $250 million for fiscal year 2024 and the following four fiscal years.

Computer Science for All Act of 2023 requires grant recipients to report biannually on the use of funds and student demographics.

Computer Science for All Act of 2023 mandates the Secretary to report to Congress within five years on program expansion recommendations.
