FinCEN Modernization Act of 2023 cites the Act as the "FinCEN Modernization Act of 2023."

FinCEN Modernization Act of 2023 requires FinCEN to establish research, development, and information-sharing programs focusing on technological advances like machine learning and data analytics.

FinCEN Modernization Act of 2023 mandates FinCEN to explore and evaluate technological innovations beneficial for financial systems and detect illicit activities.

FinCEN Modernization Act of 2023 obligates FinCEN to adopt necessary technologies for monitoring cryptocurrencies and addressing money laundering and cyber threats.

FinCEN Modernization Act of 2023 enables FinCEN to exchange information with other Treasury offices and federal departments.

FinCEN Modernization Act of 2023 authorizes FinCEN to enter into non-standard transactions and accept contributions, gifts, or donations to support technological advancements.

FinCEN Modernization Act of 2023 compels FinCEN to submit an annual report detailing transactions, contributions, and their justifications and purposes to relevant Congressional committees.

Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2024 requires the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to study  the environmental impacts of artificial intelligence, with a report on its findings submitted to Congress within two years of the Act's enactment.

Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2024 mandates that the EPA study examine the energy, water consumption, and pollution throughout the full lifecycle of AI models, hardware, and data centers, considering the effects of location, power sources, and AI model design on these environmental impacts.

Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2024 requires that the EPA study assess the positive environmental impacts associated with the use of AI, such as optimizing systems for energy efficiency or automatically monitoring environmental changes.

Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2024 directs the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to work with other government officials to form a consortium comprising academic, civil society, and industry representatives to assess and report on AI's environmental impacts, including the feasibility of open-source tools for measurement and recommendations to mitigate negative environmental effects.

Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2024 instructs the Director of NIST to work with other government officials and the consortium to establish a voluntary reporting system for entities to report on their AI systems' environmental impact.

Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2024 requires the Administrator of EPA, Secretary of Energy and Director of NIST to submit a joint report on the consortium's findings and its proposed voluntary reporting system within four years of the Act's enactment.

Tornado Observations Research and Notification Assessment for Development of Operations Act mandates the establishment of a hazard risk communication office to simplify and improve communication, using the latest social, behavioral, risk, and communication science research, including AI and machine learning technologies.

Tornado Observations Research and Notification Assessment for Development of Operations Act instructs the Under Secretary to create a research program to modernize risk-based hazard communication and establish a pilot program for tornado hazard communication.

Next Generation Pipelines Research and Development Act establishes a joint research and development program within the Department of Energy, coordinated with the Department of Transportation and the National Institute of Standards and Technology, to develop advanced materials and technologies for pipeline systems.

Next Generation Pipelines Research and Development Act forms the National Pipeline Modernization Center to collaborate on research, development, and demonstration projects for commercializing cost-effective pipeline products and procedures.

Next Generation Pipelines Research and Development Act mandates the development of measurement research, testing, and standardization programs by the National Institute of Standards and Technology to ensure pipeline integrity and support safety, security, and efficiency.

Next Generation Pipelines Research and Development Act authorizes significant appropriations for fiscal years 2024 through 2028 to support these initiatives.

Supply Chain Mapping and Monitoring Act establishes the Supply Chain Resiliency and Crisis Response Office within 180 days to monitor and enhance supply chain resilience, especially for critical industries and goods.

Supply Chain Mapping and Monitoring Act mandates the Under Secretary to map, monitor, and model supply chains, identifying gaps and vulnerabilities.

Supply Chain Mapping and Monitoring Act requires collaboration with federal agencies, private sector, labor organizations, and international partners to strengthen supply chains and prepare for shocks.

Supply Chain Mapping and Monitoring Act involves continuous monitoring of supply chain resilience, diversity, and security, and mandates quadrennial reports on supply chain resiliency and domestic manufacturing.

Supply Chain Mapping and Monitoring Act authorizes $500 million for fiscal years 2024-2028 to fund these activities, ensuring up to 2% per fiscal year for administrative costs.

Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act requires establishment of a memorandum of understanding to facilitate this collaboration through a competitive, merit-reviewed process.

Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act mandates exploration of performance portability of weather model codes between operational and high-performance computing systems.

Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act supports maintenance and improvement of scientific computing infrastructure, data sharing, and collaboration among federal entities and institutions.

Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act initiates a computing research initiative to develop advanced weather models, leveraging data and efforts from relevant interagency entities.

Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act permits establishment of up to three centers of excellence at National Laboratories to support advanced weather models through public-private partnerships and high-performance computing.

Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act prioritizes selection of Laboratories with AI-enabled computing systems and expertise in weather and climate modeling.

Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act mandates submission of reports to Congress detailing interagency coordination, achievements, and future opportunities for collaboration in advanced computing techniques.

Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2024 expands the functions of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to include developing workforce frameworks for critical and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI).

Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2024 requires the Director of NIST to develop, maintain, and update an AI workforce framework and review it at least every three years.

Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2024 mandates the inclusion of professional, support, and operational skills in AI workforce frameworks, considering nontraditional backgrounds.

Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2024 instructs the Director to consult with various stakeholders, including federal agencies and educational institutions, in developing these frameworks.

Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2024 obliges the Director to produce multilingual resources to support global adoption of these frameworks.

Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2024 requires periodic reports to Congress on updates and the process of reviewing workforce frameworks, including the National Initiative for Cybersecurity Education Workforce Framework for Cybersecurity.

Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2024 directs the development and publication of additional workforce frameworks for other critical technologies, such as quantum information science.

Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act prohibits knowingly distributing materially deceptive AI-generated audio or visual media related to Federal election activities or candidates. Exempts broadcasters, streaming services, and periodicals if they disclose authenticity concerns and covers bona fide news or satire.

Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act allows affected candidates to seek injunctive relief or damages, including attorney's fees, for violations. Requires plaintiffs to prove violations with clear and convincing evidence.

RESTRICT Act authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to review and prohibit certain transactions involving information and communications technology (ICT) between U.S. persons and foreign adversaries.

RESTRICT Act empowers the Secretary to identify, deter, disrupt, prevent, prohibit, investigate, or mitigate risks arising from covered transactions.

RESTRICT Act defines "covered transactions" broadly, including those involving foreign adversaries or entities under their jurisdiction.

RESTRICT Act establishes procedures for the Secretary to refer covered holdings posing national security risks to the President, who can then compel divestment or take other actions to mitigate risks.

RESTRICT Act prioritizes critical ICT areas such as AI, quantum computing, and telecommunications for evaluation.

RESTRICT Act exempts actions from standard administrative and judicial reviews, limiting legal challenges to specific high courts.

RESTRICT Act imposes civil and criminal penalties for violations, including fines, imprisonment, and forfeiture.

FAA Research and Development Act of 2023, Sec. 215 ("Air Traffic Control Training") requires the Administrator to carry out a research program to modernize and streamline air traffic control training, subject to available appropriations.

FAA Research and Development Act of 2023, Sec. 215 ("Air Traffic Control Training") mandates the assessment of advanced technologies, including AI, machine learning, and virtual/augmented reality, to enhance knowledge retention and training effectiveness.

FAA Research and Development Act of 2023, Sec. 215 ("Air Traffic Control Training") develops a timeline for deploying proven advanced technologies and processes for accreditation in training programs and facilities.

FAA Research and Development Act of 2023, Sec. 215 ("Air Traffic Control Training") includes collaboration with labor organizations and other stakeholders in the research process.

FAA Research and Development Act of 2023, Sec. 215 ("Air Traffic Control Training") obligates the Administrator to submit a report to Congress on the research findings within one year of the Act's enactment.

FAA Research and Development Act of 2023, Sec. 210 ("Technology review of artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies") mandates the review to cover applications of AI and machine learning in jet bridges, airport service vehicles, and aircraft taxiing.

FAA Research and Development Act of 2023, Sec. 210 ("Technology review of artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies") allows the Administrator to include other relevant areas that can improve airport efficiency and safety.

FAA Research and Development Act of 2023, Sec. 210 ("Technology review of artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies") obligates the Administrator to submit a report to Congress within one year, detailing the review's findings.

FAA Research and Development Act of 2023, Sec. 210 ("Technology review of artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies") includes a required examination of China's domestic application of AI and machine learning technologies in the report.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 304 ("Data Assimilation, Management, and Sharing Practices") establishes the requirement for the Under Secretary, in collaboration with the weather enterprise, to develop consistent and open data and metadata standards to support open science.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 304 ("Data Assimilation, Management, and Sharing Practices") mandates the consolidation and efficient arrangement of data infrastructure, considering commercial cloud technologies, to ensure effective data transfer between National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) offices.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 304 ("Data Assimilation, Management, and Sharing Practices") authorizes the Under Secretary to partner with other federal agencies to support cloud architecture transitions and data collocation.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 304 ("Data Assimilation, Management, and Sharing Practices") ensures the long-term management and stewardship of archival data acquired through the Commercial Data Program.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 304 ("Data Assimilation, Management, and Sharing Practices") requires the Under Secretary to facilitate data sharing with the weather enterprise, making data accessible to U.S. persons under certain conditions.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 304 ("Data Assimilation, Management, and Sharing Practices") instructs the establishment of a program to advance data assimilation methods, including AI and machine learning, and the creation of a university consortium to address research challenges in data assimilation.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 304 ("Data Assimilation, Management, and Sharing Practices") mandates a study on NOAA's data practices and management needs, assessing costs, benefits, and recommending improvements.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title II ("National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research Institutes") establishes a program to award financial assistance for creating and supporting a network of National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research Institutes.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title II ("National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research Institutes") requires collaboration among public and private organizations, including Federal agencies, academic institutions, and industry, to form these Institutes.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title II ("National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research Institutes") mandates the Institutes to focus on economic or social sectors and address ethical, societal, safety, and security implications of unmanned aircraft systems.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title II ("National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research Institutes") supports interdisciplinary research, education, and workforce development, including broadening participation of underrepresented communities.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title II ("National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research Institutes") provides funds for managing data sets, developing testbeds, conducting research, and supporting AI and machine learning related to advanced air mobility systems.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title II ("National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research Institutes") imposes a competitive merit review process for awarding financial assistance and prohibits duplication of efforts.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title II ("National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research Institutes") authorizes $5 million annually for fiscal years 2024-2028 to support these activities.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 116(f) ("National Harmful Algal Bloom and Hypoxia Observing Network") requires the Under Secretary, via NCCOS and IOOS, to integrate Federal, State, regional, and local observing capabilities.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 116(f) ("National Harmful Algal Bloom and Hypoxia Observing Network") mandates the use of emerging technologies and data integration methods, including artificial intelligence, for monitoring, detecting, and forecasting harmful algal blooms.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 116(f) ("National Harmful Algal Bloom and Hypoxia Observing Network") instructs the IOOS Program Office to coordinate with NCCOS for observations, data integration, and information dissemination.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 116(f) ("National Harmful Algal Bloom and Hypoxia Observing Network") establishes a Harmful Algal Bloom Data Assembly Center to integrate, disseminate, and support ecological forecasting.

Data Science and Literacy Act of 2023 directs the Secretary of Education to award competitive grants to eligible entities to enhance data literacy education from pre-kindergarten through postsecondary levels.

Data Science and Literacy Act of 2023 requires grant applications to detail plans for increasing access to data literacy and STEM education, evaluating project activities, and continuing efforts post-grant.

Data Science and Literacy Act of 2023 mandates the use of grant funds for developing data literacy curricula, providing professional development for educators, and collaborating with industry and educational institutions.

Data Science and Literacy Act of 2023 limits equipment purchases to 15% of grant funds annually.

Data Science and Literacy Act of 2023 obligates recipients to submit biannual reports on grant fund usage, with data disaggregated by race, ethnicity, gender, and eligibility for free/reduced lunch.

Data Science and Literacy Act of 2023 tasks the Secretary with submitting a comprehensive report to Congress within five years, including recommendations for program expansion.

Data Science and Literacy Act of 2023 authorizes $10 million annually for fiscal years 2024-2028, with caps on administrative expenses and program evaluation costs.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VI ("Department of Energy Activities") mandates the Secretary of Energy to execute a cross-cutting research, development, and demonstration program for unmanned aircraft system (UAS) technologies, including artificial intelligence.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VI ("Department of Energy Activities") requires coordination across relevant DOE offices, including the Artificial Intelligence Technology Office.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VI ("Department of Energy Activities") formulates goals for UAS research, leveraging existing research and providing training in AI, machine learning, and related fields.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VI ("Department of Energy Activities") establishes a data management strategy ensuring digital access, interoperability, and machine-readability.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VI ("Department of Energy Activities") supports institutes to advance UAS and DOE missions.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VI ("Department of Energy Activities") awards financial assistance for research in areas such as AI, autonomous operation, advanced algorithms, and multi-sensor fusion.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VI ("Department of Energy Activities") promotes technology transfer by partnering with industry.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VI ("Department of Energy Activities") makes available DOE research facilities and high-performance computing infrastructure.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VI ("Department of Energy Activities") coordinates with other federal departments to avoid duplication and ensure complementary activities.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VI ("Department of Energy Activities") authorizes appropriations totaling $276,282,638 from fiscal years 2024 to 2028.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VII ("Department of Homeland Security Activities") mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security to support research, development, evaluation, and testing of advanced air mobility, unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), and counter-UAS systems.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VII ("Department of Homeland Security Activities") directs coordination with relevant Department of Homeland Security offices and programs, including the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and U.S. Customs and Border Protection.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VII ("Department of Homeland Security Activities") requires production of standardized, secure, and privacy-protected data sets for advanced air mobility and UAS systems.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VII ("Department of Homeland Security Activities") supports establishing one or more Institutes to advance research in these fields.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VII ("Department of Homeland Security Activities") establishes a Counter-UAS Center of Excellence within the Department of Homeland Security.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VII ("Department of Homeland Security Activities") specifies selection criteria for host institutions, emphasizing past performance, geographic proximity to federal facilities, and capabilities in AI and machine learning.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VII ("Department of Homeland Security Activities") permits use of funds for fundamental research, evaluation, education, and training related to counter-UAS systems.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VII ("Department of Homeland Security Activities") sets the federal share of grants at no more than 75% of costs.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VII ("Department of Homeland Security Activities") authorizes appropriations totaling $30 million to $36.5 million from fiscal years 2024 to 2028.

Fair Trade with China Enforcement Act, Sec. 101 ("Establishment of list of certain products receiving support from government of People's Republic of China pursuant to Made in China 2025 policy") requires the United States Trade Representative to compile this list within 120 days of the enactment and update it annually.

Fair Trade with China Enforcement Act, Sec. 101 ("Establishment of list of certain products receiving support from government of People's Republic of China pursuant to Made in China 2025 policy") mandates inclusion of products specified in key Chinese government documents related to Made in China 2025.

Fair Trade with China Enforcement Act, Sec. 101 ("Establishment of list of certain products receiving support from government of People's Republic of China pursuant to Made in China 2025 policy") includes products that displace net exports of similar U.S. products.

Fair Trade with China Enforcement Act, Sec. 101 ("Establishment of list of certain products receiving support from government of People's Republic of China pursuant to Made in China 2025 policy") enumerates specific industries such as civil aircraft, motor vehicles, advanced medical equipment, agricultural machinery, semiconductors, lithium batteries, artificial intelligence, high-capacity computing, quantum computing, robotics, and biotechnology for inclusion.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 402 ("Hazardous Weather or Water Event Risk Communication") amends Section 406 of the Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Act of 2017 to enhance communication about hazardous weather or water events.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 402 ("Hazardous Weather or Water Event Risk Communication") requires the Under Secretary to maintain and improve NOAA's system for communicating risks of hazardous weather or water events to the public.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 402 ("Hazardous Weather or Water Event Risk Communication") mandates the creation of a social, behavioral, risk, communication, and economic sciences program to simplify and improve communication of hazardous weather or water events.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 402 ("Hazardous Weather or Water Event Risk Communication") directs the program to eliminate or modify confusing terms and improve communication methods.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 402 ("Hazardous Weather or Water Event Risk Communication") instructs the program to develop metrics for evaluating the effectiveness of these communications.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 402 ("Hazardous Weather or Water Event Risk Communication") mandates the development of a support plan informed by research and communications evaluation.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 402 ("Hazardous Weather or Water Event Risk Communication") requires recommendations to be based on the latest social, behavioral, economic, risk, and communications science research, validated using rigorous methods, including AI and machine learning.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 402 ("Hazardous Weather or Water Event Risk Communication") ensures coordination with federal, state, local, tribal, educational, and media partners.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 402 ("Hazardous Weather or Water Event Risk Communication") establishes best practices for timely and consistent communications across public platforms.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 108 ("Computing Resources Prioritization") amends the Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Act to mandate collaboration between the Under Secretary and the Secretary of Energy in leveraging high-performance computing and AI for advanced weather forecasting.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 108 ("Computing Resources Prioritization") requires a competitive, merit-reviewed process for initiative applications, including Federal agencies, National Laboratories, and higher education institutions.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 108 ("Computing Resources Prioritization") mandates coordination of AI and computing research across NOAA to avoid duplication and enhance predictive analysis.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 108 ("Computing Resources Prioritization") directs sharing of model innovations through community-based activities and interagency coordination.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 108 ("Computing Resources Prioritization") authorizes leveraging AI to enhance NOAA’s computing infrastructure for critical missions.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 108 ("Computing Resources Prioritization") allows establishment of centers of excellence for AI and machine learning in weather forecasting.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 108 ("Computing Resources Prioritization") permits multi-year contracts for high-performance and cloud computing systems.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 108 ("Computing Resources Prioritization") requires a report to Congress evaluating the initiative’s effectiveness and future computing needs within two years.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 502 ("National Integrated Drought Information System") amends the National Integrated Drought Information System Act of 2006 to advance and deploy next-generation technologies related to drought, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud technologies.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 502 ("National Integrated Drought Information System") requires incorporation of flash drought research and tools to enhance timely response.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 502 ("National Integrated Drought Information System") mandates utilization of observational networks and refinement of drought indicators for decision-support products by optimizing data from across the Federal Government.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 502 ("National Integrated Drought Information System") establishes memoranda of understanding with the National Mesonet Program to provide coordinated, high-quality, nationwide drought information.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 502 ("National Integrated Drought Information System") directs the transition of existing drought products to probabilistic forecasts and incorporation of new dynamical and statistical forecast modeling tools.

Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 502 ("National Integrated Drought Information System") authorizes appropriations increasing annually from $15,000,000 in fiscal year 2024 to $17,000,000 in fiscal year 2028.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title IV ("National Science Foundation Activities") mandates the National Science Foundation (NSF) to support research and STEM education in advanced air mobility and unmanned aircraft systems.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title IV ("National Science Foundation Activities") supports fundamental research on technologies including AI, safety, autonomous control, materials, and communications systems.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title IV ("National Science Foundation Activities") funds research on practical applications such as weather prediction, disaster response, and infrastructure monitoring.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title IV ("National Science Foundation Activities") supports research on data modeling, validation, security, and ethical use, including privacy concerns.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title IV ("National Science Foundation Activities") encourages middle and high school STEM education related to unmanned aircraft systems through curriculum development and student engagement activities.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title IV ("National Science Foundation Activities") promotes undergraduate and graduate education through curriculum development, hands-on research opportunities, and scholarships.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title IV ("National Science Foundation Activities") develops a skilled technical workforce, including veterans, through national centers and community college programs.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title IV ("National Science Foundation Activities") facilitates public-private partnerships and interagency coordination to avoid research duplication.

National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title IV ("National Science Foundation Activities") authorizes appropriations increasing from $50 million in 2024 to nearly $61 million in 2028.

Kids Online Safety Act, Sec. 13 ("Filter Bubble Transparency Requirements") requires providers of covered internet platforms that use opaque algorithms to notify users about their use and provide detailed information about their operation, including their features, user-specific data collection, and algorithmic inputs in an easily accessible form.

Kids Online Safety Act, Sec. 13 ("Filter Bubble Transparency Requirements") mandates platforms to offer an easily accessible input-transparent algorithm alternative and prohibits discrimination, via methods like differential pricing, against users who choose the alternative.

Kids Online Safety Act, Sec. 13 ("Filter Bubble Transparency Requirements") empowers enforcement by the Federal Trade Commission to treat violations as unfair or deceptive acts under the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Kids Online Safety Act, Sec. 13 ("Filter Bubble Transparency Requirements") exempts small downstream providers and non-profit organizations from certain enforcement provisions.

Fair Trade with China Enforcement Act, Sec. 102 ("Prohibition on export to People's Republic of China of national security sensitive technology and intellectual property") prohibits the Secretary of Commerce from exporting any national security sensitive technology or intellectual property to the People's Republic of China.

Fair Trade with China Enforcement Act, Sec. 102 ("Prohibition on export to People's Republic of China of national security sensitive technology and intellectual property") defines "intellectual property" to include patents, copyrights, trademarks, or trade secrets.

Fair Trade with China Enforcement Act, Sec. 102 ("Prohibition on export to People's Republic of China of national security sensitive technology and intellectual property") defines "national security sensitive technology or intellectual property" to include contributions to China's military, protection of U.S. economic security, and components of key products listed under the Trade Act of 1974.

Fair Trade with China Enforcement Act, Sec. 102 ("Prohibition on export to People's Republic of China of national security sensitive technology and intellectual property") includes in "technology" goods or services related to information systems, internet-based services, production-enhancing logistics, robotics, artificial intelligence, biotechnology, or computing.

MEANS Act establishes an Office of Manufacturing Security and Resilience within the Department of Commerce to oversee the Manufacturing Security and Resilience Program.

MEANS Act mandates the Under Secretary to develop and implement a strategy to strengthen supply chains for critical goods, reducing reliance on concentrated supply chains, particularly from countries of concern.

MEANS Act requires collaboration with other federal agencies to support allies and key international partners in building manufacturing capacity for critical goods.

MEANS Act incentivizes domestic manufacturers to relocate production from countries of concern and increase production capacity, using loans, loan guarantees, and other financial supports.

MEANS Act prioritizes support for activities that enhance the resilience, security, and diversity of supply chains and address supply chain shocks.

MEANS Act mandates periodic submission of strategy reports and program evaluations to Congress, with updates every four years.

MEANS Act allocates $35 billion for fiscal years 2024-2028 to fund the program, with specific allocations for loans, loan guarantees, and administrative costs.

Protect Working Musicians Act of 2023 grants Independent Music Creator Owners immunity from antitrust liability for collectively negotiating music licensing terms with Dominant Online Music Distribution Platforms or companies using generative AI.

Protect Working Musicians Act of 2023 defines "Dominant Online Music Distribution Platform" as entities with over $100 million in annual music-related revenue and specifies exclusions.

Protect Working Musicians Act of 2023 defines "generative artificial intelligence" as AI systems generating novel media based on prompts.

Protect Working Musicians Act of 2023 requires that collective negotiations among Independent Music Creator Owners be nondiscriminatory, not limited to price, and directly related to negotiations with Dominant Online Music Distribution Platforms.

Protect Working Musicians Act of 2023 ensures that collective negotiations do not involve parties other than Independent Music Creator Owners or Dominant Online Music Distribution Platforms.

Protect Working Musicians Act of 2023 stipulates that the Act does not modify, impair, or supersede existing antitrust laws beyond the specified provisions.

Countering Adversarial and Malicious Partnerships at Universities and Schools Act of 2023 requires the Director of National Intelligence, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, to identify Chinese institutions of higher education supporting the People's Liberation Army and Military-Civil Fusion strategy.

Countering Adversarial and Malicious Partnerships at Universities and Schools Act of 2023 mandates submission of an annual list of these identified entities to Congress.

Countering Adversarial and Malicious Partnerships at Universities and Schools Act of 2023 prohibits Department of Defense funding for research, development, testing, and evaluation to entities contracting with identified Chinese institutions.

Countering Adversarial and Malicious Partnerships at Universities and Schools Act of 2023 restricts facilities from hosting or storing classified information unless they certify no active research partnership with identified institutions.

Countering Adversarial and Malicious Partnerships at Universities and Schools Act of 2023 allows the Secretary of State to deny visas to students or employees of identified institutions.

Countering Adversarial and Malicious Partnerships at Universities and Schools Act of 2023 prohibits Department of Education funds for K-12 schools contracting with entities domiciled in China.

Countering Adversarial and Malicious Partnerships at Universities and Schools Act of 2023 authorizes grants to U.S. schools to support Mandarin language instruction and Chinese cultural programming in partnership with Taiwan.

Countering Adversarial and Malicious Partnerships at Universities and Schools Act of 2023 prohibits federal research funds for entities contracting with listed Chinese entities.

Countering Adversarial and Malicious Partnerships at Universities and Schools Act of 2023 lowers the reporting threshold for foreign gifts to institutions of higher education from $250,000 to $50,000.

TORPEDO Act of 2023, Sec. 6 (Reporting requirements on efforts of the Department of State to implement the AUKUS partnership) mandates the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Secretaries of Defense, Commerce, and Energy, to report on the Department of State's implementation of the AUKUS partnership within 90 days of enactment.

TORPEDO Act of 2023, Sec. 6 (Reporting requirements on efforts of the Department of State to implement the AUKUS partnership) requires the report to detail Australia's progress on various submarine-related goals, including infrastructure, workforce training, and basing support.

TORPEDO Act of 2023, Sec. 6 (Reporting requirements on efforts of the Department of State to implement the AUKUS partnership) instructs the report to assess Australia's submarine contributions to U.S. defense objectives and provide a strategy for integrating AUKUS and U.S. submarines.

TORPEDO Act of 2023, Sec. 6 (Reporting requirements on efforts of the Department of State to implement the AUKUS partnership) mandates reporting on U.S. export control processes and recommendations for improvements to facilitate the AUKUS partnership.

TORPEDO Act of 2023, Sec. 6 (Reporting requirements on efforts of the Department of State to implement the AUKUS partnership) demands an interagency report on changes to ITAR and export control regimes to enable defense item exchanges among AUKUS members and Canada.

TORPEDO Act of 2023, Sec. 6 (Reporting requirements on efforts of the Department of State to implement the AUKUS partnership) requires an assessment of efforts to enhance collaboration in AI, quantum technologies, cyber capabilities, and other advanced defense areas.

TORPEDO Act of 2023, Sec. 6 (Reporting requirements on efforts of the Department of State to implement the AUKUS partnership) obligates the President to brief Congress annually for seven years on AUKUS implementation progress.

Deceptive Experiences To Online Users Reduction Act prohibits large online operators from manipulating user interfaces to obscure, subvert, or impair user autonomy, decision making, or consent.

Deceptive Experiences To Online Users Reduction Act requires affirmative express consent from users for covered research and prohibits manipulation aimed at children or teens to encourage compulsive usage.

Deceptive Experiences To Online Users Reduction Act mandates large online operators to disclose the purpose of covered research to users every 90 days and ensure transparency.

Deceptive Experiences To Online Users Reduction Act obligates large online operators to establish independent review boards to oversee user interface design and research, ensuring compliance and preventing exploitative practices.

Deceptive Experiences To Online Users Reduction Act directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop resources for user interface design promoting user autonomy, choice, and decision making.

Deceptive Experiences To Online Users Reduction Act empowers the Federal Trade Commission to enforce compliance, establish regulations for independent review boards, and define acceptable conduct for large online operators.

Deceptive Experiences To Online Users Reduction Act provides safe harbor for operators acting in good faith per established guidelines.

Research and Development Program on New Approaches to Data Analysis for Aviation Safety establishes a new research and development program by the FAA’s NEXTOR III to develop new data analysis approaches for aviation safety.

Research and Development Program on New Approaches to Data Analysis for Aviation Safety includes use of new algorithms and AI methods for analyzing various data sets such as weather, equipment performance, flight delays, safety incidents, and communications.

Research and Development Program on New Approaches to Data Analysis for Aviation Safety requires collaboration among Consortium member institutions, aviation industry partners, FAA units, and NASA’s Aviation Safety Reporting System for data sharing and testing.

Research and Development Program on New Approaches to Data Analysis for Aviation Safety prioritizes understanding human factors contributing to aviation safety risk, including fatigue, distraction, workload, organizational culture, communication, and adherence to safety procedures.

Research and Development Program on New Approaches to Data Analysis for Aviation Safety seeks to improve the design of highly automated aircraft to reduce mode confusion and increase awareness of flight parameters.

Research and Development Program on New Approaches to Data Analysis for Aviation Safety authorizes $20,000,000 annually from 2024 to 2029 for program execution, including grants to participating institutions and FAA units.

Research and Development Program on New Approaches to Data Analysis for Aviation Safety terminates the program 6 years after establishment.

Disincentivizing Internet Service Censorship of Online Users and Restrictions on Speech and Expression Act amends Section 230 of the Communications Act of 1934 to limit liability protections for dominant interactive computer service providers based on their content management practices.

Disincentivizing Internet Service Censorship of Online Users and Restrictions on Speech and Expression Act deems providers as content creators if they engage in content moderation or use targeted algorithmic amplification that expresses, promotes, or suppresses a discernible viewpoint.

Disincentivizing Internet Service Censorship of Online Users and Restrictions on Speech and Expression Act excludes liability protections for actions against religious material that burden the exercise of religion.

Disincentivizing Internet Service Censorship of Online Users and Restrictions on Speech and Expression Act mandates public disclosure of content management mechanisms and practices by providers to enable informed consumer choices and entrepreneurial activities.

Disincentivizing Internet Service Censorship of Online Users and Restrictions on Speech and Expression Act reclassifies immunity under Section 230 as an affirmative defense, requiring providers or users to prove they are not information content providers in legal actions.

Autonomous Vehicle Accessibility Act/AV Accessibility Act cites the Act as the “Autonomous Vehicle Accessibility Act” or the “AV Accessibility Act”.

Autonomous Vehicle Accessibility Act/AV Accessibility Act defines key terms including “disability,” “public transportation,” and “ride-hail ADS-equipped vehicle.”

Autonomous Vehicle Accessibility Act/AV Accessibility Act prohibits states from issuing licenses for Level 4 or Level 5 ADS-equipped vehicles in a manner that discriminates against individuals with disabilities, in accordance with the ADA.

Autonomous Vehicle Accessibility Act/AV Accessibility Act mandates the Secretary of Transportation to commission a study through the National Academies to identify changes needed in public transportation infrastructure to improve accessibility for individuals with disabilities using ride-hail ADS-equipped vehicles.

Autonomous Vehicle Accessibility Act/AV Accessibility Act authorizes $5,000,000 for the completion of the accessibility infrastructure study, available until expended.

Disrupt Explicit Forged Images And Non-Consensual Edits Act of 2024 amends the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2022, to include "digital forgery" as any intimate visual depiction created via AI or other technological means to appear indistinguishable from an authentic visual depiction.

Disrupt Explicit Forged Images And Non-Consensual Edits Act of 2024 allows identifiable individuals to bring civil action against those who produce, possess, disclose, or solicit digital forgeries without consent, with knowledge or reckless disregard of the lack of consent.

Disrupt Explicit Forged Images And Non-Consensual Edits Act of 2024 specifies relief for plaintiffs, including actual or liquidated damages of $150,000, attorney’s fees, and equitable relief such as injunctions.

Disrupt Explicit Forged Images And Non-Consensual Edits Act of 2024 permits courts to issue orders to protect plaintiffs' privacy, including the use of pseudonyms and sealing personal identifying information.

Disrupt Explicit Forged Images And Non-Consensual Edits Act of 2024 establishes a 10-year statute of limitations for actions, starting from the discovery of the violation or the individual reaching 18 years of age.

Disrupt Explicit Forged Images And Non-Consensual Edits Act of 2024 ensures the Act does not preempt state, federal, or tribal laws that provide at least as much protection.

TORPEDO Act of 2023,  Sec. 12 (Expedited release of advanced technologies to Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom through the foreign military sales program) requires the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Secretary of Defense, to compile a list of pre-cleared military technologies and platforms for sale to Australia, Canada, and the UK within 90 days of enactment and annually thereafter.

TORPEDO Act of 2023,  Sec. 12 (Expedited release of advanced technologies to Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom through the foreign military sales program) expedites the processing of Foreign Military Sales requests from Australia, Canada, and the UK.

TORPEDO Act of 2023,  Sec. 12 (Expedited release of advanced technologies to Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom through the foreign military sales program) mandates the creation of an anticipatory release policy for key Foreign Military Sales capabilities, including AI, hypersonic missiles, cyber capabilities, and quantum technologies, with a presumption of approval.

TORPEDO Act of 2023,  Sec. 12 (Expedited release of advanced technologies to Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom through the foreign military sales program) requires the review and update of interagency policies to incorporate these anticipatory release provisions.

Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Sec. 909 ("Requirement to Ensure Intelligence Community Directives Appropriately Account for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Tools in Intelligence Products") requires the Director of National Intelligence to brief congressional intelligence committees within 120 days on whether current intelligence community directives provide sufficient guidance on the use of AI and machine learning tools in intelligence products.

Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Sec. 909 ("Requirement to Ensure Intelligence Community Directives Appropriately Account for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Tools in Intelligence Products") mandates the briefing to include a determination of whether Intelligence Community Directives 203 and 206, and other relevant directives, offer adequate guidance on using, sourcing, and providing transparency for AI and machine learning tools.

Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Sec. 909 ("Requirement to Ensure Intelligence Community Directives Appropriately Account for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Tools in Intelligence Products") requires the Director to assess if these directives need updates to enhance guidance and direction.

Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Sec. 909 ("Requirement to Ensure Intelligence Community Directives Appropriately Account for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Tools in Intelligence Products") obligates the Director to explain why no updates are needed if deemed sufficient, or to provide a plan and timeline for necessary updates if improvements are required.

Atomic Energy Advancement Act, Sec. 123 ("Advancement of Nuclear Regulatory Oversight") requires the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to report to Congress on actions taken during the COVID-19 emergency, including revised or suspended regulatory policies and their impacts.

Atomic Energy Advancement Act, Sec. 123 ("Advancement of Nuclear Regulatory Oversight") mandates NRC to develop a report within one year identifying improvements in nuclear oversight and inspections using risk-informed, performance-based procedures, information technologies, and AI.

Atomic Energy Advancement Act, Sec. 123 ("Advancement of Nuclear Regulatory Oversight") obligates NRC to seek input from stakeholders like the Secretary of Energy, National Laboratories, and the nuclear energy industry.

Atomic Energy Advancement Act, Sec. 123 ("Advancement of Nuclear Regulatory Oversight") directs NRC to assess the use of AI and machine learning to enhance oversight and inspection decisions.

Atomic Energy Advancement Act, Sec. 123 ("Advancement of Nuclear Regulatory Oversight") instructs NRC to identify specific actions for incorporating advanced technologies into their activities without compromising their mission.

Stop Fentanyl at the Border Act appropriates $1,090,000,000 to U.S. Customs and Border Protection for technology improvements, including non-intrusive inspection scanning systems and anomaly detection algorithms, to enhance fentanyl interdiction at land borders.

Stop Fentanyl at the Border Act appropriates $223,000,000 to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to expand efforts to interdict fentanyl and disrupt transnational criminal networks, including funds for additional special agents and joint surge operations.

Stop Fentanyl at the Border Act mandates submission of reports by March 31, 2028, detailing impacts of Border Patrol Processing Coordinator positions, equipment needs for outbound inspections, and summaries of non-intrusive inspection technology at land ports of entry.

Stop Fentanyl at the Border Act creates penalties for knowingly damaging or evading border controls, with fines and imprisonment up to 5 years for violations aimed at securing financial gain or furthering criminal organizations.

Forest Data Modernization Act of 2023 requires the Secretary to conduct timber products output studies and national woodland owner surveys.

Forest Data Modernization Act of 2023 mandates the integration of forest carbon data in bi-decadal reviews.

Forest Data Modernization Act of 2023 specifies the need for clear definitions of "forest" in reporting data.

Forest Data Modernization Act of 2023 updates strategic plan to include consistent data collection protocols, integration of new technologies, and enhanced transparency.

Forest Data Modernization Act of 2023 ensures collected data is accessible while maintaining confidentiality of sensitive information.

Forest Data Modernization Act of 2023 compiles and publishes biennial national forest statistics.

Forest Data Modernization Act of 2023 establishes an office or platform to handle complex data requests, with possible fees imposed on requestors.

Forest Data Modernization Act of 2023 publishes annual reports detailing progress on strategic plan implementation, including costs and priorities.

Forest Data Modernization Act of 2023 amends Agriculture Improvement Act to utilize advanced remote sensing and machine learning technologies for data collection and modeling.

Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness and Response Act, Sec. 407 ("Assessment of Artificial Intelligence Threats to Health Security") requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to seek a contract with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine to conduct a study on AI-related health security vulnerabilities within 45 days of enactment.

Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness and Response Act, Sec. 407 ("Assessment of Artificial Intelligence Threats to Health Security") mandates the study to assess risks posed by AI advancements, including chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats.

Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness and Response Act, Sec. 407 ("Assessment of Artificial Intelligence Threats to Health Security") describes roles and capabilities of HHS agencies and other Federal entities in identifying and mitigating these vulnerabilities.

Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness and Response Act, Sec. 407 ("Assessment of Artificial Intelligence Threats to Health Security") summarizes ongoing Federal activities related to these risks.

Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness and Response Act, Sec. 407 ("Assessment of Artificial Intelligence Threats to Health Security") identifies current or anticipated gaps in roles, responsibilities, and capabilities regarding AI-related health security.

Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness and Response Act, Sec. 407 ("Assessment of Artificial Intelligence Threats to Health Security") provides recommendations for improving Federal efforts to address these vulnerabilities.

Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness and Response Act, Sec. 407 ("Assessment of Artificial Intelligence Threats to Health Security") requires the National Academies to submit a report on the study to relevant Senate and House committees within 2 years.

Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness and Response Act, Sec. 407 ("Assessment of Artificial Intelligence Threats to Health Security") mandates the Secretary of HHS to submit a follow-up report on actions taken to mitigate AI-related health security risks within 1 year after the National Academies' report.

Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Sec. 906 ("Programs for Next-Generation Microelectronics in Support of Artificial Intelligence") establishes a program to advance microelectronics research, overseen by the Director of National Intelligence through the Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity.

Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Sec. 906 ("Programs for Next-Generation Microelectronics in Support of Artificial Intelligence") focuses research on next-generation computing models, materials, devices, architectures, and algorithms to enhance artificial intelligence and machine learning.

Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Sec. 906 ("Programs for Next-Generation Microelectronics in Support of Artificial Intelligence") addresses challenges in microelectronics engineering, including physical limits on transistors, interconnects, and memory elements.

Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Sec. 906 ("Programs for Next-Generation Microelectronics in Support of Artificial Intelligence") promotes advancements in computing technologies through multidisciplinary research, encompassing algorithm design, compute capability, generative AI, photonics-based microprocessors, new materials, optical networks, and AI safety for the intelligence community.

Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Sec. 906 ("Programs for Next-Generation Microelectronics in Support of Artificial Intelligence") requires active collaboration with government agencies, academic institutions, and private industry.

Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Sec. 906 ("Programs for Next-Generation Microelectronics in Support of Artificial Intelligence") authorizes appropriations for contracts, grants, and other transactions to support the program.

Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Sec. 906 ("Programs for Next-Generation Microelectronics in Support of Artificial Intelligence") mandates regular briefings to congressional intelligence committees on program progress, partnerships, and future research priorities.

Advancing Nuclear Regulatory Oversight Act requires the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to report to Congress within 180 days on regulatory changes made during the COVID-19 emergency, examining their impact on licensing and safety.

Advancing Nuclear Regulatory Oversight Act mandates the NRC to develop and submit a report within one year identifying specific improvements in oversight and inspection programs, emphasizing risk-informed, performance-based procedures and the use of advanced technologies, including AI and machine learning.

Advancing Nuclear Regulatory Oversight Act instructs the NRC to seek input from stakeholders including the Secretary of Energy, National Laboratories, the nuclear energy industry, and relevant NGOs in developing the report.

Advancing Nuclear Regulatory Oversight Act requires assessment of potential modifications to oversight and inspections, improvement measures, and incorporation of advanced technologies to enhance operational efficiency and safety.

Advancing Nuclear Regulatory Oversight Act obligates the NRC to identify and implement actions based on assessments and recommendations to improve training, inspection, oversight, and licensing activities without compromising its mission.

Advisory for AI-Generated Content Act requires all AI-generated materials to be labeled with a watermark.

Advisory for AI-Generated Content Act authorizes the federal government to establish requirements and standards for watermarks.

Advisory for AI-Generated Content Act enables the federal government to levy penalties against entities that violate the above stipulation.

Advisory for AI-Generated Content Act defines key terms including AI-generating entity, AI-generated material, and covered AI-generated material, specifying criteria for materials that must be watermarked.

SAFE from PRC Investments Act requires public companies and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) investing in companies with ties to the People’s Republic of China (PRC) to disclose whether senior officials of the PRC government or Communist Party of China (CPC) sit on their boards or have executive roles.

SAFE from PRC Investments Act mandates disclosure of cash held in PRC operations, restrictions on cash repatriation, and details of assets, liabilities, and technology transfers.

SAFE from PRC Investments Act obligates reporting on interactions with CPC officials, expenditures on PRC operations, and any lobbying activities in the United States.

SAFE from PRC Investments Act compels ETFs to reveal ownership, CPC branches, contractual agreements, and involvement in PRC industrial policies or military contracts of invested PRC companies.

SAFE from PRC Investments Act requires disclosure of PRC companies’ products and services, U.S. defense contracts, and involvement in sectors like AI, telecommunications, and semiconductors.

United States-Israel Health Technologies Cooperation Act authorizes $4,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2024 through 2026 to fund a bilateral cooperative program with Israel for developing health technologies. Emphasizes advancing technology, personalized medicine, and data usage in relation to emerging infectious diseases.

United States-Israel Health Technologies Cooperation Act includes artificial intelligence, drugs, vaccinations, respiratory assist devices, diagnostic tests, and telemedicine as eligible health technologies. Requires matching contributions from the Government of Israel to access funding. Allows funding for existing bilateral programs or the establishment of new programs in consultation with the Secretary of State under the 2008 Science and Technology Cooperation Agreement.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 931 ("Priority for Australia and the United Kingdom in Foreign Military Sales and Direct Commercial Sales") requires the President to institute expedited policies for defense article and service requests from Australia and the United Kingdom under the AUKUS partnership.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 931 ("Priority for Australia and the United Kingdom in Foreign Military Sales and Direct Commercial Sales") mandates prioritization of these requests over all others, except those from Taiwan and Ukraine.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 931 ("Priority for Australia and the United Kingdom in Foreign Military Sales and Direct Commercial Sales") instructs the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, to establish an anticipatory release policy for technology transfers to Australia, the UK, and Canada.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 931 ("Priority for Australia and the United Kingdom in Foreign Military Sales and Direct Commercial Sales") specifies the inclusion of technologies related to submarines, combat systems, hypersonic missiles, cyber capabilities, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, and other advanced technologies.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 931 ("Priority for Australia and the United Kingdom in Foreign Military Sales and Direct Commercial Sales") subjects technology transfer reviews to an expedited decision-making process.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 931 ("Priority for Australia and the United Kingdom in Foreign Military Sales and Direct Commercial Sales") directs the Secretary and the Secretary of Defense to update interagency policies and guidance to incorporate these anticipatory release provisions.

Do Not Disturb Act requires disclosure at the beginning of robocalls or text messages if artificial intelligence is used to emulate a human being.

Do Not Disturb Act enhances penalties for robocall and telemarketing violations involving AI impersonation, doubling fines for fraudulent or harmful AI-generated calls or messages.

Do Not Disturb Act mandates the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to offer robocall-blocking services at no charge and to develop a tracking system for the top 100 illegal robocall campaigns.

Do Not Disturb Act obligates Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) providers to verify customer identities, monitor robocall patterns, and report violations.

Do Not Disturb Act directs both the FCC and Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to study and regulate AI usage in robocalls and telemarketing, including text message authentication and inbound call restrictions.

Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2023 requires the Assistant Secretary of Commerce to promote U.S. leadership in emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), and strengthen critical supply chains and national security.

Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2023 mandates the establishment of a critical supply chain resiliency and crisis response program within the Department of Commerce, which includes mapping and monitoring AI supply chains.

Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2023 requires coordination with other agencies, industry, and international partners to identify vulnerabilities and prepare for supply chain shocks affecting AI technologies.

Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2023 promotes the growth of domestic manufacturing capacities for AI and other emerging technologies and encourages the relocation of manufacturing facilities to the U.S. or allied countries.

Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2023 supports the development and dissemination of best practices for supply chain resilience, including the use of blockchain and other technologies to authenticate and trace critical goods.

Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2023 mandates regular reporting on the state of AI and other emerging technology supply chains, including assessments of vulnerabilities and recommendations for enhancing resilience.

Promoting Digital Privacy Technologies Act requires the National Science Foundation to support research on privacy enhancing technologies, including de-identification, pseudonymization, and algorithms for data privacy.

Promoting Digital Privacy Technologies Act mandates integration of privacy enhancing technologies into the Computer and Network Security Program as per the Cyber Security Research and Development Act.

Promoting Digital Privacy Technologies Act obliges coordination among the Office of Science and Technology Policy, National Science Foundation, National Institute of Standards and Technology, and Federal Trade Commission to expedite development and use of privacy enhancing technologies.

Promoting Digital Privacy Technologies Act demands outreach by the National Institute of Standards and Technology to gather stakeholder input and promote private and public sector engagement.

Promoting Digital Privacy Technologies Act requires submission of a report within three years on research progress, development of voluntary resources, and policy recommendations to improve communication and coordination among stakeholders.

National Strategy to Utilize Microreactors for Natural Disaster Response Efforts Act mandates the President develop a national strategy for utilizing microreactors to assist with natural disaster response efforts.

National Strategy to Utilize Microreactors for Natural Disaster Response Efforts Act requires consultation with FEMA, DOE, National Guard, Army Corps of Engineers, and Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

National Strategy to Utilize Microreactors for Natural Disaster Response Efforts Act obligates submission of the strategy to Congress within one year and biennially thereafter.

National Strategy to Utilize Microreactors for Natural Disaster Response Efforts Act includes an assessment of current diesel generator usage and environmental impacts compared to microreactors.

National Strategy to Utilize Microreactors for Natural Disaster Response Efforts Act outlines goals and objectives for replacing diesel generators with microreactors.

National Strategy to Utilize Microreactors for Natural Disaster Response Efforts Act calls for a Department of Defense analysis on translating operational microreactor technology for disaster response.

National Strategy to Utilize Microreactors for Natural Disaster Response Efforts Act recommends expedited design approval and licensing for microreactors.

National Strategy to Utilize Microreactors for Natural Disaster Response Efforts Act assesses strategic considerations, including storage, transportation, and integration into existing grids.

National Strategy to Utilize Microreactors for Natural Disaster Response Efforts Act evaluates partnership opportunities for effective deployment.

National Strategy to Utilize Microreactors for Natural Disaster Response Efforts Act encourages the use of AI and predictive tools for disaster preparation involving microreactors.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 303 ("Task force to address artificial intelligence-enabled influence operations") establishes a Countering AI-Enabled Disinformation Task Force within 180 days to identify responses to AI-enabled disinformation threats.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 303 ("Task force to address artificial intelligence-enabled influence operations") requires the Task Force to collaborate with private industry and academia to develop digital content provenance detection techniques.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 303 ("Task force to address artificial intelligence-enabled influence operations") mandates internal coordination within the Department on AI-enabled disinformation issues.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 303 ("Task force to address artificial intelligence-enabled influence operations") directs the Task Force to create a unified international approach for standards and frameworks to counter AI-enabled disinformation.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 303 ("Task force to address artificial intelligence-enabled influence operations") requires the Task Force to identify necessary tools and resources for detecting AI-enabled disinformation, producing counter-messaging, expanding digital literacy, and coordinating with various stakeholders.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 303 ("Task force to address artificial intelligence-enabled influence operations") mandates a report to Congress within one year on the Task Force’s establishment and progress.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 303 ("Task force to address artificial intelligence-enabled influence operations") involves representatives from various relevant offices in the Task Force.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 303 ("Task force to address artificial intelligence-enabled influence operations") defines key terms including "artificial intelligence" and "digital content provenance."

HEARTS Act of 2022 prioritizes nonanimal methods in NIH-supported research proposals.

HEARTS Act of 2022 establishes the National Center for Alternatives to Animals in Research and Testing within NIH.

HEARTS Act of 2022 requires the new center to develop, promote, and fund nonanimal research methods, including AI.

HEARTS Act of 2022 mandates the center to provide training and resources to researchers on nonanimal methods.

HEARTS Act of 2022 obligates federally funded research entities to report the number and species of animals used and plans to reduce their use.

HEARTS Act of 2022 ensures research proposals are reviewed by experts in nonanimal methods.

HEARTS Act of 2022 implements a system of incentives to encourage the use of humane and scientifically satisfactory nonanimal methods.

HEARTS Act of 2022 requires thorough searches for nonanimal alternatives before approving animal use in research.

Diversify Tech Act establishes a Tech Industry Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility (DEIA) Task Force within the Department of Commerce.

Diversify Tech Act mandates the Task Force to conduct audits on minority representation, hiring policies, and layoff trends in the tech industry.

Diversify Tech Act requires submission of an initial audit report to Congress within 60 days of the Task Force’s establishment.

Diversify Tech Act obliges the Task Force to promote DEIA, offer guidance to tech entities, and consult with stakeholders on DEIA issues.

Diversify Tech Act tasks the Task Force with advising on outreach programs and encouraging venture capital investment in minority-owned startups.

Diversify Tech Act mandates annual reports evaluating tech industry progress on DEIA goals, the impact of AI on discrimination, and proposing policy solutions for accountability.

Diversify Tech Act requires a special report on how 2023 tech layoffs affected DEIA, including potential violations of federal laws.

Shifting Forward Vehicle Technologies Research and Development Act requires the Secretary of Energy to conduct a research, development, and demonstration program for advanced vehicle technologies, focusing on reducing greenhouse gas emissions and vehicle manufacturing costs.

Shifting Forward Vehicle Technologies Research and Development Act mandates coordination with other federal agencies and existing programs on electric vehicle integration and critical material recycling.

Shifting Forward Vehicle Technologies Research and Development Act supports the development of advanced batteries, power electronics, electric drive systems, and vehicle electrification technologies.

Shifting Forward Vehicle Technologies Research and Development Act includes provisions for cybersecurity and physical security of vehicle interconnections with the electric grid and other infrastructure.

Shifting Forward Vehicle Technologies Research and Development Act establishes a program for medium- and heavy-duty commercial and transit vehicles, emphasizing advanced energy technologies and efficiency improvements.

Shifting Forward Vehicle Technologies Research and Development Act authorizes the creation of Graduate Automotive Technology Education Centers of Research Excellence to foster advancements in automotive energy technologies.

Shifting Forward Vehicle Technologies Research and Development Act allocates substantial funding for these initiatives through fiscal year 2028, with a total authorization exceeding $2.9 billion.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 941 ("Reporting Related to the AUKUS Partnership") mandates the President to submit the text of any non-binding instrument related to the AUKUS partnership to appropriate congressional committees within 30 days of finalization.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 941 ("Reporting Related to the AUKUS Partnership") excludes the need to resubmit texts already submitted under other legal provisions, while not relieving other legal submission requirements.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 941 ("Reporting Related to the AUKUS Partnership") defines "text" to include all related annexes, appendices, side agreements, and implementing documents.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 941 ("Reporting Related to the AUKUS Partnership") requires the Secretary, in coordination with other officials, to submit a biennial report on the AUKUS partnership starting one year after enactment.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 941 ("Reporting Related to the AUKUS Partnership") specifies that reports must cover defensive capability gaps, costs, industrial base contributions, military benefits, and assessments of Australia’s nuclear submarine contributions.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 941 ("Reporting Related to the AUKUS Partnership") demands updates on progress for Australia’s nuclear submarine development, infrastructure, workforce training, and support facilities.

Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 941 ("Reporting Related to the AUKUS Partnership") requires assessments of trilateral collaboration efforts in areas including underseas capabilities, quantum technologies, AI and autonomy, advanced cyber capabilities, hypersonic technologies, electronic warfare, innovation, and information sharing.

Food and Agriculture Industry Cybersecurity Support Act establishes a food and agriculture cybersecurity clearinghouse within the NTIA to provide publicly available online resources focused on cybersecurity for the food and agriculture industry.

Food and Agriculture Industry Cybersecurity Support Act requires the clearinghouse to offer in-person or virtual support, updated FAQs, and materials for small businesses on critical cybersecurity protections and ransomware response.

Food and Agriculture Industry Cybersecurity Support Act mandates the consolidation of public and private sector best practices into voluntary cybersecurity recommendations for the food and agriculture industry, including continuous monitoring and ransomware attack responses.

Food and Agriculture Industry Cybersecurity Support Act instructs the Assistant Secretary to consult with private sector, federal agencies, trade groups, and civil society organizations in implementing the clearinghouse.

Food and Agriculture Industry Cybersecurity Support Act directs the Comptroller General to study and report on federal efforts to improve cybersecurity in the food and agriculture industry, evaluating effectiveness, resources, coordination, and potential risks of coordinated attacks.

Food and Agriculture Industry Cybersecurity Support Act sunsets the section seven years after enactment.
