Countering Communist China Act, Title I ("Matters Related to Trade, Investment, and Economic Relations"), Sec. 101 ("Preventing Adversaries from Developing Critical Capabilities") requires the President to prescribe regulations prohibiting U.S. persons from engaging in covered activities involving listed technologies and products in the AI development sector.

Countering Communist China Act, Title I ("Matters Related to Trade, Investment, and Economic Relations"), Sec. 101 ("Preventing Adversaries from Developing Critical Capabilities") directs the President to submit annual congressional reports on notifications of covered activities and assessing the need for regulatory amendments.

Countering Communist China Act, Title I ("Matters Related to Trade, Investment, and Economic Relations"), Sec. 101 ("Preventing Adversaries from Developing Critical Capabilities") encourages multilateral engagement to align with allied countries on similar mechanisms for prohibitions and notifications on technologies in the AI sector.

Countering Communist China Act, Title I ("Matters Related to Trade, Investment, and Economic Relations"), Sec. 101 ("Preventing Adversaries from Developing Critical Capabilities") authorizes $25 million for implementation and allows direct hiring to administer the entire Act.

Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act requires the Election Assistance Commission to develop and issue voluntary guidelines for election offices addressing the use and risks of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in election administration within 60 days of enactment.

Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act mandates inclusion of guidelines on the risks and benefits of AI in election activities, cybersecurity risks, the impact of AI-generated information on sharing accurate election information, and the spread of election disinformation.

Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act directs the Election Assistance Commission to study and report on the use and impacts of AI technologies in the 2024 federal elections by November 5, 2025, including the sharing of AI-generated information and the use of AI by election offices.

Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act requires the Election Assistance Commission to review and update the voluntary guidelines based on the study's findings.

Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VIII ("Forestry"), Sec. 8414 ("Public-Private Wildfire Technology Deployment and Testbed Partnership") establishes a deployment and testbed pilot program for new and innovative wildfire prevention, detection, communication, and mitigation technologies.

Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VIII ("Forestry"), Sec. 8414 ("Public-Private Wildfire Technology Deployment and Testbed Partnership") requires incorporation of the Pilot Program into an existing interagency coordinating group on wildfires.

Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VIII ("Forestry"), Sec. 8414 ("Public-Private Wildfire Technology Deployment and Testbed Partnership") mandates consultation with covered agencies to identify key technology priority areas.

Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VIII ("Forestry"), Sec. 8414 ("Public-Private Wildfire Technology Deployment and Testbed Partnership") partners with selected covered entities for real-time and on-the-ground testing of technology during wildfire mitigation activities.

Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VIII ("Forestry"), Sec. 8414 ("Public-Private Wildfire Technology Deployment and Testbed Partnership") prioritizes emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, quantum sensing, and augmented reality, for wildfire mitigation.

Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VIII ("Forestry"), Sec. 8414 ("Public-Private Wildfire Technology Deployment and Testbed Partnership") requires submission of annual reports to appropriate committees, detailing participating entities, tested technologies, costs, outreach efforts, and assessments.

Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VIII ("Forestry"), Sec. 8414 ("Public-Private Wildfire Technology Deployment and Testbed Partnership") expires the Pilot Program on September 30, 2029.

Air Tour and Sport Parachuting Safety Improvement Act of 2023 requires the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Administrator to issue a final rule within 24 months mandating safety management systems for certain operators under part 135 of title 14.

Air Tour and Sport Parachuting Safety Improvement Act of 2023 prohibits, beginning three years after enactment, commercial air tours without a certificate under part 119 of title 14, unless meeting specific temporary exceptions.

Air Tour and Sport Parachuting Safety Improvement Act of 2023 mandates new or revised regulations within three years to incorporate controlled flight into terrain and in-flight loss of control avoidance training for certificated commercial air tour operators.

Air Tour and Sport Parachuting Safety Improvement Act of 2023 convenes an aviation rulemaking committee to develop standards for flight data monitoring, terrain awareness, and traffic avoidance for commercial air tour operators.

Air Tour and Sport Parachuting Safety Improvement Act of 2023 directs the Administrator to submit reports and issue proposed rulemakings and final rules based on the aviation rulemaking committee's recommendations within specified timelines.

Air Tour and Sport Parachuting Safety Improvement Act of 2023 requires the FAA to improve the process for obtaining operating certificates and report on the efficiency and resource needs of this process.

Air Tour and Sport Parachuting Safety Improvement Act of 2023 authorizes appropriations as necessary to implement the Act.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2024, Title II ("Coast Guard"), Sec. 207 ("Report on establishment of unmanned systems capabilities office") mandates the Commandant to submit a report within one year outlining a plan for establishing an unmanned systems capabilities office within the Coast Guard.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2024, Title II ("Coast Guard"), Sec. 207 ("Report on establishment of unmanned systems capabilities office") requires the report to include a management strategy for the acquisition, development, and deployment of unmanned and counter-unmanned system technologies.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2024, Title II ("Coast Guard"), Sec. 207 ("Report on establishment of unmanned systems capabilities office") specifies the need for a service-wide coordination strategy to synchronize efforts across the Coast Guard.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2024, Title II ("Coast Guard"), Sec. 207 ("Report on establishment of unmanned systems capabilities office") identifies contracting and acquisition authorities necessary to expedite technology development and deployment.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2024, Title II ("Coast Guard"), Sec. 207 ("Report on establishment of unmanned systems capabilities office") lists commercially available technologies useful for the Coast Guard.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2024, Title II ("Coast Guard"), Sec. 207 ("Report on establishment of unmanned systems capabilities office") calls for a cross-agency collaboration plan with the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and other relevant agencies.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2024, Title II ("Coast Guard"), Sec. 207 ("Report on establishment of unmanned systems capabilities office") highlights opportunities to share unmanned system data to improve maritime domain awareness.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2024, Title II ("Coast Guard"), Sec. 207 ("Report on establishment of unmanned systems capabilities office") requires the development of a concept of operations for a data ecosystem supporting unmanned systems, including AI and machine learning tools.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2024, Title III ("Shipping and Navigation"), Sec. 342 ("Establishment of National Advisory Committee on Autonomous Maritime Systems") advises the Secretary on regulation and use of Autonomous Systems within U.S. territorial waters.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2024, Title III ("Shipping and Navigation"), Sec. 342 ("Establishment of National Advisory Committee on Autonomous Maritime Systems") comprises 9 members appointed by the Secretary with relevant expertise.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2024, Title III ("Shipping and Navigation"), Sec. 342 ("Establishment of National Advisory Committee on Autonomous Maritime Systems") ensures representation from various groups, including marine safety, vessel design, unmanned vehicle production, port authorities, vessel operators, labor unions, maritime pilots, commercial space operators, and academic institutions.

Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2024, Title III ("Shipping and Navigation"), Sec. 342 ("Establishment of National Advisory Committee on Autonomous Maritime Systems") mandates establishment of the Committee within 90 days post-enactment.

21st Century Peace through Strength Act, Division D ("Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act") prohibits entities from distributing, maintaining, or updating foreign adversary controlled applications within the U.S.

21st Century Peace through Strength Act, Division D ("Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act") requires data portability for users before prohibitions apply, enabling users to access their data in a machine-readable format.

21st Century Peace through Strength Act, Division D ("Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act") exempts applications undergoing "qualified divestiture" from prohibitions.

21st Century Peace through Strength Act, Division D ("Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act") enforces penalties up to $5,000 per user for distribution violations and $500 per user for data portability violations.

21st Century Peace through Strength Act, Division D ("Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act") mandates the Attorney General to investigate and enforce compliance through civil penalties or court actions.

21st Century Peace through Strength Act, Division D ("Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act") defines "foreign adversary controlled applications" and "qualified divestiture" to ensure clarity in application and exemptions.

21st Century Peace through Strength Act, Division D ("Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act") grants judicial review exclusively to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit, with specified time limits for challenges.

Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VI ("Rural Development"), Sec. 6303 ("Promoting Precision Agriculture") promotes United States leadership in developing standards for precision agriculture.

Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VI ("Rural Development"), Sec. 6303 ("Promoting Precision Agriculture") mandates the Secretary to develop voluntary, consensus-based interconnectivity standards for precision agriculture within two years.

Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VI ("Rural Development"), Sec. 6303 ("Promoting Precision Agriculture") requires consultation with NIST, FCC, public, and private stakeholders, including voluntary consensus standards development organizations.

Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VI ("Rural Development"), Sec. 6303 ("Promoting Precision Agriculture") considers the impact of advanced wireless communications technology and artificial intelligence on precision agriculture.

Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VI ("Rural Development"), Sec. 6303 ("Promoting Precision Agriculture") addresses cybersecurity challenges and connectivity needs of precision agriculture technology.

Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VI ("Rural Development"), Sec. 6303 ("Promoting Precision Agriculture") directs the Comptroller General to assess the developed standards one year after implementation and biennially for eight years.

Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VI ("Rural Development"), Sec. 6303 ("Promoting Precision Agriculture") obligates the Comptroller General to report findings to relevant Senate and House committees.

Countering Communist China Act, Title VI ("Matters Related to Democracy, Human Rights, and Taiwan"), Sec. 615 ("Deterring America's Technological Adversaries Act") prohibits U.S. persons from engaging in transactions involving sensitive personal data with entities subject to Chinese influence.

Countering Communist China Act, Title VI ("Matters Related to Democracy, Human Rights, and Taiwan"), Sec. 615 ("Deterring America's Technological Adversaries Act") requires the President to impose sanctions on foreign persons dealing in connected software applications under Chinese control, facilitating military, espionage, or malicious cyber activities.

Countering Communist China Act, Title VI ("Matters Related to Democracy, Human Rights, and Taiwan"), Sec. 615 ("Deterring America's Technological Adversaries Act") mandates sanctions for foreign persons involved in election interference against the U.S. or its allies, or influencing U.S. policy in favor of China.

Countering Communist China Act, Title VI ("Matters Related to Democracy, Human Rights, and Taiwan"), Sec. 615 ("Deterring America's Technological Adversaries Act") directs the President to determine and report on whether entities like ByteDance and TikTok meet criteria for sanctions.

Countering Communist China Act, Title VI ("Matters Related to Democracy, Human Rights, and Taiwan"), Sec. 615 ("Deterring America's Technological Adversaries Act") empowers the President to block all transactions involving property of sanctioned foreign persons within U.S. jurisdiction.

Countering Communist China Act, Title VI ("Matters Related to Democracy, Human Rights, and Taiwan"), Sec. 615 ("Deterring America's Technological Adversaries Act") allows the President to waive sanctions on a case-by-case basis if vital to U.S. national security interests.

Countering Communist China Act, Title VI ("Matters Related to Democracy, Human Rights, and Taiwan"), Sec. 615 ("Deterring America's Technological Adversaries Act") terminates the section's authorities five years after enactment.

AI CONSENT Act requires companies to obtain informed consent from consumers before using their data to train AI systems.

AI CONSENT Act requires companies to explain clearly and concisely how consumer data will be used for AI training.

AI CONSENT Act mandates disclosure of further data usage, including transfers to third-party entities.

AI CONSENT Act directs the FTC to issue a report on the progress of converting covered data to de-identified data (for Congress' evaluation).

AI CONSENT Act treats violations as unfair or deceptive acts under the Federal Trade Commission Act and subjects violators to penalties.

Department of Peacebuilding Act of 2023, Sec. 107 ("Office of Technology for Peace") establishes an Office of Technology for Peace within the Department, headed by the Assistant Secretary for Technology for Peace.

Department of Peacebuilding Act of 2023, Sec. 107 ("Office of Technology for Peace") tasks the Assistant Secretary with overseeing awareness, study, and ethical implications of technologies, including artificial intelligence, on domestic and international peace.

Department of Peacebuilding Act of 2023, Sec. 107 ("Office of Technology for Peace") mandates the dissemination of applicable policies and research in consultation with the Department of State.

Department of Peacebuilding Act of 2023, Sec. 107 ("Office of Technology for Peace") requires the Assistant Secretary to provide grants for technologies in transportation, communications, agriculture, medicine, and energy that are nonviolent.

Department of Peacebuilding Act of 2023, Sec. 107 ("Office of Technology for Peace") encourages grants that promote conservation and sustainability of natural resources to prevent future conflicts.

Department of Peacebuilding Act of 2023, Sec. 107 ("Office of Technology for Peace") promotes the development of a green, peaceful economy through these grants.

Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act of 2024 establishes the Export Enforcement Coordination Center within the Department of Homeland Security to coordinate export enforcement among various federal departments and agencies.

Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act of 2024 focuses the Center's efforts on sensitive technologies, including advanced artificial intelligence capabilities, semiconductors, and quantum technology.

Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act of 2024 designates the Center as the primary forum for coordinating efforts against unlawful transshipment and diversion of exports, particularly to countries like China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea.

Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act of 2024 requires the Center to develop best practices and disseminate actionable information to the private sector about export control risks.

Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act of 2024 mandates the submission of reports to Congress on the value and logistics of posting U.S. and foreign law enforcement officials to enhance export control enforcement.

Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act of 2024 authorizes $25,000,000 for the establishment of the Center for fiscal year 2025.

Countering Communist China Act, Title I ("Matters Related to Trade, Investment, and Economic Relations"), Sec. 102 ("Sanctions with Respect to Communist Chinese Military and Surveillance Companies") focuses particular attention on foreign persons engaged in AI, machine learning, robotics, quantum information science, and other advanced technologies.

Countering Communist China Act, Title I ("Matters Related to Trade, Investment, and Economic Relations"), Sec. 102 ("Sanctions with Respect to Communist Chinese Military and Surveillance Companies") utilizes the International Emergency Economic Powers Act to block and prohibit transactions involving sanctioned foreign persons' property within U.S. jurisdiction.

AI PLAN Act requires the Secretary of the Treasury, Secretary of Homeland Security, and Secretary of Commerce to submit a joint report to Congress on the risks of use of AI in financial crimes, including fraud and misinformation, within 180 days of enactment and annually thereafter.

AI PLAN Act mandates the inclusion in the report of interagency policies, procedures, and resources needed to defend against AI-driven financial crimes.

AI PLAN Act directs the report to include the consideration of risks such as deepfakes, voice cloning, foreign election interference, synthetic identities, false market signals, and overall digital fraud.

AI PLAN Act requires the subsequent submission of legislative recommendations and best practices to address risks identified within 90 days of each report.

TAME Extreme Weather Act mandates federal agencies to use AI to adapt to extreme weather, improving weather forecasts, electrical grid resilience, resource deployment, and public-private partnerships.

TAME Extreme Weather Act requires NOAA to develop and curate an Earth system reanalysis dataset, build on existing datasets, and develop AI weather models.

TAME Extreme Weather Act directs NOAA to explore advanced AI applications for weather forecasting, including data assimilation and model emulation.

TAME Extreme Weather Act tasks NOAA with providing technical assistance on AI weather models and developing best practices and public datasets.

TAME Extreme Weather Act establishes programs using AI for wildfire detection, emissions monitoring, and illegal wood product tracking, requiring dataset curation and public access to AI code and data.

TAME Extreme Weather Act instructs the Department of Energy to optimize energy grids using AI, develop environmental review documents, and ensure public access to AI models and training datasets, while protecting national security interests.

National Wildland Fire Risk Reduction Program Act, Sec. 7 (Responsibilities of Program Agencies) mandates NIST to conduct research on wildland fire impacts, firebrands, novel materials, and performance-based mitigation tools.

National Wildland Fire Risk Reduction Program Act, Sec. 7 (Responsibilities of Program Agencies) requires NIST to coordinate federal wildland-urban interface fire investigations and develop methodologies for assessing fire impacts on communities.

National Wildland Fire Risk Reduction Program Act, Sec. 7 (Responsibilities of Program Agencies) directs NSF to support research on wildland fire risks, tools, technologies, and the social and economic factors influencing fire risk reduction.

National Wildland Fire Risk Reduction Program Act, Sec. 7 (Responsibilities of Program Agencies) instructs NOAA to improve wildland fire understanding through research, weather forecasting, data interoperability, and high-performance computing.

National Wildland Fire Risk Reduction Program Act, Sec. 7 (Responsibilities of Program Agencies) tasks NOAA with establishing a Fire Weather Testbed and supporting extramural research on wildland fires.

National Wildland Fire Risk Reduction Program Act, Sec. 7 (Responsibilities of Program Agencies) requires FEMA to support community risk assessment tools, public outreach, and best practices for fire-resistant construction and response.

National Wildland Fire Risk Reduction Program Act, Sec. 7 (Responsibilities of Program Agencies) directs NASA to support wildland fire research, modeling, data systems, and the development of novel monitoring tools.

National Wildland Fire Risk Reduction Program Act, Sec. 7 (Responsibilities of Program Agencies) instructs EPA to research wildland fire smoke characteristics, impacts on air and water quality, and communication of risk reduction strategies.

National Wildland Fire Risk Reduction Program Act, Sec. 7 (Responsibilities of Program Agencies) mandates DOE to develop tools for energy sector resilience to wildland fires and coordinate data resources for improved fire understanding and prevention.

Free Credit Scores for Consumers Act of 2024 expands the definitions of "credit score" and "educational credit score" under the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA).

Free Credit Scores for Consumers Act of 2024 requires consumer reporting agencies (CRAs) to provide consumers with detailed explanations of credit score calculations, including key factors affecting scores.

Free Credit Scores for Consumers Act of 2024 mandates CRAs to disclose prominently the differences and limitations of credit scores and educational credit scores on their websites and in related materials.

Free Credit Scores for Consumers Act of 2024 provides consumers with free credit score disclosures along with their free annual consumer reports upon request.

Free Credit Scores for Consumers Act of 2024 requires private educational lenders, motor vehicle lenders, and residential mortgage lenders to provide consumers with free copies of any consumer reports and credit scores used for underwriting before signing loan agreements.

Free Credit Scores for Consumers Act of 2024 mandates the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) to issue final rules to implement these amendments within two years of enactment.

Kids Online Safety Act, Title II (Filter Bubble Transparency) requires online platforms using opaque algorithms to provide users with clear notice about the use of such algorithms and how user-specific data is utilized.

Kids Online Safety Act, Title II (Filter Bubble Transparency) mandates platforms to allow users to easily switch between opaque algorithms and input-transparent algorithms. Prohibits differential pricing or service denial based on a user's choice to use an input-transparent algorithm.

Kids Online Safety Act, Title II (Filter Bubble Transparency) empowers the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to enforce these requirements as violations of unfair or deceptive practices under the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Kids Online Safety Act, Title II (Filter Bubble Transparency) ensures that trade secrets, confidential business information, or privileged data are not required to be disclosed. Preserves the ability of platforms to allow users to personalize content restrictions and interactions.

Government Surveillance Reform Act of 2023, Title VII (Protection of Car Data from Warrantless Searches) prohibits law enforcement from accessing vehicle data without a warrant, except with operator consent or in emergencies.

Government Surveillance Reform Act of 2023, Title VII (Protection of Car Data from Warrantless Searches) defines "covered vehicle data" to include all onboard and telematics data in noncommercial vehicles, excluding certain data types like automotive software and geolocation data for traffic enforcement.

Government Surveillance Reform Act of 2023, Title VII (Protection of Car Data from Warrantless Searches) prohibits the use of any vehicle data obtained in violation of these provisions as evidence in any legal proceedings. Amends the Driver Privacy Act of 2015 to align with these new restrictions on accessing vehicle data.

Deploying American Blockchains Act of 2023 designates the Secretary of Commerce as the principal advisor to the President on blockchain technology and related applications.

Deploying American Blockchains Act of 2023 requires the Secretary to develop policies and recommendations addressing issues such as decentralized identity, cybersecurity, AI, regulatory compliance, and fraud reduction.

Deploying American Blockchains Act of 2023 instructs the Secretary to promote U.S. leadership and competitiveness in blockchain technology through a Blockchain Deployment Program.

Deploying American Blockchains Act of 2023 mandates the establishment of advisory committees with diverse stakeholders to support blockchain adoption.

Deploying American Blockchains Act of 2023 directs the Secretary to facilitate the development and dissemination of best practices for blockchain technology.

Deploying American Blockchains Act of 2023 obligates the Secretary to consult with private sector stakeholders and disseminate research on blockchain technology.

Deploying American Blockchains Act of 2023 requires annual reports to Congress on activities, recommendations for legislation, and emerging risks and trends in blockchain technology.

Deploying American Blockchains Act of 2023 terminates the Blockchain Deployment Program seven years after enactment.

Border Act of 2024, General Provisions Title allocates $170,000,000 for the procurement and deployment of autonomous surveillance tower systems using AI for border security.

Border Act of 2024, General Provisions Title prohibits the use of funds for non-autonomous border security technology.

Border Act of 2024, General Provisions Title defines "autonomous" systems as those utilizing sensors, onboard computing, and AI for identification.

Border Act of 2024, General Provisions Title mandates quarterly reports on the performance and impact of border security technologies, including AI-driven non-intrusive inspection technology.

Border Act of 2024, General Provisions Title requires acquisition of innovative technologies through open competition, integrating AI and machine learning to improve performance.

Border Act of 2024, General Provisions Title obliges U.S. Customs and Border Protection to submit detailed expenditure plans for autonomous systems, including deployment timelines and sustainment costs.

Border Act of 2024, General Provisions Title instructs the Secretary of Homeland Security to conduct cost-benefit analyses before requesting Department of Defense assistance for border operations, including AI technology impacts.

Community and Hydropower Improvement Act, Sec. 4 (Approach to Environmental Review) amends Section 2403 of the Energy Policy Act of 1992 to enhance environmental review procedures.

Community and Hydropower Improvement Act, Sec. 4 (Approach to Environmental Review) requires the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to cooperate with federal, state, local agencies, and Indian Tribes in preparing environmental assessments or impact statements.

Community and Hydropower Improvement Act, Sec. 4 (Approach to Environmental Review) mandates consideration of ongoing and reasonably foreseeable environmental effects of projects, excluding nonrecurring past effects.

Community and Hydropower Improvement Act, Sec. 4 (Approach to Environmental Review) obliges FERC and cooperating entities to evaluate impacts on fish species and consider appropriate mitigation strategies.

Community and Hydropower Improvement Act, Sec. 4 (Approach to Environmental Review) encourages the use of open-sourced technical models for environmental impact assessments, ensuring their validity and accessibility while protecting intellectual property and proprietary data.

Community and Hydropower Improvement Act, Sec. 4 (Approach to Environmental Review) directs FERC to account for hydrologic alterations over the project license term and assess their impacts on public uses and regional benefits.

Community and Hydropower Improvement Act, Sec. 4 (Approach to Environmental Review) necessitates consideration of innovative solutions and emerging technologies to meet regulatory responsibilities cost-effectively.

Community and Hydropower Improvement Act, Sec. 4 (Approach to Environmental Review) requires periodic technical conferences to evaluate new methodologies and technologies for environmental impact quantification.

Community and Hydropower Improvement Act, Sec. 4 (Approach to Environmental Review) stipulates precise citation of evidence in environmental review records to support findings on material facts.

Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2024 establishes the "Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute" to assist private and public sectors in developing best practices for AI assessment, provide technical assistance, and promote AI innovation, with a director appointed by the Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology.

Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2024 requires the Institute to conduct AI research, develop standards, and create guidelines for safe AI development and deployment, including generative AI and foundation models.

Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2024 mandates the formation of an international coalition to harmonize AI standards and support bilateral and multilateral AI research collaborations. Directs the Comptroller General to report on regulatory barriers affecting AI innovation and recommend legislative or administrative actions to enhance AI development.

AI Grand Challenges Act of 2024 mandates the Director of the National Science Foundation to coordinate with federal agencies and stakeholders, and public input, to identify and select AI grand challenges.

AI Grand Challenges Act of 2024 designates a specific grand challenge for AI-enabled cancer breakthroughs.

AI Grand Challenges Act of 2024 sets eligibility criteria for participants, requiring private entities to be U.S.-based and individuals to be U.S. citizens or permanent residents.

AI Grand Challenges Act of 2024 requires regular reporting to Congress on the program’s progress and results, ensuring public accessibility of reports and competition information.

NSF AI Education Act of 2024 mandates the Director of the National Science Foundation (NSF) to award scholarships for AI studies in fields such as agriculture, education, and advanced manufacturing, prioritizing institutions in underserved areas.

NSF AI Education Act of 2024 directs the NSF to create professional development fellowships for AI and related emerging technologies, fostering collaboration between academia and industry.

NSF AI Education Act of 2024 requires grants for AI training at land-grant colleges and universities, focusing on agricultural applications.

NSF AI Education Act of 2024 authorizes the establishment of Centers of AI Excellence at community colleges and vocational schools to advance AI education and training.

NSF AI Education Act of 2024 advises on guidelines for AI use in primary and secondary education and supports AI education research.

NSF AI Education Act of 2024 prohibits funding to institutions in violation of anti-discrimination laws.

NSF AI Education Act of 2024 directs the development of workforce frameworks for AI and other emerging technologies.

Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act requires the Election Assistance Commission to submit a report with voluntary guidelines to Congress, State and local election offices, and the public within 60 days of enactment.

Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act includes guidelines addressing the risks and benefits of using AI in election administration.

Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act addresses the cybersecurity risks posed by AI technologies in elections.

Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act guides on managing AI-generated information to ensure the sharing of accurate election information.

Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act provides strategies for countering AI-driven election disinformation that undermines public trust.

AI Advancement and Reliability Act of 2024 mandates the Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology to coordinate with federal agencies in establishing the Center.

AI Advancement and Reliability Act of 2024 creates a consortium of stakeholders to support the Center and the National Institute of Standards and Technology in AI-related activities.

AI Advancement and Reliability Act of 2024 authorizes $10 million for fiscal year 2025 for the establishment of the Center.

Lummis-Gillibrand Payment Stablecoin Act (Sec. 1-3) prohibits any person from issuing, creating, or originating an algorithmic payment stablecoin in the United States.

Lummis-Gillibrand Payment Stablecoin Act (Sec. 1-3) mandates that payment stablecoins can only be issued by a registered non-depository trust company with a limit on nominal value or an authorized depository institution as a national payment stablecoin issuer.

Lummis-Gillibrand Payment Stablecoin Act (Sec. 1-3) prohibits the offer or sale of payment stablecoins in the United States except by a U.S. person living in the U.S.

Lummis-Gillibrand Payment Stablecoin Act (Sec. 1-3) requires the Board to adjust the issuance threshold for inflation every four years.

Lummis-Gillibrand Payment Stablecoin Act (Sec. 1-3) directs the Board to establish safe harbor regulations, allowing limited issuance of payment stablecoins under specific conditions and fostering innovation and competition.

Lummis-Gillibrand Payment Stablecoin Act (Sec. 1-3) allows safe harbor status for issuers regulated by equivalent foreign authorities.

Lummis-Gillibrand Payment Stablecoin Act (Sec. 1-3) intends the section to have extraterritorial effect, extending its reach beyond U.S. borders.

Validation and Evaluation for Trustworthy (VET) Artificial Intelligence Act establishes the "VET Artificial Intelligence Act" to create voluntary guidelines for the testing, evaluation, validation, and verification of AI systems, aiming to enhance trust, adoption, and governance.

Validation and Evaluation for Trustworthy (VET) Artificial Intelligence Act mandates the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop and update these guidelines, addressing consumer privacy, harm mitigation, dataset quality, and governance.

Validation and Evaluation for Trustworthy (VET) Artificial Intelligence Act requires the establishment of an Artificial Intelligence Assurance Qualifications Advisory Committee to provide recommendations on qualifications and accreditation for AI assurance processes.

Validation and Evaluation for Trustworthy (VET) Artificial Intelligence Act directs a study to evaluate the capabilities of entities conducting AI assurances, assessing their resources, methodologies, and market demand, and exploring the use of existing accredited facilities for these purposes.

Validation and Evaluation for Trustworthy (VET) Artificial Intelligence Act obliges the publication of guidelines and recommendations for assurance qualifications, ensuring alignment with international standards, without mandating specific technologies.

Validation and Evaluation for Trustworthy (VET) Artificial Intelligence Act involves stakeholder outreach, public comment, and collaboration with various sectors to refine guidelines.

AI Innovation and Development for Efficiency Act of 2024 requires consideration of projects focusing on smart technologies for infrastructure efficiency, pollution minimization, and upgrading existing constructions.

AI Innovation and Development for Efficiency Act of 2024 obliges researchers to conduct impact assessments of energy consumption for AI-enabled technologies.

AI Innovation and Development for Efficiency Act of 2024 prioritizes research conducted at EPSCoR institutions.

AI Innovation and Development for Efficiency Act of 2024 directs the Director to report findings and recommendations on research opportunities and coordination with federal agencies and the private sector within 18 months of enactment.

AI Innovation and Development for Efficiency Act of 2024 requires a report on research results within four years to relevant Senate and House committees.

Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2024 requires these resources to cover topics such as prompt engineering, financial management, cybersecurity, and government contracting.

Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2024 obligates the review and update of these resources every year to ensure relevance and effectiveness.

Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2024 coordinates with the Small Business Administration for the distribution of these resources through its network, including development centers and business opportunity centers.

Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2024 allows for a grants program to fund training providers using the developed resources.

Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2024 demands initial and annual reports to Congress on the progress and impact of the training resources.

Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2024 establishes a sunset clause terminating the program three years after the Act's enactment.

Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act requires financial entities to apply for sandbox participation by detailing their AI project, compliance strategies, and potential public benefits.

Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act mandates applications include risk assessments for systemic financial stability and national security.

Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act obligates financial regulatory agencies to review applications within 90 days, with provisions for approval, denial, or extension.

Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act allows joint applications by multiple entities and necessitates notification to all relevant regulatory bodies.

Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act stipulates data security measures for information provided by AI project sponsors.

Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act directs each financial regulatory agency to promulgate regulations, including modification procedures and confidentiality protocols, within 180 days of the Act’s enactment.

Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act mandates annual reporting to Congress on AI test project outcomes.

Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act permits regulatory agencies to establish additional AI projects as qualifying test projects after public consultation.

Department of Energy AI Act requires the Secretary of Energy to create a centralized AI program focused on research and deployment of AI for science, security, and technology.

Department of Energy AI Act mandates the development of AI training datasets, next-generation computing infrastructure, and safe AI models.

Department of Energy AI Act directs the establishment of at least eight multidisciplinary AI Research and Development Centers to enhance U.S. leadership in AI.

Department of Energy AI Act implements an AI Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Program to address safety and security concerns.

Department of Energy AI Act allocates funds for STEM education and workforce development, emphasizing AI skill training and diversity.

Department of Energy AI Act establishes a program to use AI to improve federal permitting processes for energy projects.

Department of Energy AI Act initiates rulemaking to standardize AI use in grid interconnection.

Department of Energy AI Act requires a report on the impact of AI on data centers and energy security.

Department of Energy AI Act creates the Office of Critical and Emerging Technology to coordinate AI efforts across the DOE and assess technological impacts on national security.

Promoting Responsible Evaluation and Procurement to Advance Readiness for Enterprise-wide Deployment for Artificial Intelligence Act requires the establishment of a Chief Artificial Intelligence Officers Council to coordinate AI use in federal agencies.

Promoting Responsible Evaluation and Procurement to Advance Readiness for Enterprise-wide Deployment for Artificial Intelligence Act mandates agencies to develop risk classification systems for AI use cases, categorizing them as unacceptable, high, medium, or low risk.

Promoting Responsible Evaluation and Procurement to Advance Readiness for Enterprise-wide Deployment for Artificial Intelligence Act prohibits AI use for certain activities, such as mapping facial features for emotion detection or categorizing individuals based on biometric data for sensitive traits.

Promoting Responsible Evaluation and Procurement to Advance Readiness for Enterprise-wide Deployment for Artificial Intelligence Act directs updates to the Federal Acquisition Regulation to ensure AI procurement includes risk and impact assessments.

Promoting Responsible Evaluation and Procurement to Advance Readiness for Enterprise-wide Deployment for Artificial Intelligence Act requires agencies to implement processes for evaluating AI risks and to conduct ongoing monitoring, especially for high-risk use cases.

Promoting Responsible Evaluation and Procurement to Advance Readiness for Enterprise-wide Deployment for Artificial Intelligence Act stipulates comprehensive documentation and transparency requirements for AI models and data.

Promoting Responsible Evaluation and Procurement to Advance Readiness for Enterprise-wide Deployment for Artificial Intelligence Act establishes annual reporting protocols for obstacles in AI testing and evaluation, promoting interagency collaboration to address challenges.

Promoting Responsible Evaluation and Procurement to Advance Readiness for Enterprise-wide Deployment for Artificial Intelligence Act prohibits the use of AI for certain high-risk applications and mandates public disclosure of AI inventories and risk classifications.

Technology in the Parks Act of 2024 requires the creation of internet safety regulations for parks receiving such services to ensure cybersecurity standards similar to those for schools and libraries.

Technology in the Parks Act of 2024 mandates the Secretary of Labor to initiate a grant program for technology training directed towards needy families in local parks, focusing on topics like artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and web development.

Technology in the Parks Act of 2024 limits grant coverage to 10% of the training programs' operating costs and to a duration of no longer than two years.

Securing Elections From AI Deception Act requires election-related AI-generated content to include disclaimers, informing the public that the content was created using AI.

Securing Elections From AI Deception Act mandates developers to provide mechanisms ensuring such disclaimers are permanent or difficult to remove.

Securing Elections From AI Deception Act directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to issue regulations on disclaimer requirements and enforce compliance.

Securing Elections From AI Deception Act obliges developers and deployers to ensure their algorithms meet safety and efficiency standards as outlined.

Sensible Classification Act of 2023, Sec. 7: Implementation of Technology for Classification and Declassification requires a submission of recommendations to the President.

Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act mandates that resources promote understanding and adoption of AI, adhere to international standards, and incorporate federal educational resources.

Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act obligates the Director to review and update these resources every two years.

Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act coordinates with the Small Business Administration for the distribution and utilization of AI resources through its partners, emphasizing voluntary use.

Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act compels a report to Congress within four years, detailing resources, feedback, and recommendations for enhancing AI utilization by small businesses.

AI Leadership To Enable Accountable Deployment Act mandates the creation of Artificial Intelligence Coordination Boards within agencies to address AI issues and publish guiding principles and goals.

AI Leadership To Enable Accountable Deployment Act directs agencies to develop an AI strategy focused on responsible and trustworthy adoption, public trust, risk mitigation, and interagency coordination.

AI Leadership To Enable Accountable Deployment Act requires the Comptroller General to report on the effectiveness of AI Coordination Boards, evaluate Chief AI Officers, and assess AI costs, benefits, and risks, including job impacts.

AI Leadership To Enable Accountable Deployment Act directs the Office of Management and Budget Director to issue updated AI governance guidance within five years.

Nucleic Acid Standards for Biosecurity Act requires the Director, in consultation with Federal agencies, to conduct measurement research supporting biosecurity measures related to nucleic acid synthesis.

Nucleic Acid Standards for Biosecurity Act mandates testing to improve screening accuracy, efficacy, and reliability, along with best practices for operational security and database management.

Nucleic Acid Standards for Biosecurity Act directs the development of technical guidance for effective and secure screening and conformity-assessment standards.

Nucleic Acid Standards for Biosecurity Act establishes a consortium of stakeholders to develop and update best practices and roadmaps for synthetic nucleic acid procurement screening.

Nucleic Acid Standards for Biosecurity Act requires the consortium to report its findings to Congress within 18 months of its first meeting.

Nucleic Acid Standards for Biosecurity Act authorizes $5,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2025 through 2029 for scientific and technical research activities under this initiative.

Consumer Literacy and Empowerment to Advance Responsible Navigation of Artificial Intelligence Act requires the strategy to promote understanding of AI capabilities and limitations, and support informed decisions on AI use.

Consumer Literacy and Empowerment to Advance Responsible Navigation of Artificial Intelligence Act instructs the Secretary to coordinate with various federal agencies, local governments, and private organizations to ensure comprehensive strategy development.

Consumer Literacy and Empowerment to Advance Responsible Navigation of Artificial Intelligence Act requires the creation of specialized use cases for AI literacy in domains like healthcare, finance, and communication.

Consumer Literacy and Empowerment to Advance Responsible Navigation of Artificial Intelligence Act mandates the dissemination of educational materials through multiple communication channels, including a dedicated website, and requires periodic updates to these materials.

Consumer Literacy and Empowerment to Advance Responsible Navigation of Artificial Intelligence Act obliges the Government Accountability Office to report on existing federal AI literacy programs and the Secretary to annually report on the strategy's progress and effectiveness.

Consumer Literacy and Empowerment to Advance Responsible Navigation of Artificial Intelligence Act authorizes necessary appropriations for fiscal years 2025 through 2034 to implement the Act's activities.

Artificial Intelligence Allied Collaboration for Crucial Operations, Research, and Development Act of 2024 requires the strategy to include a summary of ongoing efforts, challenges, and recommended actions for implementing joint partner-sharing networks.

Artificial Intelligence Allied Collaboration for Crucial Operations, Research, and Development Act of 2024 directs the Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense to establish a forum for warfighters to coordinate on AI tools, methodologies, and training within 180 days.

Artificial Intelligence Allied Collaboration for Crucial Operations, Research, and Development Act of 2024 specifies that the forum should identify AI use cases, categorize risks, and prioritize AI tools while considering training shortfalls and opportunities for cooperation with allies.

Artificial Intelligence Allied Collaboration for Crucial Operations, Research, and Development Act of 2024 obligates the Secretary of Defense to report progress on the forum's establishment and recommend legislative actions to Congress within one year.

AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2024 imposes penalties for non-compliance, with fines up to $50,000 per violation, and establishes enforcement mechanisms.

AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2024 obliges the Federal Election Commission to issue regulations within 90 days, outlining criteria for AI content identification and disclosure requirements.

AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2024 requires the FEC to report biannually on compliance and enforcement, providing recommendations for improvements.

Atomic Supply Chain Solutions Act mandates the Secretary of Energy to evaluate the U.S. nuclear supply chain within 270 days, including past efforts, future needs, and lessons from projects like Vogtle 3 and 4.

Atomic Supply Chain Solutions Act analyzes regulatory challenges, including the necessity of N-stamps for nuclear components, cost implications, and potential certification streamlining.

Atomic Supply Chain Solutions Act considers advanced manufacturing and innovative technologies like AI, 3D printing, and robotics for enhancing the nuclear supply chain, with attention to cybersecurity, efficiency, and workforce training.

Atomic Supply Chain Solutions Act describes U.S.-Canada cooperation on nuclear components, assessing competitiveness and recommending collaboration to enhance North American nuclear leadership.

Atomic Supply Chain Solutions Act assesses the impact of anticipated demand for advanced nuclear technology on the supply chain, proposing strategies for resilience.

Atomic Supply Chain Solutions Act establishes U.S. policy to prioritize a robust HALEU market to strengthen energy independence and national security, addressing risks associated with increased nuclear technology demand.

AI Development Practices Act of 2024 obligates the Director to update the voluntary risk management framework for trustworthy AI systems.

AI Development Practices Act of 2024 requires collaboration with public, industry, and academic entities for guidance development.

AI Development Practices Act of 2024 demands a report to Congress within 18 months on new materials or systems produced and policy recommendations for private-public sector coordination.

Digital Social Platform Transparency Act requires translation of terms into all supported languages.

Digital Social Platform Transparency Act obligates companies to submit semiannual terms of service reports to the Attorney General, detailing content moderation practices and AI involvement, including flagged content statistics and appeal outcomes.

Digital Social Platform Transparency Act establishes penalties up to $15,000 per day for non-compliance, managed by the Attorney General, who can take legal action.

Digital Social Platform Transparency Act specifies the creation of a public repository of reports for transparency.

Digital Social Platform Transparency Act defines key terms and grants the Attorney General interpretive authority.

Digital Social Platform Transparency Act ensures Act's obligations and penalties are additional to existing laws.

NSF and USDA Interagency Research Act requires the establishment of memoranda of understanding to coordinate these activities through competitive, merit-based processes.

NSF and USDA Interagency Research Act permits collaborative research in key areas, such as AI, machine learning, automation, and digital agriculture.

NSF and USDA Interagency Research Act encourages data sharing and collaboration among federal agencies, educational institutions, and nonprofit entities.

NSF and USDA Interagency Research Act supports research infrastructure and the development of translational technologies for commercial use.

NSF and USDA Interagency Research Act facilitates public-private partnerships and awards grants to educational institutions to establish a Center for Agricultural Research, Education, and Workforce Development.

NSF and USDA Interagency Research Act authorizes reimbursable agreements to enhance research effectiveness and mandates a report to Congress on interagency coordination and future collaboration opportunities.

NSF and USDA Interagency Research Act ensures research security consistent with the CHIPS Act of 2022.

Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act mandates appointment of a representative from Chief Artificial Intelligence Officers to the Council.

Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act obligates the Council to submit biennial reports detailing recommendations for developing datasets and data governance policies to support AI adoption.

Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act instructs the Council to assess data governance challenges, clarify roles among senior agency leaders, and recommend best practices for AI data use.

Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act requires recommendations for data ownership policies to ensure government rights and pre-procurement AI reviews.

Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act directs the Director to issue guidance based on Council reports.

Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act mandates an annual data management report to Congress clarifying Chief Data Officers' roles in AI governance.

Fraudulent Artificial Intelligence Regulations (FAIR) Elections Act of 2024 sets criteria for source information, including monthly updates and non-violation of the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act.

Fraudulent Artificial Intelligence Regulations (FAIR) Elections Act of 2024 ensures severability of the Act’s provisions, maintaining the validity of remaining sections if any part is invalidated.

State Industrial Competitiveness Act of 2024 mandates that energy studies of manufacturing facilities evaluate systems, emissions, and potential efficiency measures, including AI applications.

State Industrial Competitiveness Act of 2024 allocates at least 5% of funds specifically for Indian Tribes or manufacturers in Indian Country.

State Industrial Competitiveness Act of 2024 limits financial assistance usage, capping administrative expenses at 10% and individual facility funding at $100,000 or 5% of total assistance.

State Industrial Competitiveness Act of 2024 encourages the use of both public and private financing in program implementation.

State Industrial Competitiveness Act of 2024 authorizes $100 million annually from 2025 to 2029 for the program.

Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act mandates the Secretary of Commerce to conduct a public awareness and education campaign on artificial intelligence within 180 days of the Act's enactment, in coordination with relevant Federal agencies.

Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act requires determination of key performance indicators for evaluating the AI Campaign’s effectiveness and gathering baseline data for comparison.

Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act facilitates information exchange on AI to promote knowledge and rights awareness, and identifies best practices for detecting AI-generated media like deepfakes.

Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act conducts outreach to the public about AI's prevalence and applications in daily life and commercial settings.

Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act targets outreach to vulnerable groups, such as senior citizens, to prevent AI-enabled fraud.

Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act promotes workforce opportunities in AI, including Federal Government roles, and engages with educational institutions.

Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act consults with stakeholders from academia, industry, and community organizations on AI usage.

Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act requires a report to Congress within one year on the AI Campaign’s activities, key performance indicators, and recommendations for future actions.

Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act prohibits authorization of additional funds for implementing this Act.

Ending FCC Meddling in Our Elections Act bars the FCC from enacting any rules substantially similar to the aforementioned proposal.

Supercritical Geothermal Research and Development Act requires the creation of a repository for geothermal data, with periodic updates for data standardization and accessibility.

Supercritical Geothermal Research and Development Act mandates a memorandum of understanding for data sharing regarding geothermal development among federal departments.

Supercritical Geothermal Research and Development Act directs the Secretary of the Interior to drill deep exploration boreholes for geothermal mapping.

Supercritical Geothermal Research and Development Act establishes a next-generation geothermal center of excellence to coordinate research, development, and workforce initiatives.

Supercritical Geothermal Research and Development Act authorizes $5 million annually from 2026 to 2030 for these activities.

Supercritical Geothermal Research and Development Act updates geothermal resource assessments quadrennially to include supercritical geothermal regions.

Supercritical Geothermal Research and Development Act requires progress reports on geothermal resource potential and commercialization barriers.

Social Media and AI Resiliency Toolkits in Schools Act specifies guidelines for each different type of toolkit, to be appropriately targeted to their multiple intended audiences: students, parents & guardians, educators, administrators, and healthcare professionals.

Social Media and AI Resiliency Toolkits in Schools Act directs the Secretaries to develop toolkit dissemination strategies, so that the resources reach their intended audiences.

Bureau of Industry and Security Information Technology Modernization Act requires the integration of AI and machine learning into Bureau IT systems to improve decision-making and enforce export controls effectively.

Bureau of Industry and Security Information Technology Modernization Act obligates the Bureau to automate and streamline data sharing with industry, federal agencies, and international partners.

Bureau of Industry and Security Information Technology Modernization Act demands the modernization of IT systems to support seamless data management, enhance security, and facilitate the use of cutting-edge technology.

Bureau of Industry and Security Information Technology Modernization Act stipulates objectives for technology adoption, including productivity enhancement, cost reduction, and improved user experience for U.S. exporters.

Bureau of Industry and Security Information Technology Modernization Act instructs the Under Secretary to reassess staffing needs and consult Congress on personnel adjustments during the modernization.

Bureau of Industry and Security Information Technology Modernization Act authorizes $25 million annually from 2025 to 2028 for these initiatives.

Protecting Patients from Deceptive Drug Ads Online Act mandates the issuance of guidance within 180 days to define false or misleading communications and outline compliance procedures.

Protecting Patients from Deceptive Drug Ads Online Act expands the definition of "manufacturer, packer, or distributor" to include telehealth providers involved in drug advertising.

Protecting Patients from Deceptive Drug Ads Online Act requires reporting of payments related to drug promotion to the Secretary of Health and Human Services.

Protecting Patients from Deceptive Drug Ads Online Act authorizes market surveillance activities using AI to monitor prescription drug promotions on social media and coordinate efforts with the Federal Trade Commission.

Protecting Patients from Deceptive Drug Ads Online Act allocates $15 million annually for fiscal years 2025 to 2029 to support these activities.

Protecting Patients from Deceptive Drug Ads Online Act establishes a process for notifying drug manufacturers of non-compliant communications by influencers or healthcare providers.

Protecting Patients from Deceptive Drug Ads Online Act ensures the severability of the Act's provisions, maintaining validity even if parts are invalidated.

Preventing the Algorithmic Facilitation of Rental Housing Cartels Act of 2024 prohibits rental property owners from using coordinators for algorithmic price coordination, deeming such actions per se violations of the Sherman Act.

Preventing the Algorithmic Facilitation of Rental Housing Cartels Act of 2024 prohibits coordinators from facilitating non-competitive agreements among rental property owners or performing coordinating functions.

Preventing the Algorithmic Facilitation of Rental Housing Cartels Act of 2024 prohibits coordinators from acquiring another coordinator if it lessens competition, violating the Clayton Act.

Preventing the Algorithmic Facilitation of Rental Housing Cartels Act of 2024 empowers the Federal Trade Commission, the Attorney General, and State Attorneys General to enforce the Act with the same powers and duties as the FTC Act, Sherman Act, and Clayton Act.

Preventing the Algorithmic Facilitation of Rental Housing Cartels Act of 2024 allows civil actions by injured persons to recover treble damages and litigation costs, with the option to invalidate pre-dispute arbitration agreements.

Preventing the Algorithmic Facilitation of Rental Housing Cartels Act of 2024 clarifies that the Act does not preempt State, Tribal, or local laws that supplement its provisions.

Preventing the Algorithmic Facilitation of Rental Housing Cartels Act of 2024 ensures severability of the Act if any provision is deemed unconstitutional, maintaining the effectiveness of remaining provisions.

Improving Seniors’ Timely Access to Care Act of 2024 obligates plans to provide access to authorization criteria and documentation requirements to providers, suppliers, and enrollees upon request.

Improving Seniors’ Timely Access to Care Act of 2024 empowers the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish response timeframes for prior authorization requests, potentially as short as 24 hours.

Improving Seniors’ Timely Access to Care Act of 2024 tasks the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission with analyzing and reporting on prior authorization use and recommending improvements.

Improving Seniors’ Timely Access to Care Act of 2024 directs the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to study and report on real-time decision processes and the impact of AI on patient access, especially for rural and low-income beneficiaries.

S.4862, A bill to ensure that new advances in artificial intelligence are ethically adopted to improve the health of all individuals, and for other purposes. directs the National Coordinator for Health IT to utilize electronic health records for research, establish data standards, and align with national interoperability frameworks.

Sec. 103, Supporting Affordability and Fairness with Every Bet Act prohibits sports wagering operators from using artificial intelligence to track individual wagers, target specific individuals with offers or promotions, or create gambling products like microbets.

Sec. 103, Supporting Affordability and Fairness with Every Bet Act requires sports wagering operators to ensure data security and to take reasonable steps to prevent unauthorized access or dissemination of wagering and customer data.

Sec. 103, Supporting Affordability and Fairness with Every Bet Act mandates real-time or near-real-time sharing of anonymized sports wagering data with the State regulatory entity.

Sec. 103, Supporting Affordability and Fairness with Every Bet Act imposes strict consumer protections, including restrictions on AI use, limits on deposits, and mandatory affordability checks for high-value wagers.

Sec. 103, Supporting Affordability and Fairness with Every Bet Act establishes comprehensive standards for licensing, recordkeeping, and employee background checks to ensure the integrity and accountability of sports wagering operators.

Sec. 103, Supporting Affordability and Fairness with Every Bet Act requires cooperation with investigations by regulatory authorities and sports organizations, and mandates robust internal controls for operators.

Sec. 103, Supporting Affordability and Fairness with Every Bet Act prohibits advertising targeting problem gamblers or individuals ineligible to wager, and restricts broadcast times and content.

Sec. 103, Supporting Affordability and Fairness with Every Bet Act enforces restrictions to maintain contest integrity and prevent betting on certain events and by prohibited individuals.

Modernizing Retrospective Regulatory Review Act mandates the issuance of guidance within 18 months on using technology, including AI, for conducting retrospective reviews of agency regulations.

Modernizing Retrospective Regulatory Review Act instructs agencies to use technology to identify obsolete, ineffective, or problematic regulations and adequately train personnel in its use.

Modernizing Retrospective Regulatory Review Act obliges agency heads to submit a detailed plan within two years for implementing the guidance, including identifying regulations for review.

Content Origin Protection and Integrity from Edited and Deepfaked Media Act of 2024 requires tools used commercially to create synthetic or synthetically-modified content to provide the option of including machine-readable content provenance information, with security measures to prevent tampering.

Content Origin Protection and Integrity from Edited and Deepfaked Media Act of 2024 prohibits knowingly removing or altering content provenance information in furtherance of unfair or deceptive acts.

Content Origin Protection and Integrity from Edited and Deepfaked Media Act of 2024 prohibits the non-consensual use of content with attached provenance information for training AI systems, requiring express consent and adherence to copyright terms.

Content Origin Protection and Integrity from Edited and Deepfaked Media Act of 2024 empowers the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and state attorneys general to enforce the Act, treating violations as unfair or deceptive acts.

Content Origin Protection and Integrity from Edited and Deepfaked Media Act of 2024 permits private parties to bring civil actions for violations involving content provenance information.

Content Origin Protection and Integrity from Edited and Deepfaked Media Act of 2024 ensures the Act does not alter existing copyright rights and includes provisions for severability, maintaining the Act’s effectiveness even if parts are invalidated.

Sec. 2412. Duty of Care, Digital Consumer Protection Commission Act of 2023 (1) Cause physical, psychological, economic, relational, or repetitional injuries to a person;

Sec. 2412. Duty of Care, Digital Consumer Protection Commission Act of 2023 (2) Discriminate on the basis of standard protected classes, including race and nationality; or

Sec. 2412. Duty of Care, Digital Consumer Protection Commission Act of 2023 (3) Discriminate in the granting of access to important services and opportunities, including employment, credit, and education.

Sec. 2412. Duty of Care, Digital Consumer Protection Commission Act of 2023 exempts private groups not open to the public from the requirements outlined above.

A Bill to prohibit certain uses of automated decision systems by employers, and for other purposes. requires employers to disclose to employees the use of automated decision systems for employment-related decisions and information on the workings of the system and the data used to reach its decision.

A Bill to prohibit certain uses of automated decision systems by employers, and for other purposes. establishes protections for whistleblowers who call attention to violations of this policy.

Fix Our Forests Act, Section 102 ("Fireshed Center") utilizes artificial intelligence and data tools to assess and predict fire and smoke at the wildland-urban interface for improved management, risk reduction, and recovery.

Fix Our Forests Act, Section 102 ("Fireshed Center") promotes data sharing and coordination across federal, state, local, tribal, and private sectors.

Fix Our Forests Act, Section 102 ("Fireshed Center") reduces duplication and fragmentation in predictive services and decision support related to wildland fires.

Fix Our Forests Act, Section 102 ("Fireshed Center") streamlines procurement and cybersecurity processes.

Fix Our Forests Act, Section 102 ("Fireshed Center") develops and disseminates publicly accessible data, models, and technologies for fire risk reduction and recovery planning.

Fix Our Forests Act, Section 102 ("Fireshed Center") maintains the Fireshed Registry and supports its operations with personnel and services from the U.S. Geological Survey and the Forest Service.

Synthetic Biology Advancement Act of 2024 requires the Center to prioritize research in areas like cellular biology, gene editing, and digital agriculture.

Synthetic Biology Advancement Act of 2024 mandates the use of artificial intelligence to accelerate modeling and measurement for synthetic biological solutions.

Synthetic Biology Advancement Act of 2024 provides grants to eligible institutions, fostering partnerships with entities such as nonprofits and national laboratories.

Synthetic Biology Advancement Act of 2024 sets criteria for grant applications, emphasizing the promotion of synthetic biology technologies and sustainability in agriculture.

Synthetic Biology Advancement Act of 2024 directs the Center to coordinate with technology transfer offices to commercialize innovations.

SAFE Bet Act mandates state sports wagering programs to ensure compliance with standards, including consumer protections and advertising restrictions, and requires operators to maintain data security and recordkeeping.

SAFE Bet Act enforces reporting of suspicious transactions and mandates cooperation with investigations into sports wagering activities.

SAFE Bet Act creates a national self-exclusion list to prevent individuals from placing sports wagers across states, and establishes public health initiatives to monitor gambling addiction.

SAFE Bet Act permits states and tribes to enact stricter sports wagering regulations and does not preempt their authority to tax sports wagering.

No CCP Consultants Act prohibits the Department of State from entering, renewing, or extending a contract to contractors that, in the past year, have consulted for foreign entities that pose national security or foreign policy concerns, including any entity under China’s control engaged in national security industries, such as producing AI-related products and services.

No CCP Consultants Act requires companies seeking to provide consulting services for the Department of State to disclose any conflict of interest with foreign entities above, or they may face a debarment of up to five years.

No CCP Consultants Act requires the Secretary of the Department of State to issue procurement policies for the Department to implement the above prohibition, clarify disclosure requirements and penalties when soliciting contracts, and share best practices for how companies can avoid accidentally contracting with foreign entities that pose national security or foreign policy concerns.

Combat Chinese Economic Aggression Act of 2024, Section 4 ("Protection of covered sectors.") amends the Defense Production Act to add Title VIII, focusing on protecting sectors like AI.

Combat Chinese Economic Aggression Act of 2024, Section 4 ("Protection of covered sectors.") defines "covered activities" involving U.S. persons and foreign entities in countries of concern, including AI-related investments and collaborations.

Combat Chinese Economic Aggression Act of 2024, Section 4 ("Protection of covered sectors.") mandates the President to publish and annually update a list of technologies posing national security risks.

Combat Chinese Economic Aggression Act of 2024, Section 4 ("Protection of covered sectors.") empowers the President to prohibit U.S. persons from engaging in certain activities with foreign entities in critical sectors, including AI.

Combat Chinese Economic Aggression Act of 2024, Section 4 ("Protection of covered sectors.") requires mandatory notifications for covered activities not prohibited, with confidentiality protections for submitted information.

Combat Chinese Economic Aggression Act of 2024, Section 4 ("Protection of covered sectors.") obligates annual reporting to Congress on notifications, trends, and effectiveness of measures.

Combat Chinese Economic Aggression Act of 2024, Section 4 ("Protection of covered sectors.") directs the President to issue regulations specifying covered activities and technologies.

Combat Chinese Economic Aggression Act of 2024, Section 4 ("Protection of covered sectors.") encourages multilateral engagement with U.S. allies to develop comparable mechanisms for managing risks in covered sectors.

Combat Chinese Economic Aggression Act of 2024, Section 4 ("Protection of covered sectors.") authorizes penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for violations.

Combat Chinese Economic Aggression Act of 2024, Section 4 ("Protection of covered sectors.") provides for national interest waivers, requiring notification to Congress.

Drone Safety and Efficiency Act requires the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to adopt a performance and risk-based approach when reviewing requests for certificates of waiver under Section 107 of Title 14, Code of Federal Regulations, which establishes rules for the operation of small unmanned aircraft systems (sUAS) for commercial purposes.

Drone Safety and Efficiency Act requires the Administrator to use big data analytics and machine learning to conduct the performance and risk-based approach and refrain from using open-ended descriptive prompts in the waiver application.

Investing in Tomorrow's Workforce Act of 2023 authorizes the Secretary of Labor to award competitive grants to support projects addressing the training needs of workers likely to be displaced by automation.

Investing in Tomorrow's Workforce Act of 2023 prioritizes grants for partnerships in areas with high concentrations of affected populations or industries susceptible to automation.

Investing in Tomorrow's Workforce Act of 2023 requires eligible partnerships to provide training services, develop curricula, and offer employment benefits, such as transportation stipends and paid leave.

Investing in Tomorrow's Workforce Act of 2023 mandates grant recipients to submit comprehensive reports on training outcomes, including transitions to new positions and earnings data.

Investing in Tomorrow's Workforce Act of 2023 expands the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to include training for workers impacted by automation.

Investing in Tomorrow's Workforce Act of 2023 allocates $40 million annually from 2024 to 2028 for national dislocated worker grants to address impacts of automation.

Investing in Tomorrow's Workforce Act of 2023 ensures grant usage aligns with labor standards and nondiscrimination provisions under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act.

Platform Accountability and Transparency Act, Section 9 ("Rulemaking authority") obligates platforms to disclose advertising information, including ad content, targeting parameters, and dissemination metrics, while protecting user privacy.

Platform Accountability and Transparency Act, Section 9 ("Rulemaking authority") requires disclosure of the use of platform algorithms in the recommendation, amplification, or restriction of content and advertising

Platform Accountability and Transparency Act, Section 9 ("Rulemaking authority") compels platforms to report on recommender and ranking algorithms, detailing inputs, objectives, and significant changes, without revealing trade secrets.

Platform Accountability and Transparency Act, Section 9 ("Rulemaking authority") demands transparency in content moderation, with statistics on policy violations, identification methods (including artificial intelligence), and government orders.
