Providing Individuals Various Opportunities for Technical Training to Build a Skills-Based Cyber Workforce Act of 2024 amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to establish the "PIVOTT Program" for expanding cybersecurity education and training.

Providing Individuals Various Opportunities for Technical Training to Build a Skills-Based Cyber Workforce Act of 2024 requires CISA to partner with community colleges and technical schools to offer programs and internships aiming to build a skills-based cyber workforce.

Providing Individuals Various Opportunities for Technical Training to Build a Skills-Based Cyber Workforce Act of 2024 provides full scholarships to eligible students, covering all educational and associated costs.

Providing Individuals Various Opportunities for Technical Training to Build a Skills-Based Cyber Workforce Act of 2024 mandates a two-year service obligation in a cyber role for program participants, with exceptions for military service.

Providing Individuals Various Opportunities for Technical Training to Build a Skills-Based Cyber Workforce Act of 2024 specifies eligible institutions and program components, including skills-based exercises and internships.

Providing Individuals Various Opportunities for Technical Training to Build a Skills-Based Cyber Workforce Act of 2024 directs CISA to conduct outreach initiatives and host recruitment fairs.

Providing Individuals Various Opportunities for Technical Training to Build a Skills-Based Cyber Workforce Act of 2024 establishes program completion benefits, including access to a cyber training database and additional certification opportunities.

Providing Individuals Various Opportunities for Technical Training to Build a Skills-Based Cyber Workforce Act of 2024 sets terms for scholarship repayment if obligations are not met and allows for waiver of repayments in cases of hardship.

Providing Individuals Various Opportunities for Technical Training to Build a Skills-Based Cyber Workforce Act of 2024 outlines enrollment targets and requires reporting on program enrollment and CISA's education and training initiatives.

Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 402 ("Expanding and improving electronic technologies.") mandates the use of electronic monitoring and other technologies in fisheries data collection, allowing vessels to avoid carrying observers if conditions are unsafe.

Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 402 ("Expanding and improving electronic technologies.") requires the Secretary to integrate electronic monitoring and reporting technologies into fishery information collection programs and review these systems every five years.

Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 402 ("Expanding and improving electronic technologies.") directs the Comptroller General to assess the National Marine Fisheries Service's electronic monitoring capabilities and recommend improvements.

Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 402 ("Expanding and improving electronic technologies.") establishes an electronic technologies innovation prize to encourage advancements in AI, machine learning, and data management for fisheries.

Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 402 ("Expanding and improving electronic technologies.") creates an advisory panel to guide the development and deployment of electronic technologies in fisheries, including performance standards and data ownership.

Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 402 ("Expanding and improving electronic technologies.") exempts the advisory panel from the Federal Advisory Committee Act.

Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 402 ("Expanding and improving electronic technologies.") allows Councils to independently develop electronic technologies for data collection and management.

Stop Spying Bosses Act prohibits employers from using workplace surveillance to monitor labor activities, ascertain political or religious views, or determine health or immigration status unrelated to job duties.

Stop Spying Bosses Act requires employers to disclose details about workplace surveillance practices, including data collection methods, frequency, storage locations, business purposes, and third-party transfers, to employees and applicants.

Stop Spying Bosses Act establishes a Privacy and Technology Division within the Department of Labor to oversee compliance and issue regulations.

Stop Spying Bosses Act allows employees to access, correct, and request data collected about them and prohibits data transfer to third parties without disclosure and cybersecurity measures.

Stop Spying Bosses Act grants employees and labor organizations the right to bring civil actions against violations, with potential damages and injunctive relief.

Stop Spying Bosses Act prohibits predispute arbitration agreements regarding surveillance-related disputes.

Stop Spying Bosses Act mandates annual reports to Congress on workplace surveillance impacts and recommendations for mitigating harms.

Stop Spying Bosses Act coordinates with federal and state agencies to ensure consistent regulatory treatment of workplace surveillance.

Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 401 ("Data modernization.") aligns the national strategic plan for fisheries data with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's (NOAA) Artificial Intelligence Strategy to enhance efficiency and interoperability.

Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 401 ("Data modernization.") requires the Secretary, through the Assistant Administrator for Fisheries, to provide a strategic plan to Congress within 180 days, detailing goals, implementation schedules, budgets, stakeholder engagement, and system development.

Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 401 ("Data modernization.") solicits expertise from data management and technology experts both within and outside the government to support the strategic plan.

Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 401 ("Data modernization.") mandates the Secretary to report annually to Congress on progress in implementing the fisheries data modernization efforts.

NO FAKES Act of 2024 establishes the right for individuals and right holders to authorize the use of their voice or visual likeness in digital replicas, treating it as a property right that is licensable but not assignable during the individual's life.

NO FAKES Act of 2024 allows post-mortem transfer and licensing, enabling rights to be inherited and renewed under specific conditions.

NO FAKES Act of 2024 imposes liability for unauthorized production, distribution, or public display of digital replicas without consent, with certain exclusions for news, historical, and public interest uses.

NO FAKES Act of 2024 provides safe harbors for online services that act promptly to remove unauthorized replicas upon notification.

NO FAKES Act of 2024 preempts conflicting state laws, except for those existing before January 2, 2025, or those addressing sexually explicit or election-related replicas.

NO FAKES Act of 2024 applies only to conduct and contracts occurring after the enactment date, while granting rights retroactively to deceased individuals' estates.

SPEED through Screening Act requires the Administrator to submit strategies within one year to reduce patdowns and the need for item divestiture during passenger screening without compromising security.

SPEED through Screening Act considers technological improvements, discrimination reduction among passenger populations, and next-generation screening technologies in developing these strategies.

SPEED through Screening Act mandates a feasibility study on allowing increased volumes of liquids, aerosols, gels, and powders on aircraft without reducing security.

SPEED through Screening Act permits deployment of detection at range technology for screening, subject to feasibility assessments and prioritizes reducing patdowns and enhancing security for vulnerable populations.

SPEED through Screening Act obligates collection and publication of anonymized screening statistics, considering privacy and civil rights, utilizing AI and noninvasive technologies.

SPEED through Screening Act allocates $20 million for fiscal year 2024 to research and deploy improved screening technologies.

SPEED through Screening Act requires annual briefings to congressional committees and a Comptroller General review within two years on the Act's implementation.

Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 203 amends Section 1851(d)(4) of the Social Security Act to include provisions for behavioral health information starting in 2025.

Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 203 requires the provision of information on access to in-network behavioral health providers, including average wait times for new patient appointments and data on provider participation agreements.

Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 203 mandates disclosure of payment request statistics for mental health or substance use disorder services, specifying the percentage handled by in-network versus out-of-network providers.

Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 203 requires reporting on the number and percentage of denials for prior authorization or payment for mental health services compared to non-mental health services, categorized by denial type and service type.

Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 203 specifies the use of decision support, AI, machine learning, clinical decision-making, or other technologies in denial processes, with comparisons to similar physical health conditions.

Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 203 aims to promote informed choice by enhancing transparency in behavioral health service coverage.

Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 201 amends Medicare Advantage plans to require parity in mental health and substance use disorder benefits, ensuring financial and treatment limitations are no more restrictive than those for medical benefits.

Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 201 mandates MA organizations to determine medical necessity for mental health and substance use benefits based on generally accepted standards.

Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 201 requires MA organizations to conduct and submit comparative analyses of nonquantitative treatment limitations (NQTLs) for mental health and substance use disorder benefits.

Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 201 imposes penalties for failing to comply with the mental health parity requirements.

Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 201 extends parity provisions to prescription drug plans, ensuring consistent application across Medicare Advantage and prescription drug plans.

Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 201 directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to issue implementing regulations within 18 months.

Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 201 sets the effective date for amendments to plan years beginning two years post-enactment, with $10 million allocated for implementation funding through the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services.

Agriculture and National Security Act of 2024 mandates the Secretary of Agriculture to prioritize national security alongside homeland security within the Department of Agriculture, including increasing staff with security clearances.

Agriculture and National Security Act of 2024 establishes the position of Senior Advisor for National Security to advise the Secretary and coordinate with the National Security Council on national security matters related to food and agriculture.

Agriculture and National Security Act of 2024 authorizes the Secretary to exchange personnel with defense, national security, law enforcement, and intelligence agencies to improve information sharing and risk mitigation.

Agriculture and National Security Act of 2024 requires biennial reports to Congress and the National Security Council assessing national security gaps in the food and agriculture sector, including cybersecurity and AI, and detailing actions taken and recommendations for policy changes.

Agriculture and National Security Act of 2024 addresses vulnerabilities concerning agricultural data, foreign influence, and emerging technologies.

AI Fraud Deterrence Act amends penalties for financial crimes committed with the assistance of artificial intelligence, increasing fines to $1,000,000 and imprisonment terms.

AI Fraud Deterrence Act mandates fines for AI-assisted money laundering to be not more than $1,000,000 or thrice the value of the funds involved, with imprisonment terms up to 20 years.

AI Fraud Deterrence Act defines "artificial intelligence" according to the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020 definition.

AI Fraud Deterrence Act codifies increased penalties and definitions within the United States Code to deter AI-assisted financial crimes.

Next Generation Military Education Act amends the National Defense Authorization Act to require the Department of Defense to develop and provide distance education courses on artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning for Armed Forces personnel.

Next Generation Military Education Act mandates these courses to cover AI literacy, ethical use, data protection, and awareness of AI-generated content.

Next Generation Military Education Act requires military departments to ensure access and notify personnel about these courses.

Next Generation Military Education Act obligates the Secretary of Defense to report to Congress on the progress of these activities.

Next Generation Military Education Act expands participation in the Digital On-Demand Program to all Department of Defense entities and personnel, promoting AI education.

Next Generation Military Education Act incorporates AI risks and threats into annual cybersecurity training for Armed Forces and civilian Department of Defense employees.

Next Generation Military Education Act requires annual reporting to Congress on the expansion and promotion of the Digital On-Demand Program.

Next Generation Military Education Act defines key terms, including "artificial intelligence" and "Digital On-Demand Program."

Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2024 require each agency that uses, funds, or oversees algorithms to establish an office of civil rights focused on bias, discrimination, and other algorithmic harms.

Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2024 mandate these civil rights offices to employ experts and technologists to address issues related to covered algorithms.

Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2024 obligate each office of civil rights to submit biennial reports to congressional committees detailing the state of algorithms, risks of bias and discrimination, mitigation steps taken, stakeholder engagement, and recommendations for further actions.

Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2024 establish an interagency working group on algorithms and civil rights, led by the Assistant Attorney General of the Civil Rights Division, with membership from each agency's civil rights office.

Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2024 authorize necessary appropriations for agencies to implement the Act's provisions.

Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act amends title 44 of the United States Code to define "artificial intelligence" and "data governance."

Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act requires Chief Data Officers to focus on data management and governance, including AI-related data standards.

Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act mandates the Chief Data Officer Council to enhance data governance, evaluate new technologies, and ensure AI use improves government operations.

Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act directs the Council to report on data governance progress and provide recommendations for AI and emerging technology adoption, including data transparency and privacy.

Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act obliges the Director to issue guidance on implementing Council recommendations and maintain a public inventory of Chief Data Officers.

Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act sets reporting requirements for the Comptroller General on the Council's effectiveness and challenges.

Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act establishes a sunset clause, rendering the section ineffective after December 14, 2031.

Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act prohibits the allocation of additional funds to implement the Act.

Economic Security and Diplomacy Act of 2024 transfers assets, personnel, and duties from existing offices to this new Deputy Secretary role.

Economic Security and Diplomacy Act of 2024 redesignates and relocates various offices and positions, including creating an Assistant Secretary for Technology and Innovation Security, responsible for policy on emerging technologies and research security.

Economic Security and Diplomacy Act of 2024 establishes an Office of Economic Analysis and Targeting to conduct economic analysis, prepare sanctions targeting packages, and manage a federal database on economic security data.

Economic Security and Diplomacy Act of 2024 authorizes $5 million annually for artificial intelligence and machine learning tools to support data analysis.

Economic Security and Diplomacy Act of 2024 allows hiring of additional personnel without standard competitive service requirements to support these new roles and offices.

Economic Security and Diplomacy Act of 2024 designates Foreign Service officers to represent the Deputy Secretary's mission at strategic posts worldwide.

Improving Diagnosis in Medicine Act of 2024 amends the Public Health Service Act to establish a comprehensive research program on diagnostic safety and quality, focusing on reducing diagnostic errors and integrating AI tools.

Improving Diagnosis in Medicine Act of 2024 directs funding for new and existing research centers and mandates stakeholder engagement to enhance diagnostic quality and safety.

Improving Diagnosis in Medicine Act of 2024 requires the convening of an expert panel, including the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer, to recommend data types and sources for research improvement.

Improving Diagnosis in Medicine Act of 2024 establishes an Interagency Council on Improving Diagnosis in Health Care, including members from AI-related departments, to enhance diagnosis quality and identify research gaps.

Improving Diagnosis in Medicine Act of 2024 mandates the creation of a strategic federal plan to improve diagnosis, with updates and progress reports submitted biennially to Congress.

Improving Diagnosis in Medicine Act of 2024 authorizes appropriations for these initiatives from 2025 to 2029, ensuring sustained financial support for improving diagnostic practices and integrating AI solutions.

Supercomputing for Safer Chemicals Act directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to establish a consortium representing federal, state, and academic stakeholders. The consortium will use supercomputing and machine learning to develop models that predict adverse health effects from toxic substances, establishing rapid approaches for large-scale identification of toxic substances and the development of safer alternatives.

Supercomputing for Safer Chemicals Act requires the Consortium to recommend how the information produced can be used in risk assessments by the EPA, other federal agencies, and industry.

Supercomputing for Safer Chemicals Act appropriates funding to the EPA Administrator to carry out the Consortium and requires the Consortium to make its model predictions public and accessible.

Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023 prohibits the use of federal funds to operate autonomous weapons systems which launch nuclear weapons, or select or engage targets for nuclear weapons, without meaningful human control.

Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023 defines 'meaningful human control' as the ability for humans to control the selection and engagement of targets, as well as the time, location and manner of the use of nuclear weapons.

Creating Resources for Every American To Experiment with Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023 establishes a steering committee to oversee the NAIRR.

Creating Resources for Every American To Experiment with Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023 authorizes the National Science Foundation, in coordination with the NAIRR steering committee, to establish the National AI Research Resource.

Creating Resources for Every American To Experiment with Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023 creates a NAIRR Program Management Office to manage the NAIRR's day-to-day operations.

Creating Resources for Every American To Experiment with Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023 directs the Program Management Office to solicit bids for an Operating Entity for the NAIRR and to oversee that Entity.

Creating Resources for Every American To Experiment with Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023 provides for the NAIRR to be resourced with computational resources, data, educational tools and services, and AI testbeds.

Creating Resources for Every American To Experiment with Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023 specifies eligibility for access to resources in the NAIRR, including academic, nonprofit, government, and small businesses, among others.

Creating Resources for Every American To Experiment with Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023 provides for procedures to establish privacy, ethical, safety and scientific integrity requirements for users of the NAIRR.

Creating Resources for Every American To Experiment with Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023 authorizes the NAIRR to charge fees for users at various tiers, including free and subsidized tiers.

Creating Resources for Every American To Experiment with Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023 provides for security requirements to prevent unauthorized access and protect research security.

An Act to amend the general business law, the executive law, the state finance law and the education law, in relation to enacting the "digital fairness act" - Sections 7-9 ("AUTOMATED DECISION SYSTEM IMPACT ASSESSMENTS," etc.) require the state and its entities to conduct Automated Decision System (ADS) Impact Assessments before using any ADS.

An Act to amend the general business law, the executive law, the state finance law and the education law, in relation to enacting the "digital fairness act" - Sections 7-9 ("AUTOMATED DECISION SYSTEM IMPACT ASSESSMENTS," etc.) mandate the engagement of a neutral third party to evaluate the ADS, focusing on statistical impacts on protected classes, privacy, and security.

An Act to amend the general business law, the executive law, the state finance law and the education law, in relation to enacting the "digital fairness act" - Sections 7-9 ("AUTOMATED DECISION SYSTEM IMPACT ASSESSMENTS," etc.) prohibit purchasing or using ADS without publishing the assessment and considering public comments.

An Act to amend the general business law, the executive law, the state finance law and the education law, in relation to enacting the "digital fairness act" - Sections 7-9 ("AUTOMATED DECISION SYSTEM IMPACT ASSESSMENTS," etc.) obligate the state to maintain a list of qualified neutral third parties for conducting assessments.

An Act to amend the general business law, the executive law, the state finance law and the education law, in relation to enacting the "digital fairness act" - Sections 7-9 ("AUTOMATED DECISION SYSTEM IMPACT ASSESSMENTS," etc.) require a comprehensive study on the impacts of ADS, particularly on protected classes, to be published within two years.

An Act to amend the general business law, the executive law, the state finance law and the education law, in relation to enacting the "digital fairness act" - Sections 7-9 ("AUTOMATED DECISION SYSTEM IMPACT ASSESSMENTS," etc.) demand plain-language notifications to individuals affected by ADS decisions and provide mechanisms for human review.

An Act to amend the general business law, the executive law, the state finance law and the education law, in relation to enacting the "digital fairness act" - Sections 7-9 ("AUTOMATED DECISION SYSTEM IMPACT ASSESSMENTS," etc.) ban payments for ADS that do not use open-source software or comply with assessment and policy requirements.

An Act concerning the use of automated tools to assist with hiring decisions and supplementing Title 34 of the Revised Statutes. requires anyone who uses an automated employment decision tool to screen candidates to notify each candidate of using the tool within 30 days.

An Act concerning the use of automated tools to assist with hiring decisions and supplementing Title 34 of the Revised Statutes. provides for collecting civil penalties (fines) if the provisions above are violated.

An Act concerning discrimination and automated decision systems and supplementing P.L.1945, c.169 (C.10:5-1 et seq.). bans banks, mortgage companies and other lending institutions from using AI systems which discriminate against members of a protected class; systems are deemed discriminatory if these disproportionately favor or disfavor members of a protected class in the provision of loans and credit terms.

An Act concerning discrimination and automated decision systems and supplementing P.L.1945, c.169 (C.10:5-1 et seq.). bans insurance companies from using AI systems which discriminate against members of a protected class; systems are deemed discriminatory if these disproportionately favor or disfavor members of a protected class in providing insurance coverage and setting the terms and rates of such coverage.

An Act concerning discrimination and automated decision systems and supplementing P.L.1945, c.169 (C.10:5-1 et seq.). bans health care providers from using AI systems to discriminate against members of a protected class; systems are deemed discriminatory if these disproportionately favor or disfavor members of a protected class in assessing eligibility for healthcare services.

An Act concerning discrimination and automated decision systems and supplementing P.L.1945, c.169 (C.10:5-1 et seq.). categorizes the above use of AI systems which discriminate against members of protected classes as unlawful discrimination; such companies and service providers are subject to fines not exceeding $10,000 on the first instance, if these companies have not committed prior violations within five years of the charge, and permits victims to file civil lawsuits against such companies.

An Act to amend the general business law, in relation to the management
 and oversight of personal data (Section 7) requires any entity in New York that uses AI or another automated process as the sole basis of a decision that denies access to financial services, insurance, housing, public accommodation, healthcare, or basic necessities to:

An Act to amend the general business law, in relation to the management
 and oversight of personal data (Section 7) (a) Clearly and conspicuously disclose that the decision was made solely on the basis of an automated process; and

An Act to amend the general business law, in relation to the management
 and oversight of personal data (Section 7) (b) Enable any affected individual to appeal the decision, including by giving them the right to have a human review it.

An Act to amend the general business law, in relation to the management
 and oversight of personal data (Section 7) requires the above entities, and additionally those that use an automated decision systems to determine access to employment and education, to annually solicit an outside auditor to conduct, and make publicly available, an impact assessment of the system that:

An Act to amend the general business law, in relation to the management
 and oversight of personal data (Section 7) (a) Evaluates the system's objectives, design, and training data, as well as how the system was tested for accuracy and discrimination; and

An Act to amend the general business law, in relation to the management
 and oversight of personal data (Section 7) (b) Assesses whether the system produces discriminatory results on the basis of race, color, ethnicity, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, familial status, biometric information, lawful source of income, or disability.

Voluntary Commitments from Leading Artificial Intelligence Companies acknowledges the voluntary commitments received from Amazon, Anthropic, Google, Inflection, Meta, Microsoft, and OpenAI to the Biden-Harris Administration to help move toward the safe, secure, and transparent development of AI technology.

Voluntary Commitments from Leading Artificial Intelligence Companies specifies various actionable commitments that will support three broad goals: ensuring products are safe before public release, building systems that put security first, and earning public trust. Commitments include internal and external security testing, sharing information across the industry and with governments, civil society, and academia, and investing in cybersecurity and insider threat safeguards.

Voluntary Commitments from Leading Artificial Intelligence Companies announces the Biden-Harris Administration's development of an executive order and intent to pursue bipartisan legislation in these matters.

Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights requires automated systems to undergo pre-deployment testing, risk identification, mitigation, and ongoing monitoring to ensure safety and effectiveness.

Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights requires that systems avoid the use of inappropriate or irrelevant data and that independent evaluations and public reporting confirm system safety and effectiveness.

Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights imposes protections against algorithmic discrimination by incorporating proactive equity assessments, representative data usage, and continuous disparity testing and mitigation.

Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights enforces data privacy through built-in protections, user consent for data collection, and limitations on data use and sharing, particularly in sensitive domains such as health, education, and finance.

Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights institutes heightened oversight and limits on surveillance technologies to protect civil liberties, privacy, and democratic values, with specific restrictions on continuous surveillance in sensitive contexts.

Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights requires designers and deployers of automated systems to provide clear, timely, and accessible notice and explanations of system use, including the rationale behind decisions impacting individuals.

Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights calls for independent evaluations and public reporting to ensure transparency and accountability in the use of automated systems, with detailed documentation and assessments.

Pennsylvania HB 1380 authorizes the department to utilize data analytics and artificial intelligence for eligibility verification and fraud detection in public assistance programs.

Pennsylvania HB 1380 permits the department to access data from other state agencies to verify residency and eligibility of applicants.

Pennsylvania HB 1380 empowers the department to establish rules, regulations, and standards for assistance program administration, including eligibility criteria and benefit modifications.

Pennsylvania HB 1380 requires the department to ensure expenditures do not exceed appropriations and to seek necessary federal waivers or approvals.

Pennsylvania HB 1380 allows the establishment of health savings accounts and medical assistance premiums to aid residents transitioning out of assistance programs.

Pennsylvania HB 1380 mandates physical health managed care organizations to share medical assistance claims data with providers.

New Jersey Bill A537 require automobile insurers using automated or predictive underwriting systems to annually provide the Department of Banking and Insurance with documentation demonstrating no discriminatory outcomes in pricing based on race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or religion.

New Jersey Bill A537 mandate insurers to show that each pricing segment is balanced and not disproportionate to the overall policyholder population.

New Jersey Bill A537 define ‚Äúautomated or predictive underwriting system‚Äù as a computer-generated process, including robotic process automation, artificial intelligence, or other specialized technology, used to evaluate risk and determine insurance rates.

New Jersey Bill A537 authorize the Commissioner of Banking and Insurance to adopt rules and regulations to implement the act.

New Jersey Bill A537 specify that the act takes effect on the first day of the sixth month following enactment and applies to automobile insurance policies initiated or renewed from that date.

Pennsylvania HB 49 establishes a registry of businesses operating artificial intelligence (AI) systems in Pennsylvania.

Pennsylvania HB 49 requires the Department of State to coordinate with other state agencies to create paper and online registry forms.

Pennsylvania HB 49 mandates the collection of specific information from businesses, including business name, IP address, type of AI code, software intent, and contact details.

Pennsylvania HB 49 prohibits the sale or commercial use of collected information and exempts it from Right-to-Know Law disclosure.

Pennsylvania HB 49 maintains a searchable online database for businesses operating AI systems.

Pennsylvania HB 49 obligates the Department of State to submit an annual report on the registry to legislative committees, detailing the number of registered businesses, registrant distribution by agency, and incurred expenses.

Pennsylvania HB 49 defines "artificial intelligence" as computer systems performing tasks requiring human intelligence.

Pennsylvania HB 49 sets the act to take effect 60 days post-enactment.

Rhode Island HB 6286 prohibits companies from using large-scale generative AI models to engage in targeted bias and discrimination.

Rhode Island HB 6286 mandates companies to label outputs created using large-scale generative AI models with a distinctive watermark.

Rhode Island HB 6286 requires companies to secure informed consent from consumers before using their data for training models.

Rhode Island HB 6286 requires companies, to the best of the their extent, to protect the security of collected data from individuals and shield their identities.

Rhode Island HB 6286 requires companies to conduct regular risk assessments that identify and mitigate reasonably foreseeable risks and harms.

Rhode Island HB 6286 mandates companies using large-scale generative AI models to register them with the Rhode Island Attorney General's Office.

Rhode Island HB 6286 requires the Rhode Island Attorney General's Office to maintain a public registry of all companies that have registered under the above stipulation.

North Carolina SB 460 establishes the Study Committee on Automation and the Workforce to analyze the impact of automation on North Carolina's workforce, with a focus on low-income and minority workers.

North Carolina SB 460 requires the Committee to include 11 voting members representing labor organizations, employers, and state legislators, appointed by the Governor and legislative leaders.

North Carolina SB 460 designates seven nonvoting ex officio members from key state departments and educational institutions.

North Carolina SB 460 mandates the Committee to review the effects of automation technologies such as AI, industrial robotics, and self-service technologies on employment.

North Carolina SB 460 instructs the Committee to assess educational and training requirements for workers to adapt to automation.

North Carolina SB 460 requires the Committee to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and Joint Legislative Commission on Governmental Operations before the 2025 General Assembly and biennially thereafter.

New Mexico SM 63 requests the Attorney General to convene a task force to study the Children, Youth, and Families Department's use of structured decision-making tools and philosophy.

New Mexico SM 63 mandates the task force to assess the efficacy, impact, and results of these AI-based tools.

New Mexico SM 63 requires the task force to determine if structured decision-making tools lead to better decisions in child abuse and neglect cases.

New Mexico SM 63 directs the task force to analyze staff training, understanding, and data on repeat maltreatment rates since the tool’s introduction.

New Mexico SM 63 instructs the task force to review the outcomes of voluntary placement agreements and safety plans under this new philosophy.

New Mexico SM 63 obligates the task force to make recommendations for improvements and the future use of these tools.

New Mexico SM 63 involves input from diverse stakeholders, including experts in law enforcement, child maltreatment, behavioral health, and representatives from various departments and communities.

New Mexico SM 63 requires collaboration with a post-secondary institution for research.

New Mexico SM 63 demands findings and recommendations be presented to the legislative health and human services committee by August 1, 2024.

Texas HB 4695 requires commission approval for AI mental health applications and mandates licensed supervision, informed consent, and clear AI disclosure. Permits liability-free testing with specialized consent.

Texas HB 4695 mandates that licensed mental health professionals supervise AI mental health services, ensuring availability for review, communication, and intervention. Obliges providers to obtain informed consent and clearly inform users about the use of AI technology.

Texas HB 4695 subjects AI mental health service providers to the same disciplinary actions and record-keeping requirements as licensed mental health professionals.

New Jersey SB 3876 establishes the position of Artificial Intelligence Officer to develop and update procedures regulating automated systems used by state agencies for critical decisions.

New Jersey SB 3876 mandates state agencies to comply with these procedures and submit inventories of their automated systems, which will be published online.

New Jersey SB 3876 creates the New Jersey Artificial Intelligence Advisory Board to advise state agencies, hold public hearings on preliminary procedures, and issue reports and recommendations.

New Jersey SB 3876 establishes the position of Artificial Intelligence Implementation Officer to review and approve or deny new automated systems based on compliance with procedures, and conduct periodic reevaluations.

New Jersey SB 3876 forms a task force to study AI and create an AI Bill of Rights, with a report due within one year.

New Jersey SB 3876 subjects officers and the board to open public records laws while protecting trade secrets and work product protections.

New York A7106 amends the election law to mandate disclosure of synthetic media in political communications.

New York A7106 requires disclosure for printed or digital political communications to state: "This political communication was created with the assistance of artificial intelligence."

New York A7106 mandates non-printed or digital political communications to clearly display or speak the same statement.

New York A7106 defines "synthetic media" as any media created or modified using artificial intelligence algorithms.

New York A7106 sets the effective date of this act to January 1, 2024.

Massachusetts Bill S. 31 regulate generative AI models, such as ChatGPT, to protect public safety, privacy, and intellectual property rights.

Massachusetts Bill S. 31 define "large-scale generative artificial intelligence model" as those with at least one billion parameters.

Massachusetts Bill S. 31 prohibit the use of AI models for discrimination or bias based on protected characteristics.

Massachusetts Bill S. 31 mandate AI-generated text to contain a distinctive watermark or offer an authentication process to prevent plagiarism.

Massachusetts Bill S. 31 require companies to implement reasonable security measures to protect training data.

Massachusetts Bill S. 31 obtain informed consent from individuals before collecting, using, or disclosing their data.

Massachusetts Bill S. 31 delete or de-identify data when no longer needed for the intended purpose.

Massachusetts Bill S. 31 conduct regular risk assessments to identify and mitigate foreseeable risks and harms.

Massachusetts Bill S. 31 mandate companies operating large-scale AI models to register with the attorney general within 90 days, including detailed model and data practices.

Massachusetts Bill S. 31 authorize the attorney general to adopt regulations and enforce compliance, including bringing legal action for violations.

Massachusetts Bill H.64 establishes a commission within the executive office of technology services and security to study and make recommendations on the use of automated decision systems (ADS) by the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.

Massachusetts Bill H.64 requires the commission to survey all uses of ADS by Massachusetts offices, including procurement, evaluation, training, validation, transparency, and accountability.

Massachusetts Bill H.64 mandates the commission to consult experts on machine learning, algorithmic bias, and civil rights, and to examine research on disparate impacts of ADS based on group characteristics.

Massachusetts Bill H.64 obligates the commission to examine data protection, intellectual property issues, and other opportunities and risks associated with ADS.

Massachusetts Bill H.64 compels the commission to meet at least 10 times a year and hold public hearings for feedback.

Massachusetts Bill H.64 requires the commission to submit an annual report detailing activities, findings, and regulatory recommendations to the governor and state legislature.

New York Bill A5309 amends the state finance law to require state units to purchase only products or services containing algorithmic decision systems adhering to responsible artificial intelligence standards.

New York Bill A5309 mandates the avoidance of harm, including minimizing risks of physical or mental injury, unjustified information deletion or disclosure, and unwarranted damage to property, reputation, or the environment.

New York Bill A5309 emphasizes a commitment to transparency, including full disclosure of the algorithmic decision system's capabilities, limitations, and potential problems.

New York Bill A5309 prioritizes fairness by eliminating discrimination, promoting equality, and providing feedback mechanisms to redress harms.

New York Bill A5309 amends the executive law to define "unlawful discriminatory practice" to include actions performed through algorithmic decision systems.

New York Bill A5309 require the commissioner of taxation and finance to adopt regulations to implement these provisions.

New York S7422 exclude productions using AI that displace employees from being considered a "qualified film" for the Empire State Film Production Credit.

New York S7422 carves out an exception to the above for films covered by current collective bargaining agreements that allow for AI to displace employees.

Australia’s AI Ethics Principles prioritizes AI systems that benefit individuals, society, and the environment throughout their lifecycle.

Australia’s AI Ethics Principles requires AI systems to respect human rights, diversity, and individual autonomy, promoting an equitable society.

Australia’s AI Ethics Principles mandates fairness by ensuring AI inclusivity and accessibility, prohibiting unfair discrimination.

Australia’s AI Ethics Principles demands privacy protection and data security, with ongoing data governance and vulnerability assessments.

Australia’s AI Ethics Principles ensures AI reliability and safety, mandating operation in line with intended purposes and risk management.

Australia’s AI Ethics Principles calls for transparency and explainability, necessitating timely and responsible disclosures of AI impacts.

Australia’s AI Ethics Principles establishes contestability, allowing challenges to AI impacts on individuals or communities through clear processes.

Australia’s AI Ethics Principles holds relevant parties accountable for AI outcomes, requiring identifiable responsibility and human oversight.

Maintaining American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence (EO 13859) mandates the Federal Government to maintain U.S. leadership in AI through a coordinated strategy known as the American AI Initiative.

Maintaining American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence (EO 13859) requires agencies to pursue strategic guidelines to prioritize AI R&D, enhance data accessibility, and reduce barriers for AI deployment, ensuring protection of civil liberties and privacy.

Maintaining American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence (EO 13859) obligates agencies to develop technical standards to minimize vulnerabilities and foster public trust in AI systems.

Maintaining American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence (EO 13859) directs the prioritization and training of American workers in AI-related skills to prepare them for future job markets.

Maintaining American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence (EO 13859) instructs the development of international standards and promotes global collaboration while safeguarding critical AI technologies from foreign adversaries.

Maintaining American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence (EO 13859) develops an action plan to protect U.S. advantages in AI technology against strategic competitors and adversaries.

NSTC/OSTP Framework for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening mandates the federal government to mitigate misuse risks of synthetic nucleic acids by establishing a procurement screening framework.

NSTC/OSTP Framework for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening requires synthetic nucleic acid providers and equipment manufacturers to implement comprehensive screening measures for sequences of concern (SOCs) and verify customer legitimacy.

NSTC/OSTP Framework for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to collaborate with industry to refine technical specifications for effective screening.

NSTC/OSTP Framework for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening obliges federal funding agencies to ensure compliance with the framework for research funded by federal life sciences grants.

NSTC/OSTP Framework for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening instructs providers and manufacturers to report suspicious purchase orders to relevant authorities and retain records for at least three years.

NSTC/OSTP Framework for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening imposes cybersecurity measures to protect sensitive data and customer information, following specific security guidelines.

NSTC/OSTP Framework for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening anticipates framework updates based on technological advancements and encourages the use of independent audits for compliance verification.

AI Liability Directive establishes common rules for non-contractual fault-based civil claims related to damages caused by high-risk AI systems.

AI Liability Directive requires disclosure of evidence from AI providers or users to substantiate claims, with courts empowered to order such disclosures.

AI Liability Directive presumes non-compliance with duty of care if defendants fail to comply with evidence disclosure orders.

AI Liability Directive presumes a causal link between defendant’s fault and AI system's output if certain conditions are met, allowing defendants to rebut the presumption.

AI Liability Directive permits Member States to adopt more favorable rules for claimants, compatibility with Union law required.

AI Liability Directive mandates evaluation and review by the European Commission within five years, considering the necessity of no-fault liability and insurance for AI operators.

AI Liability Directive amends Directive (EU) 2020/1828 to include AI Liability Directive.

AI Liability Directive obligates Member States to transpose the Directive into national law within two years and communicate relevant national legislative texts to the Commission.

AI Safety Summit - Enhancing Frontier AI Safety (Amazon) facilitates AI development and deployment through Amazon Web Services (AWS), offering a comprehensive suite of AI and ML services, including Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Titan Foundation Models, which support generative AI applications.

AI Safety Summit - Enhancing Frontier AI Safety (Amazon) implements risk management and safety protocols, including systematic model evaluation, red teaming, and ongoing security assessments, to mitigate potential AI risks.

AI Safety Summit - Enhancing Frontier AI Safety (Amazon) protects AI models and data using robust logical and physical security measures, such as encryption, access controls, and least privilege principles.

AI Safety Summit - Enhancing Frontier AI Safety (Amazon) shares AI service information transparently through AI Service Cards, detailing intended use cases, limitations, and responsible AI design considerations.

AI Safety Summit - Enhancing Frontier AI Safety (Amazon) encourages responsible AI use and prohibits misuse through the AWS Responsible AI Policy, which addresses concerns like disinformation and privacy violations.

AI Safety Summit - Enhancing Frontier AI Safety (Amazon) invests in research and academic partnerships to advance responsible AI practices and develop tools for bias mitigation and human oversight.

AI Safety Summit - Enhancing Frontier AI Safety (Amazon) monitors AI misuse post-release, employing classifier guardrails and automated abuse detection to identify and address harmful content and misuse patterns.

OpenAI's Approach to Frontier Risk (An Update for the UK AI Safety Summit) states that OpenAI's is establishing a Preparedness Framework to manage risks from frontier AI models, focusing on a development process governance structure and preemption of catastrophic outcomes; this work will complement existing risk mitigation work and includes a joint Deployment Safety Board with Microsoft.

OpenAI's Approach to Frontier Risk (An Update for the UK AI Safety Summit) states that OpenAI is creating Superalignment and Preparedness teams within the company to align AI systems with human intent and track and prepare for frontier risks, including cybersecurity, CBRN, persuasion, and autonomous replication and adaptation. Notes that OpenAI is also increasing investment into cybersecurity and insider threat safeguards.

OpenAI's Approach to Frontier Risk (An Update for the UK AI Safety Summit) states that OpenAI implemened red-teaming and evaluations to assess new models for safety, including GPT-4 and DALL-E 3, focusing on dual-use capabilities, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and self-replication.

OpenAI's Approach to Frontier Risk (An Update for the UK AI Safety Summit) states that OpenAI will include the publication of a system card in every new AI system, which informs users of key factors impacting system behavior.

OpenAI's Approach to Frontier Risk (An Update for the UK AI Safety Summit) states that OpenAI has initiated a reporting mechanism for responsible disclosure of dangerous capabilities among AI labs, focusing on national security-related risks.

OpenAI's Approach to Frontier Risk (An Update for the UK AI Safety Summit) details OpenAI's emphasis post-deployment monitoring for misuse, security controls to protect intellectual property and data, and the development progress provenance techniques to identify AI-generated content.

OpenAI's Approach to Frontier Risk (An Update for the UK AI Safety Summit) states that OpenAI implemented data input controls and provides mechanisms for users to opt-out of their data being used for AI training.

Inventorship Guidance for AI-Assisted Inventions mandates that inventors named on U.S. patents and applications must be natural persons, reaffirming that AI systems cannot be recognized as inventors.

Inventorship Guidance for AI-Assisted Inventions clarifies that AI-assisted inventions are not unpatentable due to improper inventorship, provided a natural person significantly contributed to the invention's conception.

Inventorship Guidance for AI-Assisted Inventions requires that patent applications for AI-assisted inventions name natural persons who meet the Pannu factors as inventors, ensuring each claim has a human contributor.

Inventorship Guidance for AI-Assisted Inventions outlines the duty of disclosure and reasonable inquiry, emphasizing the importance of factual inventorship claims and compliance with regulations.

Inventorship Guidance for AI-Assisted Inventions establishes guidelines for correcting inventorship errors and emphasizes that AI systems cannot hold inventorship rights.

Inventorship Guidance for AI-Assisted Inventions applies guidance to design and plant patents, affirming that significant human contribution is necessary for patent eligibility.

Inventorship Guidance for AI-Assisted Inventions prohibits naming AI systems as inventors in priority claims for U.S. patents and applications, ensuring compliance with U.S. inventorship requirements.

Our Policy on Frontier Safety (Inflection) commits Inflection to a disciplined, phased approach to scaling AI models, emphasizing pre-deployment safety, post-launch monitoring, and global governance.

Our Policy on Frontier Safety (Inflection) requires robust evaluations and third-party red-teaming before public launch to ensure models do not provide harmful information or engage in discriminatory conduct.

Our Policy on Frontier Safety (Inflection) implements strict data input controls and audits, involving executive review and legal evaluations of training data for compliance with legal and ethical standards.

Our Policy on Frontier Safety (Inflection) ensures high-level security controls to prevent unauthorized access and misuse of AI models, including internal restrictions and a bug bounty program.

Our Policy on Frontier Safety (Inflection) maintains around-the-clock monitoring to detect and mitigate model misuse, employing frontier AI to enhance situational awareness.

Our Policy on Frontier Safety (Inflection) publishes model capabilities and limitations, supporting transparency and enabling risk assessment by users and regulators.

Our Policy on Frontier Safety (Inflection) advocates for standardized vulnerability reporting structures and participates in a pilot bug bounty program to encourage third-party disclosures.

Our Policy on Frontier Safety (Inflection) prioritizes research on AI risks and supports the creation of an International Panel on AI Safety.

Our Policy on Frontier Safety (Inflection) promotes cross-industry collaboration for identifying AI-generated material, focusing on child safety and standardized watermarking.

Pay Flexibility, Incentive Pay, and Leave and Workforce Flexibility Programs for Artificial Intelligence (AI), AI-enabling, and Other Key Technical Employees (OPM) allows recruitment, relocation, and retention incentives up to 25% of basic pay, and provides for waivers to increase this limit to 50% based on critical needs.

Pay Flexibility, Incentive Pay, and Leave and Workforce Flexibility Programs for Artificial Intelligence (AI), AI-enabling, and Other Key Technical Employees (OPM) permits setting higher pay rates for employees with superior qualifications or special needs, and requests OPM approval for special rates and critical position pay.

Pay Flexibility, Incentive Pay, and Leave and Workforce Flexibility Programs for Artificial Intelligence (AI), AI-enabling, and Other Key Technical Employees (OPM) authorizes alternative work schedules, telework, and remote work to enhance recruitment and retention.

Pay Flexibility, Incentive Pay, and Leave and Workforce Flexibility Programs for Artificial Intelligence (AI), AI-enabling, and Other Key Technical Employees (OPM) provides service credit for non-Federal work experience towards higher annual leave accrual rates.

Pay Flexibility, Incentive Pay, and Leave and Workforce Flexibility Programs for Artificial Intelligence (AI), AI-enabling, and Other Key Technical Employees (OPM) encourages collaboration with agency officials to design tailored recruitment and retention strategies utilizing available human resources tools.

Bipartisan Framework for U.S. AI Act establishes a licensing regime requiring companies developing sophisticated A.I. models to register with an independent oversight body.

Bipartisan Framework for U.S. AI Act requires developers to maintain risk management, pre-deployment testing, and reporting programs as part of licensing conditions.

Bipartisan Framework for U.S. AI Act grants the oversight body authority to audit companies and cooperate with state Attorneys General.

Bipartisan Framework for U.S. AI Act mandates Congress to ensure A.I. companies are legally accountable for harms caused by their models, including privacy breaches and civil rights violations.

Bipartisan Framework for U.S. AI Act urges Congress to use export controls and sanctions to limit A.I. technology transfers to adversary nations.

Bipartisan Framework for U.S. AI Act promotes transparency by requiring companies to disclose A.I. model information and ensure users know they are interacting with A.I.

Bipartisan Framework for U.S. AI Act requires A.I. system providers to label deepfakes and maintain a public database of A.I. information.

Bipartisan Framework for U.S. AI Act obliges companies to implement consumer protections, including safety brakes and data usage control, especially concerning children.

Part 170: Health Data, Technology, and Interoperability: Certification Program Updates, Algorithm Transparency, and Information Sharing outlines certification criteria for health IT, including decision support interventions that must be evidence-based and use specified data standards.

Section 106.11 Application: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Sex in Education Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance acknowledges requests for examples involving AI and other specific circumstances but declines to provide additional examples or exhaustive lists.

Section 106.11 Application: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Sex in Education Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance confirms obligations for conduct during institution-sponsored events, online classes, and use of digital platforms, including AI technologies.

Train Crew Size Safety Requirements (New Technology and Automated Operations) mandate a risk assessment before initiating operations under special approval processes.

Train Crew Size Safety Requirements (New Technology and Automated Operations) acknowledge freight rail industry's concerns about competition with automated trucking but emphasize rail safety hazards from reduced crew sizes.

Train Crew Size Safety Requirements (New Technology and Automated Operations) disagree with assertions that labor-saving technologies like PTC justify removal of crew members, stating such technologies are not fully developed.

Train Crew Size Safety Requirements (New Technology and Automated Operations) support technological advancement in rail through research on AI and automation, including drones and real-time safety systems.

Train Crew Size Safety Requirements (New Technology and Automated Operations) permit railroads to petition for rulemaking or waivers to use technology that doesn't meet existing regulatory requirements, ensuring safety justifications are provided.

Train Crew Size Safety Requirements (New Technology and Automated Operations) clarify that the rule does not impede innovation but requires description of technology used to support tasks typically performed by a second crew member.

2023 UK AI Safety Summit Response (Meta) demonstrates actions taken in furtherance of the White House Commitments to establish AI guardrails, focusing on safety, security, and trust.

2023 UK AI Safety Summit Response (Meta) conducted extensive model evaluations and red teaming, including external testing at DEFCON, to identify and mitigate risks in AI models including adversarial inputs like unqualified advice.

2023 UK AI Safety Summit Response (Meta) requires information sharing and reporting on AI vulnerabilities with established feedback mechanisms for continuous improvement.

2023 UK AI Safety Summit Response (Meta) implemented robust security controls for AI model weights to ensure model relliability, treating them as core intellectual property.

2023 UK AI Safety Summit Response (Meta) participated in industry initiatives like the Synthetic Media Framework to ensure identification and disclosure of AI-generated content.

2023 UK AI Safety Summit Response (Meta) invested in research on AI societal, safety, and security risks, and collaborates with policymakers through the Open Loop program.

2023 UK AI Safety Summit Response (Meta) conducted privacy reviews for AI data inputs, excluding private user data, and offers users control over data shared with generative AI features.

HHS Public Benefits and AI requires the United States Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to promote responsible AI use in public benefits administration by State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Governments (STLTs).

HHS Public Benefits and AI encourages STLTs to align with the principles of the National Institute of Standards and Technology AI Risk Management Framework and the Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights.

HHS Public Benefits and AI recommends STLTs assess AI systems for equitable outcomes, notify recipients about AI use, and ensure human oversight and appeal processes.

HHS Public Benefits and AI supports STLTs in developing AI policies and practices through guidance, technical assistance, and resources.

HHS Public Benefits and AI urges STLTs to focus on safeguarding privacy, civil rights, and safety, and to provide opt-out options for AI systems.

HHS Public Benefits and AI emphasizes the need for transparency, public engagement, and governance to manage AI-associated risks.

HHS Public Benefits and AI directs HHS to work with STLTs and other agencies to ensure AI systems in public benefits programs are safe, equitable, and efficient.

USDA Framework for State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Use of Artificial Intelligence for Public Benefit Administration requires notification to the Secretary in cases of reliance on AI, allowing appeals to human reviewers and ensuring auditability of AI decisions.

USDA Framework for State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Use of Artificial Intelligence for Public Benefit Administration advocates for transparency and accountability, providing opt-out options from AI systems.

USDA Framework for State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Use of Artificial Intelligence for Public Benefit Administration encourages responsible innovation, requiring AI usage only with appropriate training and governance.

USDA Framework for State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Use of Artificial Intelligence for Public Benefit Administration requires SLTT agencies to report AI usage and its impact, with ongoing monitoring to mitigate risks and biases.

USDA Framework for State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Use of Artificial Intelligence for Public Benefit Administration stresses collaboration with tribes to respect data sovereignty.

Frontier AI Safety Commitments, AI Seoul Summit 2024 announces on behalf of the UK and Republic of Korea governments companies, including Amazon, Google, and OpenAI, that have committed to the Frontier AI Safety Commitments. Mandates that companies publish a safety framework, requires transparency on evolving safety approaches, and implement various best practices.

Frontier AI Safety Commitments, AI Seoul Summit 2024 defines outcome one as organizations identifying, assessing, and managing risks when developing and deploying frontier AI systems. Defines five sub-outcomes, including internal and external evaluations, establishment of risk thresholds and response processes for violations, and investment in risk mitigation effectiveness.

Frontier AI Safety Commitments, AI Seoul Summit 2024 defines outcome two as organizational accountability established through the development and review of governance frameworks.

Frontier AI Safety Commitments, AI Seoul Summit 2024 defines outcome three as established transparency about organizational approaches to frontier AI safety for external actors, including governments. Mandates provision of information about best practice implementation to the public and explanation of how external actors are involved in risk assessment and framework adherence.

Guidance on Application of the Fair Housing Act to the Advertising of Housing, Credit, and Other Real Estate-Related Transactions through Digital Platforms explains how the Fair Housing Act applies to housing-related advertising via AI and algorithmic systems on digital platforms.

Guidance on Application of the Fair Housing Act to the Advertising of Housing, Credit, and Other Real Estate-Related Transactions through Digital Platforms prohibits discriminatory advertising practices based on protected characteristics such as race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, or disability.

Guidance on Application of the Fair Housing Act to the Advertising of Housing, Credit, and Other Real Estate-Related Transactions through Digital Platforms warns that audience categorization and algorithmic delivery tools can unintentionally lead to discrimination by excluding or targeting groups based on protected characteristics.

Guidance on Application of the Fair Housing Act to the Advertising of Housing, Credit, and Other Real Estate-Related Transactions through Digital Platforms requires advertisers and platforms to avoid using AI tools that segment audiences by protected characteristics or proxies like geographic location.

Guidance on Application of the Fair Housing Act to the Advertising of Housing, Credit, and Other Real Estate-Related Transactions through Digital Platforms urges ad platforms to disable certain targeting functions for housing ads and conduct regular audits to ensure compliance with the Act.

Guidance on Application of the Fair Housing Act to the Advertising of Housing, Credit, and Other Real Estate-Related Transactions through Digital Platforms recommends that advertisers and platforms manage discriminatory risks by utilizing separate processes for housing-related ads and monitoring ad delivery outcomes for bias.

Guidance on Application of the Fair Housing Act to the Advertising of Housing, Credit, and Other Real Estate-Related Transactions through Digital Platforms advises documenting and publicly sharing information on ad targeting functions to ensure transparency and accountability.

Increasing AI Capacity Across the Federal Government: AI Talent Surge Progress and Recommendations proposes an AI scholarship-for-service program and public service cultivation within the tech ecosystem.

Increasing AI Capacity Across the Federal Government: AI Talent Surge Progress and Recommendations encourages global AI talent engagement and provides guidance for improving Federal hiring experiences.

Government-wide Hiring Authorities for Advancing Federal Government
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) permits use of excepted service Schedule A appointments for temporary staffing to support the implementation of EO 14110, with appointments valid for up to two years.

Government-wide Hiring Authorities for Advancing Federal Government
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) requires agencies to submit quarterly reports detailing hires made under this direct hire authority, including job announcements and number of hires.

Government-wide Hiring Authorities for Advancing Federal Government
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) stipulates agencies must adhere to veterans’ preference and public notice requirements when filling positions under these authorities.

Government-wide Hiring Authorities for Advancing Federal Government
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) allows OPM to request information and assess the continued need for these authorities, with the possibility of modification or termination.

Safe and Responsible AI in Australia Consultation, Interim Response proposes strengthening existing laws and considering new legislation to address AI-related risks, particularly in high-risk settings.

Safe and Responsible AI in Australia Consultation, Interim Response considers mandatory safety guardrails for AI systems in high-risk contexts, focusing on testing, transparency, and accountability.

Safe and Responsible AI in Australia Consultation, Interim Response plans to work with industry to develop a voluntary AI Safety Standard and explore options for voluntary labelling and watermarking of AI-generated materials.

Safe and Responsible AI in Australia Consultation, Interim Response emphasizes a risk-based regulatory framework to ensure proportionality and avoid unnecessary burdens on low-risk AI applications.

Safe and Responsible AI in Australia Consultation, Interim Response commits to collaborating with international partners, aligning with global standards, and contributing to initiatives like the Bletchley Declaration on AI safety.

Safe and Responsible AI in Australia Consultation, Interim Response supports investments in AI capability development and aims to maximize AI benefits, including through initiatives funded by the 2023–24 Budget.

Safe and Responsible AI in Australia Consultation, Interim Response establishes an interim expert advisory group to explore AI guardrail options and harmonizes efforts with state and territory governments.

Public Act 103-0804 amends the Illinois Human Rights Act to regulate the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in employment-related decisions.

Public Act 103-0804 prohibits employers from using AI in recruitment, hiring, promotion, or other employment practices if it results in discrimination based on protected classes.

Public Act 103-0804 requires employers to notify employees if AI is used in employment decisions.

Public Act 103-0804 mandates the Illinois Department of Human Rights to adopt rules for implementing these AI-related provisions, including specifying conditions and timelines for providing notice.

Public Act 103-0804 defines "artificial intelligence" as a machine-based system generating outputs like predictions or decisions that can influence environments.

Public Act 103-0804 includes "generative artificial intelligence" as systems producing content simulating human-produced content based on prompts.

Public Act 103-0804 takes effect on January 1, 2026.

Artificial Intelligence for California Research Act directs the California Department of Technology to develop and implement a research plan on the feasibility and risks of advanced technologies, specifically AI, to improve state and local government services.

Artificial Intelligence for California Research Act requires the research plan to include an analysis of the potential benefits and risks of using AI chatbots/assistance in various government benefit and welfare programs (such as disability insurance or affordable housing), a review of best practices from other governments, a cost-benefit analysis of implementing AI in government services, recommendations for effective integration (including risk management and monitoring and evaluation guidelines), and recommendations for mitigating privacy issues.

Artificial Intelligence for California Research Act instructs the Department of Technology to report its findings to the legislature before January 1, 2026.

Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Draft for Comment) requires AI-generated content in China to meet a series of criteria, including accuracy, non-discrimination with regard to an array of protected characteristics, intellectual property protection, exclusion of violent content or content that subverts state power, and respect for individual privacy.

Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Draft for Comment) requires AI developers to conduct a security assessment on generative AI systems that evaluates the cybersecurity of the system and its ability to comply with regulations; the assessment must be submitted to regulators before the system can be released for public use.

Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Draft for Comment) requires AI developers to prevent their generative AI systems from being used for various purposes, including engaging in unfair economic competition, and requires generative AI systems to make themselves inaccessible to individuals who use the systems for such purposes.

Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Draft for Comment) describes the legal liability that developers hold for the content generated by their AI systems and the punishments, including fines, they may face for violating these rules.

National New Generation AI Standards System Construction Guide aims to clarify top-level design and develop key standards by 2023, focusing on data, algorithms, systems, and industry-specific applications.

National New Generation AI Standards System Construction Guide outlines an AI standards architecture, comprising eight categories: basic standards, supporting technologies, software/hardware platforms, general/niche technologies, products/services, industry applications, and security/ethics.

National New Generation AI Standards System Construction Guide emphasizes the need for international cooperation and alignment with global standards to ensure high-quality AI development.

National New Generation AI Standards System Construction Guide prioritizes the development of standards for key technologies such as machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, and quantum computing.

National New Generation AI Standards System Construction Guide addresses AI applications across various sectors, including healthcare, transportation, finance, and smart cities, ensuring cross-industry standardization.

National New Generation AI Standards System Construction Guide focuses on security and ethics, proposing standards for AI data, algorithms, models, and application security, alongside ethical guidelines for impactful AI use.

National Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Strategic Plan 2023 Update reaffirms eight strategies and adds a ninth to emphasize international collaboration in AI research.

National Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Strategic Plan 2023 Update prioritizes investments in fundamental and responsible AI research, human-AI collaboration, and understanding ethical, legal, and societal implications.

National Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Strategic Plan 2023 Update advances safety and security standards for AI systems, ensuring they are reliable and secure from vulnerabilities.

National Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Strategic Plan 2023 Update develops shared public datasets and environments for AI training and testing to democratize access to AI resources.

National Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Strategic Plan 2023 Update establishes benchmarks and standards for evaluating AI systems, including fairness, privacy, and bias considerations.

National Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Strategic Plan 2023 Update addresses workforce needs by training and retraining a diverse AI-ready workforce.

National Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Strategic Plan 2023 Update expands public-private partnerships to accelerate AI advances and facilitate global collaborations for responsible AI development.

National Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Strategic Plan 2023 Update emphasizes the importance of AI governance and the development of international guidelines and standards for AI systems.
